institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Financial Accounting Fundamentals
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Expand your foundational literacy in accounting, the language of business. This course helps you to build a firm grounding in financial accounting principles and methods. Understanding how accounting works is vital for effectively communicating business performance, and is your window to understanding financial drivers of business success. To this end, you will learn the basics of recording, summarizing, and reporting financial transactions, preparing financial statements, and analyzing financial information to make informed business decisions.
learning_outcomes: Construct clear and accurate financial statements and explain the inter-relationships of their components to support strong business decision-making.
Confidently communicate accounting concepts to stakeholders to influence business and investor decisions.

Synthesise information relating to national and international developments in accounting standard setting, accounting research, and media reports to discuss how real-world companies are impacted by accounting.
Evaluate the appropriateness of accounting policies used to prepare financial statements to accurately determine the financial position and performance of a range of companies.
Use accounting methods and industry software to accurately record business transactions.
Discuss the potential impacts of business decisions on internal and external stakeholders to develop and express professional judgment.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM1140 or COMM1240 or ACCT1501

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Placement 1
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course provides scholars with a practical application of the fundamental principles of accounting in an industry environment. This course is only available to Accounting, UNSW Business School Co-op Scholars who are enrolled in the BCom(Coop).
learning_outcomes: Apply tools, techniques and frameworks to evaluate and understand the role of accounting and business management practices in attaining the sponsor organisation’s goals.
Discuss the importance of relationships within the sponsor’s workplace.
Collaborate effectively and display collaborative skills in teamwork.
Demonstrate the professional competencies accounting students need for entry-level success in sponsor organisation.
Describe the sponsoring organisations’ business practices relevant to the discipline of accounting and business management.
Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in Accounting Co-op Major (ACCTB13554)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Management Accounting for Decision Analysis
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Become an indispensable advisor to contemporary organisations and create value for both customers and shareholders. This course will equip you with the knowledge and analytical skills to become a trusted business partner and effective decision maker. You will learn to improve business processes, enhance managerial decision making and develop critical thinking and communication skills. You will be introduced to a range of management accounting tools and techniques and learn to apply them critically and creatively in a variety of business contexts.
learning_outcomes: Use management accounting tools and analytic techniques to improve business processes and enhance organisations' competitiveness through managing costs, quality, and time.
Identify, evaluate, and analyse relevant management accounting information to make strategic and operational decisions.
Demonstrate the ability to work individually and in teams.
Develop insightful recommendations based on analyses of financial and nonfinancial information, and present these to stakeholders in a professional manner.
Design performance measurement systems and incentive schemes that motivate internal stakeholders to achieve organisational goals.
Demonstrate the importance of accurate costing and apply different costing techniques and systems to support organisational decision-making.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (COMM1170 AND COMM1180) OR ACCT1511

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Corporate Financial Reporting and Analysis
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course covers financial accounting at an advanced level, with a focus on business combination accounting, group accounting (subsidiaries and joint arrangements), and foreign currency accounting (translation). The topics of this course are useful for understanding mergers and acquisitions valuation, financial statement analysis, and financial valuation methods. Financial analysts, financial statement preparers, and merger and acquisition specialists are examples of professions that use this knowledge taught in this course. Students develop their judgement, and critical-thinking skills through study of complex financial accounting issues. The topics provide coverage to develop skills to understand and know the areas that involve professional judgement in financial statement preparation, annual report analysis and insights into potential impacts of contemporary accounting uses affecting the business community under consideration by accounting standard setters.
learning_outcomes: Combine financial accounting concepts and communication skills to effectively address a specific audience and purpose.
Apply selected Australian Accounting Standard Board requirements to the preparation of a general-purpose financial report for a group of related companies and their associated entities.
Critically think about how responsible and ethical accounting policy choices impact the usefulness of financial reports and the welfare of stakeholders.
Demonstrate the ability to work independently and seek and use feedback to ensure continuing self-improvement.
Describe the financial reporting requirements that apply to Australian corporate groups.
Explain the main issues involved in the preparation of a general-purpose financial report for a group of related companies and their associated entities.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT1511 or ACCT2511

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: ESG: Current Developments for Sustainable Business
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Discover how companies are evolving to meet today's dynamic Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) demands. This course takes you on a deep dive into the evolving world of business reporting, where you'll uncover how emerging reporting frameworks are enabling companies to interpret and communicate their social, environmental, and economic performance. By the end of the course, you'll master the art of identifying material ESG risks and learn to effectively report these risks to stakeholders. You'll also gain the expertise to craft a persuasive business case that showcases how addressing ESG risks can drive long-term sustainability and substantial value creation.
learning_outcomes: Observe the process of assurance for emerging forms of business reporting and critique the challenges of offering assurance over material ESG risks.
Apply business reporting frameworks to identify and interpret the material ESG-related risks faced by modern companies.
Design and prepare a business case that showcases how a company can respond to ESG-related risks to ensure long-term value creation.
Identify and critique the different forms of business reporting that have emerged in response to contemporary ESG demands.
Identify the foundations and purpose of traditional business reporting and assess its suitability to incorporate ESG factors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM1140 or COMM1240

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Strategic Value Management
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Learn to co-create value for multiple stakeholders in contemporary organisations. In this course, you will learn how to collect, analyse, and use both financial and non-financial information in order to develop, implement and assess the success of the strategy, while simultaneously balancing the needs of stakeholders including shareholders, suppliers, community and environment, and employees. You will also learn how strategies are developed and evaluated given the external environment an organisation operates in and the resources and capabilities they have. You will develop your skills in a team environment by researching an organisation's strategy, writing a report, and presenting persuasive recommendations to stakeholders.
learning_outcomes: Produce business reports and presentation of a professional standard suitable to address senior management.
Formulate and implement organisational strategies based on thorough research of an organisation's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats.
Identify and apply a set of management tools, techniques, and frameworks to an organisation in a team setting.

Evaluate organisational strategy by focusing on four perspectives of strategic performance (i.e., shareholder perspective, customer perspective, internal process perspective and, learning and growth perspective).
Work collaboratively by navigating the teamwork process and providing meaningful evaluative feedback to team members.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completion of at least 84 UOC

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Global Financial Reporting and Analysis
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Do you want to work for Goldmans in New York, Tencent in Shanghai or Bain in London? Or run a business with international operations? Planning on having investments with international diversification? In each case you will come across financial reports prepared under different reporting environments. This course will help you understand why there are international differences in financial reporting rules and regulations, and what the key differences are. Most importantly, you will see why these differences matter when you are assessing accounting quality, undertaking valuation tasks, or analysing credit quality. Real-world examples and international databases are key learning tools in this course.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and compare major IFRS/US-GAAP treatments and enforcement regimes, highlighting implications for analysis and valuation.
Communicate actionable financial insights through concise, stakeholder-tailored stories that integrate quantitative analysis and strategic context.
Analyse how different legal, cultural and capital-market institutions shape global reporting environments and strategic choices.
Critically appraise alternative performance and sustainability metrics across jurisdictions, including their decision usefulness and ethical dimensions.
Apply analytic technologies to transform raw data into clear visuals and narratives that support business decisions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT2542

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Issues in Financial Reporting and Analysis
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Aspiring to become a CFO, audit partner, professional investor, or accredited accountant? You'll need a deep understanding of the complex topics and significant issues influencing corporate reporting outcomes. This course covers critical reporting choices financial leaders make and the ethical, theoretical, market, and other influences that bear on these choices. You will also learn how to account for complex matters such as financial instruments and leases, along with how accounting information affects share prices. Mastering the skills from this course will enable you analyse and positively influence accounting decisions that shape a firm's bottom line.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate current controversial trends in financial accounting.
Describe alternative theories that explain accounting practices.
Evaluate measurement issues, for example, fair value versus historical cost, related to the covered topics.
Work collaboratively to complete a group assignment and class activities.
Make judgments about measurement and recognition issues in relevant areas of accounting.
Communicate clearly to a professional standard appropriate to an audience of senior accounting executives.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT2542

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Thesis (Accounting) A
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Honours students complete a thesis under the direction of a supervisor. The thesis requires the reporting of research in an approved topic area in accounting including a literature review, analysis of a research problem along with presentation of research methods and data analysis.
learning_outcomes: Advanced knowledge of a field: Our graduates will have the ability to understand, apply and critically reflect on an advanced body of knowledge within a particular field.
Research capability: Our graduates will have the ability to undertake a piece of research in the relevant field.
Communication: Our graduates will have the ability to communicate research effectively.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Independent research - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Placement 3
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: It is the third of three fully assessable Industry Training courses Co-op Scholars complete as part of their Bachelor of Commerce (Co-op) degree. It allows you to apply the fundamental principles of accounting and business management to accounting practices in their sponsoring organisation. Note: Only available to Accounting, UNSW Business School Co-op Scholars.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse accounting and business management concepts through reflective practice.
Apply tools, techniques and frameworks to evaluate and understand the role of accounting and business management practices in attaining the sponsor organisation’s goals.
Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner for a business context.
Collaborate effectively and display collaborative skills in teamwork.
Demonstrate the professional competencies accounting students need for entry-level success in sponsor organisation.
Discuss the importance of relationships within the sponsor’s workplace.
Describe the sponsoring organisations’ business practices relevant to the discipline of accounting and business management.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in Accounting Co-op Major (ACCTB13554)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Accounting Analytics for Business Decision Making
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Analytics combined with accounting data is at the heart of most forward-looking corporate decisions. Investment bankers, equity research analysts, portfolio managers, credit analysts, lenders, and capital market regulators rely on accounting data to identify investment opportunities, assess business risks, and negotiate business contracts. This course will help you gain basic understanding of how professionals use analytics tools to leverage accounting data to produce significant insights and make meaningful predictions. Most importantly, you will learn how accounting analytics are applied in real-world business contexts, such as quantitative investing, financial fraud prediction, earnings forecasting, etc. You will use numerous real-world case studies in lectures, tutorials, and assessments to reinforce your learnings. NOTE: This course was previously identified as ACCT2672 . Students who have completed ACCT2672 cannot enrol in ACCT3672.
learning_outcomes: Extract the right data from different sources to solve accounting and business problems.
Ability to identify and define business problems
Work effectively both individually and in teams to communicate accounting and business insights to a specific audience and to inform, persuade or decide on the best course of action.
Visualise and translate insights into concrete actions that businesses can take.
Select and apply the appropriate analytical tools to generate insights in accounting and business contexts.
Explain the importance of data analytics in contemporary business contexts and developing an appropriate analytical mindset
prerequisites: Pre-requisite: (ACCT1501 or COMM1140 or COMM1240) AND 65+ WAM

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Reporting for Climate Change and Sustainability
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Climate change and sustainability are key challenges for our society and economy today and these areas provide great opportunities for future employment. Governments and non-governmental organisations around the world have engaged in various climate change mitigation and adaptation policy initiatives to ensure survival and prosperity of current and future generations. This course explores issues related to climate change and sustainability and the implications for businesses that will lead to better business reporting. Insights on established and proposed policy frameworks will provide students with an overview of the trends in sustainability reporting and the ability to start preparing a sustainability report in their current or future employment. Impact of the recent establishment of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) by the IFRS Foundation will also be covered particularly the release of sustainability standards and how Australia is responding to this generational shift in business reporting. Finally, the credibility enhancing mechanisms used to increase trust in sustainability reports will also be discussed and in particular how this may deter organisations from greenwashing.
learning_outcomes: Interpret the role of assurance in sustainability reporting and GHG reporting.
Develop critical thinking, oral and written communication skills and professional approaches to emerging business issues in a competitive and carbon constrained economy.
Observe why businesses need to support sustainable development practices.

Articulate mandatory and voluntary reporting frameworks on sustainability and be able to identify the costs and benefits of these initiatives (e.g. GHG Protocol, GRI, SDGs, TCFD, ISSB, and the NGER Act).
Identify emerging issues that arise due to climate change and its implications to businesses.
Identify strategies to adapt and mitigate the effects of climate change.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM1140 or COMM1240 or DPBS1140

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Fraud Examination Fundamentals
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: How can you, as a future accountant or manager, join the fight against organizational fraud? This course teaches you how to safeguard businesses against fraud. It covers what fraud is, why people do it, and how you can best prevent and detect it. You will also learn how to investigate fraud using the latest available methods and techniques. Designed in collaboration with experts from a leading forensic accounting firm and law enforcement agencies, this course equips you to understand organizational fraud vulnerabilities and take control. It is also an essential first step toward an exciting career in forensic accounting.
learning_outcomes: Investigate a range of sources to assess and report on fraudulent activities with accuracy, confidentiality, and following best practice.
Explain and apply recognised, practical approaches for preventing and detecting fraud in organisations.
Design a fraud investigation interview to extract information from a range of unique stakeholders effectively and sensitively.
Explain common types of fraud offence and current fraud trends observed in organisations.
Apply researched theories and frameworks to explain the motivations and factors leading to fraud.
Make cohesive, evidence-backed recommendations both individually and within a group to persuade a managerial audience.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM1140 or COMM1240

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Analysis and Valuation
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course equips you with essential skills to analyse and value firms using information primarily sourced from company financial reports. For students aspiring to careers in consulting, investment banking, or entrepreneurship, this course builds your ability to examine financial statements and disclosures for insights into the core strategic attributes and value drivers of a company. You will learn to use techniques for structured analysis of profitability, growth and develop forecasts of earnings and cashflows. Theoretical foundations are blended with hands-on application through real-world case studies and practical exercises using financial databases. By the end of the course, you will be well-equipped to make informed equity (share) valuation and credit assessment, and debt valuation decisions.
learning_outcomes: Identify and assess environmental and sustainability considerations in valuation and portfolio construction.
Explain the linkage between strategic business analysis, accounting analysis and financial analysis. Identify and utilize relevant information contained in financial statements.
Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented.
Identify and analyse issues relating to accounting quality. Prepare and substantiate a valuation that incorporates the strategic, accounting and financial activities of a business entity.
Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Work collaboratively to complete tasks.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT2511 AND (COMM1180 or ECON1102)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: ESG Reporting and Enterprise Value Creation
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Are you interested in learning about how business leaders embed responsible decision making throughout an organisation? How they lead managers, staff and others across their value chain to not only deliver financial outcomes, but also sustainable business outcomes that deliver positive returns over time to all key stakeholders, including society and the environment. Do you want to work in investment banking, as an executive at a major corporate, join a consulting firm or start your own business? Do you have a passion for both business and sustainability and having a positive impact on society and the environment? This course will help you understand how business leaders are driving change across their organisations to ensure all key decisions more effectively consider the broader impact of potential outcomes on all important resources and relationships before taking action to deliver the most sustainable outcomes over time. Most importantly, through real world examples and worked case studies, you will be asked questions to assist you in making more responsible business decisions. You will also learn about the importance of intangibles to business value and understand how these together with ESG matters, are being identified, managed and reported on by quality 21st century organisations.
learning_outcomes: Explain ethical, environmental and sustainability considerations in business reporting
Identify the Integrated Reporting Framework and its requirements for the preparation of an Integrated Report.
Communicate professionally both orally in writing in class discussions, presentations, teamwork and written work.

Detail the changes required in a business to change the underlying systems, processes and behaviours to implement 'investor grade' Integrated Reporting and embed Integrated Thinking across the organisation.
Identify ESG, other intangible value drivers and Integrated Reporting and its relevance to business decision making and enterprise value creation.
Critically evaluate examples of integrated reports, case situations and the related academic research.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completed 72 UOC

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Placement 2
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course provides you with a practical application of the fundamental principles of accounting in an industry environment. Note: Only available to UNSW Accounting & Business Management Co-op Scholars.
learning_outcomes: Describe the sponsoring organisations’ business processes relevant to the discipline of accounting and business management.
Identify and research issues in business situations, analyse the issues, and propose appropriate and well-justified solutions in a particular industry.
Demonstrate a better understanding of professional competencies and skills which can be improved.
Participate collaboratively and responsibly in teams, and reflect on your own teamwork, and on the team’s processes and ability to achieve outcomes effectively.
Select and apply relevant disciplinary knowledge to support organizations' business functions.
Identify and assess ethical, environmental and/or sustainability considerations in business processes (may be addressed if relevant to student's ITE2 Research Project)
Communicate effectively in diverse workplace situations.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in Accounting Co-op Major (ACCTB13554)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Auditing and Assurance Services
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Assurance is a cornerstone of the modern international economy as it allows investors and other stakeholders to have faith in the reliability of financial reports and other information produced by companies. Auditing is the systematic process by which assurance is provided to stakeholders. In this subject you will learn how to audit the financial statements of an Australian company following the rules set down in the Corporations Act (2001) and Australian Auditing Standards. This will include assessing business risk, evaluating internal controls, collecting sufficient appropriate audit evidence, forming an audit opinion, and expressing this opinion in a written audit report. In this subject, you will also examine auditing and assurance in their broader social context through an analysis of the economic benefits of assurance, ethical behaviour and legal obligations of auditors, fraud risks and responses, and assurance of sustainability reports.
learning_outcomes: Write a report of a suitable standard for presentation to senior auditors.

Design an audit strategy to address the risks of errors in the financial statements through the collection and analysis of sufficient appropriate audit evidence and the communication of the auditor’s findings.
Evaluate the role of the auditor in its broader social context, with reference to the economic value of assurance, ethical considerations, fraud, and the provision of sustainability assurance.
Analyse the business risks faced by a company and the extent to which these are mitigated by internal controls.
Work in a team and manage and evaluate the teamwork process through peer evaluation.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT2542 or approval from the School

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Current Developments in Accounting Research - Financial
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Review of alternative approaches to the development of theories in external reporting. Explication and evaluation of substantive theories and associated research studies. Examination of research findings related to the accounting and reporting environment, agency cost and financial contracting, the properties of reported accounting numbers, predictive value of accounting information, the use of information in capital markets, and the use of accounting reports by individual decision makers.
learning_outcomes: Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented.
Collaborate actively in learning activities aimed at achieving the above objectives
Critically analyse and evaluate extant and proposed financial accounting research.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in program 4501 (Accounting)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Current Developments in Accounting Research - Managerial
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of contemporary management accounting research, which emanates from different philosophical perspectives and employs different theories and research methods. Research is divided into two broad streams: work that seeks (a) to explain and design, and (b) to understand and interpret the practice of management accounting in organisation and societies.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and evaluate extant and proposed management accounting research.
Understand the strengths and weaknesses associated with management accounting research.
Identify contemporary research areas in the field of management accounting.
Prepare a research proposal in the context of management accounting.
Appreciate a range of paradigms and methods for conducting management accounting research.
Defend a research proposal to peers.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in program 4501 (Accounting)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Current Developments in Auditing Research
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Current Developments in Auditing Research is designed to extend disciplinary perspectives in auditing and provide training for research in auditing and assurance services. The course focuses on current areas of research in auditing and related assurance services. The following topics will be covered: some of the main empirical and theoretical developments in auditing research; the main research methods used in auditing research; alternative research methods; the practical implications of current research in auditing; the relationship of research to practice and standard-setting, and statistical tools to use in audit research.
learning_outcomes: Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented.
Conduct research in an ethical manner.
Identify possible future developments in audit theory and research.
Collaborate effectively in learning activities aimed at achieving the above objectives.
Identify possible relationships between research in auditing, auditing practice and auditing regulation.
Identify and articulate contemporary research issues and trends in the field of auditing and assurance.
Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Critically analyse and evaluate extant and proposed audit and assurance research.
Identify and differentiate a range of intellectual frameworks and methods for conducting auditing and assurance research.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Seminar in Research Methodology
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: To assist BCom Hons students in completion of research project requirement. This course considers the relationship between science and scientific method; reviews some of the research methods commonly used to conduct research in accounting; and provides an introduction to the interpretation of the key statistical techniques used in accounting research. May consist of an examinable readings program defined to meet the needs of a particular student or a formal program undertaken by a group of students whose research projects are in a common area.
learning_outcomes: Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Construct written work that is logically and professionally presented.
Critique and evaluate a research design.

Conduct a literature review, develop a research question and related hypotheses and design an appropriate study to test the hypotheses. You should be able to conduct research using experimental, survey, archival and qualitative research methods.
Understand and conduct basic quantitative data analysis.
Conduct reading of academic accounting articles, understand them and critique them.
Demonstrate awareness of ethical issues in conducting research.
Design a research study to address a specific research question and/or hypotheses.
Evaluate the pros and cons of various research methods to evaluate a research question.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in program 4501 (Accounting)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Financial Literacy for Business Decisions
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Join us on a dynamic exploration of pivotal accounting concepts tailored to empower innovative business leaders. This course gives you the “Ten Most Important Things” you need to know to understand and run a successful business. We will give you the ability to be a successful manager, by applying an entrepreneurial mindset to ensure financial success. The knowledge you acquire is not only relevant, but critical for aspiring business professionals seeking to manage your own business and make informed financial decisions.
learning_outcomes: Apply investment analysis techniques to make sound decisions that enhance shareholder value, including applying the cost of capital in decision-making where appropriate..
Describe the purpose and use of the major external financial statements; identify the differences between cash and accrual accounting, and develop a basic understanding of transaction analysis
Apply financial knowledge to real-world situations and integrate business literature where appropriate, and reflect on personal learning and growth.
Articulate how managing margins and product costing directly impacts the value creation process in a business.
Identify and apply taxation fundamentals for running a successful business.
Develop skills to effectively collaborate, lead teams, and manage differences in a business setting.
Identify and explain the strategic role of performance measures in achieving competitive advantage.
Develop a business plan that demonstrates a deep understanding of how planning drives business success.
prerequisites: Students in programs 8409, 8415, 8413 OR in ACCTES or ACCTYS Masters of Commerce specialisations are not permitted to take this course. Students who have taken ACCT5930 previously should not take this course.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: International Financial Statement Analysis
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course introduces analytics tools used in the analysis of financial statements to identify and understand the economic reality and strategic use of accounting numbers. You will learn to evaluate financial performance, identify sources of value creation and risk and credit assessment, and techniques used in assessing the achievement of financial targets and strategic goals. If you are aiming to become a future CFO at a leading company or a financial analyst at a top investment bank, this course is for you.
learning_outcomes: Identify and infer red flags of company performance from financial statements and other public sources such as news articles.

Respond appropriately to conclusions from financial statement analysis and adjustments, such as by developing questions to pose to management in conference calls and making investment decisions or recommendations.
Apply financial statement analysis techniques to current corporate actions, business trends, and regulatory filings of companies from the US, Europe, and Asia.
Gather and apply information from company investor relations webpages, and filings from regulatory sources (such as US SEC EDGAR).
Present results of analysis and adjusted financial results, to an informed investor audience, in writing and/or in oral presentations with visual aids.
Identify and explain financial reporting and earnings quality.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT5930

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Auditing and Assurance Services
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Do you want to understand the operations of a broad range of businesses and threats to the success of those businesses? Do you want to apply that knowledge to the determination of whether financial and other corporate reporting is reliable? Assurance is the cornerstone of the modern international economy as it allows investors and other stakeholders to have faith in the reliability of financial and other information produced by companies. This course will help you understand how to develop and use a comprehensive understanding of the business and its interdependencies to test the reliability of corporate reporting. You will focus on financial reporting as well as emerging and increasingly important corporate reporting on climate and other sustainability topics.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply the ethical, professional, legal, commercial, and regulatory framework governing audit and other assurance services.
Exhibit effective communication, encompassing the delivery of clear and concise plans, summaries, and conclusions related to audit activities, enhanced by emotional intelligence and self-awareness.
Critically analyze business environments to pinpoint audit and assurance challenges, ensuring a consistent and competent approach to performing the work and interpreting results.
Demonstrate independent learning and collaborative excellence, employing strategies that enhance teamwork and generate synergy in outcomes for the group.
Evaluate the role and impact of audit and assurance services on the economy and society, maintaining a focus on their relevance and contributions.
Critically apply contemporary audit processes and diverse techniques effectively across various contexts to achieve audit and assurance objectives.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT5942

assessment_tasks.task_name: In-person - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly) - T1
In-person - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly) - T3

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Current Developments in Auditing Research
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Current Developments in Auditing Research is designed to extend disciplinary perspectives in auditing and provide training for research in auditing and assurance services. The course focuses on current areas of research in auditing and related assurance services. The following topics will be covered: some of the main empirical and theoretical developments in auditing research; the main research methods used in auditing research; alternative research methods; the practical implications of current research in auditing; the relationship of research to practice and standard-setting, and statistical tools to use in audit research.
learning_outcomes: Conduct research in an ethical manner.
Identify and differentiate a range of intellectual frameworks and methods for conducting auditing and assurance research.
Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented.
Identify possible future developments in audit theory and research.
Critically analyse and evaluate extant and proposed audit and assurance research.
Identify and articulate contemporary research issues and trends in the field of auditing and assurance.
Identify possible relationships between research in auditing, auditing practice and auditing regulation.
Collaborate effectively in learning activities aimed at achieving the above objectives.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in program 4501 (Accounting)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Analysis and Valuation
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course provides you with vital skills to analyse and assess companies using data primarily obtained from corporate financial statements. Aimed at students pursuing careers in consulting, investment banking, or entrepreneurship, it enhances your capability to scrutinise financial statements and disclosures to uncover a company's core strategic traits and value drivers. You will master techniques for systematically analysing profitability and growth, and develop forecasts for earnings and cash flows. The course combines theoretical foundations with practical application through real-world case studies and exercises using financial databases. By its conclusion, you will be adept at making informed decisions regarding equity valuation, credit assessment, and debt valuation.
learning_outcomes: Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Identify and analyse issues relating to accounting quality. Prepare and substantiate a valuation that incorporates the strategic, accounting and financial activities of a business entry.
Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented.
Identify and assess environmental and sustainability considerations in valuation and portfolio construction.
Work collaboratively to complete tasks.
Explain the linkage between strategic business analysis, accounting analysis and financial analysis. Identify and utilize relevant information contained in financial statements.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ((ACCT5930 or ACCT5906) AND (FINS5511 or FINS5513 or FINS5514)) OR (enrolment in program 8406)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Risk Management
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to prepare you to navigate the complexities of modern business environments, ideal for those aspiring to leadership roles or strategic management positions. In today’s global landscape, businesses face unprecedented challenges and uncertainties, including rapid technological advancements, shorter product life cycles, heightened customer and societal expectations, and various internal and external risks. This course provides a comprehensive exploration of business risk management, addressing key risks that impact value creation such as competition, financial constraints, regulatory and legal requirements, corporate leadership issues, strategy execution, and organisational capabilities. Through a blend of conceptual frameworks, technical skills, and speculative approaches, students will gain a deep understanding of how to identify, assess, and manage these risks. Case studies and research are integral to the curriculum, offering practical insights and real-world applications. By the end of this course, you will be well-equipped to contribute to an organisations' resilience and sustainability in an ever-changing global environment.
learning_outcomes: Formulate and develop persuasive arguments relevant to major fields of study that can be applied to business problems.
Collaborate effectively in groups of diverse backgrounds to manage, persuade and influence others.
Apply fundamental theories and concepts in diverse and unpredictable business environments to better understand commercial and business issues.
Critically analyse underlying theories, concepts, assumptions, and arguments in major fields of study.
Communicate effectively in verbal, written, and group contexts to a professional standard.

Apply specialist skills, tools, techniques, and frameworks to critically analyse business risks and to integrate these with knowledge drawn from other disciplines of commerce in business and professional practice.
prerequisites: Prerequisite or Corequisite: ACCT5930 or COMM5003 or ACCT5906

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing Intangible Resources
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: In today’s dynamic business landscape, intangible assets account for ninety percent of market capitalisation. This course provides hands-on experience and tools and frameworks to measure and evaluate these assets, including the Balanced Scorecard. You will learn to translate complex data into meaningful narratives through real-world cases and explore concepts like Reputation Quotients and Net Promoter Scores. Understanding the constitution and value of intangible assets is crucial for business success because it allows companies to better leverage their intellectual property, reputation, and customer relationships, leading to more informed decision-making and sustained competitive advantage.
learning_outcomes: Learn how to successfully communicate in written work and pitch your ideas in a succinct and compelling (persuasive) manner using storytelling skills that engage an audience.
Evaluate how various tangible and intangible resources combine to create unique competitive strengths.
Describe and analyse tangible and intangible resources using leading frameworks.
Collaborate effectively as leaders, and display strong teamwork skills.
Measure and calculate intangibles using global tools and frameworks incorporating responsible business practices.
Interpret and critique the results of numbers produced by leading edge tools and frameworks for measuring intangibles.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: ESG Reporting and Enterprise Value Creation
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on the drivers of Enterprise Value creation, emphasizing the need for changes in business decision-making and reporting. It explores the significance of intangible value drivers, including ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) factors, and the growing importance of the Integrated Reporting Framework for responsible decision-making and transparent reporting on enterprise value over the short, medium and long-term. With ESG reporting gaining traction among investors and new sustainability accounting and reporting standards, the course demonstrates how Integrated Reporting enhances communication of performance and future prospects, enabling more sustainable value creation. Highly interactive with practical illustrations and case studies, this course prepares participants for careers in leading accounting, sustainability and consulting firms, Government and regulatory bodies, NGOs, and innovative corporations, all demanding expertise in sustainable business practices and corporate responsibility.
learning_outcomes: Identify ESG, other intangible value drivers and Integrated Reporting and its relevance to business decision making and Enterprise Value creation.
Critically evaluate examples of integrated reports, case situations and the related academic research.

Detail the changes required in a business to change the underlying systems, processes and behaviours to implement 'investor grade' Integrated Reporting and embed Integrated Thinking across the organisation.
Communicate professionally orally and in writing in class discussions, presentations, teamwork and written work.
Explain drivers of change and ethical, environmental and sustainability considerations in business reporting, including impact of the new Sustainability Accounting Standards.
Explain and apply the elements of the Integrated Reporting Framework and its requirements for the preparation of an Integrated Report.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Financial Accounting
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Accounting is the language of business, and this course is designed for future professionals in the accounting and finance field and entrepreneurs needing a solid foundation in financial accounting principles. This course will provide you with the foundations to prepare financial statements and communicate the financial impact of business events or decisions. You will also learn to interpret the key financial statements as well as sustainability performance to facilitate informed decision-making.
learning_outcomes: Apply the accounting cycle, including identification and recording of business transactions, financial period adjustments and prepare accurate and appropriately classified financial statements to assist decision-makers.
Execute the accounting cycle through to the creation of key financial statements for a simulated business in a commonly used accounting information system.
Decide the appropriate accounting treatment that aligns with the organisation’s objectives, regulatory requirements and financial reporting needs.
Analyse and interpret the key financial statements and sustainability performance to facilitate and contribute to informed decision-making of stakeholders.
Analyse and communicate the impact of business events or decisions on accounting policy choice on the key financial statements.
prerequisites: Students who have previously completed ACCT5906 should not enrol into this course.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Sustainable Management Accounting
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: In the words of Chanticleer at the Australian Financial Review (2024): “Making money is hard, let alone doing it when the goalposts are shifting around”. In the ESG (environmental, social and governance) era, sustainability matters – and it shift the goalposts for organisations. Whether you’re studying to become a sustainability consultant, financial analyst, business leader or young investor, this course will enable you to develop, analyse and evaluate business strategies to create sustainable value. We’ll bring strategy together with the numbers to look at financial, environmental, social and governance performance. Completing the course, you’ll be equipped to make business decisions using a sustainable performance lens, and considering different stakeholder perspectives.
learning_outcomes: Conduct applied business research (including case-based analyses) – to acquire, analyse and present knowledge.
Propose strategic initiatives and analyse their suitability, acceptability and feasibility for sustainable value creation.
Communicate knowledge and business insights – to inform and persuade through professional presentations using contemporary delivery modes.
Design appropriate performance measures, based on an understanding of the organisation’s environmental context and strategy for sustainable value creation.
Evaluate the business strategies of organisations, based on an understanding of their external and internal environments and key stakeholder expectations.
Learn how to work within teams – to collaborate with team members, to assume leadership and to manage differences and conflicts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (Completion of ACCT5996 and enrolled in 8409 or 8415 or 8413) OR (Completion of 42 UOC and ACCT5996 and enrolled in 8404 or 8417 or 8544 or 8339)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Ethics and Governance
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Ethics and governance are core components of the knowledge and skill base of professional accounting. As key business decision-makers, accountants must be proficient in regulatory regimes, compliance requirements and government mechanisms to ensure lawful, ethical and effective corporate behaviour and operations. Furthermore, today's professional accountants are involved with leadership and management more than ever, and are directly involved in many important decisions. An understanding of ethics and governance is thus essential. This course provides students with the analytical and decision-making skills and knowledge to identify and resolve professional and ethical issues they may face in future. This course is delivered in conjunction with CPA Australia.
learning_outcomes: Identify the strategic, leadership and global issues impacting accountants and the accounting profession
Explain the expectations placed on various internal and external stakeholders arising from organisational governance responsibilities
Describe key governance and regulatory frameworks, including international perspectives on corporate governance and the roles of various stakeholders
Ascertain various compliance and regulatory regimes impacting the global business environment
Explain from a global perspective the nature of the accounting profession and the roles of professional accountants
Apply the key professional responsibilities of an accountant from the perspective of a member of CPA Australia
Explain the importance of ethics and professional judgment
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415), OR (Enrolment in 5415)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Strategic Management Accounting
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Strategic management accounting is a key component of the overall skills base of today’s professional accountant. This course examines the management accountant’s strategic and value creating role in dynamic organisations operating in the global business environment. This course highlights the management accounting tools and techniques of value chain analysis and project management that have become increasingly important in contemporary operating environments. This course is delivered in conjunction with CPA Australia.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of performance measurement and control systems in value creation, strategy implementation and monitoring performance to improve strategies
Apply the strategic management process and organisational and industry value analysis to understand value drivers, cost drivers and the reconfiguring of value chains
Explain the role of the management accountant as a trusted adviser and a business partner in supporting strategy development and the day-to-day operations of an organization
Apply strategic management accounting tools and techniques to improve the contribution and sustainability of value-creating activities.
Identify and interpret stakeholders’ various decision-making needs and provide adaptive information solutions
Design an effective budgeting system that incorporates uncertainty to assist in strategy implementation
Discuss the role of project selection, planning, monitoring and completion in strategy implementation
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of (ACCT5930, ACCT5931, ACCT5942, ACCT5943, ACCT5996, ECON5258, FINS5511 and TABL5543) OR (Enrolment in 5415).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Global Strategy and Leadership
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course consolidates and builds on the learnings candidates have gained in the other three prerequisite courses: Ethics and Governance, Financial Reporting and Strategic Management Accounting. In the increasingly complex business environment in which organisations operate, characterised by change, uncertainty and escalating competition, the disciplines of strategy and leadership have become critical to successful organisational performance. This course links the knowledge expected of the future finance professional to the concepts of strategy and leadership. The course materials address the needs of accounting professionals operating in different international markets in varying roles, and in relation to current and emerging technologies and emerging business models. This course is delivered in conjunction with CPA Australia.
learning_outcomes: Use business information for decision making from an organisational perspective.
Observe the role of the accountant in the development and implementation of strategy.
Use analytical tools and models to analyse the industry and the market in which an organisation operates.
Use analytical tools to understand and measure the performance of the organisation.

Identify strategy and leadership concepts through the use of real-world examples integrated throughout the material, and apply these concepts to business case scenarios through the use of case studies.
Identify and explain the key challenges faced in implementation of strategy and the role of the accountant in the implementation and leadership functions.
Apply skills in thinking strategically and formulating broad strategies for consideration and application in their organisational environment.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPAA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415) OR (Enrolment in 5415). Students must also have completed ACCT5935, ACCT5936, and ACCT5937.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Financial Reporting
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to provide you with financial reporting and business skills that are applicable in an international professional environment, based on the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRSs). In a competitive international environment, financial reporting provides users with information to formulate corporate strategies, business plans and leadership initiatives. Members of the accounting profession who provide assurance services also require a good understanding of the financial reporting, IFRSs. Directors are also required to state that the financial statements are fairly stated. These examples reinforce the importance of financial reporting. This course is delivered in conjunction with CPA Australia.
learning_outcomes: Prepare general purpose financial statements for designated entities, including the exercise of professional judgment.
Explain details relating to general purpose financial statements
Explain the application and basis of selected IFRSs issued by the IASB
Apply IFRSs in the preparation of general purpose financial statements
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of (ACCT5930, ACCT5931, ACCT5942, ACCT5943, ACCT5996, ECON5258, FINS5511 and TABL5543) OR (Enrolment in 5415).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Advanced Audit and Assurance
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course provides a body of knowledge for you to understand the nature and diversity of audit and assurance engagements. The course provides an insight on audit and assurance processes, methodologies and procedures. It also examines the objectives of assurance engagements and current and future developments in assurance engagements. The environment within which the auditor or assurance practitioner operates and the respective roles of the private and public sector auditors and internal audit are also discussed. Contemporary developments in assurance engagements are discussed in this course in the context of future practice management opportunities.
learning_outcomes: Describe the various types of assurance engagements
Evaluate historical financial information by applying professional scepticism and judgement
Apply the appropriate standards that relate to a range of engagement circumstances that impact the auditor’s report and the auditor’s opinion
Design audit processes and procedures to be undertaken by auditors in conducting audit and assurance engagements
Understand and apply the framework for assurance engagements in audit and review engagements, and other assurance engagements, and discuss the elements of an assurance engagement
Evaluate circumstances that may give rise to modifications to the auditor’s report or the auditor’s opinion
Apply the standards to assurance engagements, and the fundamental ethical principles for the auditing profession
Evaluate the indicators of potential fraud and recommend a course of action
Explain the responsibilities of management and the auditor in relation to an audit
Apply the relevant auditing standards to the assessment for fraud and going concern in an audit of financial statements
Evaluate the sufficiency and appropriateness of the audit evidence gathered
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415), OR (Enrolment in 5415). Students must also have completed ACCT5935, ACCT5936, and ACCT5937.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Corporate Accounting and Regulation
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: ACCT5942 is an advanced course designed to decode the complexities of financial reporting within large, complex corporations, particularly those with subsidiaries, significant investments in other companies and joint venture projects with other entities. It aims to provide you with the necessary skills to prepare and analyse detailed financial reports, simulating the role of a Chief Financial Officer or financial analyst within a multinational corporation. This course delves into accounting for business combinations, consolidated financial reports, equity accounting, accounting for joint ventures, translation of foreign currency financial statements and the intricacies of accounting for company income tax, making it an essential toolkit for anyone aspiring to excel in the financial domain of complex business structures.
learning_outcomes: Explain the main issues involved in the preparation of a general-purpose financial report for complex corporations, particularly those with subsidiaries, significant investments in other companies and joint venture projects with other entities.

Prepare accurate and reliable financial reports for corporate groups, analyse consolidated financial statements which are critical for making informed business decisions and meet legal and regulatory obligations.

Analyse the impact of the accounting choices made by directors and think critically about accounting developments at the national and international level in order to take a leadership role and express a public interest viewpoint.
Describe the financial reporting requirements that apply to Australian corporate groups.
Demonstrate the ability to work independently and seek and use feedback to ensure continuing self-improvement in their understanding and application of relevant accounting standards.
Identify and apply the applications of IFRS for public companies. Approximately 140 nations and reporting jurisdictions permit or require IFRS for their listed companies.
Account for income tax in accordance with Australian Accounting Standard AASB 112. Accounting for preparing consolidated financial statements including intra-group transactions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT5930

assessment_tasks.task_name: In-person - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly) - Terms

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Financial Reporting
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: The primary objectives of the course are to provide students with applied knowledge in financial reporting. Through relevant theoretical lenses, the course aims to enhance students' practical skills in applying the Australian equivalents of international financial reporting standards that cover specific industries, contexts, and financial statement items. Students will gain an appreciation of the conceptual strengths and weaknesses of required accounting methods and the motivations underlying the choices made by directors and managers in circumstances where flexibilities are permitted in the accounting standards. The course will build students' capacity in critically evaluating controversial issues in external reporting and in contributing to debates on the usefulness and value relevance of financial reporting.
learning_outcomes: Articulate and address measurement and recognition issues in covered topics.
Identify and assess environmental and sustainability considerations in financial reporting.
Locate and implement disclosure requirements in covered topics.
Have a working knowledge of alternative perspectives on the theorisation of accounting practice.
Communicate ideas in a succinct manner logically and professionally.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT5930 and Corequisite: ACCT5942

assessment_tasks.task_name: In-person - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly) - Terms

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Contemporary Business Issues
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course examines contemporary and emerging global issues in order to familiarise you with the business environment that you will likely be operating in as an accountant. It uses contemporary issues as a vehicle for advancing the development of professional skills, values, ethics and attitudes. In particular, Contemporary Business Issues is designed to help you develop a future-focused perspective on professional accounting work. It will also highlight the challenges and opportunities for the accounting profession in the contemporary business environment.
learning_outcomes: Encourage an attitude of professional curiosity by challenging assumptions about contemporary and emerging issues and how they should be addressed

Judge the effects that disclosure requirements will have on financial and non-financial reporting, and consider the overall impact that a shift towards non-financial, sustainability and integrated reporting will have on enterprises and accounting functions.
Critically evaluate current research and practice on the origins and effects of contemporary and emerging global issues
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415), OR (Enrolment in 5415). Students must also have completed ACCT5935, ACCT5936, and ACCT5937.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Financial Risk Management
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: High levels of debt exist across the world following the Global Financial Crisis. Combined with slow economic growth this has created a volatile global economic environment. As a result, organisations are vulnerable to financial risk, including funding and liquidity risk, market risk from interest rate, exchange rate or commodity price movements, credit risk and operational risk. The purpose of this course is to equip you with the necessary skills to assess these financial risks and manage them strategically with the use of financial instruments.
learning_outcomes: Apply tools and techniques to assess, monitor, and manage organisational financial risk, including the selection of suitable financial instruments and derivatives.
Recommend funding, liquidity and long-term investment decisions considering risk, return, and organisational objectives.
Demonstrate the accounting, governance, and regulatory requirements relevant to derivatives, hedging activities and financial risk control.
Analyse an organisation’s risk profile using an appropriate financial risk management framework.
Evaluate the major sources of financial risk faced by organisations, including funding, liquidity, interest rate, foreign exchange, commodity price, credit and selected operational risks.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415), OR (Enrolment in 5415)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Digital Finance
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: In today’s rapidly evolving digital landscape, including a vast array of new capabilities and use cases, accounting and finance professionals must stay ahead of both the opportunities and challenges presented by emerging technologies and the ways in which they are utilised to disrupt extant industry practices. It is imperative to learn to recognise and reap the full benefit of these technologies and the digital finance environment. This course explores the knowledge and skills necessary to understand and navigate the complex world of digital finance and provides the tools to apply emerging technologies in a real-world context. More specifically, the course discusses the topics of: the digital finance ecosystem; the future of money; technology and its use in finance; data analytics, interpretation and visualization; and risk management, governance and regulation.
learning_outcomes: Examine where we are today, and where we will be in the near future, with technologies used in the digital finance environment such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Robotic Process Automation (RPA), big data, digital payments and digital currencies
Use insights into digital finance technologies to navigate the changing technological environment in which accounting and finance professionals work
Examine the regulatory and organisational implications of digital finance technologies and how they can be applied in a range of settings including compliance in organisational contexts.
Apply knowledge to translate complex digital finance concepts and terminology to support informed strategic decision-making around the use of key digital finance technologies in business
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of 36 UOC in Program 8415), OR (Enrolment in 5415). Students must also have completed ACCT5935, ACCT5936, ACCT5937, and (ACCT5908 OR ACCT3708 OR equivalent course credit).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Australia Taxation
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to provide you with an awareness of the key provisions of the relevant taxation legislation and enable you to apply the relevant legislative concepts to determine taxation consequences. It also introduces fundamental concepts of income tax law and provides an in-depth understanding of relevant Australian tax laws and their application in the areas of income tax law for individuals and simple business structures, capital gains tax, goods and services tax, and fringe benefits tax. This course also covers the tax administration system, and the ethical and professional obligations a tax adviser.
learning_outcomes: Identify the key administrative components of the Australian taxation system and interpret the basic principles of Australian income tax, fringe benefit tax and goods and services tax legislation.
Analyse events and apply the relevant taxation law to determine the tax liability for individuals, companies, partnerships, trusts, and superannuation funds.
Explain taxation law that relates to the taxation of individuals, companies, partnerships, trusts, and superannuation funds.
Analyse, discuss and resolve issues relating to the determination of assessable income and allowable deductions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in ACCTKS CPA Specialisation AND completion of (ACCT5930, ACCT5931, ACCT5942, ACCT5943, ACCT5996, ECON5258, FINS5511 and TABL5543) OR (Enrolment in 5415).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing Agile Organisations
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course is tailored for aspiring managers and professionals eager to refine their resource management skills in today’s fast-paced and competitive business landscape. Through a curated mix of contemporary and foundational readings, you will learn to effectively mobilize resources to foster and maintain organizational agility. By the end of the course, you’ll gain a deeper understanding of how agile organizations operate, enabling you to critically reflect on and shape relevant practices. This knowledge prepares you for future leadership roles, by enabling you to be a more effective manager in driving and leading agile organizations.
learning_outcomes: Describe and understand the nature of agile organisations, leadership and management and resources.
Evaluate and justify choices of managerial practices in particular situations.
Explain and critically analyse the various resources available to facilitate managerial work in agile organisations.
Work both independently and collaboratively to complete tasks and collaboratively in a global community.
Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented and communicated ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Apply the concepts learned in this course to practice and case scenarios.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CPA Australia Taxation - Advanced
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course explores certain complex areas of taxation, affords an advanced understanding of tax theory and policy, and provides practical application of complex tax knowledge across core and specialist tax areas. It examines advanced tax issues including income tax law for a variety of business structures and investment entities; goods and services tax; international tax; and anti-tax avoidance regimes. It also considers the tax implications of complex business structures and corporate financing arrangements to equip candidates with the skills they need to advise their corporate clients.
learning_outcomes: Advise on the tax implications arising from various complex business structures, superannuation and associated investment decisions

Apply advanced taxation knowledge in complex business areas at local and international levels, such as transactions involving complex goods and services tax (GST) law, cross-border tax issues and anti-tax avoidance
Understand the principles of tax theory and explain how tax policies will impact on business decisions
Explain the tax consequences of various corporate financing arrangements
Recommend an appropriate business or investment structure to achieve commercial and personal goals within the remit of Australian taxation law
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in program 8415 Professional Accounting (Extn) and completion of ACCT5935, ACCT5936 and ACCT5937

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Current Developments in Accounting Research - Financial
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Review of alternative approaches to the development of theories in external reporting. Explication and evaluation of substantive theories and associated research studies. Examination of research findings related to the accounting and reporting environment, agency cost and financial contracting, the properties of reported accounting numbers, predictive value of accounting information, the use of information in capital markets, and the use of accounting reports by individual decision makers.
learning_outcomes: Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Critically analyse and evaluate extant and proposed financial accounting research;
Collaborate actively in learning activities aimed at achieving the above objectives.
Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Current Developments in Accounting Research - Managerial
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of contemporary management accounting research, which emanates from different philosophical perspectives and employs different theories and research methods. Research is divided into two broad streams: work that seeks (a) to explain and design, and (b) to understand and interpret the practice of management accounting in organisation and societies.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and evaluate extant and proposed management accounting research.
Defend a research proposal to peers.
Appreciate a range of paradigms and methods for conducting management accounting research.
Identify contemporary research areas in the field of management accounting.
Understand the strengths and weaknesses associated with management accounting research.
Prepare a research proposal in the context of management accounting.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Management Control Systems in Contemporary Contexts
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Learn how to design, implement, and utilise management control systems for better management and decision-making around organizational resources and operations. This course provides a strategic and executive perspective on how MCS work and are changing with new business models, new technologies, digitalisation and increasingly blurred organizational boundaries. You’ll engage with industry examples and apply proven frameworks to solve real-world business challenges. Through this course, you’ll develop critical thinking and leadership skills in leveraging MCS to effectively navigate modern organisational complexities and drive business success.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the impact of technological advancements and changing business environments on management controls.
Analyse real-world case studies to assess the effectiveness of management control systems.
Cultivate teamwork and leadership skills through collaborative projects and presentations focusing on management control systems.
Demonstrate how to navigate changing landscapes, ensuring your MCS remain effective and relevant (adapt and thrive).
Apply knowledge of management control systems to design effective systems for different and international organizational contexts.
Analyse the basic ingredients of management control systems design.
Develop pitching skills so that you can successfully communicate your ideas to many stakeholders. Learn to navigate group dynamics for maximum efficiency and synergy.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Reporting for Climate Change and Sustainability
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Climate change and sustainability are key challenges for our society and economy today and these areas provide great opportunities for future employment. Governments and non-governmental organisations around the world have engaged in various climate change and adaptation policy initiatives to ensure survival and prosperity of current and future generations. This course explores issues related to reporting on climate change and sustainability and its implications for businesses. As the course is offered in the Business faculty, it is only appropriate to focus on business activities with ethical and social significance that are often omitted from conventional profit-oriented business transactions. Insights on established and proposed policy frameworks will provide students with an overview of sustainability reporting and the ability to start preparing a sustainability report in their current or future employment.
