Impact of the recent establishment of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) by the IFRS Foundation will be covered particularly the release of sustainability standards and how Australia is responding to this generational shift in business reporting. This course will be useful for students who aspire to work in leading accounting and consulting firms and climate and sustainability advisors.
learning_outcomes: Identify emerging issues that arise due to climate change and its implications to businesses.

Articulate mandatory and voluntary reporting frameworks on sustainability and be able to identify the costs and benefits of these initiatives (e.g. GHG Protocol, GRI, SDGs, TCFD, ISSB and the NGER Act).
Observe why businesses need to support sustainable development practices.
Identify strategies to adapt and mitigate the effects of climate change.
Interpret the role of assurance in sustainability reporting and GHG reporting.
Develop critical thinking, oral and written communication skills and professional approaches to emerging business issues in a competitive and carbon constrained economy.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Accounting Analytics for Business Decision Making
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Analytics combined with accounting data is at the heart of most forward-looking corporate decisions. Investment bankers, equity research analysts, portfolio managers, credit analysts, lenders, and capital market regulators rely on accounting data to identify investment opportunities, assess business risks, and negotiate business contracts. This course will help you gain basic understanding of how professionals use analytics tools to leverage accounting data to produce significant insights and make meaningful predictions. Most importantly, you will learn how accounting analytics are applied in real-world business contexts, such as quantitative investing, financial fraud prediction, earnings forecasting, etc. You will use numerous real-word case studies in lectures, tutorials, and assessments to reinforce your learnings.
learning_outcomes: Work effectively both individually and in teams to communicate accounting and business insights to a specific audience and to inform, persuade or decide on the best course of action.
Select and apply the appropriate analytical tools to generate insights in accounting and business contexts.
Extract the right data from different sources to solve accounting and business problems.
Visualize and translate insights into concrete actions that businesses can take.
Explain the importance of data analytics in contemporary business contexts and developing an appropriate analytical mindset.
Ability to identify and define business problems.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CA Module Financial Accounting & Reporting
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This is one of five Chartered Accountant Program modules which are embedded in the Master of Professional Accounting Extension Program and enable students to pursue a CA qualification. This course includes practical examples and activities that will develop the students (in their role as CA candidates) understanding of the conceptual framework for financial reporting, and enable the candidate to reference Accounting Standards and pronouncements and apply knowledge to a variety of practical scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Explain the interaction between national and international reporting frameworks including their relationships with their respective accounting standards.
Describe the conceptual framework for financial reporting.
Reference and apply applicable accounting standards and pronouncements to prepare financial reports.
Analyse reporting requirements of an entity based on the national regulatory framework.
Discuss contemporary issues affecting financial reporting.
Apply financial accounting principles to a range of practical financial reporting scenarios.
Explain a Chartered Accountant's ethical requirements relating to financial reporting.
prerequisites: Pre-req: ACCT5943

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CA Module Audit & Assurance
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: The Audit and Assurance (AAA) module examines and applies the relevant Auditing, Assurance and Ethics Standards to various scenarios. It is practical in nature with candidates required to apply the Standards to different scenarios, including a comprehensive case study which integrates Units 1 through 10 and a simulated case study which integrates Units 1, 11 and 12. The AAA module is one of the five (5) compulsory modules in the Chartered Accountants Program.
learning_outcomes: Undertake significant elements in the planning, performance and completion of other assurance service engagements.
Prepare an auditor’s report in accordance with relevant Auditing Standards.
Explain current issues in assurance and auditing and the impact these will have on clients and professional practice.
Plan, perform and complete the audit of historical financial statements.
Apply International Auditing Standards or National Generally Accepted Auditing Standards, and applicable laws and regulations to an audit assignment.
prerequisites: Pre-req: ACCT5908

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CA Module Management Accounting & Applied Finance
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Management accounting continues to evolve. The traditional function of collating, preparing and presenting financial and non-financial information for decision making has changed. The way information is collated (including the increased use of data analytics) and the volume of data now available has had a significant impact. To add value, management accountants need to analyse and interpret the vast amount of available information in a concise manner, providing insight to enable management (and other users) to make informed decisions that align with strategic goals. Management accounting is forward looking and predictive analysis is becoming increasingly important in proactively guiding organisations in an ever changing business environment. Finance functions now partner closely with management accountants as the breadth of traditional management accounting concepts expand and integrate across all aspects of business. MAAF includes two integrated case studies and other practical examples and activities that will give you the skills and knowledge to identify, analyse, interpret and communicate information to help an organisation manage its resources and achieve strategic goals. Given the integration of the content covered in each unit of the MAAF module, the material has been constructed on the basis that candidates will complete each unit sequentially in order to maximise their learning benefit. The MAAF module is one of the five (5) compulsory modules in the Chartered Accountants Program.
learning_outcomes: Apply KPIs and financial and non-financial reporting metrics in government and not-for-profit organisations.
Discuss the necessary tools used in public practice which can be used to advise and help clients maximise the returns on their businesses.

Understand how to contribute and add value to an organisation in any sector by being able to evaluate pricing decisions; review business spending processes; implement budgets and forecasts; develop performance management reporting; assess capital investment decisions; assess working capital management; and conduct business valuations.
prerequisites: Pre-req: FINS5511 - Corporate Finance (PG) & ACCT5996 - Management Accounting and Business Analysis (PG)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CA Module Taxation Australia
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: The Taxation Australia (TAXAU) module examines and applies relevant Australian taxation law to various tax entities. It is practical in nature with candidates required to explain and calculate the taxation consequences applicable to a range of real-life simulated scenarios, including a comprehensive tax reconciliation which integrates the various units. The CA TAXAU module is one of the five (5) compulsory modules in the Chartered Accountants Program.
learning_outcomes: Identify and explain the taxation of relevant financial transactions and international transactions.
Understand and apply taxation principles relevant to partnerships.
Explain and calculate Goods and Services Tax.
Prepare tax reconciliations between accounting profit and taxable income.
Understand and apply taxation principles relevant to consolidated entities.
Explain and calculate fringe benefits tax (FBT) and employment remuneration.
Understand and apply taxation principles relevant to trusts.
Explain Australian Tax Fundamentals
Outline tax planning, controls and anti-avoidance.
Understand and apply taxation principles relevant to superannuation.
Explain and apply capital gains tax to different scenarios.
Understand and apply taxation principles relevant to small business entities.
Explain and calculate relevant tax measures relating to capital expenditures
Understand and apply taxation principles relevant to companies.
Understand and apply taxation principles relevant to individuals.
prerequisites: Pre-req: TABL5551 - Taxation Law (PG)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: CA Module Capstone
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: The Capstone module integrates knowledge and skills from the technical modules in developing the professional competence required to become a Chartered Accountant. While the module requires candidates to apply technical skills and current knowledge, the focus is on the development of competencies that candidates will need to perform effectively in the professional environment. Candidates attend three compulsory workshops throughout the module. Each workshop builds on activities and research completed to achieve the Capstone learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Solve business problems.
Integrate technical knowledge and professional skills.
Behave ethically.
Access data, analyse information and synthesise knowledge.
Think critically.
Communicate effectively.
Engage in lifelong professional development.
Work in and lead teams.
prerequisites: pre-reqs: ACCT5975 - CA Module Financial Accounting & Reporting (PG) ACCT5976 - CA Module Audit & Assurance (PG) ACCT5977 - CA Module Management Accounting & Applied Finance (PG) ACCT5978 - CA Module Taxation Australia (PG)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Fraud Examination Fundamentals
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Do you want to investigate fraud, protect and safeguard businesses from fraud? This course will arm you with the expertise to safeguard businesses against the pervasive threat of fraud. You will learn to detect and prevent fraud, learn why fraud occurs and learn the latest fraud investigation methods and techniques.
learning_outcomes: Conduct a comprehensive investigation using diverse sources to assess and report on fraudulent activities with precision, confidentiality, and adherence to best practices.
Develop and implement a fraud investigation interview strategy to extract information effectively and sensitively from a diverse range of stakeholders.
Formulate well-supported, evidence-based recommendations independently and within a group to effectively persuade a managerial audience at a higher level.
Describe common types of fraud offenses and explore current fraud trends observed in organisations.
Apply researched theories and frameworks to understand the motivations and factors leading to fraud at an advanced level.
Explain and apply sophisticated, recognised approaches for preventing and detecting fraud in organisations.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACCT5906 or ACCT5930

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Management Accounting and Business Analysis
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Take a deep dive into business activities to learn how to make informed and effective decisions with the resources at your disposal. In this course, you will explore the creation and use of management accounting information to analyse business activities and drive operational improvement. You will develop skills to enhance your business acumen in managing costs and resources and identify sources of value creation for superior, sustainable performance. Adopting an active learning approach, this course utilizes student-led discussions, individual and team-based activities, and real-world applications to empower you to engage more effectively with organizational planning, control and process improvement for more efficient and effective business operations.
learning_outcomes: Explain some behavioural aspects of using accounting management accounting techniques and concepts.
Apply management accounting skills to specific business problems.
Develop well-justified decisions and recommendations in response to specific business problems.
Identify and explain management accounting knowledge in areas of managing costs and resources, operational efficiency and effectiveness, and sources of value creation.
Communicate clearly and concisely management accounting concepts and ideas orally/in written form.
Analyse and discuss real-world issues connected to management accounting tools and concepts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite or Corequisite: ACCT5930 or COMM5003 or ACCT5906

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Seminar in Research Methodology
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: This course considers the relationship between science and scientific method; reviews some of the research methods commonly used to conduct research in accounting; and provides an introduction to the interpretation of the key statistical techniques used in accounting research.
learning_outcomes: Conduct a literature review, develop a research question and related hypotheses and design an appropriate study to test the hypotheses. You should be able to conduct research using experimental, survey, archival and qualitative research methods.
Understand and conduct basic quantitative data analysis.
Demonstrate awareness of ethical issues in conducting research.
Critique and evaluate a research design.
Evaluate the pros and cons of various research methods to evaluate a research question.
Communicate ideas in a clear and succinct manner.
Conduct reading of academic accounting articles, understand them and critique them.
Design a research study to address a specific research question and/or hypotheses.
Construct written work which is logically and professionally presented

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Actuarial Studies
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to provide an introduction to actuarial studies. It covers the fundamental modelling tools used by actuaries (probability, statistics, financial mathematics), as well as some of the basic actuarial models in areas such as insurance, superannuation or financial risk management, and which will be studied in great depth during the remainder of the degree. The main areas of actuarial practice and research are also introduced and discussed. Finally, labs will provide a foundation in programming, as well as data manipulation and visualisation, with a particular focus on R.
learning_outcomes: Use relevant computer software to perform efficient computations, manipulate data, as well as create and interpret algorithms
Evaluate and apply fundamental actuarial mathematics techniques
Communicate data insights effectively
Evaluate and apply basic principles of probability, statistics and financial mathematics
Describe how the actuarial profession is organised, its code of conduct, its main practice areas, as well as its current challenges and opportunities
Evaluate the fundamental principles underlying risk management and insurance
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MATH1151 AND in Actuarial Studies programs.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Placement 1
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: The main aims of this course is to provide the Scholars with practical experience in Actuarial Studies that complements their academic studies, and to give Sponsors enthusiastic and talented young achievers who may wish to work with them upon graduation. Industry placement 1 is intended to be an introduction to the Sponsor's business, and the structures and policies in place to support the core business activities. Ideally, the Scholars should interact with several areas of the organization. Note: Only available to Actuarial Studies, UNSW Business School Co-op Scholars
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively and display collaborative skills in teamwork.
Undertake relevant research in the actuarial studies industry.
Describe the sponsoring organisations’ business practices relevant to the field of actuarial studies.
Communicate effectively and confidently in oral and written forms in a business context.
Apply tools, techniques and frameworks to evaluate and understand the role of actuarial studies in attaining the Sponsor organisation’s goals.
Business awareness.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in Program 3587

assessment_tasks.task_name: Independent research - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Foundations of Actuarial Models
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course introduces the stochastic models used by actuaries to model both liabilities and assets and illustrates their applications in actuarial work. Topics covered include discrete-time and continuous-time Markov chains and their applications to experience rating; Markov process models and applications to actuarial modelling practice including in areas such as insurance, financial risk, and social policy; methods for simulation of a stochastic process; estimation of Markov chains. Students will be expected to implement models using the R software in a numerical computer package.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate Markov processes in financial and insurance modeling.
Describe and utilize Markov Processes in insurance and financial models.
Apply Markov Chains to frequency-based NCD schemes using data.
Produce professionally structured reports based on actuarial modelling.
Present complex actuarial models effectively in written form.
Implement Monte Carlo simulations for stochastic processes.
Identify features and properties of Markov Chains.
Use Monte Carlo simulations in simple actuarial problems.
Explain terminologies and classifications of stochastic processes.
Define key principles of actuarial modeling.
Discuss actuarial models with an understanding of their ethical implications.
Estimate transition probability and matrix of discrete-time and continuous-time Markov chains.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (ACTL2131 or MATH2901) and in Actuarial single or dual degrees.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Probability and Mathematical Statistics
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course covers probability and statistics topics relevant to actuarial studies. Topics covered include univariate/multivariate random variables, moments, probability generating functions, moment generating functions, marginal and conditional distributions, sampling distributions, estimation methods, hypothesis tests. Examples relevant to actuarial studies, finance and insurance are used to illustrate the application of the topics covered.
learning_outcomes: Utilize standard models of probability and statistics to analyze real-world actuarial and risk modeling issues.
Produce professionally structured and logically organized written work.
Communicate complex ideas succinctly and clearly to facilitate understanding.
Collaborate effectively on team projects to solve actuarial tasks.
Identify and define foundational concepts of probability and statistical theory essential for actuarial studies.
Apply statistical skills and probability knowledge to present data and address actuarial problems.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACTL1101 AND (MATH1251 or MATH1241 )

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Financial Mathematics for Actuaries
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course develops the financial mathematics required for the analysis of financial and insurance transactions. Topics covered include: mathematics of compound interest; analysis and valuation of annuities, bonds, loans and derivative securities; yield curves and immunisation; introduction to stochastic interest rate models and actuarial applications.
learning_outcomes: Develop formulas for the expected value and variance of accumulation under stochastic interest.
Assess the reasonableness of financial calculations and their underlying assumptions.
Outline basic market conventions in securities and money markets.
Communicate complex financial concepts effectively.
Apply financial valuation concepts to practical situations like investment appraisals.
Articulate the relationship between present value, cash flows, and interest rate risk.
Describe and value various financial securities including bonds, shares, loans, forwards and futures contracts, options and annuities.
Identify and clarify the concept of time value of money and its applications.
Explain various types of interest and their applications.
Modify simple valuation problems to include tax and transaction costs.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MATH1251 AND (ACTL1101 OR in MATHE1, MATHM1 or MATHT1 majors)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Modelling and Prediction of Life and Health Related Risks
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course equips students with the technical skills needed to estimate survival models, emphasising their applications in insurance, finance, demography, and epidemiology. These models help understand and predict risks related to events such as mortality, health changes, and credit defaults, allowing for better risk management. Key topics include: survival models; estimation of lifetime distributions; maximum likelihood estimation of transition intensities in multi-state models; graduation and smoothing of crude death rates and transition intensity estimates; and models for projecting mortality trends. The course will also focus on implementing these concepts using numerical computer packages. Additionally, it will address ethical considerations and issues related to discrimination and heterogeneity in mortality and health outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Describe the main methods of projecting/forecasting mortality rates
Describe how to estimate transition intensities depending on age, exactly or using the census approximation
Identify maximum likelihood estimators for the transition intensities of a multiple state model.
Describe estimation procedures for lifetime distributions.
Describe how to test crude estimates for consistency with a standard table or a set of graduated estimates, and the process of graduation.
Describe the concepts of survival models.
Describe the Binomial and Poisson models of mortality.
Discuss the ethical dimensions and implications of the modelling introduced in the course.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (ACTL2131 or MATH2901) and ACTL2102 Corequisite: ACTL3142 or MATH2931

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Statistical Machine Learning for Risk and Actuarial Applications
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to statistical learning techniques and their application to actuarial analysis and decision-making. It covers various aspects of data analysis, including: exploratory data analysis; classification and prediction using regression and generalized linear models; descriptive, inferential, and predictive analysis and models; statistical and machine learning, including supervised and unsupervised learning. The course also addresses ethical, regulatory, and professional issues, as well as risks and risk management associated with data analysis. A particular focus is placed on effectively communicating technical results for business applications.
learning_outcomes: Describe the key aspects of the theory and practice of predictive analytics and data analytics for insurance and financial applications.
Communicate the results and implications of statistical learning models through presentations, discussions, and written reports.
Evaluate predictive analytics and data analytics models, identifying their benefits and limitations.
Explain ethical and regulatory considerations in the use of data and analytic techniques.
Estimate and apply various statistical learning models to practical scenarios.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACTL2131 or (MATH2931 and in B. Data Science and Decisions (3959)) or MATH2901

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning Models for Actuarial Applications
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: Advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning - especially in deep learning methods - are creating products and services with the potential to change the insurance industry and actuarial work. This course will introduce students to concepts in Artificial Intelligence (AI), with particular focus on deep learning models, and their applications to actuarial work. A particular focus of the course will be on how those AI models can be combined with other actuarial techniques in order to solve business problems in insurance and risk management including pricing, reserving and capital management, and insurance business processes. Students will be expected to understand the theory behind the models considered and their relationship to other actuarial techniques, and to fit and evaluate various deep learning models using appropriate software.
learning_outcomes: Implement deep neural networks using deep learning software and real-world datasets.
Describe the key features of various deep neural networks, highlighting their applications, differences, and limitations in actuarial studies and insurance tasks.
Describe the ethical considerations in data collection, design, and implementation of AI and deep learning models for actuarial and insurance applications.
Combine deep neural networks with other actuarial techniques to solve problems in insurance business, including pricing, reserving, and capital management.
Describe the key aspects of artificial intelligence techniques and their applications in insurance business processes.
Communicate and interpret results from deep learning algorithms and AI systems through effective discussions, presentations, and written reports.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (ACTL2131 and ACTL3142) or (MATH2931 and in B. Data Science and Decisions (3959)) or (MATH2901 and MATH2931)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: General Insurance Techniques
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course explores various actuarial models and statistical techniques applicable to general insurance practice. It includes topics such as loss data analysis, model evaluation; frequency, severity, and aggregate loss models; reinsurance; premium calculation; claims reserving; ruin theory; Bayesian statistics; credibility. Students will apply these methods to the principles of pricing and reserving for common general insurance and reinsurance coverages.
learning_outcomes: Determine the Bayesian premium for losses using both parametric and non-parametric approaches.
Compute the distribution of the sum of losses, considering both deterministic and random number scenarios.
Apply Generalized Linear Models (GLM) in basic actuarial situations.
Estimate the expected present value of future liabilities from existing claims.
Estimate parameters of specific distributions using both complete and censored or truncated data.
Evaluate the effectiveness of statistical models using diverse metrics.
Compute descriptive statistics and choose appropriate distributions for effective data modeling.
Assess the probability that losses will exceed premiums in the future, specifically in straightforward cases.
Calculate the financial value of various reinsurance contracts.
Explain the principles of the classical model of risk theory, focusing on the dynamics between premiums and losses.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACTL2102 or (MATH2901 AND MATHE1, MATHM1 or MATHT1 major)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Actuarial Mathematics for Insurance and Superannuation
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: Long-term contingent cashflow valuation is fundamental for actuarial work, especially for life-, disability- and health insurance, pensions and superannuation. They are also increasingly applied in broader areas in social protection and policy. This course introduces models and techniques from actuarial mathematics combining the present value principles with stochastic modelling, in order to derive the value of contingent cashflows for pricing, reserving, projections and profit testing purposes. The course also covers contemporary management issues in life, health and superannuation products such as longevity, and premium rating. Spreadsheets will be used to perform computations.
learning_outcomes: Describe life insurance and life annuity products available in the market.
Assess the risks associated with cash flows from contingent events.
Assess the reasonableness of premium and policy value calculations for financial contingent products.
Integrate and apply these technical skills to practical valuation problems in the life insurance and annuity markets.
Apply contingent valuation concepts to practical scenarios.
Describe fundamental techniques for valuing cash flows involving contingent events such as death and survival.
Describe the basic valuation and funding principles of superannuation benefits.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACTL2111 and ACTL2102

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Superannuation and Retirement Benefits
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course provides a comprehensive analysis of the economics and finance of retirement income provision. It is designed to provide students with a solid understanding of the theoretical and public-policy issues associated with the design and implementation of policies for retirement income provision in Australia and internationally. Topics covered include: demographic trends and the economic impact of population ageing; rationale for public provision and/or regulation of private retirement income provision; assessment of alternative models for retirement income provision; retirement income provision in Australia; the taxation and regulation of retirement savings and benefits; the structure, performance and efficiency of the superannuation industry; and international comparisons in policy design and implementation.
learning_outcomes: Explain key economic and financial principles underlying the efficient accumulation and decumulation of retirement savings.
Describe and use the complex terminology surrounding the field of superannuation and retirement benefits.
Evaluate the design and implementation of polices for retirement income provision in Australia and internationally.
Analyse the superannuation industry and assess the regulations that govern it.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ECON2101 or (ECON1101 and ACTL1101) or (completed at least 84 UOC and enrolled in a Commerce Program).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Retirement Saving and Spending Over the Lifecycle
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: Helping individuals make better financial decisions and improve their financial well-being over the lifecycle represents a grand challenge for government, business, and not-for-profit organisations. This synthesis course provides opportunities for students to work in diverse teams to solve real-world problems related to this grand challenge through applying, integrating and synthesising their knowledge and skills from multi-disciplinary perspectives. This course will be a fully problem-based learning experience. Throughout the course, students will apply their multi-disciplinary knowledge, critical thinking, problem-solving and teamwork skills to solve real industry problems. Students will have opportunities to engage with and receive feedback from industry partners. Building on students' pre-existing knowledge in their specific disciplinary domain, this course will cover the following topics to further equip students with relevant theoretical framework, industry knowledge and research insights to solve the industry problems: lifecycle theories of consumption and saving; human capital and the retirement decision; lifecycle investment strategy; risks facing individual retirees and providers of retirement income products (employment risk, investment risk, longevity risk, inflation risk, health risk); retirement income products; behavioural explanations for non-rational saving and investment behaviours including myopia, procrastination, mental accounting, framing, loss aversion etc. NOTE: This course is equivalent to ECON3117 Retirement Saving and Spending over the Lifecycle, which is no longer offered. Students intending to enrol in ECON3117 should instead enrol in this course.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on your professional skills and behaviours, including identified gaps, and how you will adapt to a changing business environment.
Access, manage and use the appropriate digital resources and tools to deliver your recommendations or conclusions.
Examine the influences of the global business environment on key ethical or sustainability considerations in relation to the contemporary business problem.
Identify, apply and adapt business skills and knowledge acquired from across your program to critically analyse a contemporary business challenge.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ECON2101 or (ECON1101 and ACTL1101) or (completed at least 84 UOC and enrolled in a Commerce Program) and be in good academic standing.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Placement 2
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course provides scholars with a practical application of the principles of actuarial studies in an industry environment. The main aims of this course is to give the Scholars practical experience in Actuarial Studies that complements their academic studies, and to give Sponsors enthusiastic and talented young achievers who may wish to work with them upon graduation. The aims of industrial placement 2 are to give Scholars: Experience in basic business and actuarial practices; an understanding of the role of actuarial studies and business functions in supporting business operations and management, The opportunity to develop their communication skills. Note: Only available to Actuarial Studies, UNSW Business School Co-op Scholars
learning_outcomes: Undertake relevant research in the actuarial studies industry.
Communicate effectively and confidently in oral and written forms in a business context.
Demonstrate an understanding of the wider environment in which an businesses and organisations operate.
Collaborate effectively and display collaborative skills in teamwork.
Describe the sponsoring organisations’ business practices relevant to the field of actuarial studies.
Apply tools, techniques and frameworks to evaluate and understand the role of actuarial studies in attaining the Sponsor organisation’s goals.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACTL2101 and enrolment in program 3587

assessment_tasks.task_name: Independent research - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Asset-Liability and Derivative Models
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course is to provide students with an appreciation of the mathematical and economic models of investment markets and highlight their application (and shortcomings) in asset-liability management for insurance, superannuation and funds management and in the pricing of derivatives. Topics covered include; risk and utility; risk measures; mean variance models; factor models; asset liability models using portfolio selection models; equilibrium and arbitrage-free valuation; valuation of derivatives; term structure models; credit risk models and actuarial stochastic investment models and their application. The topics will be illustrated with applications to the valuation and risk management of insurance and superannuation contracts especially those with embedded options and financial guarantees - with a particular focus on the inadequacies of the models for investment risk management. The course will include case studies on investment and derivative disasters.
learning_outcomes: Enhance skills in communication, discussion, and report writing.
Apply methods for risk measurement and decision-making under uncertainty, using techniques frp, financial economics and actuarial science.
Use contingent-claim pricing methods to assess the risks associated with options and guarantees.
Describe stochastic investment models in actuarial contexts and their use in asset-liability management.
Explain key asset-pricing models and their implications for actuarial practice.
Utilise mean-variance criteria to optimise asset allocation for long-term investors such as insurers and superannuation funds.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACTL2111 and ACTL2102

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Quantitative Risk Management
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: Australia is vulnerable to natural disasters with the highest economic consequences. Typical examples include heatwaves, floods, cyclones, bushfires, and earthquakes, many of which are on the rise in both frequency and severity. Similarly, financial market losses have significant impacts on financial institutions and society. This course introduces students to advanced statistical and actuarial models for a variety of risks in financial institutions such as banks, insurance/reinsurance companies, and superannuation funds. The course explores quantitative methods of risk measurement and modelling, with a special focus on extreme losses, extreme dependence, and loss aggregation over time. Topics covered include: risk measures; multivariate models; copulas and dependence; financial time series; extreme value theory; market credit and operational risk. Students will be implementing the models using computer software.
learning_outcomes: Review and analyse advanced risk models to understand their structure and applicability.
Identify and apply key theories and practical applications of quantitative risk modeling specific to insurance and financial risks.
Enhance skills in presenting, discussing, and writing about complex risk-modeling concepts to effectively communicate their importance in quantitative risk management.
Explore and review current literature concerning emerging trends and advancements in quantitative risk modeling.
Evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of risk management models used in real-world settings.
Estimate parameters and implement various risk models in relevant scenarios, demonstrating their utility.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACTL2102 and (ACTL3142 or MATH2931).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Placement 3
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course provides scholars with a practical application of the principles of actuarial studies in an industry environment. The main aims of this course is to give the Scholars practical experience in Actuarial Studies that complements their academic studies, and to give Sponsors enthusiastic and talented young achievers who may wish to work with them upon graduation. The aims of industry placement 3 are to give Scholars: Experience in basic business and actuarial practices; an understanding of the role of actuarial studies and business functions in supporting business operations and management; the opportunity to develop their communication skills. Note: Only available to Actuarial Studies, UNSW Business School Co-op Scholars
learning_outcomes: Communicate effectively and confidently in oral and written forms in a business context.
Apply tools, techniques and frameworks to evaluate and understand the role of actuarial studies in attaining the Sponsor organisation’s goals.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Generative AI for Actuaries
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course positions generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as a transformative tool for identifying, assessing and mitigating risks across financial services and related sectors. Through research-infused seminars, hands-on labs and real-world case studies, students will learn to: integrate GenAI into enterprise risk management frameworks; apply stochastic and simulation techniques to quantify uncertainty in model outputs; generate synthetic risk scenarios for stress-testing and capital planning; and design responsible prompt-engineering workflows. Ethical, governance and regulatory considerations—including transparency, bias mitigation and auditability—are embedded throughout. Graduates will be equipped to lead the responsible adoption of GenAI in high-stakes risk management environments.

Design and execute stochastic simulations and synthetic scenario generators to quantify tail risks and stress-test exposures.
Develop responsible prompt-engineering pipelines tailored to risk-management use cases, balancing model performance with compliance requirements.
Evaluate and mitigate ethical, governance, and regulatory risks in GenAI workflows, ensuring transparency, bias control, and auditability.
Critically assess emerging research and tools in generative AI for risk applications, synthesising findings to inform best practices.
Communicate complex GenAI-driven risk analyses effectively in professional reports and executive presentations for both technical and non-technical audiences.

syllabus_overview: This course equips advanced undergraduate students in risk and actuarial studies with the quantitative and conceptual foundations needed to responsibly design and evaluate ethical AI systems in high-stakes domains such as insurance and financial services. Students will explore practical challenges in embedding fairness, accountability, transparency, and robustness throughout the AI development process. Through applied frameworks, essential theory, and real-world case studies, the course develops students’ ability to analyse ethical risks, understand regulatory contexts, and communicate ethical reasoning in professional settings. It prepares graduates to implement responsible AI practices and contribute to ethical decision-making in data-driven environments.

Evaluate ethical risks in the AI lifecycle—covering data, model design, and deployment—using industry-relevant frameworks and standards.
Collaborate effectively in teams to analyse real-world ethical scenarios and present well-reasoned, responsible AI solutions.
Explain key ethical principles such as fairness, transparency, accountability, and robustness as they relate to AI systems in actuarial and financial applications.
Interpret algorithmic decision-making and communicate its implications for actuarial practice.

title: Survival Analysis and Prediction of Life and Health Related Risks
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course covers the actuarial profession syllabus for survival models, focusing on understanding and predicting mortality, morbidity, and longevity risks. It applies these techniques to life, health, and disability insurance, superannuation, finance, and epidemiology. These models help forecast risks related to events such as mortality, health changes, and credit defaults, leading to better risk quantification, pricing, and management. Key topics include: survival models and actuarial notation; Estimation of lifetime distributions; Maximum likelihood estimation of transition intensities in multi-state models, considering age and duration; graduation of crude estimates and tests for fidelity and smoothness; and models for projecting mortality trends. The course emphasizes implementing these concepts using numerical computer packages. Additionally, it will address ethical considerations and issues related to discrimination and heterogeneity in mortality and health risks.

syllabus_overview: This course covers the actuarial mathematics, models and techniques for valuing long-term contingent cashflows. In-depth understanding of valuation of claims is a key aspect of actuarial work, specifically in the areas of life insurance, health, disability insurance, superannuation and pensions, as well as broader financial institutions. This course combines the present value principle with various stochastic tools in pricing, reserving, cashflow projection and profit testing tasks for various products in life insurance, health and disability, and pension and superannuation space. The fundamental techniques covered in the course help insurers to adequately price and manage the risks of various contracts in life insurance and pension systems, hence allowing the creation of products to help individuals manage risks. They are also increasingly applied in broader areas including social protection and government policy.

title: Quantitative Risk Management Techniques

syllabus_overview: Recent occurrences of significant losses in the financial and insurance markets associated with catastrophic events such as heatwaves, floods, cyclones, bushfires, and earthquakes have intensified the need for a systematic approach to modelling, measuring, and managing catastrophe risks. Culprits behind catastrophe risks include frequency, severity, and dependence. This course introduces students to advanced statistical and actuarial models for a variety of risks in financial institutions such as banks, insurance/reinsurance companies, and superannuation funds. Traditional and newly emerging risks encountered therein will be studied, with a special focus on extreme losses, extreme dependence, and loss aggregation over time. Topics covered include: risk measures; multivariate models; copulas and dependence; financial time series; extreme value theory; market credit and operational risk. Students will be implementing the models using computer software.
learning_outcomes: Develop and refine skills in presenting, discussing, and writing about risk-modeling concepts, ensuring clarity and effectiveness in communicating quantitative risk management.
Systematically search, identify, and review recent research on quantitative risk modeling to stay updated with cutting-edge advances.
Estimate using diverse models and implement these models in real-world applications, demonstrating their practical use.
Critically assess various models used in risk management, identifying their benefits and limitations to enhance their practical applications.
Conduct a comprehensive review of advanced risk models to enhance understanding of complex modeling techniques.
Identify both theoretical and practical aspects of quantitative risk modeling as applied to insurance and financial risks.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ACTL5103 or program 4520

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning Models for Risk and Insurance
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course will introduce students to Artificial Intelligence techniques, with particular focus on deep learning and applications to risk and insurance. Particular importance will be on various deep learning algorithms and how they can be combined with other actuarial techniques in order to solve business problems in insurance and risk management including in pricing, reserving, capital management, and insurance business processes improvements. Ethical considerations of AI models will also be discussed. Students will be expected to understand the deep learning algorithms considered, their relationship with other actuarial techniques, as well as be able to fit and evaluate various deep learning models for actuarial applications using appropriate software.
learning_outcomes: Implement deep neural networks using deep learning software and real-world datasets.
Communicate and appraise critically results from deep learning algorithms and AI systems through effective discussions, presentations, and written reports.
Explain the key features of various deep neural networks, highlighting their applications, differences, and limitations in actuarial studies and insurance tasks.
Identify and analyse the ethical considerations in data collection, design, and implementation of AI and deep learning models for actuarial and insurance applications.
Develop models that combine deep neural networks with other actuarial techniques to solve problems in insurance business, including pricing, reserving, and capital management.
Explain the core aspects of artificial intelligence techniques and their applications in insurance business processes.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ACTL5101

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Risk and Capital Management
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course covers the motivations and techniques for risk and capital management in financial institutions, including insurers, reinsurers, superannuation funds, and banks and the major types of risks encountered. Topics covered include: economic and regulatory capital; regulatory frameworks for banks and insurers; quantitative and qualitative issues of measuring and management of market risk, credit risk, interest rate risk, operational risk, liquidity risk and model risk, with particular emphasis on data issues met when quantifying those risks; scenario analysis and stress testing methods.
learning_outcomes: Propose ERM solutions or strategies to address real (case study) and hypothetical situations, including how an ERM process can create value for an organization
Demonstrate presentation and discussion skills for risk and capital management concepts
Apply risk management tools and techniques
Concisely put forward your considered views on a topic orally and in writing
Identify how you can contribute to risk management in the financial sector
Describe risk categories and be able to identify risks and dategorise risks
Demonstrate an understanding of the theory and practice of enterprise risk management and the ERM process
Develop and apply an economic capital model
prerequisites: Completed at least two of the following courses: ACTL5105, ACTL5106 and ACTL5109 or (program 4520)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Actuarial Data Science Applications
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course covers the actuarial professional associateship syllabus for the actuarial data science principles. It combines data analytics and modelling concepts with the practical applications of modern analytical tools and techniques, as well as their actuarial applications. This course covers the key iterative steps involved in building a model - business understanding, data understanding and preparation, modelling, evaluation, communication and deployment. Particular focus will be on the selection of appropriate predictive modelling techniques for a stated situation and how to evaluate the suitability of a model, taking into account business context and objectives, as well as on the communication of modelling results to a range of business decision making audiences.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate critically the appropriateness of predictive analytics models in practice, emphasising business understanding.
Discuss and identify the ethical considerations in data science and algorithm development.
Communicate effectively and appraise critically the modelling results through presentations, discussions, and written reports.
Explain the features and recognise the limitations of predictive analytics techniques and apply each technique in practice.
Explain the key iterative steps involved in building a model, including business understanding, data understanding and preparation, modelling, evaluation, communication, and deployment.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Quantitative Ethical AI in Risk and Actuarial Applications
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: This course equips research-focused and PhD-level students in risk and actuarial studies with rigorous quantitative and conceptual tools to critically design, assess, and govern ethical AI systems in complex, high-stakes environments, such as insurance and financial services. Students will investigate the deeper methodological and societal challenges involved in embedding fairness, accountability, transparency, and robustness into the AI development process. Through a combination of theoretical frameworks, frontier research, quantitative tools, and real-world case studies, the course fosters critical reflection on ethical principles, regulatory implications, and professional responsibilities. It prepares students to lead the development of ethically sound AI solutions and contribute to scholarly and policy debates in responsible AI.
learning_outcomes: Communicate complex ethical trade-offs and modelling decisions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including regulators and industry professionals.
Engage with and critique frontier research in algorithmic fairness, ethical AI governance, and regulatory developments.
Apply and assess advanced quantitative techniques for fairness evaluation, bias mitigation, and interpretability in predictive modelling applications.
Conduct independent or collaborative research that contributes to ethical AI practice, policy, or scholarly understanding in actuarial science.
Critically analyse ethical and societal challenges arising from the use of AI in high-stakes actuarial and financial decision-making.
Integrate ethical considerations into the design of AI systems, including data sourcing, model architecture, evaluation, and deployment strategies.
prerequisites: Students should have completed ACTL5305 or equivalent courses and achieved an exemption level for that course (65 and above).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Work Integrated Learning
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Work Integrated Learning (WIL) provides undergraduate students in the School of Art & Design with an opportunity to apply their prior academic learning in a creative workplace. Through this course you will explore possible career pathways by undertaking a professional placement relevant to your studies and professional interests. Professional placements require prior approval from the Course Convenor and must be appropriate in duration (typically 100 hours). Placement opportunities can be either self-sourced or advertised by the School. Please contact the Faculty WIL Unit for further details: ada-wil@unsw.edu.au
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and describe awareness of social and ethical responsibilities relevant to professional creative contexts.
Apply collaboration, communication, and professional practice skills to contribute effectively to a professional creative organisation.
Reflect on and evaluate professional experiences to identify personal strengths and opportunities in relation to career goals and aspirations.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: One of the following courses, DART3203, DDES2102, DART3100, DART3310, or FADA2020.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Art and Design in Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The course enhances your Honours research by helping you to identify key professional practice skills, attributes, and aspirations aligned with your practice, research, and professional interests. The course brings students together from across Art & Design Honours programs to explore and share a multitude of research and career trajectories. By asking you to pro-actively identify pathways, precedents, and opportunities that align with your current project and future interests, the course encourages you to consider how you can build on your research for contexts beyond the frameworks of the Honours year. Whether you are interested in developing an independent practice, working collaboratively, engaging with industry, seeking employment, and/or postgraduate study, this course is designed to enhance your repertoire of skills for a successful transition post-Honours. The course also actively contributes to your Honours project by facilitating the integration of professional practice skills in your research and seeking critical feedback through an open studio event showcasing your works in progress.
learning_outcomes: Apply professional practice skills and attributes in a peer-to-peer environment to develop and realise a showcase of works in progress.
Identify, analyse, and evaluate professional pathways and opportunities aligned with your research interests and career aspirations.
Critically examine exemplars in your field to develop a professional practice plan.
prerequisites: Must be enrolled in an Honours program in the School of Art & Design (program codes 4516, 4526, 4527, 4528, 4814, 4816, 4809).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Honours Professional Experience Program
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course will prepare students to pursue a full-time creative career and develop into versatile artists, designers, thinkers and creative practitioners that work in a constantly shifting design, arts and media arts landscape. Students will investigate creative opportunities that align with their honours major projects and work towards making their aspirational career goals explicit. This course also addresses the challenging aspects of the independent, freelance nature of the creative and cultural industries by providing students with the ability to recognise areas within their creative spheres where they may develop other income streams to support their creative practice.
learning_outcomes: Identify and investigate diverse structures and scales within professional industries to apply tailored creative practice skills within and beyond the studio environment.
Tailor their professional profile to meet creative selection criteria for work in professional industries.
Apply attributes and behaviours to a professional standard that are consistent within the professional work environment.
Evaluate and articulate shifts in practice, drawing on specific skills and attributes used during their professional placement.
Critically reflect on their professional practice and approaches to working with future key stakeholders within creative ecosystems.
Critically analyse, plan and prepare applications and documentation that respond appropriately to creative research project criteria.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Research Foundations in Art, Design and Media
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide an environment for postgraduate students to develop research foundations necessary for doctoral and/or masters of philosophy candidature, both theoretical and practice-based, in art, design and media arts at UNSW Art & Design . It is designed to assist those who come to postgraduate research without having immediately undertaken extensive written, theoretical or rigorous practice-based training in a prior degree. The course will introduce you to art and design as research, facilitate the refinement of your research proposals, develop understanding of relevant practice-based and literature research fields; understand the use and limits of theoretical frameworks; develop and refine research approach and methods; investigate the thesis as proposition and original contribution and their implications for practice-based research; refine research skills in secondary literature and referencing; and discuss the expectations and approaches to practical components of an art, design or media arts thesis. All meetings will follow a small group discussion format.
learning_outcomes: Present and discuss this thesis proposal with the class.
Write a draft thesis proposal that will provide the basis for your first-year review
Locate your topic in a broader field of theoretical and/or practice-based research and explain the intellectual contribution of your work
Begin planning your research strategy for the remainder of your thesis project
Articulate a clearly defined research topic

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)

syllabus_overview: This studio course is designed to develop your skills and knowledge in 3D visualisation and modelling. The course provides hands-on experience using key techniques, methods, and workflows so you can develop your own 3D digital models and assets relevant to your field of practice. The course introduces you to the fundamentals of 3D visualisation and industry-relevant workflows so that you can apply and adapt them in a variety of projects and contexts as part of your future practice.
learning_outcomes: Document and critically reflect on the conceptual and technical processes used in 3D modelling and computer visualisation.
Use visual analysis and experimentation to explore 3D visualisation principles and concepts.
Apply 3D computer generated imaging techniques and processes to create digital assets for CG pipelines.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)

faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture

This course develops your ability to confidently engage with, interpret and express complex ideas using an appropriate mix of communication strategies tailored to creative disciplines. In addition to an appreciation of fundamental research protocols in creative disciplines, you will enhance your academic reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills to better express coherent intellectual arguments, towards developing your own academic 'voice'. Collaboration in and out of class, using a mix of communication tools, will model cross-disciplinary interaction with colleagues, peers, professionals and the public.
learning_outcomes: Critically read, interpret and reflect on academic discourse across different creative disciplines
Lead oral presentations and audience discussions using visual, verbal, and written information
Discuss and write using appropriate technical terminology and Information Communication Technologies to meaningfully engage in professional communication
Identify and analyse English language forms, features, structures and referencing protocols appropriate for research, academic writing, critiques and/or artist statements

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)

faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The course provides an understanding of the various definitions of leadership and how they intersect, influence and are shaped by the cultural and creative industries. Leadership is examined from a theoretical and real word perspective to provide you with knowledge and practical techniques to help shape your careers. The idea of leadership takes many forms as distinct from organisational hierarchy, role or status. Cultural leadership is reflected in and by the organisation and industry, and this course demonstrates the interconnectedness of leadership to other disciplines such as marketing, writing, management, creative practice and production. Through lectures, workshops, case studies and action learning you will engage with examples of leadership in cultural and creative organisations, reflect on your own understanding of leadership and develop your own leadership capacity, preparing you for the rapidly evolving cultural landscape.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Aerospace Design 1
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: Aerospace Design 1 provides students with a grounding in aerospace design, in terms of both structural design and aerospace systems. In this course, you will consider the safe design of aerospace structures, through learning to access and use approved material data, understanding critical regulations, applying appropriate safety factors, and combining this with detailed structural analysis to produce technical design reports. You will also be introduced to a range of aerospace systems, and delve into the design drivers and redundancy requirements for flight safety, as well as exploring different systems implementations for mission requirements. To consolidate learning, the final experiential project requires you to work in small teams to design, manufacture, and test to failure a representative aerospace part, demonstrating structural strength requirements. Students are expected to have a sound understanding of engineering design and drawing, statics and free body diagrams, manufacturing, aerospace structural analysis, and flight performance prior to attempting this course.
learning_outcomes: Identify appropriate engineering data sources and regulations and apply in the context of aerospace design.
Design an aerospace structure to meet regulatory requirements and a given design brief.
Evaluate and justify systems selection and implementation for a variety of aerospace systems.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (DESN2000 or MMAN2100) AND (ENGG2400 OR MMAN2400)

You will learn how to apply experimental principles and techniques that will be applicable in your chosen fields or disciplines. The course focuses on process over product, exploring a range of tools to unlock your creative potentials, and helping you to produce more diverse, serendipitous and unexpected results. Through short activities, experimentation, reflection, and iteration you will develop a refined body of creative work based on experimental processes. The course aims to provide you with skills to open up your practice, overcome creative blockages and attune you to the creative potential in the world around you.
learning_outcomes: Explore and evaluate the role of experimentation and process-led artistic practice
Initiate and undertake advanced artistic experiments to produce diverse and experimental creative outcomes
Iterate, refine, and synthesise experimental processes to produce resolved and critical artistic practice

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Aerospace Structures
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course covers introductory and intermediate topics related to analysis and design of airframes: Basics Basic flight mechanics and simple manoeuvres (to understand airframe loads) for both terrestrial and launch aerospace vehicles Weights and balances Introduction to aerostructure design and function Aeroelasticity (optional flex week topic) Thin Walled Structures Thin-walled beam approximation Solid mechanics - Stress, strain, invariants Structural idealisation Bending, shear and torsion of complex beams Aerospace Materials Lightweight materials - Alloys and composites Failure prediction Material degradation through fatigue Analysis of composite materials Buckling Buckling of columns and plates Stiffened panel analysis and design
learning_outcomes: Determine internal loads in airframe components as a function of airframe layout and aircraft manoeuvres
Predict the onset of instability of thin-walled structures under static loads and be able to recommend amendments to the structural design to avoid instability and/or improve efficiency
Choose and justify materials to be used for specific aerospace applications based on component function, design drivers, material properties and ageing constraints
Productively contribute to a complex group engineering analysis task

Use methods for determining stress and deflections of thin walled single and multi-celled stiffened structures for axial, bending and shear loads and apply these techniques to the analysis of wing and fuselage structures in aircraft
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ENGG2400 OR MMAN2400 OR CVEN2301

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Aerodynamics
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: The overall aim of this course is to introduce students to the art and science of aerodynamics: how fluid motion generates the forces and moments on air vehicles required for flight. In this course you will learn how air creates the forces - lift and drag - on aerospace vehicles. You will learn how to measure these forces in the ab and calculate them using theory. You will also learn how to design a wing for subsonic and supersonic aircraft. Additionally, you will have a brief introduction to the science of aeroacoustics.
learning_outcomes: Analyse viscous flow over aerodynamic surfaces.
Analyse and predict the low speed aerodynamic performance of wings.
Analyse and predict the high-speed aerodynamic performance of objects (wings and other relevant devices).
Examine aerodynamic phenomenon in terms of basic principles of fluid motion.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (MMAN2600 or ENGG2500) and MMAN2700

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Flight Performance and Propulsion
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: The course starts with an introduction to the atmosphere, especially the troposphere and lower stratosphere where aircraft spend most of their time. We discuss the difference between true and equivalent airspeeds. Then we introduce the basic equations that describe straight & level flight. You are introduced to the propeller as a means of propulsion. Propellers are often driven by reciprocating piston engines and so we discuss their behavior as well as the basics of chemical reactions and the behavior of gas mixtures. Then we get back to flight mechanics introducing the basic equations that describe of climbing, gliding, and turning flight. We introduce the fundamental equations associated with compressible flows, normal shocks, oblique shocks prior to looking at gas turbine engines. Then we discuss the basic operation of helicopters and quad rotor drones. We give a very basic introduction to electric motors. Finally, we return to flight mechanics again introducing the Breguet range equations, take-off, landing, and energy methods.
learning_outcomes: Understand compressible flow analysis.
Understand the thermodynamics of combustion and gas mixtures
Analyse the strengths and weaknesses of Cumpsty's approach in examining the behaviour of gas turbines.
Understand the workings of modern propulsion systems (reciprocating piston engines, propellers, gas turbines)
Apply mathematical analysis to predict flight performance and to recognise the short comings of analysis.
Analyse the workings of helicopters, quadrotors and electric motors
Understand the difference between true and equivalent airspeeds.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (MMAN1300 or ENGG1300 or DPST1072 or CVEN1300 ) AND (MMAN2600 or ENGG2500) AND MMAN2700

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Aerospace Design 2
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course is a capstone aerospace design project. In design teams, students develop a preliminary design of an aircraft to meet a given request for proposal. The course aims to give a holistic approach to the aerospace design process. Students are required to consider the requirements of several disciplines including conceptual design, configuration, weights, sizing, payload, aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, systems, stability and control, performance, and cost. The course will give students the opportunity to integrate these elements into a single congruous design of an aircraft. Teamwork, report writing, and presentation skills are a focus to develop important professional skills for industry. Students are expected to have a sound understanding of aerospace regulations, aerodynamics, flight performance, propulsion, structural design and analysis, materials, computer aided design, flight dynamics, and aerospace systems prior to attempting this course.
learning_outcomes: Apply aerospace cross-disciplinary principles appropriately for a congruous design.
Produce a preliminary aircraft design to meet request for proposal and regulatory requirements.
Professionally communicate design concepts and information.
Demonstrate professional conduct, cooperatively manage and effectively contribute to an engineering team.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: AERO3110 AND AERO3410 AND AERO3630 AND AERO3660 AND MMAN3200
Prerequisite: At least 144 Units completed in AEROAH stream

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Dynamics of Aerospace Vehicles, Systems and Avionics
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: AERO4620 is one of the core courses in the Aerospace Engineering degree. it consists of three distinct modules: Module A deals with all systems onboard flying vehicles that are necessary for their proper functioning. Module B covers avionics, as well as all other non-electronic systems that are integrated with the avionic ones. Module C is about dynamics of aerospace vehicles. Topics include: Fluidic, mechanical and electrical systems in aerospace vehicles; environment control; avionics and advanced aircraft systems; computer-aided vehicle management; avionics requirements; avionics integration; airborne sensors; navigation; stability and control systems; cockpit environment; static and dynamic stability of atmospheric vehicles; flight control; handling and flying qualities
learning_outcomes: Analyse aspects of aircraft static and dynamic stability.
Demonstrate an understanding of the regulatory requirements for static stability.
Apply linear systems and controls to aircraft stability and control.
Establish the connection between the aircraft’s mission and the selection of systems and components
prerequisites: Prerequisite: AERO3660 and (MMAN3200 or ELEC3114)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Space Systems Architectures and Orbits
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course gives an overview of satellite systems, describing their main applications and providing a detailed introduction into the principles of orbital mechanics. The course focuses on orbital mechanics, covering orbit description and analysis, perturbations, orbital manoeuvres, interplanetary transfers and launch systems.
