title: Functional Anatomy of the Head, Neck and Back
syllabus_overview: You will gain an understanding of functional and clinically relevant anatomy of the head, neck and back regions of the human body. You will develop comprehensive knowledge of head and neck region of the human body, including its musculoskeletal, visceral and neurovascular components. The learning activities in this course aim to develop thorough understanding of the normal anatomy that can be applied to clinically relevant scenarios and medical imaging using problem-solving skills.
learning_outcomes: Describe and explain the functional anatomy of the head, neck, and back, including the musculoskeletal framework, viscera, neurovasculature, and lymphatics.
Identify the anatomy underpinning clinical and functional presentations related to the head, neck, and back.
Correlate normal anatomy with clinical imaging and cross-sectional anatomy.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 3831 Science (Medicine) Honours OR (Completed ANAT2111 or ANAT1521 or ANAT2511)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Functional Anatomy of the Limbs
syllabus_overview: This course follows on from ANAT2111 and ANAT2511 and complements the other level III anatomy courses (ANAT3121 and ANAT3131). The course aims to provide a detailed understanding of the anatomy of the limbs and the functional principles underpinning limb movement including an understanding of the functional aspects of muscle, joints and the mechanics of movement. Lectures focus on the musculoskeletal anatomy of joints and joint movement of the limbs. This is correlated to movement as it is related to function, exercise conditioning, clinical case applications and surface anatomy. Laboratory classes involve the study of prosected and plastinated specimens, models, X-rays and surface anatomy. Tutorials focus on the anatomy of the limbs using the applications of clinical cases, functional tasks and muscle conditioning exercises - these use online learning tools. For more detailed information, please click on "Course Outline" in box below.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the development of the limbs, and their evolutionary adaptations for function
Apply knowledge of limb organisation to interpretation of medical imaging data
Demonstrate knowledge of the anatomy of the upper limbs, and apply this to understand the principles related to joint movement and biomechanics
Demonstrate an understanding of the surface/living anatomy of the limbs
Demonstrate and apply knowledge of the anatomy of the lower limbs and apply this to understand the principles related to joint movement and biomechanics
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ANAT2111 or ANAT1521 or ANAT2511

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Neuroanatomy
syllabus_overview: Neuroanatomy is an advanced neuroscience course that provides students with an understanding of the development, structure, function and vascular supply of the spinal cord, brainstem and forebrain. By using a systems approach, you will acquire an in-depth knowledge of the neural structures and connections that underpin sensory processing and perception, reflexive and voluntary motor control and the emergence of complex higher functions in the cerebral cortex such as language and emotions. This comprehensive systems neuroscience course will equip you with skills directly applicable to research in neuroscience and pre-medical training.
learning_outcomes: Correlate the neuroanatomical organisation of the central nervous system to its functions, including the processing of sensory inputs, control of motor outputs and emergence of higher brain functions.
Correlate structural and functional knowledge of the central nervous system and its vascular supply with neurological presentations and deficits.
Integrate knowledge of neuroanatomy with the disciplines of physiology, psychology, and pathology, to understand the relationships between structure, function and behaviour in the nervous system.
Describe the external and internal features of the spinal cord, brainstem and forebrain and their vascular supply.
Identify neural structures in neuroanatomical diagrams, images, illustrations, radiological images, and 3D models.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 3831 Science (Medicine) Honours OR (Completed ANAT1521 or a minimum mark of 55 in ANAT2111 or ANAT2511)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural History and Theory 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural History and Theory 1 presents an inquiry into Western architecture, with an emphasis on the relevance of historical theories to contemporary design strategies. The course begins with the principles set out in antiquity and the Renaissance, such as order, the human analogy, proportion and decorum. These were adapted during the ensuing centuries. A tradition survived, where an architect is concerned with a person, who feels an affinity with the human-like character of a building. Along with the study of architecture in Europe, you will examine how classical buildings served the ambitions of imperial powers in different parts of the world. Skills acquired in the course include academic referencing, as well as writing short visual essays.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate foundational architectural enquiry skills through research, interpretation and reflection.
Communicate historical architectural concepts, principles, strategies and themes through sketches and text.
Analyse the ideas, themes and theories relevant to the history of Western architecture

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Architecture and Enabling Skills
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architecture and Enabling Skills introduces you to the discipline of architecture as a field of intellectual and creative endeavour. By exploring case studies of significant residential buildings, you will learn the key architectural terms and concepts used to describe and analyse architecture. Field excursions to local Sydney projects provide an opportunity to practice this architectural vocabulary and to develop essential architectural skills of sketching and describing built form. Through written assignments and in class presentations you will learn methods of researching and writing about architecture and verbal and graphic techniques for presenting architecture.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate with peers on a small research project responsibly and effectively.
Observe and describe built form using architectural terms and vocabulary.
Engage in architectural enquiry and research in a scholarly manner.
Express your knowledge and understanding of architecture and architectural concepts through writing, drawing and speaking.
Prepare an architectural precedent analysis.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Design Studio 1 introduces you to the disciplinary foundations for architectural design. Through small scale and experimental design projects, you will explore the main concepts and activities of architectural design. There is a focus on making and thinking about human inhabitation including space, form, order, structure, material, scale and proportion. You will learn manual and digital representational techniques as primary design communication tools, and explore the relationship between plan, section, elevation and three-dimensional forms.
learning_outcomes: Apply foundational knowledge of social, ethical, environmental concerns and regulatory requirements to the architectural design process.
Communicate architectural concepts through hand sketches, models and digital representation.

Develop the fundamentals of the architectural design process comprising of the interpretation of the design brief and architectural precedents, and the creation of conceptual and schematic design proposals.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: enrolment in program 3261 Architectural Studies or 3635 Civil Engineering (Civil Engineering with Architecture).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In Architectural Design Studio 2, you will develop an architectural proposition that thoughtfully responds to place, materiality, and spatial experience. Through careful observation and analysis of a site, you will investigate how architectural design connects multiple building levels and how movement through space shapes perception and experience. You will analyse architectural precedents to understand how history and material can influence design thinking. Through drawings, models, and diagrams, you will test how architectural design contributes to the character and quality of space. The course will guide you from site and precedent analysis to the development of your own architectural project. You will learn how to communicate ideas precisely using both digital and analogue methods, building the foundational skills needed for later studios.
learning_outcomes: Design spatial sequences that explore how movement and vertical transitions shape architectural experience.
Interpret site histories and precedents to generate contextually responsive and innovative design.
Formulate an architectural proposition that demonstrates an understanding of site conditions, precedents, scale and materials.
Apply materials to express architectural intent and contribute to the character and quality of public space.
Communicate architectural ideas with precision through integrated digital and analogue representation methods.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH1101

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 3A
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Design Studio 3A introduces you to core environmental principles for minimising a building’s operational energy consumption. You will explore how climate, topography, and site conditions influence architectural design, with a focus on passive strategies such as orientation, natural ventilation, and solar access. Through a residential design project, you will investigate how to integrate environmental sustainability into your design decisions. You will also develop skills in climate analysis, sustainable diagramming, and site positioning to enhance energy efficiency and thermal comfort. This studio provides a strong foundation in environmentally responsive design while strengthening your ability to communicate ideas through diagrams, models, and technical representation.
learning_outcomes: Communicate design ideas effectively through drawings, models, and diagramming techniques.
Analyse site conditions and environmental factors to inform architectural design decisions.
Apply an iterative design process, including interpretation of a design brief and architectural precedents, to the creation of a conceptual and schematic architectural proposal.
Assess materials and construction principles to develop environmentally responsive design.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH1102

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 3B
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Design Studio 3B explores how architecture can respond to the growing challenges of housing supply and the changing needs of communities. It focuses on innovative housing models such as intergenerational living, housing for older women, and other inclusive forms of shared habitation. Through the interpretation of site topography, landscape, and local context, you will develop design strategies that integrate social, environmental, and spatial considerations. Planning frameworks and environmental benchmarks will guide your design thinking, while key aspects of the National Construction Code will inform your understanding of buildability and compliance. The studio encourages you to imagine architecture as a social and spatial framework that supports diversity, inclusion, and resilience in the way people live together.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and analyse site topographies, features, and movement patterns to inform coherent architectural strategies
Evaluate and incorporate planning, National Construction Code, and environmental considerations to ground architectural propositions within their regulatory and ecological contexts
Communicate architectural concepts and design proposals through hand sketches, physical models and digital representation
Develop and apply design strategies that respond to the challenges of housing supply and support diverse models of community living
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH1102, or completion of the UNSW College Diploma of Architecture

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Construction and Structures 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Construction and Structures 1 introduces you to the foundations of architectural construction and structures. It provides you with the vocabulary and understanding to engage in dialogue with experts involved in the building process and the confidence to apply your newfound knowledge to the design of a small piece of residential architecture. Fundamental techniques for constructing floors, walls and roofs are covered. Principles of architectural structure are introduced and explored through structural idealisation, stability and bracing.
learning_outcomes: Relate the selection of materials and structural options for a simple architectural design proposal to relevant quality and performance standards
Communicate the material, construction, and structural information of a simple example of architectural design to professional standards
Apply foundational knowledge of the physical characteristics of materials and their structural implications to the selection of construction options for a simple example of architectural design

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 4
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this studio, you will explore the design of adaptable, dynamic built spaces and landscapes on a dramatic Sydney foreshore site with indigenous and industrial heritage. It builds upon your work in previous design studios in the Architecture Program. You will need to bring your accumulated design knowledge to this studio in order to negotiate a major transition in terms of scale and complexity. This studio involves a major shift from a series of highly defined sites to a broader landscape, from a private program to a public program, from single buildings and landscapes to multiple buildings and landscapes, and from a series of discrete projects to one major design project.
learning_outcomes: Design architecture incorporating the interpretation of a design brief, conceptual design and detailed design to an intermediate level of resolution.
Apply ethical judgement in architectural design with an emphasis on sites incorporating indigenous and industrial heritage.
Apply skills in architectural communication with an emphasis on freehand drawing, experimental casting and model-making.
Develop a design method with an emphasis on experimentation in the context of a single, complex design project on a challenging site.
Demonstrate intermediate skills in the application of social, ethical, environmental and regulatory knowledge to architectural design.
Demonstrate collaborative skills in teamwork that ensure productivity and shared responsibility
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH1201

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 5
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Design Studio 5 challenges you to design housing that balances affordability, quality, and sustainability. You will explore the complex social, economic, and environmental factors shaping affordable housing today and investigate space efficiency, material economy, and standardisation as strategies for the design of a residential project. You will develop adaptable design solutions that respond to diverse community demographics and integrate communal spaces that foster social interaction and well-being. This studio deepens your understanding of housing as both an architectural and a societal challenge, and prepares you to create innovative and inclusive design solutions.
learning_outcomes: Communicate architectural concepts and design strategies effectively through drawings, models, and verbal presentations.
Apply material economy and standardisation principles to achieve cost-effective and sustainable housing solutions.
Analyse the social and environmental factors influencing affordable housing design.
Develop space-efficient and adaptable residential design proposals that respond to diverse community needs, and integrate affordable housing policies and participatory design strategies.

Recognise Country and its significance to First Nations Peoples, acknowledging the ongoing effects of colonisation on communities and individuals, and apply culturally responsible methods for engaging and co-designing with First Nations Peoples.
prerequisites: ARCH1105

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 6
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Design Studio 6 challenges you to transform an existing structure by applying adaptive reuse strategies and balancing preservation, innovation, and sustainability. Building on your growing design skills, you will explore how to repurpose buildings while respecting their historical, cultural, and architectural significance. You will conduct research into building history, assess structural conditions, and develop strategies for integrating new and old elements into a cohesive design. A key focus will be designing flexible, contextually responsive spaces that support contemporary needs while preserving the character of the original structure. You will also engage with material selection, energy efficiency upgrades, and resource-conscious renovation strategies to promote sustainability. Through detailed analysis, and design iteration, you will refine your ability to work within existing built environments, ensuring projects remain culturally sensitive and inclusive. This studio strengthens your capacity to approach adaptive reuse with creativity and technical understanding, preparing you to engage meaningfully with the complexities of sustainable architectural transformation.
learning_outcomes: Apply culturally responsible methods to incorporate Aboriginal ways of knowing, being, and to site analysis and design processes.
Assess existing buildings for adaptive reuse potential, inclusive of their material qualities, structural conditions, and cultural significance.
Communicate advanced design concepts and technical solutions effectively through drawings, models, documentation, and innovative digital strategies.
Apply resource-efficient strategies and cultural awareness to minimise environmental impact and foster social sustainability in architectural design outcomes.
Develop contextually responsive and innovative design proposals that integrate new and existing architectural elements.
prerequisites: ARCH1205

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 7
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architecture Design Studio 7 is the first phase of your Capstone Studio experience. You will engage with complex urban or regional conditions through deep design research and critical analysis and explore the role of public architecture in strengthening community resilience by applying culturally and ethically informed awareness to your design proposals. Through a rigorous, multidimensional investigation of site, history, social context, and material availability, you will develop design strategies that enhance equity, inclusivity, and environmental sustainability. You will refine your ability to interpret project requirements, respond to contextual constraints, and articulate your design intentions with clarity. By synthesising research, technology, and architectural practice, this studio equips you to address complex societal and environmental challenges and sets the foundation for your capstone project in Architectural Studio 8.
learning_outcomes: Analyse complex urban or regional conditions through multidimensional research into a site, its history, social context, and material conditions.
Communicate advanced design concepts and solutions effectively through drawings, models, documentation, and digital strategies.

Identify and apply culturally responsible methods for engaging and co-designing with First Nations Peoples, incorporating Aboriginal ways of knowing, being, and doing in site analysis and design choices.
Interpret project requirements and navigate contextual constraints of design briefs to enhance environmental sustainability.
Develop design strategies that apply culturally and ethically informed awareness to enhance community resilience, equity, and inclusivity.
prerequisites: ARCH1206

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural History and Theory 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural History and Theory 2 explores modern and contemporary architecture (1900- present) in four ways: over time, by type, through place, and as theoretical ideas. You will examine significant buildings and their typologies through architectural readings to learn about their social, political, technological factors. Assessment activities focus on developing your skills in architectural research, analysis and communication.
learning_outcomes: Explain changes in modern and contemporary architecture over time and in relation to social, political, technological and intellectual influences.
Demonstrate skills of architectural enquiry through research, analysis, and critical reflection.
Analyse architectural typologies in terms of the principles and vocabulary of architecture.
Engage in peer-to-peer learning to develop skills in collaboration.
Apply architectural communication skills including text and visual modes of presentation.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Construction and Structures 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Construction and Structures 2 expands your technical understanding of materials, construction and structures through in-depth case studies and direct project applications. You will investigate and apply knowledge of reinforced concrete, steel and timber construction integrated with architectural design. You will learn the relations between structural design, construction procedures and architectural narratives through a focus on detail design and material specification. You will also learn how to use building codes, standards and regulations applicable to medium-scale buildings.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of the relevant legislation, quality and performance standards and codes applicable to the selection of materials and construction systems.
Appraise concrete, steel and timber construction options informed by knowledge of their physical characteristics and their assembly procedures.
Communicate material, construction and structural information using drawings, models, specifications and schedules.
Integrate construction and structural knowledge of concrete, steel and timber, as well as including environmental performance, into architectural design.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH1162, or completion of the UNSW College Diploma of Architecture

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 6
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In Architectural Design Studio 6, as the final studio of the undergraduate degree, you will develop a single architectural proposal to a detailed level of programmatic, spatial and material complexity. In doing so, you will focus on how architectural thinking and production is influenced by multiple environmental, technological and social factors. You will research, analyse and interpret the physical and cultural content of a complex site to generate an architectural design strategy. From this strategy you will develop your proposal, or part of the proposal, to a detailed technical resolution. You will be assessed in relation to the resolution, coherence and imagination evident in your final design solution, as well as evidence of consistent application of thought, consideration and understanding. The employment and interface of relevant computational tools and analogue skills will be assessed alongside the final design outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Communicate architectural concepts and resolved design proposals through hand sketches, formal and technical drawings, physical models and digital representations.
Apply knowledge of social, ethical, environmental concerns and regulatory requirements to the architectural design process and its outputs.
Implement an iterative and reflective architectural design process based on site analysis and research, the interpretation of the design brief, and the study of architectural precedents.
Create conceptual and schematic design proposals to a detailed level of aesthetic, functional and technical resolution.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH1311

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 5
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Design Studio 5 explores how architecture shapes and is shaped by the urban environment. It focuses on understanding the city as a dynamic field of social, spatial, and material relations where architecture operates as an agent of transformation. You will analyse sites within their broader urban context to identify key spatial, cultural, and environmental forces that inform design. Drawing on principles from urban design theory and precedent studies, you will test how architectural form, program, and structure can respond to public space and connectivity. The studio emphasises the integration of architectural and urban scales, requiring you to balance conceptual thinking with technical and aesthetic resolution.
learning_outcomes: Apply key concepts and principles from urban design theory and practice to guide the development of a public architectural proposal within its urban context
Communicate architectural concepts through hand sketches, models and digital representation
Analyse a site and evaluate relevant precedents to identify spatial issues and opportunities that inform the architectural design process
Design a public architectural project that responds to its surrounding urban environment and demonstrates structural, functional, and aesthetic coherence
Critically reflect on your current standpoint and recognise how it informs your current design practice and impacts diverse stakeholders
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH1203

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural History and Theory 3
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will examine selected themes that embody architectural developments in Australia from the late nineteenth century to the present. These themes include nationalism and its presence in architecture and architectural discourse, the reception and interpretation of modernism, and concepts and practices of architectural regionalism. You will also explore three compositional traditions - the tectonic, abstraction and figuration - in the Australian context, through academic scholarship, media commentary and criticism.
learning_outcomes: Investigate a range of themes pertinent to the study of the history of modern architecture in Australia.
Apply architectural communication skills with an emphasis on the written text as a means of conveying an understanding of topics and themes.
Employ ethical judgement in architectural scholarship with an emphasis on the role of discourse in generating architectural significance.
Demonstrate competent skills of architectural enquiry through research, analysis, critique and reflection.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 96 UOC

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Fabrication
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Fabrication expands your knowledge and understanding of construction material properties and their integration with architectural forms. The course is focused on exploring the role of the building façade, as a multi-layered system able simultaneously to deliver thermal comfort and empower interaction between inside and outside of a building. You will be provided with new tools and methods to understand the technical narrative behind architectural case studies. You will also explore and develop the relationship between design and tectonics in your own projects. The course is a combination of technical analysis and workshop-based experimentation directed to understanding the hierarchy of building components and the logic behind architectural construction. Modern conceptions of architectural tectonics will be explored, and physical precedents analysed.
learning_outcomes: Assess material and construction options informed by disciplinary knowledge.
Apply knowledge of relevant legislation, quality and performance standards and codes in the selection of materials and construction systems.
Communicate material, construction and structural information using drawings, models, specifications and schedules.
Integrate construction and structural knowledge, including their environmental performance into an architectural design.
prerequisites: Pre-requisites ARCH1261

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Science and Building Environment
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Science and Building Environment focuses on applying the principles of acoustics, lighting and comfort to achieve indoor environmental quality (IEQ) and enhanced environmental performance. The course contextualises the science of acoustics, lighting and comfort within architectural design with an emphasis on environmental data collection, analysis and application to optimise IEQ and environmental performance. You will explore the role of architectural design in mitigating indoor and outdoor thermal comfort impacts through real-world case-studies and online tools. You will investigate the significance of daylighting and artificial lighting design in IEQ and building environmental performance and apply acoustic principles to your studio designs. You will learn how to identify, evaluate and apply strategies to optimise acoustics, lighting and thermal comfort integrated with architectural design compliant with the regulatory standards applicable to environmental performance.
learning_outcomes: Communicate Indoor Environmental Quality using descriptive, visual and numerical formats, suited to building environmental specialists.
Evaluate acoustic, lighting and comfort strategies to optimise Indoor Environmental Quality and building environmental performance.
Apply Australian building codes and standards applicable to acoustics, lighting and comfort to architectural designs.
Apply knowledge of scientific principles of acoustics, daylighting and lighting and thermal comfort to architectural design.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH1161 or BENV1161 or completion of the UNSW College Diploma of Architecture

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Critical Review of Literature
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Critical Review of Literature is a major research-based investigation into a subject related to the your area of specialisation. This leads to a culmination of a well-informed understanding of the chosen research topic, offering a critical interpretation of the existing knowledge and literature. The course aims to create a community of learners. Effective research and writing support will come from fellow students, supervisors and the course convenor through both individual research consultations and class/peer led discussions.
learning_outcomes: Locate and collate relevant literature to form a foundation for a research project.
Critically review scholarly literature related to a selected research topic.
Write a critical literature review that identifies the fundamental issues of importance to your topic area and themes of significance within the published research.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Building Information Modelling for Sustainable Design: Lifecycle Carbon Analysis
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Building Information Modelling (BIM) for Sustainable Design: Lifecycle Carbon Analysis introduces the concepts and methods of BIM in sustainable building design. You will explore the key concepts and real-world applications of BIM, and use it to model building designs and assess their carbon impact across the entire lifecycle. Through the process, you will assess design options to identify sustainable solutions, while developing your skills in documentation and visualisation of buildings.
learning_outcomes: Prepare a professional documentation set generated from BIM models that meets industry standards
Apply key concepts and methods of Building Information Modelling (BIM) to support building design
Produce BIM-based lifecycle carbon analyses to evaluate the environmental performance of building design
Critically assess sustainable design strategies using digital platforms

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Honours Thesis
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course is a research-based investigation into a subject related to your area of interest. It is a continuation of work undertaken in ARCH1481 and BENV4000, but it is a standalone project and yields its own outcome – the honours thesis. This is the culmination of a well-informed understanding of your chosen research topic. It is expected that the honours thesis will offer an in-depth interpretation of the existing knowledge and literature. Through this course, you will develop as an architectural scholar with an understanding of the discipline in its interdisciplinary context and be capable of independent and collaborative enquiry.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise knowledge of architectural concepts and theories in response to complex research problems.
Collect and analyse evidence using research methods that meet professional and scholarly standards.
Formulate an argument based on research findings and analysis.
Communicate your research process and findings both verbally and through a written thesis that includes a range of visual material.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architectural Design Studio 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Architectural Studio 1 focuses on the project initiation and conceptual design phases of architectural practice, with an explicit commitment to learning from First Nations cultures. In this studio you will engage with the thoughtful, creative, iterative, and culturally responsive processes of initiating a project and the early stages of design. You will undertake research, analysis, critical self-reflection, and explore diverse design approaches, design ideas, and design proposals. You will develop a design concept that meets the client’s brief, respects Country, and demonstrates a clear understanding of site, architectural spaces and conventions.
learning_outcomes: Relate your understanding and awareness of Country and First Nations culture to Australian architectural practice.

Independently and collaboratively research relevant site histories, environmental factors, Indigenous concepts, and human and more-than-human relationships to deepen your analysis and inform design decisions.
Develop, test, and evaluate siting and conceptual design options to develop place-based design options and proposals.
Undertake in-depth site analyses which encompass Indigenous, spatial, experiential, social, environmental, and historical contexts and conditions of a given site.
Demonstrate advanced architectural communication skills in the expression and presentation of different stages of the design process.
prerequisites: Currently enrolled in program 8143 Master of Architecture or 8144 Master of Architecture / Property and Development

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Integrated Design Studio 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: ARCH7112 Integrated Design Studio 1 prepares you for ARCH7113 Integrated Design Studio 2 and Graduation Studio by providing a foundation in architectonics: an integrative practice exploring interrelationships between design, technology and performance across architectural scales, processes and representations. Within the thematic of the four major streams offered in the Master of Architecture degree, and using architectonics as the theoretical framework, in this course you will develop the knowledge and ability to apply the relevant units of competency required for professional architects. You will focus on Project Initiation and Conceptual Design and prepare for Detailed Design and Documentation which are further explored in ARCH7113 Integrated Design Studio 2.
learning_outcomes: Develop a conceptual design into a detailed design through iterative refinement and testing of options.
Document and present an architectural design including key generative concepts and organising principles.
Assess the regulatory, environmental, disciplinary, technical, contextual and social considerations of a design proposal.
Appraise architectural design ideas and alternative solutions in the formulation of a creative and coherent conceptual design proposal.
Apply reflective practice, critical thinking and creativity in the initiation and concept design phases of an architectural project.
prerequisites: Currently enrolled in program 8143 Master of Architecture or 8144 Master of Architecture / Property and Development. Students are required to have completed ARCH7111.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Construction and Structures
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Advanced Construction and Structures explores specialised topics in structural design and the architectural implications of specific construction solutions. You will learn tools and methods to develop complex architectural schemes that embrace environmentally sustainable principles. As part of the course, you will be exposed to various structural solutions and construction methods that support non-standard architectural projects. You will learn how to develop a façade system emphasising thermal comfort and assembly procedures. Through a series of technical drawings and details, you will demonstrate how architectural projects address structural logic, assembly, shading and ventilation strategies.
learning_outcomes: Apply structural concepts and construction principles into the design of building frames.
Test low-carbon solutions to structural components with an emphasis on joint design and component assembly.
Evaluate structural and construction solutions to complex architectural systems.
Develop environmentally sustainable and structurally sound architectural schemes.
Employ design and research methodologies to develop façade systems for a range of building types.
prerequisites: Currently enrolled in program 8143 Master of Architecture or 8144 Master of Architecture / Property and Development

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: The Profession of Architecture
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The Profession of Architecture examines a range of concepts and contemporary issues related to professional practice and the architectural profession. Scales and types of architectural practice models, the agency of the architect and the role of the architect as advocate and public intellectual will be explored. Key learnings are founded in a review of the development of the architectural profession and its structures and networks, as well as the role of the architect in the past and present. You will engage in detailed study of the expectations placed on the architect and the ethical and legal requirements of the architect as a professional practitioner. You will also investigate the ongoing shaping of the profession’s narratives via traditional, alternative and emerging modes of practice. This will include a review of management and business structures and the contexts of the public sphere, power and politics will also be considered alongside professional responsibilities and opportunities within and outside of traditional architectural practice. You will examine a range of concepts and current issues related to professional practice and the architectural profession. As well as looking at the expectations placed on the registered architects and the ethical and legal requirements of the architect as a professional practitioner, this course examines scales and types of architectural practice models, the agency of the architect and the role of the architect as advocate and public intellectual.
learning_outcomes: Identify and discuss ethical principles and processes in relation to the broader community where architectural practice intersects with legislative and legal frameworks.
Identify and interpret regulatory requirements and obligations for the practicing architect.
Articulate and analyse the architectural process in relation to professional communications and ethical demands placed on the practicing architect.
Interrogate and compare the complex and challenging social, ethical, environmental, political and regulatory contexts that impact the agency of the practicing architect.
prerequisites: Currently enrolled in program 8143 Master of Architecture or 8144 Master of Architecture / Property and Development

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Professional Practice 2: Projects and Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Professional Practice 2: Projects and Practice introduces you to the professional expectations and requirements of the practicing architect with a focus on the realisation of architectural projects. You will examine the practice of architecture through topics addressing the core responsibilities and activities of the architect. This includes client and stakeholder engagement and management, project types, procurement methods, documentation and approval processes, and regulatory, legal, ethical, contractual and business responsibilities. The course content and activities encourage the development of professional behaviours, particularly around communications, writing and technical language, strategic thinking, and how best to consider sustainability and societal concerns. Aspects of practice are presented and discussed in relation to the design, documentation and delivery of architectural projects: from client architect agreements and fee proposals through to briefing, documentation and approval processes, tendering, the establishment of building contracts and contract administration. Procurement and contracting methods are explored alongside an understanding of key professional relationships such as those with specialty consultants, external and internal stakeholders, and contractors.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and examine regulatory requirements and obligations relevant to the professional practice of architecture in Australia.
Explain procurement, cost and risk management processes in each stage in an architectural project.
Assess ethical and sustainability implications of tendering, procurement and construction.
Apply principles of contract establishment and administration to a hypothetical architectural project.
Identify and discuss the roles of the architect, consultants, contractors, suppliers and stakeholders in the delivery of a project.
Apply communication and research techniques relevant to contemporary architectural practice, including professional writing and presentation, engagement and collaborative working skills.
prerequisites: Currently enrolled in program 8143 Master of Architecture or 8144 Master of Architecture / Property and Development. Students are required to have completed ARCH7182.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Integrated Design Studio 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: ARCH7113 aims to prepare you for your final-year Graduation Studio and post-graduate professional work by consolidating your design competency with an emphasis on the principles, modes and tools of architectural documentation. Documentation is the process of resolving, detailing and communicating an architectural project through all project stages. Documentation includes the use of drawings, models, specifications and schedules to communicate design intent and construction details. You will develop design and documentation skills through assessment tasks mapped to the Detail Design and Documentation of an architectural assembly or detail building component. Detail Design will address the integration of regulatory, structural, services, constructional and material requirements. Documentation will focus on the preparation of resolved 3D models and coordinated drawings, schedules and specifications of quality and performance standards in relation to materials, finishes, fittings and systems. ARCH7113 logically builds on the design integration processes introduced in ARCH7112 (Integrated Design Studio 1) by reinforcing the regulatory, environmental and communication knowledge, skills and application required for the practice of architecture. Through the development of design and documentation competencies, you will build capacity to produce fit-for-purpose documentation at different project stages that progressively conform to accepted standards of professional architectural practice.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and integrate environmental sustainability and systems performance of an architectural design.
Develop and resolve an architectural design through research, detailed assessment of options and the integration of technical solutions.
Apply reflective practice and creativity to the detailed design and documentation of an architectural project.
Document the detail design of an architectural project evidencing structural, building services, constructional and material considerations, using drawings, models, specifications and schedules.
Apply relevant regulatory requirements, including planning controls and construction codes, to an architectural design.
prerequisites: Currently enrolled in program 8143 Master of Architecture or 8144 Master of Architecture / Property and Development. Students are required to have completed ARCH7112.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Research Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The Graduation Studio in the Master of Architecture Program runs over two terms; the first term is the Research Studio where you will engage in a design-based research inquiry to develop a conceptual framework for your graduation project, along with your initial architectural proposals. The second term is the Major Design Studio where you develop your proposal into a highly resolved architecture project. In the Research Studio, you will select a thematic option allied with the UNSW Built Environment Architecture Program streams, namely: Architecture and High-Performance Technology; Architecture and Housing, Architecture and Social Agency, and Architecture and Urban Conditions. The Research Studio structure encourages and supports theoretical and site research, as well as exploration, speculation and analysis. Weekly studio-based activities guide your development of a conceptual architectural proposal that describes the parameters and architectural ambitions of your individual project.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse site, precedents and thematic studies to identify implications, draw conclusions and establish directions for architectural design options.
Propose an architectural design brief that responds to the stream's studio premise and a broad range of disciplinary knowledge.
Apply advanced architectural communication skills and techniques to describe the qualities and characteristics of the conceptual design options.
Evaluate architectural design and siting options inspired by the proposed brief with conclusions that display creativity, social awareness and disciplinary insight.
Develop an approach to architectural design from self-directed and collaborative research across cultural, political, environmental and disciplinary contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH7113

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Major Design Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The Graduation Studio in the Master of Architecture program runs over two terms; the first term is the Research Studio where you will engage in a design-based research inquiry to develop a conceptual framework for your graduation project, along with your initial architectural proposals. The second term is the Major Design Studio where you develop your proposal into a highly resolved architecture project. In the Major Design Studio you will continue in your Research Studio group to create rigorous and compelling architecture: namely Architecture and High-Performance Technology; Architecture and Housing, Architecture and Social Agency, and Architecture and Urban Conditions. Each studio explicitly supports the detailed design development of individual architectural proposals as realised through appropriate modes of architectural representation. Emphasis is placed on the development of an architectural proposition through critique, evaluation and the testing of options. The developed design will reach an ambitious level of programmatic, spatial, material, environmental and technological integration and resolution. This is expected at an imaginative and ingenious level of experimentation. You will evaluate and develop options for architectural representation styles and techniques to establish the most effective methods to communicate your work. Weekly studio-based activities, regular presentations to peers, and studio reviews with eminent critics and practitioners will guide your design development process to a coherent final graduation design project. It will be celebrated in a public graduation exhibition.
learning_outcomes: Integrate construction systems, materials, services and technologies into a complex architectural design through a holistic consideration of material properties, occupant lifestyle, aesthetics, energy consumption, regulations, human well-being and the welfare of future generations.
Integrate expertise from relevant consultants and specialists into the development of an advanced architectural design.
Develop an architectural design that demonstrates a high-level interpretation of the brief, conceptual and schematic exploration, and then detailed to a comprehensive level of resolution.
Appraise advanced architectural representation styles and techniques to adopt culturally responsive methods appropriate to different audiences.

Evaluate and test detailed architectural design options inspired by the project brief with conclusions that display creativity, social awareness including consideration of implications for Country, and disciplinary insight.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH7201

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architecture and Politics
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In Architecture and Politics, you will undertake a philosophical investigation of architecture over time with a particular focus on architecture’s entangled relationship with politics. You will explore the power basis of design and its social and ethical responsibilities. In this course you will engage with current thoughts in architectural theory, reflect on the state of contemporary architectural and city-making practices, and begin to identify your own aims as a practicing architect.
learning_outcomes: Critically read scholarly texts in architecture and urban studies.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of selected examples of architectural theory through verbal and written communication.
Write grammatically correct and well-structured essays.
Independently research the historical, political, economic, and cultural contexts of cities and buildings.
Lead verbal presentations and in-person learning activities.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Performance over Time of Building Systems
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Performance over Time of Building Systems introduces you to the analysis of the users’ needs in relation to related to the architectural space and translating these into performance-based requirements and specifications to prevent building defects and durability issues. You will investigate the durability of building envelope components and possible design countermeasures to the most common defects due to errors in conception, construction, or maintenance. Your detailed technological design will be informed by software simulations of the hygrothermal performance of building components. Finally, you will orient your work in relation to regulatory frameworks, including the National Construction Code and technical standards (e.g. AS/NZS or ISO standards), to develop specifications, and verify the delivered performance and building quality.
learning_outcomes: Develop specifications applying technical standards to ensure building quality and performance and prevent building defects.
Analyse modes of failure in building components in relation to improving building technology and preventing major building defects.
Apply users’ needs and performance requirements to the design of building envelope systems.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Designing Diversity: Architecture and Urbanism in a Multicultural Context
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Designing Diversity: Architecture and Urbanism in a Multicultural Context explores the relationships between built environment, culture and society. It presents social and cultural processes as well as modes of engagement vital in the shaping of urban space and a sense of place. Building on interpretative techniques and visual methodologies of sociology, cultural studies and anthropology, the course develops an understanding of the interconnections between the built fabric, the individuals and communities for whom cities are created. You will develop skills to interpret relationships between urban spaces and specific cultural practices and patterns of habitation. Sydney provides the primary site for student projects; its multicultural character offers a rich context for interrogating the relationship between architecture and culture. The course introduces several distinct types of spaces, such as migrant and minority groups’ religious and community spaces, for their spatial representation of beliefs and practices. We explore diverse community and public spaces as well as places of consumption to understand their cultural significance and representation dynamics.
learning_outcomes: Explain the relationships between religious and cultural diversity and city-making.
Demonstrate analytical skills to interpret complex urban and suburban networks and the relationship of these to design practice.
Demonstrate advanced skills in methods of visualisation, representation and spatialisation of research findings.
Demonstrate creative and interpretative skills in presenting research data and analysis.
Analyse the cultural and social phenomena that influence design of cities and buildings in Sydney.
Interpret the relationships between social and cultural practices and architecture and urban design.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Graduation Exhibition Design
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Graduation Exhibition Design uses a real-world exhibition of student design work as a scaffold for exploring the history and evolution of exhibition and display as a cultural marker in societies, and the palette of materials and tools at the design and production team’s disposal. Through guided case study research, you will consider a variety of possibilities for the design and delivery of an exhibition. This course is ideal for those undertaking a design focused degree as it supports the annual exhibition of student work in the School of Built Environment.
learning_outcomes: Engage in research to assess the factors that influence the conception and delivery of an exhibition for built environment disciplines.
Collaborate as a member of an interdisciplinary exhibition design team to develop and communicate a design proposal for an exhibition.
Develop conceptual designs for exhibitions, suited to a stated purpose, with reference to audience, context and historical precedent.
Translate a design concept for an exhibition into material choices and installation methods.
prerequisites: Prereq ARCH7202 or ARCH1302 or ARCH7251/7252/7253/7254

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Themes in Australian Architecture
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course offers an in-depth study of Australian architecture through the work of selected architects and themes. It will explore the complexity of ideas and philosophies that have influenced and shaped the work of some of Australia's leading architectural practitioners both historically and in the present. The course consists of lectures and tutorial discussions.
learning_outcomes: Generate thematic studies of the work of selected Australian architects
Demonstrate an understanding of a range of topics and themes that are pertinent to the study of modern and contemporary architecture in Australia
Demonstrate skills of architectural enquiry through reading, research and analysis.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Architecture and Urbanism in Asia
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course introduces you to Architecture and Urbanism in Asia through investigations of the built environment from pre-modern to contemporary times. You will critically explore the main characteristics of selected Asian works of architecture and cities, in particular in East Asia, their history and presence, looking at their specific cultural, social, economic and political conditions, while tracing their urban development and learning about more recent transformations in a global context. You will learn to analyse architecture and urban environments through texts and visual material such as maps, photographs, and videos, and clearly communicate your ideas through discussions, presentations, and written work.
learning_outcomes: Critically interpret scholarly texts and other forms of writing about architecture and urbanism in Asia.
Analyse cities and buildings through maps, photographs, videos, paintings and texts.
Critically analyze and understand architecture and cities in Asia by exploring the historical, cultural, social, political and economic context of the urban form.
Aquire knowledge of architectural history and urban development of various regions in Asia from deverse sources.
Communicate your interpretation and analyses of Asian urbanism and architecture through oral presentations, visuals and essays.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Urban Climate Change - Mitigation and Adaptation in the Urban Built Environment
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will learn about urban climate problems together with the relevant mitigation and adaptation design techniques and technologies to counterbalance the temperature increase in the urban built environment. The first part of the course, will explore the major issues around the climate of cities, will offer advanced knowledge on the interaction between the urban climate, buildings, and open spaces, and will analyse the main impact of local climate change on energy, indoor and outdoor thermal comfort, health, and economy. The second part of the course will explore, analyse, and present in detail the major mitigation and adaptation design techniques and technologies to counterbalance the urban temperature increase. It will investigate and present issues related to the appropriate use of materials in cities, new advanced and cutting edge materials for open spaces and buildings, heat dissipation and amortization technologies for buildings and open spaces based on the use of low temperature environmental sinks, smart energy and environmental management technologies for cities, Anthropogenic heat avoidance technologies and all aspects related to the proper use of urban greenery in the urban built environment. Examples from successful real case studies will be presented. You will present and analyse modelling techniques to simulate the thermal characteristics of cities and evaluate the impact of the main mitigation technologies.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the specific impact of the urban climate on the energy consumption of buildings, thermal comfort and the global environmental performance of the urban built environment
Apply advanced computational methods to optimise the environmental design of urban buildings and open spaces and minimize their environmental impact
Apply advanced mitigation and adaptation techniques and technologies to design and enhance the performance of urban buildings and urban structures counterbalancing the urban climate change
Analyse the major climatic phenomena and mechanisms in the urban environment affecting the performance of urban buildings and open spaces

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Elements of Architectural Design
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Elements of Architectural Design investigates contemporary architectural case studies to uncover the professional knowledge, values, and technical expertise that shape their realisation. Working collaboratively, you will undertake fieldwork, gather documentation, and develop cultural, social, and environmental analyses of selected projects. Through critical reflection on teamwork and interdisciplinary problem-solving, you will gain insight into the professional competencies embedded in complex architectural production. This learning process in this course supports the articulation of your own professional focus and inform the development of a tailored career plan.
learning_outcomes: Analyse complex professional architectural knowledge required to deliver exemplary projects across diverse contexts
Apply professional strategies for career development, including self-directed learning, goal setting, and reflective practice
Communicate architectural ideas and research findings to academic and professional audiences through visual, verbal, and written modes within interdisciplinary collaborative settings
Demonstrate collaborative skills in teamwork that ensure productivity and shared responsibility

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: A History of Housing
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: A History of Housing explores the complex and diverse discussions around the design, innovation, planning, policies and economics of social housing. Social and affordable housing, whether considered as a reflection of social policy, a commodity, or a site of social struggle, plays a significant part in our everyday life. The debates concerning social housing are products of various ideologies that affect our society and shape our built environment. Through this course, you will gain an understanding of the long history of the ‘housing question’ and the key concepts that have underpinned such discussions. You will examine historic and contemporary architectural and urban responses that have emerged from debates. Through the exploration of relationships between design, regulatory frameworks and housing policy, you will develop tools for critical analysis and participation in the production of this significant and ever-evolving typology.
learning_outcomes: Examine and apply theoretical models to practice, by critically analysing social housing design typology within the broader socio-political context of city-making.
Interpret the relationship between design, planning policies, economic factors, and the sustainability of social and collective housing.
Demonstrate creative and interpretative skills in presenting research data and analysis.
