institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Use and Misuse
syllabus_overview: Big Data and Artificial Intelligence have changed business forever. Business leaders and managers – not just technical specialists – need to understand the opportunities and risks for business in collecting, analysing, sharing and using data, including what is legally permissible and what is ethically appropriate. Getting this wrong can harm individuals and societies and cause significant financial and reputational damage to the businesses involved. This course equips students to identify and engage thoughtfully with the fundamental questions of data governance – what may we do, and what should we do, with data analytics?
learning_outcomes: Examine issues arising from ethics, management and governance in the context of the collection, sharing, processing, analysis and presentation of data in for-profit and for-purpose businesses and in the business of government.
Work constructively in teams to identify and address the social impact of innovations in business and technology.
Critically reflect on the values, practices, and role as a potential agent of positive change.
Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of different philosophical approaches to complex problems.

Analyse ethical, managerial and governance issues in a logical and structured way, including by identifying non-financial risks, researching relevant sources, proposing an outcome and identifying possible challenges to the proposed outcome.
Present written work addressing ethics, management and governance issues in a succinct, logical, balanced and professional manner.

syllabus_overview: Welcome to Side Venture, a virtual start-up that has reached a critical stage in its growth. institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Social Entrepreneurship Practicum
syllabus_overview: This course is managed by the Centre for Social Impact. COMM3030 Social Entrepreneurship Practicum is a Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course designed to integrate theory with experiential practice and involve authentic and purposeful engagement with partner organisations. It enables undergraduate students to develop professional skills while working in a team on a real social entrepreneurship project. Students work with partners from industry, social enterprises, not-for-profits and foundations to develop and conduct a variety of applied projects in different areas of social entrepreneurship. In doing so, they have the opportunity to develop their professional skills, including critical thinking, communication, teamwork, research, innovation and creativity, entrepreneurship, leadership and many others In each teaching session, projects may be offered from the following fields: Social entrepreneurship and social innovation; Philanthropy; Impact investing; Business and human rights; Corporate social responsibility; Pro bono and volunteering; Measuring social impact; Collective impact; Social finance; and Other related fields.

title: Industry-Research Integrated Learning
syllabus_overview: Industry-Research Integrated Learning empowers students to critically analyse and provide solutions for a small-scale business challenge, whilst being mentored by both academic and industry supervisors. Students will better understand the research process and be able to gauge their learning and development as a researcher, through completing a journal and sharing their findings using written and oral channels. Their regular industry and academic supervisor meetings will provide formative and summative feedback throughout the term to assist the students with building their self-leadership capacity.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Quantitative Business Analytics
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: Quantitative business analytics empower business decision makers to analyse complex business problems, and make better and faster decisions. It is an essential skill for an analyst in all business disciplines to use modern analytical tools and quantitative techniques. This course aims to provide students with quantitative techniques used in business analytics, with a particular focus on practical applications of modelling skills and analytical tools (e.g. using R). The course focuses on how to select appropriate predictive modelling techniques for a stated situation and how to evaluate the suitability of a model, taking into account business context and objectives. The course covers topics including regression techniques and classification methods, model selection and validation methods, linear and non-linear models, decision trees, supervised and unsupervised learning techniques, and ethical, social and regulatory issues associated with quantitative analytics. A particular focus will be placed on communication of technical results to a wide range of business decision making audiences.
learning_outcomes: Apply quantitative analytics tools and techniques to a range of business problems
Identify and explain the ethical, social and regulatory issues associated with the use of data and analytics techniques
Communicate business analytics results and insights effectively to a variety of audiences
Explain the theories and practices of quantitative data analytics in the context of business applications
Critically evaluate quantitative analytics models

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: AI in Action
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: AI in Action introduces you to the practical application of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in solving real-world challenges. This course emphasises hands-on, activity-based learning, allowing you to experiment with AI tools and techniques to understand the potential and applicability of AI across various contexts. For example, applications could include image recognition, natural language processing, and voice technologies, though the specific focus areas may vary. While the expectation is not for students to develop and implement new AI tools and gadgets, you will engage in practical exercises to apply existing AI tools. This will allow you to critically assess current AI capabilities and limitations to address real-world challenges in various industries. Activities will be structured to provide hands-on experience with AI applications, gradually building your confidence in interacting with AI. In addition, you will work on a team project that leverages the AI applications for real-world problem-solving. Designed to be inclusive and accessible to students from all disciplines, the course goes beyond mere AI applications to foster problem-solving while emphasising the ethical and responsible use of AI. By engaging with the interdisciplinary use of AI tools, you will not only gain insight into AI’s transformative role in industries such as business, design, media, and the arts but also develop timeless skills, such as broader understanding of AI fundamentals, critical thinking, and problem-solving. While you will engage with evolving AI technologies, the emphasis is on understanding fundamental AI concepts, evaluating AI outputs, and applying AI in real-world scenarios. More importantly, you will have the opportunity to apply the Responsible AI principles explored in the course to real-world scenarios. By fostering strategic and ethical AI thinking, the course will equips equip you with long-term skills that remain valuable despite technological advancements. While the use of AI tools may be introduced in each faculty’s individual courses, this course provides a structured, interdisciplinary environment where you actively experiment with AI application tools, apply them across various industries, critically evaluate their effectiveness and risks, and design and implement mitigation plans to alleviate them. This will allow you to gain deeper expertise and confidence in integrating AI into your career, complementing what you learn in other courses. No coding skills required to undertake the course.
learning_outcomes: Work effectively in teams to design, build, and present AI-based projects, demonstrating collaboration and innovation.
Identify and apply appropriate AI tools and techniques to address real-world challenges in domains, such as business, design, media, or the arts.
Apply foundational AI techniques to solve practical problems in areas such as data analysis, automation, or decision-making.
Analyse and reflect on the ethical and societal implications of AI applications.
Demonstrate the ability to use AI tools as both productivity and creativity enhancers in real-world scenarios to foster innovation and influence others to achieve positive societal outcomes.
Use AI to communicate the process and outcomes of AI-driven projects effectively using multiple forms of communication and channels.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2604

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: AI in Business and Society Capstone
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: With AI rapidly transforming industries worldwide, it is increasingly important for you to be familiar with AI and demonstrate the ability to confidently leverage and apply it as you prepare for the future workforce. This AI-focused capstone course provides you with a valuable opportunity to integrate the theoretical knowledge and diverse skills you have acquired across your studies, applying them to complex, interdisciplinary projects that mirror the grand real-world AI-driven challenges professionals face today. The course is structured around a major team-based capstone project, where you will collaborate over an extended period to research and design AI-driven applications. Building on the foundations established in previous courses within the AI major, such as Interaction Design, AI Fundamentals, and Machine Learning, this course empowers you to create innovative AI solutions, while encouraging you to critique and reflect on their societal impact. Throughout the course, you will further develop essential skills such as problem-solving, collaboration, and innovation, while gaining hands-on experience with the latest AI tools and technologies in a project-based environment. You will also receive training in Agile methodologies, enabling you to effectively structure, manage, and execute your capstone projects using frameworks that closely resemble how AI projects are implemented in industry. Applying Agile principles to AI projects will provide you with valuable experience in teamwork, adaptability, and iterative problem-solving, mirroring the collaborative skills essential for real-world AI initiatives. This capstone course will enhance your employability by equipping you with cutting-edge skills and interdisciplinary knowledge relevant to the AI-driven world. It will enable you to combine creativity, technical fluency, and agile methodology to produce AI solutions with lasting societal impact, preparing you to contribute meaningfully to an AI-powered future.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and discuss the legal requirements, ethical considerations and responsibilities associated with AI.
Evaluate and apply agile project management methodologies to foster effective collaboration and manage cross-functional teams.
Evaluate the potential benefits and risks associated with the use of AI in individuals, organisations, and society
Demonstrate reflective learning, opportunity appreciation for personal growth and life-long learning.
Synthesise and apply disciplinary knowledge to identify, analyse and frame complex, open-ended challenges through open ended exploration.
Collaborate with AI and human to improve productivity and creativity in real-world scenarios.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completion of 108 UOC at UNSW AND LAWS3999 AND [COMP3411 OR DDES2900 OR COMM3614 OR INFS3822 OR MATH3856]

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Sustainability and Social Impact Capstone Project
syllabus_overview: You will have the opportunity to apply knowledge and skills gained through your business degree program to a complex societal challenge in this interdisciplinary project-based course. Project teams explore innovative responses to co-create sustainable value that will contribute to repairing, restoring and regenerating economic, environmental and social systems. Projects involving evidence gathering and analysis are developed in consultation with research, industry and community stakeholders. You will have the opportunity to demonstrate versatile communication, agile and inclusive team-work, independent critical thinking, active problem-solving and leadership. It is strongly recommended that students only complete this course within their final 2 terms of study.
learning_outcomes: Access, manage and use the appropriate digital resources and tools to deliver your recommendations or conclusions
Critically reflect on your professional skills and behaviours, including identified gaps, and how you will adapt to a changing business environment
Examine the influences of the global business environment on key sustainability considerations in relation to the contemporary societal issue
Identify, apply and adapt business skills and knowledge acquired from across your program to critically analyse a contemporary societal challenge
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completed a minimum of 108 UOC (including First Year core).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Coding for Business
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Coding for Business is an introductory course tailored for beginners, offering a foundational understanding of coding using Python. This foundational course equips you with essential skills for future business decision-making. In this course, you will gain skills in using key programming software to solve real-world problems, collaborate with your peers in seeking these solutions, and confidently communicate their solutions to a professional audience.
learning_outcomes: Use analytical, creative, and collaborative approaches to solve real-world problems effectively.
Effectively document, communicate, and manage collaborative programming projects and findings.
Design and implement robust Python solutions to generate data insights from real-world data.
Demonstrate proficiency in Python fundamentals and key concepts.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: myBCom Graduation Portfolio
syllabus_overview: COMM3999 is the final part of a degree-spanning professional development exercise (myBCom). It enables students to synthesise their academic learning, co-curricular experiences, and professional achievements from across the Bachelor of Commerce into a final professional portfolio. Through this course, students consolidate their development across the Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs) and demonstrate their readiness for ethical, responsible, and impactful professional practice in a global business environment. Evidence of these PLOs includes demonstrated capability in problem solving, communication, teamwork, responsible business practice, global and cultural competence, and leadership, which align directly with the UNSW Graduate Attributes. The portfolio assessments are scaffolded throughout the myBCom series, with ongoing guidance and structured reflection provided from first year through to this capstone experience. This approach supports students in achieving their personal, professional, and academic goals, and in articulating a coherent and confident professional identity as they transition from university to the workplace.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate evidence-based business communication skills to meaningfully reflect on future career planning and life-long learning.
Collect, select, and curate evidence of learning and skill development, to showcase personal achievements through the Program Learning Outcomes and UNSW graduate attributes.
Curate an integrative portfolio to demonstrate achievements of PLOs and UNSW graduate attributes to a professional audience, effectively communicating orally, in writing, and through digital media.
Demonstrate global and cultural awareness and responsible business practice including an awareness of cultures in the region and issues related to cross-cultural communication.
Engage in collaborative problem solving, and teamwork both face-to-face and in online environments.
Effectively communicate ideas, the ethical dimensions of written, digital and oral communication to a range of audiences including business leaders.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completed myBCom First Year Portfolio (COMM1999) and in their final year of a single or double Commerce degree (ie. completed at least 72 UOC of Business courses including DPBS equivalent courses).

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Quantitative Methods for Business
syllabus_overview: Modern business decisions rely on data-driven insights and analytical precision. This course builds the mathematical and statistical toolkit needed to interpret data, model complex problems, and make informed, evidence-based decisions—skills that are indispensable in today’s data-centric economy. Students will learn to address economic and business problems using analytical and computational methods. The first half of the course develops core techniques in algebra, calculus, financial mathematics, and optimization. The second half introduces probability, descriptive statistics, and inferential methods such as hypothesis testing and linear regression. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply quantitative reasoning to analyse complex business problems, interpret data effectively, and communicate insights with clarity and precision.
learning_outcomes: Identify ethical issues in business practice and statistical reporting.
Engage in independent and reflective learning to analyse business data and problems using critical thinking.
Work collaboratively to discuss and solve problems.
Solve problems using a variety of mathematical and statistical techniques and produce an associated business report.
Use a calculator and a spreadsheet program (Microsoft Excel) effectively to perform calculations.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Literacy for Business
syllabus_overview: In an era defined by data, the ability to extract insights from information is fundamental to effective leadership, policy development, and business strategy. This course develops foundational skills in data analysis and interpretation to support sound, evidence-based decision-making in business and broader societal contexts. It introduces core concepts in descriptive and inferential statistics, including data visualisation, regression analysis, and causal reasoning, while also developing practical skills in using Microsoft Excel to analyse real-world data and generate impactful insights. Emphasising critical thinking, clear communication, and ethical data use, it prepares students to navigate data-informed decision-making in professional contexts. By the end of the course, you will have a strong foundation in descriptive and inferential statistics, causal analysis, and quantitative methods sought by employers in both the public and private sectors.
learning_outcomes: Apply foundational analytical tools to transform, analyse, and predict with data.
Identify and evaluate different types of data and their relevance for decision making.
Synthesise insights from diverse data sources to evaluate solutions to complex real- life scenarios and deliver recommendations to stakeholders.
Recognise and evaluate ethical and governance issues in data collection, storage, and use.
Synthesise ideas through succinct and clear work that communicates ideas in a logical, professional manner.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Strategy, Marketing and Management
syllabus_overview: This course is designed as a capstone core course in the Master of Commerce program. The course addresses perspectives from core and disciplinary courses in the MCom. It aims to provide students with broad business competencies and skills in developing strategic objectives for creating, maintaining, developing and capturing value for organisations and enhancing competitive advantage. It draws on knowledge and skills from completed courses in their study plans in addressing the Program Learning Goals of the Master of Commerce degree. The course seeks to: a) integrate knowledge and skills in a framework for conceptualising, developing and implementing corporate and business strategy drawing on key concepts in marketing and organisational capabilities; b) synthesise knowledge from alternative perspectives and generate critical thinking and problem-solving skills in developing and implementing strategy; and c) engender critical reflection on the practice of business and management in working with people, and ethical decision-making; d) provide opportunities for considering global business career. Students will have opportunities of applying the above in case-studies and projects with course participants.
learning_outcomes: Ascertain and apply the ethical elements of business decisions;

Discover how to enhance sustainable strategic success by integrating knowledge on managing people, marketing, organisational strategy, innovation, data analytics, international business, and business ethics;

Demonstrate a high level of written and oral communication about the subjects of managing people, marketing, organisational strategy, innovation, data analytics, international business, and business ethics;
Identify and assess business problems from varying social and cultural perspectives;
Enhance teamwork skills through real-world cases analyses;
Solve classic business problems related to managing people, marketing, organisational strategy, innovation, data analytics, international business, and business ethics;
Develop the capacity to take initiative and innovate.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: MGMT5050 AND (enrolment in program 8404 or 8417 or 8371) AND completion of 42 units of credit.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Enterprise Skills
syllabus_overview: This course offers students the opportunity to experience the Australian start-up community first-hand. COMM5008 Enterprise Skills will help develop their professional skills, enhance employability, and get students ready to successfully take on the global workplace. Students work as part of a cross-disciplinary consulting team on a real business challenge for an industry partner. Student teams will be based in-company (minimum 1 day per week, 70-100 hours during the term) as part of the course, where they will apply their academic knowledge to the business challenge. Students will be supported throughout by a company mentor, the course lecturer, and face-to-face workshops. For enquiries please contact the Career Accelerator team.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively within a team and with a mentor, giving and receiving feedback and contributing to team outcomes
Present business recommendations as a consulting team to industry in the form of a verbal pitch and written report
Critically reflect on team process and professional skills and identify own strengths, capabilities and growth areas
Research and analyses a real-world business problem as directed by a host company and develop recommendations
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completion of 42 UOC of business courses and completion of Career Accelerator Essentials module.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Global Business Practicum
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to enable postgraduate students to gain international understanding, exposure and workplace skills through studying and working in a specified location outside Australia. Examples of locations include Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Hong Kong, China, India and South Korea. Structure: Prior to departure students undertake preparatory workshops in skills development and cultural context for the country they will be visiting. These workshops include topics such as professionalism; reporting and other professional writing and communication skills; expectations during the practicum; cultural understanding; and “getting to know” other team members. While in the designated country, students will work in a local organisation for a minimum of 2 weeks full-time (70-80 hrs). Acting as consultants to the client organisation, teams of 4-5 students will work on a business issue provided by the client organisation. Students will be supported by an academic and will attend master classes, provided by local leaders of business and government organisations, to understand the conduct of business in this local context. After returning to Australia, students will attend a debrief session, and complete the major assessment. Further details can be found on the Career Accelerator website.
learning_outcomes: Identify, analyse and apply global business knowledge and practices to a real-world business issue
Develop recommendations with a variety of stakeholders to address the business issue within an appropriate cultural context
Participate collaboratively and responsibly in a team, and reflect on your own teamwork, and the team’s processes and ability to achieve outcomes
Develop the capacity for self-leadership and self-directed learning from reflection on working in a business, working in another country, cultural understanding and yourself
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completion of 42 UOC, Good Academic standing and Completion of Career Accelerator Essentials module

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Experience Program
syllabus_overview: Develop and refine your professional skills, gain practical work experience, and apply your academic knowledge in a real working environment. This course will allow you to gain valuable work experience, explore a career path, and network with professionals in your chosen field. You will be required to combine your work practice with academic workshops and assignments throughout. Workshops are delivered online for this course. Enrolment in the course is restricted and only Business School postgraduate students that meet the eligibility criteria will be approved and admitted. This course is an elective or alternative capstone practicum (approval required). For enquiries please contact Career Accelerator
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on your personal and professional development and outline how you will improve or change your practice in the future
Analyse your organisation’s purpose and culture and how it impacts responsible business practices
Utilise appropriate professional digital tools to communicate respectfully in a global environment
Effectively communicate your ideas and knowledge to influence business outcomes
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completion of at least 24 UoC and Career Accelerator Essentials module. Students must also be in good academic standing.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Social Entrepreneurship Practicum
syllabus_overview: This course is managed by the Centre for Social Impact. COMM5030 investigates in real time how businesses can create social and environmental impact while generating economic value. In COMM5030 Social Entrepreneurship Practicum, you will work with a social enterprise or a mission driven organisation to tackle a real-world problem. Whether it’s improving business operation practices, understanding competition and consumers, measuring impact, securing investment, or creating opportunities for marginalized communities or environmental protection, you’ll help design solutions that matter. This is a hands-on class working with a real social enterprise or a social mission driven organisation, exploring the challenges of social entrepreneurship. This course is designed to provide students with the opportunity to apply their cumulative learning and build practical business and leadership capabilities within a social entrepreneurship context. The course is taught through student engagement with a social entrepreneurship project, supported by both online modules and face-to-face workshops. Each practicum experience will be different depending on the particular client project on which each student will work. Assessment tasks are designed to provide a consulting style framework to both create value for the social entrepreneurship project, and to enable students to demonstrate their ability to apply and synthesise social entrepreneurship concepts. The course is the capstone course for the Master of Commerce Global Sustainability and Social Impact specialisation. It is also an alternative capstone practicum course for other MCom and MCom (Ext) specialisations. This course may also be taken as a free elective in other Master of Commerce and Master of Commerce (Ext) specialisations and as an elective in the Master of Professional Accounting (Ext) program. Please refer to the specialisation Handbook entries. The course is offered in Terms 1, 2 and 3. For enquiries please contact CSI Students at: csistudents@unsw.edu.au.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the principles and practices of social entrepreneurship within diverse social, cultural, environmental, and economic contexts.
Demonstrate clear, concise, professional and persuasive communication to various stakeholders.
Evaluate and design social business enterprise models that can effectively and sustainably deliver on social and/or environmental and economic goals.
Reflect on learning experiences in the course, analysing how these contribute to personal and professional development.

Apply social entrepreneurship approaches and integrate the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to develop and assess innovative solutions that create sustainable and meaningful social and environmental impact.
Collaborate effectively and responsibly in a team to deliver project outcomes and achieve shared goals.
prerequisites: Completion of 42 UOC prior to undertaking this course as it is recommended that students do not undertake this course in their first term.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystems
syllabus_overview: Entrepreneurship in the 21st century is rapidly evolving. Disruptive changes in technology, manufacturing, supply chains, talent, communication, and capital markets have led to the rise of global startup ecosystems. Governments, corporates and universities are recognising the potential for the next wave of economic growth to emerge from disruptive startup enterprises, and are working together to nurture them via grants, tax incentives, direct funding, subsidised space, education, competitions, purchasing policies, mentoring and partnerships. This course provides exposure to the fundamentals of global entrepreneurship ecosystems and the practical aspects of identifying, evaluating, and moving business ideas forward in them. The course inspires students to critically think about how entrepreneurs identify opportunities, understand customer needs, harness resources, create innovative business models, attract capital and solve real-world challenges. The course addresses key contemporary topics in entrepreneurship ecosystems and their application in any field—from business and design to healthcare and product development. The course aims to provide foundational knowledge of entrepreneurship ecosystems, lean startup and design thinking methodologies applied in startups. Students will explore the rise of Sydney as one of the world’s emerging entrepreneurial cities through experiential learning, employing the latest in VR and AR technologies. This course provides an initial overview of entrepreneurship ecosystems that can be built on with courses from the Innovation and Entrepreneurship specialisation including MGMT5611 Entrepreneurship and New Venture Management. This course also provides a pathway into the UNSW Founders Program. For more information visit: https://founders.unsw.edu.au
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on your own practise as an emerging entrepreneur.
Adopt a global perspective when assessing startup ecosystems
Describe the interdependencies, opportunities and challenges of startups within ecosystems.
Apply research skills to the analysis of emerging startups/social enterprise opportunities
prerequisites: Completion of 42 UOC

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Future of Work Project
syllabus_overview: What skills will you need for your career in ten years? How can businesses become sustainable for the future? COMM5044 Future of Work Project is a project-based practicum aimed at developing and applying your business and consulting knowledge while learning to tackle challenges facing a future workforce. In small cross-disciplinary teams (maximum 5 students) you will work with an industry host to investigate a real-life business challenge relating to their future sustainability, while applying your teamwork, creativity and cross-cultural communication skills. You will then present your findings and recommendations to a group of industry professionals. Throughout the course you will also reflect on key future work issues such as AI and sustainability, and how they relate to yourself and your project. You will be supported by an industry mentor and your lecturer. Each practicum experience will be different depending on the organisations we partner with. For enquiries please contact the Career Accelerator team.
learning_outcomes: Identify challenges to economic, social, and environmental sustainability within future global work environments
Reflect and critically evaluate their current and future professional goals in the context of Future of Work
Making viable business recommendations as a consulting team on a Future of Work challege posed by industry partner
Demonstrate thought leadership and initiative in a team environment
Analyse the skills and capabilities needed by a future workforce in a global context
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completion of 42 UOC of business courses and completion of Career Accelerator Essentials module.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business for Social Impact
syllabus_overview: COMM5201 Business for Social Impact is an experiential postgraduate course that examines how enterprise-based models can be designed and implemented to address complex social and environmental challenges. The course develops students’ capacity to apply analytical frameworks to the design of financially sustainable and socially impactful enterprise models. Students critically assess systemic drivers of social problems, analyse stakeholder environments, evaluate market and institutional gaps, and construct enterprise responses grounded in commercial logic and impact measurement principles. The course progresses through a structured sequence beginning with rigorous problem analysis and root cause identification, advancing to enterprise model development and financial sustainability design, and culminating in the articulation of a coherent Theory of Change and impact evaluation framework. COMM5201 is a core course in the Master of Commerce and Master of Commerce (Extension) Global Sustainability and Social Impact specialisation but may also be taken as an additional General Elective in the MComm.
learning_outcomes: Present ideas in a succinct, clear and professional manner.
Identify, research, analyse, evaluate and propose evidence-based social enterprise solutions to a specified social issue.
Engage appropriately with different socio-economic stakeholders.
Work effectively and collaboratively as part of a team.
Identify and assess ethical, environmental and sustainability considerations as they apply to social enterprises.
Develop written work that is logically and professionally presented.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Social and Environmental Sustainability
syllabus_overview: Why do poverty, hunger, and conflict still persist—despite decades of global effort? And how is it that, even with all warnings from scientists, we’re pushing the planet beyond its limits, facing crises like climate change and mass biodiversity loss? What if these challenges aren’t isolated, but deeply interconnected? What if the way we do business could be part of the solution? This course invites you on a journey to explore the complex relationships between social, environmental, and economic issues—and to examine the root causes driving today’s most urgent global problems. Using a systems thinking approach, you’ll learn to analyse sustainability challenges, identify key leverage points for change, and assess the real-world impacts of corporate strategies and governance practices. You’ll also develop practical skills in collaboration, communication, and self-leadership—equipping you to drive meaningful, positive change. If you've ever wondered whether it’s still possible to make a meaningful difference—this course is for you.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the interconnections between economic, social, political, and ecological systems and their implications for sustainability.
Communicate effectively and persuasively to inspire and influence others toward positive social and environmental change.
Reflect critically on internal and external factors—including values, philosophy, mindsets and contextual pressures—that shape ethical and sustainable decision-making.
Collaborate effectively with peers from diverse cultural and disciplinary backgrounds to achieve shared goals.
Critically evaluate corporate sustainability reporting and governance practices, understanding strategic role and position in complex systems.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Social and Environmental Outcomes Measurement
syllabus_overview: Across government, business, and the not-for-profit sector there is a growing demand for organisations to measure their social and environmental outcomes and impact while social enterprises in particular rely on the ability to evaluate and communicate their social and financial impact for investment and scalability. Yet measuring outcomes and impact is not a straightforward process. What and how to measure, how to communicate outcomes and impact effectively, and how to manage the process of evaluation within an organisation are just some of the associated challenges. Beginning with an examination of ‘why measure’, this course will then turn to a practical application of ‘what and how to measure outcomes and impact’, how to communicate social and environmental measurement outcomes and impact to key stakeholders, and conclude with an assessment of how an outcomes and impact framework might facilitate organisations to deliver on their mission, support organisational learning, and provide capacity for organisational change and sustainability.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse ethical and political considerations of impact assessment and approaches to outcomes measurement

Identify and describe why, when and how organisations assess their social and environmental outcomes and impact (the theory, principles and frameworks of social and environmental outcomes measurement).
Differentiate between inputs, activities, outputs and outcomes, and develop SMART indicators to develop the program logic of a given program or initiative in an applied setting
Identify, describe and critically evaluate key methodologies for measuring social and environmental impact and their use in organisational change and sustainability

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Investing for Local and Global Impact
syllabus_overview: Investing with the specific aim of achieving positive social and/or environmental impact has become increasingly recognised as holding enormous potential for unlocking private capital, enabling new solutions to pressing social and environmental challenges, and helping to shape a new landscape that is blurring the traditional lines between investment and philanthropy. Investments can be made by business and corporations, governments and individual investors (small and large) while social purpose organisations are developing investment strategies to attract investors to finance the development of social innovation and to trial environmentally friendly production processes and delivery. Impact investment has been particularly popular within developing and emerging markets across the globe. The aim of this course is to examine the history, concepts and current practices in investing for local and global impact while providing the opportunity to develop practical skills in including the development and application of social impact investment strategies from an investor, investee and policy development perspective. COMM5204 Investing for Local and Global Impact is a general elective in the Finance specialisation and an elective in the Global Sustainability and Social Enterprise specialisation in the Master of Commerce and Master of Commerce (Extension) programs.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a strong understanding of the challenges, constraints, and opportunities provided by investing for social and environmental impact.
Work effectively to conduct analyses of contemporary examples of social impact.
Explain the trends, drivers, and challenges shaping the dynamics of the current impact investment market in Australia and globally
Demonstrate a strong understanding of the emergence of investing for local and global impact and the role it plays within the capital spectrum.
Demonstrate a strong understanding of the characteristics and application of the key instruments of impact investment.

Demonstrate research, communication, and team work skills necessary to engage in informed discussions on the application of impact investment across a range of organisations and social and environmental areas.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Leading Change for Sustainability
syllabus_overview: Leading Change for Sustainability is a course designed for future leaders who are passionate about creating positive social and environmental change. Your ideas and passion for sustainability and resilience are just the first step. You need skills in leadership, creativity, systems thinking, communication and models for cultural change so that you can influence key decision-makers, build networks and make your idea a reality. You need an awareness of change processes and an understanding of ethics and human rights to lead sustainable change, locally and globally. How do you support cultural change towards a sustainable future for all organisational types? How do you pursue social and environmental goals from within a multinational company or a start up? Sustainability has become a key driver in many organisations, from large foundations to social enterprises, not-for-profits working with government to provide services, and small to large businesses. This course explores how to create and implement sustainability strategies for different organisational types. We take a broad view of sustainability based on the Sustainable Development Goals, acknowledging the human, social, economic and environmental elements of positive cultural change.
learning_outcomes: Become familiar with transformation strategies in the context of sustainability initiatives in business.
Recognise and apply the features of sustainable leadership practice in organisational sustainability initiatives (including ethical and human rights concerns).
Reflect upon skills in building teams and networks in order to align businesses with sustainability objectives.
Communicate written and oral ideas in a clear and succinct manner.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Interdisciplinary Applications of Analytics Techniques
syllabus_overview: This course provides you with a comprehensive understanding of complex business interdisciplinary approaches to problem solving with a focus on the practical application of data analytics. You will sharpen your ability to select the most effective methods for diverse business situations, while also learning to critically assess the performance and appropriateness of chosen models in alignment with organisational aspirations. An integral part of the course is a hands-on project that mirrors real-world, industry-oriented scenarios. This approach ensures that students' learning extends beyond theoretical concepts and is effectively applied across various business domains addressing important areas of such as ethics and sustainability in business practice.
learning_outcomes: Use computer software to estimate and apply various statistical learning models for business applications.
Collaboratively effectively to communicate business analytics results and insights to a variety of audiences.
Explain, describe and summarise the key aspects of the theory and practice of data analytics in the context of business applications.
Use effective presentation, discussion and report writing skills for explaining data analytics concepts used in business applications.
Judge the performance, advantages and shortcomings of models used for predictive analytics in practice.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completion of 42 UOC AND One of (COMM5000 OR COMM5501 OR COMM5007)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Visualisation and Communication
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: How can data help you tell a story? How can you use data storytelling to then tackle some of the big challenges we are facing around the world? Data visualisation and communication are critical skills in many professions. The creation of targeted, easily digestible visuals allows us to make sense of complex information in an accessible and easily understandable way. The ability to employ visuals will enhance almost any presentation to better engage our audience, make our messages more memorable, and facilitate more effective decision-making. In this course, we will give you the tools to create your own data story addressing a pressing and current global challenge as identified by the UN SDGs. You will learn how to design your story for your chosen audience, how to criticise misrepresentations of data (especially the intentional ones), and drive action to address your chosen challenge. So, how will you leave the world a better place?
learning_outcomes: Produce appropriate high quality data visualisations using a variety of software packages and techniques
Communicate data insights effectively to a variety of audiences
Apply data storytelling techniques to a range of business and societal problems
Critically evaluate and interpret data graphics

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Systems Thinking and Business Dynamics
syllabus_overview: This course introduces leading edge systems thinking mapping and modelling tools to enhance your ability to diagnose and solve complex business and social problems. You will learn a flexible and powerful approach to structuring managerial problems and visualising the interconnectedness of business, social and environmental systems. You will develop skills to conceptualise and build simulation models of an enterprise, enabling you to explore the dynamic consequences of different strategy/policy decisions and identify key leverage points in the system. For example, you will build and use simple simulation models to examine the growth dynamics of businesses such as Airbnb, Uber, What’sApp, and Tesla. You will explore a broad application of business and public policy issues including firm growth and stagnation, competitive strategy, capability development and human resource policies, environmental sustainability, and the boom and bust dynamics of start-up businesses. In addition, you will examine cases of organisations that have successfully applied systems thinking and business dynamics.
learning_outcomes: Conceptualise and map complex business or societal problems
Recognise and apply the key elements of systems thinking
Test and build confidence in systems models
Develop and simulate business dynamics models

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Social Impact
syllabus_overview: COMM5701 Social Impact is the core course in the Graduate Certificate in Social Impact and the MBAX (Social Impact) programs. It is highly recommended that students take COMM5701 either as their first Social Impact course (or one of the courses in their first study session that includes Social Impact courses). The course is an introduction to Social Impact covering fundamental concepts and key developments in what has become a complex social purpose eco-system. The course introduces an understanding of changes across what was formerly seen as a distinct social sector to examine the cross-sectoral social purpose developments that includes traditional organisational structures of Charities and Not For-Profits, Business and Government, and new and emerging ‘hybrid’ structures and programs, including social enterprises. Key concepts include: systems thinking and mapping, measuring impact, funding and investing in impact, organisational challenges including scaling, strategy, hybridity, and leadership for social impact. The course explores how intractable social, economic, and environmental problems embedded in society are being addressed through social innovation in business entrepreneurship, enterprises and cross-sector collaboration.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical analysis and systems thinking to an understanding of the complex and changing social purpose eco-system
Explain and describe the trends and drivers re-shaping the dynamics of the social economy and its impact on complex, social issues
Develop critical thinking, research and communication skills for social impact work
Identify new organisational forms, business models and cross-sector collaborations for social innovation and impact
Analyse and respond to global trends and organisations that effect social change, social innovation and impact
Demonstrate a strong understanding of key foundational concepts within the social impact field

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Social Impact Investment
syllabus_overview: This course is managed by the Centre for Social Impact. The landscape of social finance and impact investment has undergone a transformation – driven by global economic realignment, the privatisation of community and government services, shifting patterns of wealth distribution and intergenerational wealth transfer, and the rising expectations of corporate citizenship and philanthropy. These forces have accelerated the growth of social impact investment: a field in which commercial enterprise, blended finance, and philanthropic capital are increasingly deployed together to address complex social and environmental challenges. COMM5703 Social Impact Investment develops critical understanding of the history, core concepts, and current issues shaping philanthropy, fundraising, and social impact investment – both in Australia and globally. Students will examine the full capital spectrum, from philanthropic giving to impact bonds and ESG-aligned investment vehicles, exploring how these instruments are structured, deployed, and evaluated across diverse economic regulatory, and cultural contexts. Ethical and philosophical perspectives, impact measurement, and the legal dimensions of social investment programs are also examined, equipping students to engage as informed and strategic practitioners in this field.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply key instruments of social impact investment
Identify and critically evaluate the roles and interrelationships of diverse players in the social impact investment ecosystem
Explain the trends, drivers and challenges shaping the dynamics of the social impact investment market in Australia and globally
Discuss the drivers of the emergence of social impact investment and the role it plays within the capital spectrum

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Demonstrating Social Impact
syllabus_overview: Demonstrating Social Impact is an elective subject for the Graduate Certificate in Social Impact and M Com, or AGSM MBAx programs. It provides an overview and introduction to evaluation and social impact assessment, the underpinning principles of evaluation and social impact assessment. The course will provide the knowledge and tools necessary to understand and apply social impact frameworks and methodologies at a project and organisational level.
learning_outcomes: Describe and critically assess the concept of Social Impact and Social Impact measurement.
Collaborate in teams to develop skills in communication, research, and reporting social impact findings to diverse stakeholders.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Design for Social Innovation
syllabus_overview: Social innovation can be developed in almost any context. It is often a response to an identified problem, issue or opportunity. One of the most challenging aspects of developing and delivering social innovation is identifying the essence of what needs to be addressed, as the problems can be wicked in nature. Design thinking, methods and practices offer a broad set of tools that facilitate a multi-disciplinary to transdisciplinary approach to solving problems and innovating, taking a whole systems (rather than a silo) approach to offer different perspectives to traditional business tools and problem solving. Design for Social Innovation offers participants the opportunity to learn and apply design tools and methods to real projects. COMM5706 Design for Social Innovation is an elective subject for the Graduate Certificate in Social Impact and other post-experience programs. It provides an overview and introduction to the role and application of design methods in social innovation and social enterprise. This course will provide the knowledge and tools necessary to understand and apply design thinking principles at a project or organisational level.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Corporate Responsibility and Accountability
syllabus_overview: Corporate Responsibility and Accountability is a core course for the Global Sustainability and Social Impact specialisation in the Master of Commerce, and an elective for those undertaking the Graduate Certificate in Social Impact, Graduate Diploma in Social Impact or MBA Programs. It examines how business manages its social, environmental and economic impact on society. The course first reviews the historical evolution and development of the concept of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Corporate Citizenship (CC) and why it is now a key part of managing the business enterprise. Second, the course examines what acting responsibly means for corporations in terms of the market, community, environment, workplace and government. Issues covered include business and human rights, business-community partnerships, corporate philanthropy, the human resource management implications of CSR, business and the environment and businesses' relationship with government. Third, the course examines how business accounts for its behaviour and impact in society through sustainability reporting and the role of external assurance and outlines debates on the appropriate role of government policy in either regulating and/or enabling responsible corporate behaviour.

Describe the key drivers behind its adoption by business

Apply Corporate Responsibility theories and frameworks to critically evaluate corporate responsibility performance;
Describe and critically evaluate the concepts of Corporate Responsibility and Accountability, and future trends in the role of the corporation in society

The course provides students with an introduction to the challenges and opportunities of leading organisations with the purpose of improving social outcomes. The course will examine the following areas: current challenges in achieving social benefit; leadership in the social economy; challenges and opportunities of leadership during a time of inflexion; a model of leadership centred on identifying adaptive challenges for leaders; intervention of leaders and practices for more effective and positive social outcomes; new forms of organising designed to address breakdowns in the social economy; governance systems and demands; diagnosis of leadership challenges.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing Just Transitions
syllabus_overview: Managing Just Transitions introduces students to the emerging framework of Just Transitions , to examine how leaders can manage complex socio-ecological transitions in the face of systemic challenges such as climate change, economic inequality, and unsustainable development. It focuses on the governance of change across interconnected systems, where decisions in one domain can create significant implications for markets, organisations, communities, and the environment. A central question is: how can systemic transitions be governed effectively and equitably, while balancing competing interests, risks, and opportunities? This course adopts a systems-level perspective that investigates decisions of justice, fairness, and inclusion in navigating structural changes such as decarbonisation, digitalisation, artificial intelligence, and automation. Students will critically examine how businesses, investors, governments, and civil society can work together to reimagine economic futures that are both environmentally sustainable and socially inclusive . Through interdisciplinary theories and real-world case studies, students will explore Just Transitions across five key conceptual domains: System Thinking – A system value domain sits at the core of this course, recognising that just transition occur within interconnected systems shaped by power, institutions, stakeholder relationships and competing ideas of justice. Civic Wealth Creation – Examining how community-driven entrepreneurship, participation, and coalition-building generate economic, social, and communal value. Place-Based Development and Investment – Investigating financial models that acquire, absorb, and deploy capital equitably across different communities and geographies. Indigenous Knowledge and Systems – Exploring the Indigenous business sector and the role of cultural values in fostering sustainable, community-led development. Ethical Infrastructure and Intergenerational Equity – Engaging with long-term governance frameworks that consider who benefits from change, who bears the costs, and how future generations are impacted. Designed for future leaders, strategists, and change agents, this course equips students with the critical tools to design, assess, and lead transitions that align business innovation with societal and environmental resilience.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the range of theoretical and conceptual frameworks that inform Just Transition strategies across economic, social, and environmental domains.
Demonstrate advanced research, analytical, and communication skills relevant to professional and academic work in the field of Just Transitions.

Analyse emerging trends, drivers, and governance challenges shaping Just Transitions at local, national, and global levels.
Identify and apply the core design elements, stakeholder considerations, and measurement approaches required to develop effective Just Transition initiatives.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Nomad
syllabus_overview: Situated in a real-world international setting, students will collaborate in interdisciplinary and intercultural teams to collectively develop innovative ideas to address the pressing challenges presented by the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, adopted by all United Nations Member States in 2015, provides a shared blueprint for peace and prosperity for people and the planet, now and into the future. At its heart are the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which are an urgent call for action by all countries - developed and developing - in a global partnership. The goals recognise that ending poverty must go hand-in-hand with strategies that build economic development. Students will apply different problem-solving frameworks to complex sustainability problems and develop viable, inclusive and equitable solution options that promote sustainable development and economic security at the local level and further afield.

school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course will enable students to acquire fundamental knowledge, skills, and experience necessary to conduct a qualitative research study. It aims to develop understanding of the nature of qualitative research, major philosophical foundations underpinning qualitative research and more specifically the interpretivist research perspective. The course focuses on fundamental issues critical for qualitative inquiry, such as philosophical foundations, theory building, the design and conduct of qualitative studies (of different types), methods of qualitative data collection and analysis, researcher role and relationships with subjects researched, the quality of qualitative research, and presentation of findings and writing a research proposal and a thesis. As such, the course will introduce qualitative research methods most often applied in the Management, Accounting and Information Systems disciplines. it will also develop fundamental research skills and prepare students for undertaking an independent research study.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Foundations of Cyber Security
school: School of Computer Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with an introduction to the rapidly growing field of cyber security. It is suitable for anyone who wishes to understand more about this fascinating and rapidly emerging global challenge. The course provides an overview of the main aspects of contemporary cyber security, including cyber crime, cyber criminals, cyber war, scams, exploitation, human errors and mistakes, vulnerabilities, responding to emergencies, sensible risk assessment and risk management. We consider the question: We can build a bridge that doesn't fall down; why can't we yet build a system that can't be hacked? We consider what we can learn from established disciplines, including engineering, safety science, investment, and military intelligence, that can help us establish the new discipline of cyber security. This course introduces an engineering-style approach to how we can design, manage, and improve secure systems. However students do not have to be engineers to take this course, indeed the interactive parts of the course work best when we have a multi-disciplinary, diverse range of students. As well as learning core cyber security terminology and concepts (such as introductory cryptography, the main classes of computer vulnerabilities that hackers exploit, and how to analyse risk), students also work in diverse teams to analyse and respond to a range of case studies drawn from historical security and security related scenarios (such as incident response to emergencies, system design, root cause failure analysis).
learning_outcomes: Apply an engineering approach to the design and operation of solutions to security problems and in the analysis and control of security risks.
Design, analyse and critique cryptographic solutions to security problems using cryptographic elements and concepts of attacker work.

syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to how computer systems are structured in terms of basic electronic components, how they are used to implement procedural programs, and how they are structured as a collection of software layers. It introduces students to low-level software layers such as operating systems, and introduces concurrency concepts. The goal is to give students a solid understanding of what happens when high-level programs are executed, as a basis for further study in important areas of computing such as computer architecture, operating systems.
learning_outcomes: Design, implement, and analyse small programs at the assembly/machine level.
Describe the components comprising, and the services offered by, an operating system.
Explain how the major components of a CPU work together, including how data and instructions are represented in a computer.
Implement simple programs involving communication and concurrency.

Describe the relationship between a high-level procedural language (C) and assembly (machine language) which implements it, including how a compiled program is executed in a classical von Neumann machine.
Describe the architectural layers (fundamental parts) of a modern computer system from hardware device (chip) levels upwards.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Programming Fundamentals
school: School of Computer Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview: From recent innovations in AI like self-driving cars to humanoid robotics navigating complex environments, leapfrogs in battery technology to sequencing the human genome - the world is benefiting and evolving thanks to computer systems. At the core of all these systems are computers executing instructions to solve exciting problems. In this course, you will learn the fundamentals of how we instruct computers to solve problems. You will explore the architecture and mechanics of how computers operate and how you can translate real-world problems to computer programs that solve these problems. The concepts you learn will provide a foundation for your future endeavours in computing and, we hope, will begin to change the way you think about real-world problems. This course is an introductory course to the basics of computer programming and Computer Science. It is intended as an introduction to studying further in Computer Science or related fields. Topics include: Fundamental programming concepts Introduction to Computer Science The C programming language and use of a C compiler Programming style Program design and organisation concepts Program testing and debugging
