Throughout the course, you will be encouraged to experiment with 3D animation processes and concepts as you create your own sequences. Particular emphasis is given to performance as a key aspect of 3D animation. You will also focus on planning and iterating your creative work, to help you develop greater awareness of the relationships between form, content, and meaning in animation practice.
learning_outcomes: Understand and explain animation concepts in relation to animation practice
Creatively experiment with concepts and forms in animation practice
Apply intermediate 3D animation techniques to create animated sequences
Plan and iterate creative processes in the production of animated sequences
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART1210

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Animation 3
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course further enhances your animation practice by engaging you with a range of advanced processes and techniques in animation. With a sustained focus on 3D animation techniques and workflow processes, the course helps you to contextualise and refine your animation skills as you develop a short, animated project. By exploring iterative and collaborative creative processes as well as professional practice principles, you will develop skills to generate and refine your ideas, taking them from conception to completion. By working towards an animation project ready for viewing by an audience, this course prepares you to take the next steps in continuing to expand and develop your media arts practice.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on and evaluate contributions to collaborative and iterative animation processes
Work independently and collaboratively to plan, test, and resolve an animation project
Integrate advanced 3D animation techniques and workflow processes to create and resolve a screen-based project
Creatively engage with animation concepts in relation to a range of creative and cultural contexts
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2210

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Rigging for Animation
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio elective introduces you to the foundations of rigging for animation. The course is designed to build on your existing knowledge of 3D CGI principles and techniques so that you can enhance your practice in this area. Throughout the course, you will expand your understanding of this specialised field of practice by creating rigging systems that drive and control the movement of 3D objects. The course draws on a wide range of sources, including virtual sculpting processes, anatomy, physiology, colour theory, and visual storytelling. In a supportive studio environment, you will be encouraged to experiment with new approaches and concepts, as well as integrate workflow techniques that can be applied in other contexts.
learning_outcomes: Apply animation rigging techniques to create a functional 3D prototype
Integrate effective project management principles to create a fully functional 3D control system that can be integrated into an advanced workflow
Experiment with movement to explore the construction of meaning in animation

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Motion Capture
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio elective introduces you to Motion Capture technologies and processes that digitally capture human movement for use in moving image, animation, visual effects, game production, and numerous other related media arts applications. You will gain theoretical and practical experience with motion capture through a series of studio exercises, enabling you to experiment with these processes in your own media arts practice. The course is designed for those with prior experience in 3D animation and visualisation, and has an emphasis on collaborative, group-based learning in media arts studio environments. In this supportive studio environment, you will be encouraged to experiment with new approaches and concepts, further expanding the potentials of your media arts practice.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and reflect on creative processes, workflows, and outcomes that use motion capture in media arts contexts
Work collaboratively to develop and deliver a media arts project integrating motion capture principles, workflows, and production techniques
Explore the construction of meaning in media arts contexts by experimenting with motion capture processes and techniques
Apply motion capture production processes and techniques to create media arts projects
prerequisites: Must have completed DART1210 or DDES1110

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Visual Effects 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course allows you to further develop your practical, technical, and conceptual skills in visual effects. Building on your foundational skills and knowledge in visual effects practice, the course focuses on intermediate compositing processes and 3D CGI integration. As you develop your own sequences, you will be encouraged to experiment and to explore pertinent concepts in relation to screen-based practice. Particular emphasis is given to planning and iterating your creative work, as you develop greater awareness of the relationships between form, content, and meaning in visual effects practice.
learning_outcomes: Creatively experiment with concepts and forms in visual effects practice
Understand and explain screen-based concepts in relation to visual effects practice
Plan and iterate creative processes in the production of visual effects projects
Apply intermediate visual effects techniques to create moving image sequences
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART1220

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Visual Effects 3
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course further enhances your visual effects practice by engaging you with a range of advanced compositing processes and techniques. With additional focus on 3D CGI integration, as well as emerging techniques and processes, the course helps you to advance your practice in visual effects. By emphasising iterative processes and collaborative workflows, the course also supports you to develop creative and professional approaches that can be applied in future projects and contexts. Taking a project from conception to completion, you will continue to explore new ways of working in this dynamic field of practice, assisting you in continuing to expand and develop your media arts practice.
learning_outcomes: Integrate advanced visual effects techniques and workflow processes to create and resolve a screen-based project
Work independently and collaboratively to plan, test, and resolve a visual effects project
Creatively engage with visual effects concepts in relation to a range of creative and cultural contexts
Reflect on and evaluate contributions to collaborative and iterative visual effects processes
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2220

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Moving Image 2: Studio Processes
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course enables you to further develop your creative and technical skills in contemporary moving image practice. Building on your foundational skills and knowledge, this course focuses on developing your understandings of key conventions, forms, genres, and studio production techniques so that you can apply and experiment with them in your own works. By developing deeper understandings of the medium’s visual language, as well as gaining new production skills, this course provides a platform from which to explore a range of creative possibilities in contemporary moving image practice. Particular emphasis is given to planning and delivering a creative work within a team environment to allow you to build collaborative skills necessary for professional practice within the field.
learning_outcomes: Apply and adapt intermediate moving image techniques to create new work in collaboration with peers.
Design and implement a production plan that incorporates professional standards.
Identify and analyse a range of moving image conventions, forms, and genres.
Create a moving image work that creatively engages with existing conventions, forms, and genres in the field.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART1230

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Moving Image 3: Advanced Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course supports you to explore the expanded potentials of contemporary moving image practice. Extending on the skills and knowledge you have developed in moving image practice, this course enables you to push beyond familiar conventions, structures and formats to experiment with new and innovative possibilities. Throughout the course, you will be encouraged to identify and develop your creative interests as a moving image practitioner and to consider how your self-initiated practice is situated within broader contexts. Particular emphasis is given to resolving a final creative work with consideration of how it is communicated to an audience through professional presentation formats.
learning_outcomes: Apply and synthesise a range of advanced moving image techniques to create new work that meets professional standards.
Integrate practice-led research principles to create a resolved moving image work.
Critically engage with concepts through self-initiated moving image practice.
Experiment with display and installation techniques to resolve a self-initiated moving image work.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2230

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Sound 3
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course provides you with opportunities to further develop and explore your sound practice by constructing screen-based audiovisual works that focus on sound as a key artistic and storytelling component. You will examine various ways that sound can shape experiences of both traditional and experimental audiovisual forms, and you will experiment with sound to create new artistic connections between sound and image. The studio focus of the course will help you develop audiovisual skills through which you can expand on traditional and experimental techniques across a range of platforms for media arts practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and contextualise sound practice within relevant contemporary and historical discourses
Apply advanced technical skills to record, edit, and post-produce multi-channel sound for media arts contexts
Conceive, develop, and create soundtracks that enhance storytelling in audiovisual artworks
Individually and collaboratively script, plan and execute sound design to produce a soundtrack for a screen-based audiovisual artwork
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2240

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Sound 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will conceive and develop sound installation projects that respond to and transform our experience of space. You will examine contextual examples and theories of listening and sound to investigate the capacity of sound to alter meanings and interpretations of our surroundings. You will apply this knowledge to produce context-aware soundscapes, and experiment with real-time generative and interactive sound practices to explore the potentials of sound in sculptural, installation or performative scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Create stand-alone sound works that transform a sense of place, using various sound recording, editing, manipulation and assemblage techniques
Identify and articulate the ways in which sound transforms experiences of place with reference to relevant experimental outcomes and precedent works as examples
Apply intermediate technical skills to develop original sound works from conception to completion
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART1240

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Real-Time Production
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio elective introduces you to foundational concepts, processes, and techniques for working with virtual production workflows. Through practical, hands-on activities in the studio, you will develop skills for real-time pre-visualisation and in-camera visual effects, including digital cinematography, camera tracking and live chroma keying, enabling you to integrate CGI assets and environments with live action in real-time. As industry practices and techniques continue to evolve, this course focuses on developing your foundational skills for real-time workflows, extending your knowledge of digital compositing principles and techniques to enhance your broader creative practice. As you develop your understanding of real-time virtual production workflows, you will develop your own creative projects that combine CGI assets, scenes, and environments with live action footage. As part of a supportive studio environment, and with access to real-time visual effects tools and facilities, you will be encouraged to experiment with new approaches and concepts, as well as integrate technical workflows that can be applied in future projects.
learning_outcomes: Apply foundational real-time processes and techniques to create virtual production projects.
Explore the construction of meaning in animation and visual effects contexts by experimenting with real-time virtual production processes and techniques.
Document, analyse, and reflect on creative processes, workflows, and outcomes that use real-time virtual production processes in animation and visual effects contexts.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Game Art 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course allows you to further develop your practical, technical, and conceptual skills in game art by extending your engagement with real-time workflows and production techniques. Building on your foundational skills and knowledge in game art practice, this course focuses on game art production pipelines so that you can expand the potential of your practice. Emphasis is given to optimising your workflow while also advancing your understandings of user interaction, game logic, and storytelling. You will be encouraged to combine these skillsets as you experiment with game art techniques and concepts to create your own real-time screen-based project. You will also focus on planning and iterating your creative work, to help you develop greater awareness of the relationships between form, content, interactivity, and the production of meaning in game art practice.
learning_outcomes: Draw on game art concepts to critically explore and create novel assets for game environments
Use intermediate game art tools and techniques to create game-ready assets
Identify and explain game art concepts in relation to real-time and screen-based game contexts
Apply iterative game art processes in a team-based setting to develop game assets and environments
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART1260

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Generative AI for Artists
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio elective focuses on conceiving, researching, and realising creative works that engage with an utilise computational processes, with a particular focus on the use of and critical thinking about artificial intelligence and generative systems. This course invites students from a range of backgrounds to work in a collaborative studio environment that fosters interdisciplinary and experimental approaches to develop skills in creative computational practice. By introducing you to key concepts, skills, and methods for engaging critically and creatively with computational systems and artificial intelligence, this course will enable you to work effectively in a landscape of rapidly evolving media technologies and develop artworks that engage in contemporary public debates about power structures, technological progress, work, and the role of the artist. Throughout the course, you will develop skills in experimentation and creative research by working with the latest creative technologies through project-based learning. As you develop your own creative projects, you will be encouraged to explore, interrogate, and integrate current innovations in generative AI and related media technologies, thereby enhancing the conceptual and technical scope of your creative practice.
learning_outcomes: Plan, implement, and document innovative creative projects that use computational processes and artificial intelligence in a collaborative studio environment.
Use exploratory creative processes to critically engage with concepts relevant to computational processes and artificial intelligence and their impacts on social, cultural, and artistic contexts.
Systematically experiment with computational processes and techniques to produce media-based artworks.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Game Art 3
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course further enhances your game art practice by connecting you with a range of advanced production processes and techniques in the game development pipeline. With a sustained focus on optimising game art workflows alongside a critical engagement with game art concepts and contexts, this course helps you to refine and extend your game art skills as you develop a real-time screen-based game. By embedding iterative and collaborative creative processes as well as professional practice principles, you will develop skills to extend your practice, taking ideas from conception to completion. Working towards a functioning interactive project as part of your game art portfolio, this course prepares you to take the next steps in expanding and developing your creative practice.
learning_outcomes: Work independently and collaboratively to plan, test, and resolve a real-time and screen-based game art project.
Apply self-reflexive practices and professional practice frameworks to evaluate contributions to collaborative and iterative game art processes.
Creatively and critically engage with game art concepts in relation to a range of creative and cultural contexts.
Integrate advanced real-time game art techniques and workflow processes to create and resolve a screen-based project.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2260

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Game Design 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: What makes a game fun? This intermediate studio course explores this question through the lens of ludology and related interdisciplinary frameworks. Building on your existing skills and knowledge in game design, this course focuses on theories and practices that enable you to create new ways of working with pre-existing affordances. You will engage with these topics by designing and creating your own stand-alone game through processes of continuous iteration and refinement. You will also explore the profound effects that games can have on players and integrate responsible and ethical considerations into your creative process. Industry standards and professional practice principles are woven into a supportive peer-oriented studio context, helping you to develop an informed and well-rounded approach to your game design practice.
learning_outcomes: Combine intermediate professional practice skills and industry standards to iterate and document game design processes.
Apply intermediate game design principles, techniques and processes to create engaging interactive experiences.
Creatively and ethically explore the effects of and relationships between mechanics, dynamics, and aesthetics in game design practice.
Apply key game design concepts and principles including game loops, game mechanics, and game dynamics.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART1270

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Game Design 3
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Can games also be meaningful experiences? This advanced studio course explores this question through the lens of narratology and related interdisciplinary frameworks. Taking your game design practice to the next level, this course focuses on theories and practices that enable you to create meaningful interactive experiences through narrative design. You will be encouraged to explore wider possibilities for games as artistic forms of expression, tools for political commentary, and powerful vehicles for education. You will also continue to explore the profound effects that games can have on individuals, players, and communities, expanding your capacity to integrate responsible and ethical considerations into your practice. Through a process of continuous iteration and refinement, you will develop more complex and compelling narrative experiences. The course also emphasises industry standards, professional practice, and iterative design in a supportive peer-oriented studio context to help you continue to expand your repertoire of skills and knowledge in game design practice.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise industry standards and professional practice principles to plan, test, iterate, document, and resolve a game design project.
Integrate advanced game design principles, techniques and processes to create engaging and meaningful interactive experiences.
Creatively and critically engage with game design concepts and principles in relation to a range of creative, cultural, and ethical contexts.
Integrate principles of narratology and ludology to explore the construction of meaning in game design practice.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2270

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course introduces you to contemporary Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art by examining current practices and discourses and the histories and theories that shape them. Focused through a series of specific artist case studies, the course aims to facilitate rigorous discussion and analysis of contemporary First Nations' art in Australia as well as its intersections with complex and diverse social, cultural, political, and artistic contexts. By privileging First Nations' voices and perspectives and by enabling close analysis and detailed discussions, the course will deepen your engagement and appreciation of the diversity of Indigenous artistic and cultural practices.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret examples of contemporary Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art practice.
Research and situate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art practices in relation to diverse social, cultural, political, and artistic contexts.
Identify and articulate key ideas that inform contemporary Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art practice and discourse.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: East Asian Contemporary Art
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course provides a critical introduction to contemporary art in and from East Asia. It focuses particularly on art from mainland China, Japan, and South Korea, from the mid-twentieth century to the present. Contemporary art in and from East Asia is characterised by intersections between local and western(ised) cultural thinking and practice. This course will enable students to develop understandings of the varied historical, cultural, political, and social conditions that have shaped contemporary art’s development in East Asia as well as its relationships to the international art world. Exploring how contemporary artists deploy materials, techniques, and conventions from East Asian artistic traditions, this course will enable students to critically reflect on the concepts of ‘tradition’, ‘modernity’, and ‘contemporaneity’ as they are used in contemporary art discourses. Examining how contemporary art from East Asia has been discussed, theorised, and displayed in different local and international contexts, this course will encourage multiple critical interventions into international and localised perspectives on contemporary artistic theory and practice.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the developmental trajectories of twentieth and twenty-first century art in/from East Asia.
Critically interpret the formal and material characteristics of artworks in relation to associated economies of production, display, and reception.
Select appropriate sources, employ appropriate referencing conventions, structure scholarly writing, and respond to clearly identified research questions.
Examine and contextualise twentieth and twenty-first century art in/from East Asia in relation to historical, cultural, creative, theoretical, and/or social frameworks.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Art and the Body
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course concentrates on contemporary art and gender, sexuality and the body. You will be introduced to a variety of key issues that contemporary practitioners address in work that explicitly engages with the body and its political meanings. The course will examine historical precedents for this diverse work: debates, controversies, resistances and social/political movements. The question of how art has influenced and responded to these broader movements for social change will be explored, with a particular emphasis on gender studies, transnational feminisms, queer theory, critical race theory, critical disability studies and postcolonialism. Ideas about how the body has been theorised, represented, ignored or fetishised will be considered in the context of contemporary art. Difference - here understood as a critical aspect of political identities and orientations - will be investigated through art that addresses the body.
learning_outcomes: Investigate the historical development of art about gender, sexuality and the body
Visually analyse artworks dealing with gender, sexuality and the body
Discuss key ideas (such as the meaning of the body, sexuality and gender) in contemporary art history and theory.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Sensing the Arts
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course will expand your knowledge and understanding of the role of the senses in recent and contemporary arts practices. It will demonstrate that the senses have played a particularly crucial and often experimental role in the arts. The course will focus on one or more of the senses and their conceptual / theoretical role in the arts. In terms of the wider critical context of contemporary art, this course will raise your awareness of the significance of post-object or immaterial elements in art practices.
learning_outcomes: Critically Analyse the role of the senses within contemporary and recent art.
Distinguish and Evaluate distinct arguments about the nature of senses in the arts.
Describe the sense experience within various arts practices.
Construct a research paper based on self-directed learning and research.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Art, Exhibitions, and Institutions
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course reviews current research and theoretical frameworks on museums and art museums. It examines the history of collecting and exhibiting, and the museum as an institution. Taking the 'new museology' as its theoretical starting point, it considers the cultural role of museums and explores critical theoretical approaches to museum culture. Its emphasis is on material culture, objects, artworks and curatorship in the contexts of collections and exhibitions.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and analyse contemporary museums and art galleries, including the roles of curators, artists, audiences, exhibitions and objects
Investigate and discuss the history and theory of museums and cultural institutions
Contextualise art institutions within contemporary museum theories and practices

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: AI, Culture and Aesthetics
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the key concepts, theories, and impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) in today’s creative and cultural industries. The course connects students with critical issues in social, cultural, political, economic, and artistic contexts to help students develop critical understandings of the ever-changing relationships between artificial intelligence and creative practice. The course specifically examines theories of human, social and machine creativity; copyright and its crisis under AI; histories of artistic remixing, re-appropriation, and imitation and their relation to AI; and theories of the value of the arts. The course also draws on specific contemporary creative AI practices and encourages students to connect these discussions to your preferred creative domain area (for example, visual art, design, film, music).
learning_outcomes: Develop and evaluate arguments relating to generative AI innovation and a variety of social, political, economic, and artistic contexts.
Critically analyse creative works to expand understandings of contemporary issues in AI, art, and culture.
Select and integrate appropriate scholarly sources to support and substantiate distinctive arguments in relation to AI, art, and culture.
Describe key concepts, theories, and debates relating to AI, copyright, ethics, and moral rights in the context of contemporary creative practices.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Studio Art Practice 5
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Studio Art Practice 5 is the fifth in a sequence of six core courses that enables you to develop your independent artistic practice throughout the BFA program. This course builds on Studio Art Practice 1-4, and provides opportunities for you to develop your emerging practice by critically reflecting on your creative journey so far, and planning ahead for the future. With greater emphasis on self-initiated practice, the weekly topics and examples are responsive to the individual and collective needs of the class. Structured and semi-structured studio classes allow you to focus on your specific areas of interest, while also connected with other students in a peer-to-peer studio environment. You are expected to regularly contribute to and lead class discussions and group critiques so as to build the collegiate and critically-engaged studio environment. Professional contexts and standards are also scaffolded into the course so as to help prepare you for future pathways.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on and communicate the influences and trajectories of artistic practice
Create, present and document a self-initiated body of work that addresses technical, formal, and conceptual concerns
Propose and plan a self-initiated body of work in a format appropriate for professional contexts
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2101

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Studio Art Practice 6
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Studio Art Practice 6 is the sixth in a sequence of six core courses that enables you to develop your independent artistic practice. This course builds on Studio Art Practice 1-5, and provides opportunities for you to deepen your self-initiated work through practice-led research. As it is the final course in the sequence, you are encouraged to follow the materials, processes, and ideas that are fundamental to your practice, and to cultivate a deep engagement with your creative interests. Through structured and semi-structured studio classes, you are given opportunities to plan, develop, and resolve your works in peer-to-peer contexts. You are expected to regularly contribute to and lead class discussions and group critiques. With a particular focus on the discourses that shape contemporary art practice, the weekly topics and examples provided are responsive to the individual and collective needs of the class. Professional contexts and standards are also scaffolded into the course so as to help prepare you for future pathways.
learning_outcomes: Select, install, and display artworks in formats appropriate for professional artistic contexts
Create a self-initiated body of work that integrates practice-led research methods and ethical awareness to synthesise technical, formal, and conceptual concerns
Analyse and situate artistic practice within relevant artistic, critical, and professional contexts
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART3100

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Drawing 3: Advanced Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on expanding the artistic strategies, concepts, and vocabulary of your drawing practice in the context of contemporary art. By making and learning in the studio, you will be encouraged to explore new ideas, materials, processes, and technologies as well as consolidate your existing skills and knowledge in drawing. A significant focus of this course is planning, developing, and completing a self-initiated body of work that demonstrates an advanced, independent enquiry into drawing. To assist you in doing this, the course offers diverse conceptual and thematic frameworks, and concentrates on identifying resonances with other artists’ ideas, techniques, and processes.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on and articulate the artistic concepts, frameworks, and methodologies that inform a self-initiated drawing practice.
Engage in self-initiated practice-led research to support and develop advanced drawing practice.
Undertake advanced studio practices by employing a range of drawing materials, techniques, creative approaches, and skills.
Plan, develop, and create drawings that explore self-initiated areas of interest in the context of contemporary art practice.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2110

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Painting 3: Advanced Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on advancing your self-initiated painting practice in the context of contemporary art. Throughout this course, you will develop new work in the studio as well as undertake contextual research and engage in supportive peer-to-peer discussions, helping you to develop a critically informed painting practice. There is a particular focus throughout the course on considering new developments in painting, as well as how contemporary painting is informed by a range of technological, social, and cultural contexts. By engaging with a diverse range of painting practices, exhibitions, and institutions, this course will also help you to broaden your understandings of painting in professional contemporary art contexts both locally and globally.
learning_outcomes: Implement practice-led research principles to create a self-initiated body of work that is suitable for public exhibition.
Create paintings that reflect an awareness of and engagement with contemporary painting practices and related technologies.
Contextualise contemporary painting practice in relevant local and global contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2120

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Photography 3: Advanced Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course further extends your skills and knowledge across analogue and digital processes in contemporary photographic practice by introducing you to large format cameras and flash lighting. You will develop and enrich your practice’s material and conceptual frameworks through iterative techniques, peer review, supported and independent studio practice research, and written analysis. Underpinned by contextual research and feedback throughout the course, you will develop, refine, and resolve a portfolio of work following your individual studio interests in dialogue with contemporary art contexts.
learning_outcomes: Develop, refine, and resolve a body of photographic work using advanced iterative, experimental and self-reflexive artistic processes.
Independently and critically engage with historical and contemporary photographic concepts, theories, and practices through contextual research, photographic art practice, and written reflections.
Apply and integrate technical proficiencies in flash lighting, large format analogue cameras, medium format digital cameras, and photographic printing processes.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2130

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Printmaking: Advanced Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will extend your printmaking practice by exploring new ideas and processes in the studio. Building on the knowledge and skills generated in earlier Printmaking course(s), this studio-based course engages you with the concepts, materials and procedures related to advanced printmaking techniques. The course enables you to develop a strong framework for your self-initiated practice by focusing on individually conceived and managed projects. Supported by lectures, demonstrations, consultations, and a collaborative peer-oriented studio environment, you will have opportunities to investigate new conceptual and technical approaches that align with and extend your artistic practice. You will be encouraged to be conceptually and technically ambitious in this course as you develop your self-initiated practice through printmaking.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced printmaking techniques to explore concepts relevant to contemporary printmaking contexts.
Independently manage projects and undertake safe working practices in a printmaking studio environment.
Develop and articulate artistic concepts in a contemporary printmaking context.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: One of the following courses, DART1140, DART1141, DART2140, DART2141, DDES1040, or SDES2463

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Sculpture 3: Advanced Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course allows you to extend your sculptural practice by creating a new body of work ready for exhibition. With a specific focus on resolving your artworks for public display, this course focuses on the ways that site, venue, spatial relations, and audience impact your work as it emerges from the studio. While your work will be self-initiated, you will also be working in peer-oriented environments as you plan and prepare for an exhibition outcome. Through this combination, you will have opportunities to integrate professional practice principles into your work as you plan, install, and document your artwork for exhibition contexts.
learning_outcomes: Integrate professional practice principles to create and frame a portfolio of sculptural work ready for exhibition and professional contexts.
Create self-initiated sculptural artworks that incorporate advanced sculptural concepts, processes, and techniques.
Articulate artistic ideas and practice-led research methodologies relevant to a contemporary sculptural practice.
Work collaboratively to plan and organise an artistic event or exhibition.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART2150

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Major Project 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course enables you to extend your media arts practice by planning and working towards an ambitious major project that aligns with your creative interests. The course builds on your previous studies and provides opportunities for you to deepen your skills and knowledge by integrating practice-led research principles in a supportive and collaborative studio environment. Throughout the course, you are encouraged to explore the ideas, techniques, and processes that are important to you and to extend the conceptual and technical potentials of your practice. With a particular focus on integrating professional and ethical standards into the production workflow of your project, this course helps prepare you for future pathways and career aspirations.
learning_outcomes: Apply collaboration, project planning, and management skills to incorporate ethical and professional standards in a major media arts project.
Situate media arts practice in relevant creative and cultural contexts.
Experiment with a range of advanced media arts processes and techniques to create works in progress.
Integrate practice-led research principles to develop ideas for self-initiated media arts practice.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 72 UOC overall, including one of the following courses, DART2211, DART2221, DART2231, DART2241, or DDES2111

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Major Project 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course enables you to extend your media arts practice by creating a resolved and ambitious major project that extends your creative interests. The course builds on your previous studies and provides opportunities for you to deepen your skills and knowledge by integrating practice-led research principles in a supportive and collaborative studio environment. As a culminating creative experience, you are encouraged to explore the ideas, techniques, and processes that are important to you and to extend the conceptual and technical potentials of your practice. With a particular focus on resolving an ambitious major project appropriate for display in public and professional contexts, this course helps prepare you for future learning and professional creative pursuits.
learning_outcomes: Integrate a range of advanced media arts processes and techniques to resolve a major project ready for display in public and professional contexts.
Critically contextualise and reflect on media arts practice in specific creative and cultural contexts.
Apply practice-led research principles to investigate self-initiated ideas through media arts practice.
Incorporate collaboration, ethical, and professional standards in the planning, refining, and realisation of a major media arts project.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DART3200

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Professional Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course helps you to develop a range of skills and strategies for working in the dynamic and constantly changing media arts sector. With a diverse array of possible pathways, this sector often sees emerging practitioners move between large and small organisations, as well as develop their own independent and self-initiated projects. With this in mind, this course aims to give you the tools to seek out, cultivate, and activate these opportunities in professional contexts. To do so, the course focuses on developing a combination of practical, interpersonal, and communication skills that will help you succeed in the wider field of media arts professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Create a portfolio that represents existing and future potential as a media arts professional
Apply a self-reflective approach to identify existing skills and their application to professional media arts contexts
Use professional communication strategies and formats to articulate relevant skills, knowledge, practice, and ideas in media arts
Identify and investigate career opportunities and professional pathways in media arts contexts
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 72 UOC in the Animation and Moving Image major or a Media Arts single or double degree program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Global Contemporary Art
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course introduces you to global contemporary art; art that critically reflects, responds to and intervenes in the key forces shaping the present condition. Globalisation, border politics and decolonisation are the key socio-historical contexts for this course, as you examine art’s relationship with, and response to, economic, historical, ecological, and political contexts. To navigate the breadth and complexity of global contemporary art, you will engage with a series of key concepts such as ‘contemporaneity’ and ‘global art’, drawing from a range of contemporary writers and artists. By doing so, you will develop a vocabulary and tool kit, grounded in theory and practice, through which to critically engage with the intersections of art, culture, and the processes and politics of making and re-making worlds today.
learning_outcomes: Apply scholarly research skills to analyse art of the twenty-first century
Analyse how artists, thinkers and curators engage with a range of political, social, economic and ecological issues to critically engage with the global present
Articulate key concepts relevant to global contemporary art practice and discourse

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Art, Gender, and Sexuality
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course looks at the human body and its representation over time and across diverse contexts. It considers both the human and the body as historically, socially, culturally and politically determined concepts. You will explore different ways that bodies have been interpreted and made meaningful, in particular, via the history of pornography and the emergence of the 'post-pornographic' body. Post-pornography refers to the politics of embodiment in the context of post-humanism, a moment in which sex is understood beyond 'natural' biology and reproductive futurity. Each week, representations of the body will be considered according to a different set of concepts and frameworks. Issues of identity, technology and power will be discussed alongside examples from contemporary art and culture. The course is designed to bring into relief a long interpretative history of sexual practices and the politics of desire.
learning_outcomes: Construct and articulate a self-directed research project that engages with key concepts in post-pornography and porn studies.
Summarise key concepts underpinning the emerging fields of post-pornography and porn studies.
Produce scholarly writing that demonstrates critical engagement with key concepts and their application to the analysis of contemporary art and culture.
Interpret and analyse visual and material culture with a particular focus on gender, sex, sexuality and desire.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Affect in Art
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course explores contemporary and recent art and design in the context of new thinking about affect. The 'affective turn' crosses cultural and political theory and aesthetics and places emphasis on the role and status of affect in relation to perception, cognition and experience in the world today. You will proceed from this broader context of discussion and debate about affect to examine how art and design contribute to and modulate new concepts of affect. We will explore how human and more-than-human bodies produce and transmit affect and how this has been taken by artists and designers. You will gain an understanding of the debates, context and vocabulary around affect and will be able to identify art and design that contributes to affective aesthetics. You will develop skills that facilitate affective art and design practices especially in relation to art forms that enhance embodied experience, sensory engagement, and immersion.
learning_outcomes: Understand and use a basic vocabulary of affect in relation to art and design and identify issues concerning affect in art and design.
Locate their own and/or others’ practices and conceptual approaches in relation to issues of affect in art and design and affect theory.
Use interdisciplinary techniques across a range of art and design practices that engage and deepen thinking and making in relation to affect and the sensory body.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Art and Climate
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course critically analyses art in an epoch of climate change. It examines the emergence of various forms of enviro-art, bio-art, and eco-art, using ‘plant humanities’ as a focal point. The course pays close attention to how artists harness, activate, and propel environmental concepts and debates. Foregrounding ethical and theoretical frameworks such as extractionism, eco-feminism, and decolonisation, this course supports you in developing knowledge about art practices that address extinction and eco-catastrophe, and the complex intertwining of human/nature relations more broadly. Looking to the horizon, the course also speculates about the future of art in new climates and seeks sustainable and critically informed creative alternatives.
learning_outcomes: Apply scholarly research skills to develop and communicate arguments about art and climate.
Critically analyse and interpret examples of contemporary art practice that engage with climate concepts, debates, and discourses.
Identify and articulate key concepts and theories connecting art and climate.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Global Visual Cultures
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course explores contemporary histories of visuality, from early ethnography to avant-garde cinema verité to post-documentary experiments with the truth. Set within a broad and emergent field of global visual studies, this course examines critical moments in the social, political and historical role of film, art and media activism to explore how vision has been shaped and transformed by technologies of the camera. Beginning with the invention of photography, the course tracks theories of representation and cultural production across a range of visual practices and platforms, including video, satellite television, digital and the phone-made, AI, VR, immersive new media, Tubesites/the blogosphere/vlogosphere, as well as short and long form documentary and feature films. With a focus on Australian practices in relation to transnational histories and contexts, the course introduces theoretical frameworks and interdisciplinary techniques of critical ethnography, documentary and decolonial analytics to advance your skills in visual literacy and art analysis.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply research skills, analytic techniques, and critical frameworks to examine fundamental concepts, practices, and histories of visual technologies.
Articulate fundamental concepts and themes relevant to global and transnational histories of visuality.
Analyse and contextualise diverse global visual practices and technologies in relation to social, cultural, and political contexts of production and reception.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Art and Activism
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course traces artistic responses to the urgencies of contemporary life. It focuses particularly on lineages and practices of activist art, including artistic forms of resistance, campaign, intervention, advocacy, and protest. With social practice, participatory art, and institutional critique key reference points, the course examines a variety of activist artists, collectives, exhibitions, and curatorial approaches, both inside and outside the cannon of art history. By examining diverse examples in relation to historical, theoretical, and ethical frameworks, the course provides opportunities to consider the complexities of how art meets its audience, how it interacts with publics and communities, and how art can drive change across social, cultural, political, and environmental contexts.
learning_outcomes: Integrate ethical, scholarly, and professional practice principles to formulate and plan artistic interventions in social, cultural, political, and/or environmental contexts
Critically analyse and interpret examples of contemporary art practice that engage with activist concepts, strategies, and discourses
Identify and articulate key concepts and theories about art and activism

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Writing as Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Writing as Practice examines contemporary critical and creative writing, bringing art history and theory, literary studies, and cultural studies together to consider writing as a material practice in the broader arts ecology. It focuses on the ‘essay’ as an expanded form that includes text, video, film, photography, and poetry and that emphasises the experimental nature of thinking through writing. The weekly themes approach the practice of writing in the expanded essay form from different perspectives and by different means. Students will be introduced to a diverse corpus of contemporary writing and will be taught critical reading and practical writing skills. Lectures will provide historical and theoretical frameworks, tutorials will offer hand-on activities to put the lecture content into practice, and assessments will be supported by workshopping.
learning_outcomes: Compare, contrast and critique theories of reading and writing, in particular, in relation to contemporary art and culture.
Work independently and collaboratively to investigate, draft, edit and present creative and critical writing projects.
Write for different audiences and in a variety of registers according to context.
Identify, interpret and analyse a variety of contemporary forms and modes of writing, including experimental non-fiction, autobiography, poetry, text-based art and performance.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: World Biennales: Field Trip
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course offers first-hand experience of biennales in various parts of the world. As part of this course, you will visit two to three biennale (or triennale) exhibitions over a two-week intensive. The exhibitions and their content will be examined from the point of view of various disciplines, such as curatorial, art history and theory. The course provides you with an understanding of contemporary, innovative approaches to art and exhibition-making. In addition to introductory seminars prior to departure as well as on-site discussions led by lecturers, you will hear from curatorial and/or education staff at the biennales, and, where possible, participating artists. Each course is unique, depending on which biennales are on in any given year. Generally, the course will cover European biennales one year (e.g. Venice, Istanbul, Lyon) and Asian biennales in the next year (e.g. Gwangju, Shanghai, Singapore, Sharjah). Note: You are responsible for your own travel arrangements and associated costs. An additional up-front fee is also required by the university to cover the cost of delivering a course overseas (specific details are confirmed each year).
learning_outcomes: Engage selected theoretical frameworks to analyse contemporary art exhibitions in relation to local and global contexts
Analyse the impact of different geographical and cultural contexts on art and curatorial practice
Identify and articulate the conceptual, collaborative, and practical approaches to exhibition-making in local and global contexts
Use research methods and scholarly analysis to describe and analyse innovative art and curatorial approaches

This course is taught in a studio context, emphasising contemporary studio practice as a key mode of investigation and discovery. The studio also operates as a collegiate and peer-oriented environment, fostering a supportive and rigorous culture of creative practice, critical discussion, and exchange.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Contemporary Art Research Methods
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course introduces you to inquiry, analysis, and research skills relevant for contemporary art research at Honours level. The course focuses on the foundational research skills of: formulating a clear topic, situating your research in a field of thinkers and practitioners (communities of practice), building literature and practice reviews, and understanding which methods are relevant for your research. The course fosters a community of student and academic researchers willing to experiment with ideas and learn from each other to develop innovative projects that advance contemporary art practice and thinking in Australia and beyond. Through seminars, small group discussions, and one-on-one feedback, the course supports you to create a toolkit for planning and undertaking research that contributes ideas and experimental practices to the art community. It encourages you to understand the foundations of your practice, whether in art making, writing, or curating, and to learn how to hone your research skills for various professional contexts after graduating.
learning_outcomes: Adapt and apply a variety of research methods in contemporary art practice, history, and theory
Evaluate and explain research methods in contemporary art discourse and practice
Develop and plan a research project that engages with contemporary art contexts by integrating the principles of research methods
