institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Art Theory Honours Research Project
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Art Theory Honours Research Project is a 12 UOC core course in the Art Theory Honours program. Taken across three terms for a total of 36 UOC, this course supports students to develop and complete a 15,000-18,000-word Honours research thesis in art history/theory. Submitted at the conclusion of term 3, this thesis is the major research component of the program. It is assessed by 2 examiners (1 internal and 1 external) and constitutes 75% (36 UOC) of a student's overall results in the program. Students are guided by assigned supervisors through regular meetings, correspondence, and formative milestones. Students also receive support and guidance from the course convenor.
learning_outcomes: Produce a research thesis that demonstrates independent critical thinking and judgement in relation to a complex issue in art history and theory
Analyse and evaluate contemporary art practices in relation to relevant historical and theoretical frameworks
Apply a research methodology that integrates ethical research principles and demonstrates awareness of diverse perspectives
Construct a research thesis that demonstrates technical skills in research and communication
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in Art Theory (Honours) program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Animation Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio course introduces you to key principles and processes in animation practice. The course focuses on developing fundamental techniques for animating movement and provides core skills that will underpin your ongoing animation practice. Through hands-on learning in a supportive peer environment, you will also develop understandings of the key ideas and theories of animation. An emphasis on concept art, visual development, and pre-visualisation also helps you begin to understand and refine key elements of your creative workflow.
learning_outcomes: Document and critically reflect on the conceptual and technical processes used in animation practice
Apply fundamental animation skills and processes to create a short animated sequence
Use visual analysis and creative experimentation to explore animation principles and concepts

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio course provides opportunities to work with industry-relevant processes and workflows to respond to a project brief. Agility, collaboration, and teamwork are key capabilities needed across animation and visual effects contexts and this course prepares you by simulating a real world project. By working in small teams to create a resolved output, you will develop crucial skills in collaboration and project planning, as well as the ability to incorporate feedback through your iterative creative processes.
learning_outcomes: Use collaboration and teamwork to plan, develop, and resolve an animation and visual effects project that responds to a given brief
Integrate and apply industry-relevant technical workflows and professional practice principles to realise a project in animation and visual effects
Incorporate critical and constructive feedback through an iterative creative process in animation and visual effects
Creatively interpret a project brief to explore the construction of meaning for professional contexts in animation and visual effects
prerequisites: Must have completed at least 36 UOC in the MAVFX program.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: VFX Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio course introduces you to key principles and processes in visual effects. The course focuses on foundational compositing techniques that can be applied to a diverse range of content, providing essential skills for working in this fast-evolving field of practice. As you develop your own composited sequences integrating CG elements and live action, you will be encouraged to explore visual effects concepts and screen aesthetics. Through practice-based learning in a supportive visual effects studio environment, the course also encourages you to develop your creative skills by experimenting and iterating during the creative process.
learning_outcomes: Apply fundamental visual effects skills and processes to create a short composited sequence
Document and critically reflect on the conceptual and technical processes used in visual effects practice
Use visual analysis and creative experimentation to explore visual effects principles and concepts

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Production Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio course provides an opportunity to work in interdisciplinary teams to develop a resolved creative project. Team members are encouraged to bring their specific skills and knowledge to the project, allowing for a variety of ideas and techniques to be explored and integrated through collaboration and teamwork. A key focus of the course is on conceptualising and delivering a project for a specific audience or display context, with diverse and experimental outcomes possible. By focusing on external contexts for your work, the course encourages you to develop understandings of digital aesthetics and consider how your work is received by viewers and audiences.
learning_outcomes: Creatively explore the construction of meaning for audiences in a site-specific display context using animation and visual effects
Integrate and adapt a variety of technical and creative skills to realise a collaborative project in animation and visual effects
Use collaboration and teamwork to conceive, develop, and resolve a project in animation and visual effects
Document and critically reflect on the creative, technical, and conceptual processes used to realise a collaborative project
prerequisites: You must have completed at least 48 UOC in the MAVFX program.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Capstone Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course allows you to integrate the knowledge and skills gained throughout your previous studies to create an ambitious major project in the field of animation and visual effects. The course is designed to be taken in the last study period prior to graduation and focuses on realising a project that assists you in taking the next steps in your professional journey. The course fosters both independent and collaborative practice, allowing you to tailor your project to your professional aims and aspirations. You will be supported throughout the course through a variety of workshops, group discussions and consultations, all aimed at giving you the feedback to advance your chosen pathways in animation and visual effects.
learning_outcomes: Integrate professional practice principles to document and critically reflect on the creative, technical, and conceptual processes used to realise a major project
Research and evaluate a variety of professional pathways relevant to your goals in the animation and visual effects sector
Creatively explore and communicate meaning for audiences in a major animation and visual effects project
Use self-initiative and/or teamwork to conceive, develop, and resolve a major project in animation and visual effects
Adapt and synthesise advanced technical and creative skills to realise a major project in animation and visual effects
prerequisites: Must have completed DART9004

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Motion Capture Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This postgraduate studio elective introduces you to key concepts, processes, and techniques for using motion capture technologies in animation and visual effects projects. You will gain theoretical and practical experience with motion capture technologies through a series of studio exercises, enabling you to experiment with these processes in your own animation and visual effects practice. The course is designed to build on prior experience in 3D animation and visualisation, and has an emphasis on collaborative, group-based learning in studio environments. In this supportive studio environment, you will be encouraged to experiment with new approaches and concepts, further expanding the potentials of your animation and visual effects practice.
learning_outcomes: Document, analyse, and reflect on creative processes, workflows, and outcomes that use motion capture in animation and visual effects contexts
Work collaboratively to develop and deliver a project integrating motion capture principles, workflows, and production techniques
Explore the construction of meaning in animation and visual effects contexts by experimenting with advanced motion capture processes and techniques
Apply advanced motion capture processes and techniques to create animation and visual effects projects

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Rigging Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This postgraduate studio elective introduces you to the key concepts, processes, and techniques for rigging animated forms. The course is designed to build on your existing knowledge of 3D CGI principles and techniques so that you can enhance your practice in this area. Throughout the course, you will expand your understandings of this specialised field of practice by creating rigging systems that drive and control the movement of 3D objects. The course draws on a wide range of sources, including virtual sculpting processes, anatomy, physiology, colour theory, and visual storytelling. In a supportive studio environment, you will be encouraged to experiment with new approaches and concepts, as well as integrate workflow techniques that can be applied in other contexts.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced animation rigging techniques to create a functional 3D prototype
Experiment with animation rigging techniques to explore advanced animation concepts and principles
Integrate effective professional practice and project management principles to create a fully functional 3D control system that can be integrated into an advanced workflow

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Creature Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This postgraduate studio elective introduces you to the key concepts, processes, and techniques for creating characters and creatures for animation and visual effects projects. The course is designed to add to your repertoire of skills and knowledge in animation practice by extending your capabilities in character and creature design. Throughout the course, you will be encouraged to experiment with a range of creative processes and techniques to assist with ideation and realisation in a development workflow. As part of a supportive studio environment, you will be encouraged to seek feedback and discuss your approaches and ideas with peers, sharing knowledge and insights as you develop characters and creatures that can be integrated into future projects.
learning_outcomes: Explore the construction of meaning in animation and visual effects contexts by experimenting with advanced creature design processes and techniques
Document, analyse, and reflect on creative processes, workflows, and outcomes in the design and development of creatures for animation and visual effects contexts
Experiment with a variety of artistic processes to develop and design creatures for integration into animation and visual effects projects

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Procedural FX Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This postgraduate studio elective introduces you to the key concepts, processes, and techniques for creating procedurally generated FX for animation and visual effects projects. The course is designed to extend your existing knowledge of digital workflow principles and techniques to enhance your animation and visual effects practice. Throughout the course, you will expand your understandings of procedural workflows by experimenting with processes to create particle effects and simulations. In a supportive studio environment, you will be encouraged to test out new approaches and concepts, as well as integrate workflow techniques that can be applied in larger projects.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced procedural processes and techniques to create CGI FX for animation and visual effects projects
Explore the construction of meaning in animation and visual effects contexts by experimenting with advanced procedural FX processes and techniques
Document, analyse, and reflect on creative processes, workflows, and outcomes that use procedural FX processes in animation and visual effects contexts

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Real-Time Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This postgraduate studio elective introduces you to key concepts, processes, and techniques for creating real-time CGI environments for animation and visual effects projects. The course is designed to extend your existing knowledge of digital compositing principles and techniques to enhance your animation and visual effects practice. Throughout the course, you will expand your understandings of real-time workflows by creating CGI scenes, sets, lighting, and environments. In a supportive studio environment, you will be encouraged to experiment with new approaches and concepts, as well as integrate workflow techniques that can be applied in future projects.
learning_outcomes: Explore the construction of meaning in animation and visual effects contexts by experimenting with advanced real-time processes and techniques
Apply advanced real-time processes and techniques to create 3D environments for animation and visual effects projects
Document, analyse, and reflect on creative processes, workflows, and outcomes that use real-time processes in animation and visual effects contexts

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Digital Cinematography Studio
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This postgraduate studio elective introduces you to key concepts, processes, and techniques in digital cinematography. The course is designed to complement animation and visual effects workflows, expanding your skills and knowledge in digital content creation. Throughout the course, you will work directly with digital cameras to compose and shoot moving image sequences. With additional focus on lighting, colour management, editing, and sound design, the course enables you to add to your repertoire of skills and capabilities for a variety of applications in the production pipeline. Contributing to a supportive studio environment, you will be encouraged to work with peers as you develop projects that extend your collaborative and professional practices.
learning_outcomes: Explore the construction of meaning in moving image contexts by experimenting with advanced digital cinematography processes and techniques
Document, analyse, and reflect on creative processes, workflows, and outcomes that use digital cinematography relevant for animation and visual effects contexts
Work collaboratively to develop and deliver a project integrating digital cinematography principles, workflows, and production techniques
Apply advanced digital cinematography processes and techniques to create moving image sequences

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Major Exhibitions and Events
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Large-scale exhibitions, art fairs, biennales, and festivals are increasingly important to the contemporary art ecosystem. While complementing the traditional functions of galleries and museums, these major cultural events also offer new models for engaging audiences with art. This course provides an opportunity to learn in the context of a major exhibition, art fair, biennale, or festival, in a local setting. Through structured coursework and ‘on the ground’ experiences, you will develop theoretical and practical understandings of the ways that contemporary art production, presentation, and reception are shaped by major exhibitions and events. The course uses intensive delivery modes including an initial period of preparatory work and then a period of direct engagement with a specific large-scale exhibition or cultural event.
learning_outcomes: Contextualise and explain strategic aspects of a specific major exhibition or event
Critically reflect on professional experiences relating to the production, presentation, and reception of contemporary art in the context of a specific major exhibition or event
Independently research, synthesise and articulate information about contemporary art in the context of a specific major exhibition or event
prerequisites: Enrolled in 9318 program and completion of 48 Units of Credit

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Digital Aesthetics
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course explores the histories and theories informing contemporary animation and visual effects practices. Throughout the course, you will be introduced to key terms, concepts, and frameworks through which to analyse and interpret examples and practices in this fast evolving field. Through discussion, analysis, and research you will interrogate fundamental aspects of digital screen aesthetics and explore the role of new technologies in shaping our ways of seeing, thinking, and generating meaning in contemporary contexts.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and interpret examples of animation and visual effects in relation to contemporary cultural contexts.
Construct a persuasive and supported argument in relation to animation and visual effects using appropriate essay structure.
Apply academic research skills to select and integrate high quality scholarly sources.
Examine and evaluate the histories and theories informing contemporary animation and visual effects practices.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Data Science and Decisions
syllabus_overview: Students will be provided with a broad overview of Data Science as a platform for further studies in Data Science and an understanding and appreciation of Data Science in the modern world. Students will study the fundamentals of Data Science as it is applied in Computer Science, Economics and Mathematics and Statistics. They will be introduced to topics such as databases, data analytics, data mining, Bayesian statistics, statistical software, econometrics, machine learning and business forecasting. The content of this course will be delivered via weekly live lectures with academics from three different schools, the School of Mathematics and Statistics, the School of Economics and the School of Computer Science and Engineering. These concepts will be further explored through a series of tutorials/workshops.
learning_outcomes: Apply key methods of statistical inference in applied settings.
Apply fundamental data science techniques and tools, including machine learning, Naïve Bayes classification, Decision trees, K-NN, unsupervised learning and neural networks.
Use key theoretical tools to explore the properties of random variables.
Use R/RStudio to perform statistical computations and simulations.
Apply probability rules in a given setting to calculate key quantities.
Apply various data visualisation tools, perform regression analysis and draw causal inference from data.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Science and Decisions in Practice
syllabus_overview: This is the capstone course for the Data Science and Decisions program. The course will bring students in the three Data Science Majors together to share their knowledge, expertise and training in a way that is typical of industry. Students will attend seminars by industry representatives from Data Science industries, and students will work on group projects related to real world industry problems. Typical groups will be composed of students across the three different streams of the Data Science and Decisions program. The course will expose students to Data Science as it is practiced in industry. Assumed knowledge: students are assumed to have completed all Level 1 and 2 courses in the 3959 program before enrolling in this course, as well as a level 3 course on advanced modelling methods: one of COMP9417, MATH3821, ECON3208 or ECON3210.
learning_outcomes: Write a technical report that clearly communicates project outcomes and recommendations.
Apply mathematical and computational techniques, and business sensibilities, to real-world problems in data science.
Present the rationale, analyses, and results for a data science project to a client in oral and multimedia formats.
Collaborate effectively with people with different expertises within data science to solve a real-world problem.
Assess reports and provide constructive feedback on draft technical reports written by others.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 3959 Data Science or 4795 Data Science and Decisions / Law

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Visualisation
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to data visualisation in the areas of statistical analysis and data science. Students will learn how to make their own effective and impactful visualisations using software tools including R. There will be a strong focus on developing the skill of data storytelling: combining data, its visualisation, and a narrative to create a powerful story to drive change. Key topics include visualisation for exploratory and statistical data analysis and interactive visualisations such as dashboards.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and interpret data graphics, including understanding and interpreting the output of software packages.
Apply data storytelling techniques to a range of problems in data science, statistics, and applications.

Communicate data insights effectively and successfully to a variety of audiences. Successful communication can include accurately portraying insights, promoting understanding, or informing effective decisions.
Apply basic principles and concepts of data visualisation design.
Produce appropriate high quality data visualisations using a variety of software packages and techniques.
prerequisites: Enrolment in program 5659 or 5959 or 7659 or 7959 or 8161 or 8719 or 8750 or 8959

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Science and Decisions Project A
syllabus_overview: This course exposes students to research methods in applying data science and decisions techniques to a research project. The project courses serve as a capstone in the Master of Data Science and Decisions program. Students will be required to apply and demonstrate their learning from the courses in the program. It also requires students to present their work in visual and verbal forms including a presentation. The Data Science and Decisions Project course is done over two terms under the course code DATA5011 and DATA5012. The assessment is a final report which is worth 80% and a presentation worth 20%. The project report is due at the end of DATA5012 and presentation is held at the end of DATA5012. Therefore there is no formal assessment while the student is enrolled in DATA5011. Please note: Students in the 8959 program have an alternative 12 UOC Masters project course: DATA5925 - Data Science and Decisions Project. Please visit Handbook for more advice.

Apply robust research methods to design, build, or evaluate a data science project.
Communicate technical information clearly, in both verbal and written form.

Prerequisite: Must have successfully completed at least 36 UoC in their current Program

Students will work in a small group and present results in thesis form and in a presentation. Students will be supervised by an academic staff member from the School and meet one hour per week to discuss and work on the group project. Students are not eligible to start a project until they have completed at least 36 UoC (typically, 6 courses) over at least three terms.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Design Fieldwork on Country
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: DDES1000 Design Fieldwork on Country is an object design focussed course that offers the opportunity to engage in field research to inform design and making practice. This intensive residency-based course provides immersion in a specific site, where you will experience learning activities that facilitate engagement with the natural and built ecosystems of the site. Informed by best practice Indigenous design theories and methods, DDES1000 provides the opportunity to develop sensitive work practices with places and people outside of the usual classroom scenario. Working with the site as the source of primary research, you will learn the skills needed to develop place-based design projects, this will include observation, making, secondary research and collaboration.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of and engagement with Indigenous practices and protocols associated with designing and making
Investigate and experiment with a range of material culture production and making processes in response to a site
Apply field-based research to design and making processes
Develop and communicate effective design project outcomes

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Ceramic Design: Wheel Throwing
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course introduces you to the fundamental fabrication method of wheel throwing for the production of ceramics. Using the potter’s wheel, you will develop ceramic designs that respond to the historical and theoretical considerations and debates that frame contemporary ceramic practice. Design projects give prominence to ideas and processes associated with the development of ceramic multiples.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and critically review ceramic wheel throwing approaches and processes in the field of ceramic design.
Demonstrate and apply knowledge of wheel throwing techniques in the production of ceramic design.
Develop and resolve a design project from concept development through to communication and documentation of ceramic design outcomes.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Jewellery Design for Fashion
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Jewellery for Fashion focuses on contemporary jewellery practice and the concepts of jewellery as expressed in a fashion context. The course takes a holistic approach to a design task across interlinked assessments that will see you working with jewellery techniques and a range of materials to design and make jewellery in response to a specific Runway collection by a selected fashion designer or fashion house. This includes a large scale piece of jewellery suitable for the Runway, to be photographed and presented as a magazine cover, followed by designing and making a High Street collection of jewellery prototypes.
learning_outcomes: Investigate contemporary jewellery and adornment practices as vehicles for expressing ideas.
Create finished jewellery supported by professional presentation documents.
Identify, analyse, and research a jewellery design problem.
Identify and use appropriate jewellery and object making processes, techniques, tools, materials and safety procedures.
Develop a methodology for exploring ideas in two and three dimensions and translating these to finished works.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Object as Architecture: Jewellery and Metal Design
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will focus on the design and fabrication of functional and/or wearable objects in response to architecture and interior spaces. You will apply jewellery and metal fabrication skills and small-scale production methods to develop a series of designs that engage with spatial and conceptual relationships between architecture and the body. Your design outcomes will be contextualised by contemporary practices in Jewellery and Object Design.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and apply digital literacies and processes relevant to object design and prototyping.
Experiment with a range of materials and methods and apply findings to the design, fabrication and presentation of objects.
Investigate and communicate an effective synthesis of concepts, forms, materials and processes.
Examine and critique the contextual and relational significance of design objects.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Furniture and Lighting Design
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Furniture and Lighting Design will engage you in the field of furniture and lighting design for social and environmental impact and innovation. Studio briefs will be framed around the use of designed objects as vessels for sharing critical perspectives, to inspire debate and activate personal and societal shifts in perspective and behaviour. As a ‘change agent’ your research will be driven by real life issues affecting individuals and/or communities, and your design outcomes will educate and activate social and ecological advancement. Design outcomes for this studio will be framed by your response to the brief. You will work on one project throughout the course and have two sequential assessment tasks covering research, concept and design development, through to final design synthesis and presentation.
learning_outcomes: Use an iterative design process to develop highly resolved, well justified and clearly communicated design solutions.
Experiment with materials and processes relevant to the design and fabrication of furniture or lighting responding to the project brief and conceptual framework.
Develop an innovative design solution or solutions that inspire debate and activate personal and societal shifts in perspective and behaviour.

Use research to build knowledge on issues presented in the project brief and best practice theories, methods and design precedents addressing these issues. Synthesise into a conceptual framework for use in a design process.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Jewellery: Experimental Wearables
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course develops your knowledge, skill and understanding of designing and making contemporary wearables. The focus is on contemporary jewellery that challenges what wearables can be; experiments with materials and scale; and explores the conceptual relationships between jewellery and the body. A self-directed approach to learning is encouraged, through which you will acquire and apply skills in developing and articulating a project brief. You will be engaged in a series of preparatory workshops that introduce materials and processes suitable for the finished wearable or series of wearables. You will be encouraged to experiment with materials, and develop a conceptual and technical understanding of Jewellery and Object Design as applied to the body. In some instances you may need to liaise with industry partners to resolve your design solutions. Project documentation and presentation methods are expected to demonstrate independent thinking and the articulate communication of design ideas and concepts, supported by relevant practical and written research.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and discuss the work of designers, artists and writers engaged in research in the area of Jewellery and Object Design as it relates to large scale body works, installation and performance.
Experiment and record investigations into a variety of materials, processes and techniques including those undertaken in the studio and those conducted in liaison with industry partners.
Develop personal briefs through written work, drawings and models for contemporary body related design.
Demonstrate engagement with key themes in contemporary jewellery design practice through research, critical reading, group discussion and creative inquiry.
Apply research to record and create a variety of jewellery object solutions to projects.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Multi-Modal Experiences
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will investigate the principles of multi-modality in Experience Design and the ways they can be harnessed to enhance spatial encounters. You will critically analyse the role of digital technology in fostering new dimensions of experience, and explore how both digital and analogue modalities can challenge expectations, subvert norms, and innovate. Focusing on selected everyday experiences, you will propose and prototype innovative approaches, designing for specific subjects, actions, states, and circumstances through the tool of multi-modality.
learning_outcomes: Create an experience through an iterative design process that incorporates multi-modal components.
Demonstrate a capacity to document and communicate multi-modal designs to an advanced level.
Critically analyse experience designs with reference to a theory of multi-modality.
Investigate and apply knowledge of appropriate materials, digital and analogue interfaces and methods of assembling and integrating them.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Crisis Spaces: Interventions and Activations
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will explore and interrogate spatial interventions and the role they can play in the prevention and response to crises. Surveying, selecting, and researching a critical issue , you will investigate how the crisis can be either mitigated, or the needs of the community assisted, through a designed intervention. Across two assessment tasks, you will undertake an in-depth study into your selected crisis, its broader context, the stakeholders affected and any current solutions. In response to this research and through an iterative process you will propose and prototype new interventions of both a preventative and curative or remedial nature. With the intention of using your design skills to make a difference in critical times, the course presents you with a broad range of case studies from wearables to parasitic architecture and challenges you to consider and design solutions to urgent global issues.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate technical skill and an understanding of the materiality and fabrication requirements of a design intervention.
Develop a design intervention through an iterative process that considers community, culture, place, and human behaviour in times of crisis.
Research and analyse the contextual factors that impact a crisis.
Communicate a design intervention or activation using discipline specific methods.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Small Spaces: Representing Imagination and Experience in Model-Making
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Simultaneously representative and highly crafted miniature constructions in themselves, scale models are a critical tool for communicating a designer’s intent. This course focuses on model-making and provides you with a comprehensive range of both analogue and digital making techniques to ideate, iterate and create evocative small spatial encounters. Within the model-making process, key decisions will determine the materials used and construction choices you select for each model undertaken. Playing with ideas of scale inherent in the production of models, you will create and assemble miniature constructions. You will design and make models with a range of intents; from informing the viewer of spatial arrangements to igniting their imaginations with richly rendered designs of tiny, uninhabitable, wondrous worlds.
learning_outcomes: Ideate and translate a concept into a scaled representation of a design.
Identify and apply techniques appropriate to different uses.
Present and document a model to a professional standard.
Analyse and select an appropriate range of materials for models of different purposes.
Critically evaluate and construct scaled models using analogue and digital fabrication methods.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Playful Spaces: Soft Structures
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Acknowledging the value of play for adults, this course explores and experiments with different ‘soft’ structures and building methods. You are invited to produce human-centred spatial outcomes that facilitate unique connections between yourself and others, and the surrounding. Examining and experimenting with conventional notions of enclosure and construction methods of walls, ceilings, and floors, you will design and prototype solutions for temporary spaces uniquely suited to enhance playful experience and connection. You will examine tactility and other sensory activations to promote and produce immersive experiential outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Investigate and select relevant materials and construction methods in the development and prototyping of a spatial design solution.
Demonstrate and implement technical skills and knowledge in the construction and installation of a design solution.
Research, evaluate and apply theories of play to inform the development of experimental and participatory spatial design solutions.
Develop a range of documentation methods that communicate the experience of a spatial installation.
Demonstrate and implement independent and collaborative design process skills and reflection that evidence the contribution of each member of the team.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Illustration and Rendering
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will engage with traditional and contemporary methods for illustration, such as concept and process drawing, editorial illustration, comics and storyboarding for a range of graphic design contexts. During the course, you will practice and apply a range of techniques, processes, and media. By the end of the course, you will have developed your understanding and experience of applying a consistent approach to the task of illustrating narratives.
learning_outcomes: Experiment with a range of media and techniques for rendering and illustration.
Develop an extended narrative using a consistent approach to illustration.
Identify and apply methods of illustration appropriate to a brief.
Recognise and reference leading practitioners and movements in the field of illustration.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Graphics and Print/Making
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Graphics and Print/Making combines experimental typography and image making with a range of analogue and digital methods for making and printing. Historical and cultural precedents supporting your own concept development will be explored in weekly lectures. Open to students from a range of specialisations, studio time will combine concept generation in response to a creative design brief with workshop time in the Printmaking Studios and The Making Centre. You will be assessed on the iterative development of your concepts and documentation of your process, as well as your final screen printed and/or relief printed posters for exhibition.
learning_outcomes: Resolve an advanced portfolio of printed outcomes for in-studio exhibition.
Develop poster concepts that respond to social, cultural, political, ethical, and historical issues of our times.
Document experimental approaches to the development of image and typography through a process journal or visual diary.
Demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between digital and analogue making studios in the application of print techniques.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Publication Design
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course will introduce you to conceptual and technical principles of publication design. You will develop both small and extended publications from initial planning and concept development for client presentation, through to the creation of files ready for print and digital distribution. The course emphasises the development of skills using standard industry software, and the positioning of briefs in real world contexts. You will be introduced to the systematic processes that make designing publications more efficient. Assessment will be based on documentation of your conceptual and iterative design process, technical skills, and quality of your final design files.
learning_outcomes: Develop publication design concepts that respond to real world contexts.
Develop and resolve an extended publication for print or digital distribution using industry standard software.
Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of publication design including grids, typographic and image styles, and publication forms.
Document approaches to the development of publication design through a process journal or visual diary.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Visualisation and Wayfinding
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This studio-based course develops your skills in graphic design to create compelling stories through data, and inspirational experiences of navigation in public places. Assessment in this course will be on the basis of conceptual and technical approaches to projects that engage with data visualisation and wayfinding programs.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on the implications of information interfaces from the perspectives of designers, clients and users.
Develop and resolve design outcomes that aid with experiential navigation with reference to contemporary design standards.
Experiment with design concepts and techniques for innovative visual communication forms.
Develop and resolve design outcomes that communicate a concept through a range of data visualisation methods.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Drawing for Design
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Drawing is a critical tool for the design process, and is a must-have skill for design practitioners - even in today's highly computerised age. From analysing the client’s brief, developing a return brief, generating design concepts, communicating ideas with collaborators, to presenting possible solutions to the client, drawing is a simple but quick means that can significantly contribute to both design thinking and communication in the design process. Drawing for Design is designed to support essential design drawing skills through three studio projects focusing on observational drawing, visualisation drawing and presentation drawing. You will explore the materials to test different drawing methods and purposes; study techniques and ways to generate and reflect on ideas; examine shape, form, surface and structure to question the aesthetics, appearance and functions of 2D and 3D objects; as well as de-construct / re-construct 2D and 3D design products to make visible design ideas and concepts. This course will support you to develop your own personalised drawing methods, and use them as an effective means to support your design thinking mapping and design communications.
learning_outcomes: Develop a personalized drawing style that can be used as an effective tool for design studio projects.
Use different forms of drawings in the investigation of design outcomes
Integrate the drawing process (doing) with design procedure (thinking) for mapping and communication

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Web Design
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course will introduce you to the digital design industry by focusing on the processes involved in the creation, design and development of web content. It provides an introduction to the basic underlying technologies and methodologies of client-side web design and development. It covers basic web page composition using HTML, CSS and JavaScript as the underlying mechanism for realising creative, online content.
learning_outcomes: Design and build (Hand code) web pages using HTML and CSS as static web sites.
Demonstrate appropriate basic HTML and CSS skills during class tasks and coursework exercises.
Demonstrate relevant capacity for design composition, iterative planning and management for web projects.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Information Graphics
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Note: The code for this course was previously SDES4205. With continuous and rapid changes in communication technologies, it is increasingly challenging for consumers to process the vast amounts and diverse types of information. The proliferation of textual, visual, video, and audio data has produced a profound impact on how information is generated, packaged and communicated. This course introduces you to design principles and methods to influence the ways that the communication and presentation of data can be made intelligible to consumers as information.
learning_outcomes: Work individually and collaboratively to develop a design outcome in response to a brief
Demonstrate design iteration, critical thinking and reflection through documentation of process
Research and analyse issues from a range of information design case studies

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Textiles for Fashion
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Textiles for Fashion introduces you to textiles explored in the context of experimental fashion design. The course employs garment draping as a method to create fashion ideas that will embrace the manipulation of the textile surface. You will research and analyse industry precedents to understand how specific textile techniques are integrated into experimental fashion concepts. In addition, you will analyse the methods used to interpret and produce fashion ideas on the human form. A particular emphasis will be placed on the use of sustainable design principles, such as material reuse and waste reduction strategies for experimental design outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the creative possibilities in fashion design through draping techniques.
Conduct and critically analyse relevant fashion and textile research and effectively communicate outcomes in comprehensive and considered documentation.
Apply textile processes to fashion design to express an understanding of the aesthetic qualities inherent in textile design for fashion outcomes.
Evidence an understanding of responsible practice through the application of materials and processes appropriate to experimental fashion and textile design and production methods.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Interaction Design for AI
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course introduces you to fundamental principles of interaction design as they are applied specifically to the domain of AI applications, services and experiences. Interaction design is a field that has emerged in the digital age around the needs of designing effective physical and graphical user interfaces. Through broad design thinking centered around the experience of the human user, it is a field that is adept at handling emerging interaction contexts. You will encounter fundamental principles of user-centered design, design thinking, user experience, user interface design, rapid prototyping and user research. They will consider how traditional design principles apply to the design of AI experiences, and how AI introduces new constraints, affordances and design principles. You will critically examine AI experiences using frameworks and concepts from the interaction design field. You will undertake basic user-experience research to identify design issues. You will then work collaboratively to conceptualise, develop and prototype new ideas for AI apps, services and experiences, using design thinking methods to articulate user needs, identify affordances and ideate designs.
learning_outcomes: Analyse AI-based products, services and experiences from a user-experience perspective, using concepts including affordances, constraints, the user’s mental model and capacity for error.
Conduct user testing of new AI-based products, services and experiences.
Develop rapid prototypes of, and communicate the design of, new AI-based products, services and experiences.
Apply design thinking to AI in a range of cultural contexts with a foundation in ethical principles and awareness of socioeconomic context.
Use diverse sources of information, and diverse design thinking methods, to ideate new concepts for AI-based products, services and experiences.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Textiles: Illustration and Pattern Design
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This practice-based course offers undergraduate students the opportunity to engage with professional textile and fashion studios through real-world design briefs. Over the course of one term, you will develop original design responses informed by research, critical reflection, and studio feedback. Assessment is based on two key submissions that evaluate process, conceptual development, and final design outcomes focused upon the creation of motif illustration and pattern design. This course provides industry knowledge that will be incorporated into project work so that you understand industry requirements, and the strategies to respond to industry briefs for contemporary textile ranges. Working with studios on real-world design briefs provide a unique pathway to industry exposure and professional practice
learning_outcomes: Resolve a design project and showcase in a professional design portfolio.
Apply technical and visual communication proficiencies to a design project.
Demonstrate textile design skills that reflect industry or commercial standards.
Investigate creative responses to an industry design brief using research and reflection.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Smart Textiles
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Smart Textiles introduces a range of new technologies and processes developed by industry specialists, including artists and designers, combining emerging science and materials with traditional techniques for applications in the worlds of fashion, architecture, medical, engineering, science, and wearables. The course covers recent developments in textile fabrics, materials, structures, manufacture, technologies and processes, and acknowledges the textile traditions that these developments reference. Areas examined will include bio-fabrication, e-textiles, adaptive, soft-robotics, pneumatic, molecular/nano technology, and other emerging systems. The course encourages experimentation and hybrid approaches at the intersection of biological, digital, mechanical and analogue systems to design smart textiles that consider design futures of material scarcity and ethical responsibility. With the emergence of bio/fab/maker labs, new modes of production are emerging that challenge and provide alternatives to current unsustainable mainstream global textiles production. This course is based on an ‘open-source’, ‘maker’ mentality, leveraging the Art and Design Making Centre facilities to develop hybrid approaches utilising textile technologies such as knitting machines, digital embroidery, weaving looms, felting machines, 3D print, laser cutting and etching, digital print etc. The course enables you to investigate innovative textile concepts that explore the integration of the handmade with these emerging, new and smart technologies. Projects will involve research into new technologies and development of a self-directed project that aligns with individual interests to design a collection of your own unique smart textile samples. In this course, risk taking, exploration, critical speculation, and failures are celebrated along the pathway to discovery.
learning_outcomes: Explore the design and creation of sample prototypes using hand-made, existing and future textile technologies through experimentation with materials, techniques and processes.
Investigate and communicate recent innovation in textile technologies.
Apply research findings and propose how to integrate new technologies into textiles practice.
Demonstrate accurate, informative documentation of processes and experimentation results, including critical reflection and speculation of potential application of findings.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Studio 2: Design and Identity
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course builds on the fundamental principles and skills learnt in the introductory core course, FADA1010 Design Collaboration Studio 1. You will begin to establish your identity as a designer by responding to a range of design considerations and contexts. You will develop skills in design process including documentation of research and design development, as well as skills in communication and presentation methods.
learning_outcomes: Explore communication methods in design appropriate to a range of different contexts and considerations.
Present project outcomes using effective visual, written and verbal communication in digital and analogue formats.
Establish an identity as a designer through research and making methods.
Demonstrate an ability to work collaboratively and independently through design projects.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: FADA1010 or DDES1100

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Object 1: Objects and the Hand
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course introduces you to object design by emphasising thinking-through-making as a framework to creatively explore and generate ideas. Thinking-through-making describes an iterative design process that involves critical evaluation of making processes. In the course you will develop an understanding of how to work with, research and experience materials to produce a portfolio of design objects. You will also develop knowledge of contemporary craft in the field of design practice. A unique feature of this course is the acquisition of fundamental design and making skills in the Jewellery Studio that can be applied to specific design contexts including domestic and wearable objects.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and communicate a synthesis of concepts, forms and processes
Experiment with a range of materials and methods relevant to the design, fabrication and presentation of objects
Develop an iterative design process to create a series of objects

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: 3D Visualisation 1: 3D Virtual Objects
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This foundation studio course will develop your understanding of creative 3D computer visualisation. It will provide you with live, hands-on experience of the key technologies and creative thinking that is required when designing 3D virtual objects. You will be introduced to the historical and contemporary developments in 3D Visualisation and Computer Generated Imagery (CGI). Practical studio workshops will explore 3D CGI workflow for a variety of digital media, 3D modelling techniques, the application of foundational art and design theoretical thinking, and the previsualisation and planning of a virtual object. The course will primarily focus on constructing virtual objects for pre-rendering screen-based output. At the end of the course you will have planned and created a 3D virtual object through the application of a series of techniques and methods, giving you an introductory experience of the field of computer modelling.
learning_outcomes: Establish foundational self-directed previsualisation and data gathering processes to create a 3D virtual object.
Communicate a foundation level understanding of theoretical and conceptual thinking when working in the field of creative-led 3D computer visualisation.
Apply 3D Computer Generated Imagery workflow from planning to execution.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Experience 1: Spaces and Senses
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will explore the way people experience and interact with space, connecting this with ideas of the body, materiality, culture and spectacle. You will learn to design spatial, time-based and atmospheric conditions that affect engagement with the built world. The course offers multi-dimensional exploration of spatial experience that incorporates ideas from philosophy, architecture and neuroscience to better understand, anticipate and design for human behaviour. Through the design of installations you are invited to experiment, examine, measure and critically interpret space, time and narratives with an emphasis on the investigation of social, cultural, ethical and environmental sustainability issues and practices. You will work with diverse design and presentation methods to develop skills and techniques that communicate your ideas. Advanced study in this discipline can lead to careers in exhibition and event design as well as pathways centred on your own inquiry-led design practice.
learning_outcomes: Experiment with methods of spatial production
Identify and map elements of experience
Identify and describe a conceptual framework and explore practical responses through iterative design processes
Organise information to communicate spatial and experiential solutions to an introductory standard

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Graphics 1: Image and Type
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course offers you an introductory opportunity to develop critical skills in the creation of graphic images through photography and various types of illustration. You will then begin to understand how to manipulate typography within formal grids and structures, and as an expressive medium. Graphic design is built on a sound understanding of the relationship between image and type. Whether you are intending to work either commercially or experimentally within the visual communications industry, or as a design entrepreneur working in another context, this course will provide you with fundamental graphic design skills. Through application to your individual practice, you will understand the importance of research, an iterative design process, ethical considerations, as well as the personal and presentation skills required to communicate a concept.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of typographic fundamentals
Demonstrate a range of techniques for the creation and manipulation of images
Generate and refine design concepts using an iterative process
Present design projects using effective communication techniques
Evidence research and experimentation through comprehensive and considered documentation

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Interaction 1: Principles and Practices
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This foundational course in the Interaction Design disciplinary specialisation introduces the core principles, methods, and processes that underpin the design of interactive experiences between humans and technology. You will explore how user needs, behaviours, and contexts inform design decisions, and develop an understanding of the complete interaction design process from ideation to iterative evaluation. Emphasis is placed on prototyping as a way of thinking and testing through both physical and digital methods, aligned with established methods of inquiry in industry. Through hands-on activities and reflective practice, you will build the critical and creative skills necessary to design cohesive, meaningful, and engaging user experiences.
learning_outcomes: Conduct evidence-based user experience research towards understanding key aspects of interaction design within physical and digital contexts
Design physical prototypes and mock-ups that effectively explore interaction design concepts using a variety of making and creative approaches
Apply theoretical knowledge and practical skills towards analysing and evaluating user experiences
Document and reflect on the design process, demonstrating critical thinking and professional communication

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Textiles 1: Concepts and Context
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course will introduce you to the narrative aspect of textiles, and their story telling ability via patterns, materials and construction. It will familiarise you with the qualities and characteristics of textiles, as well as the key processes for designing and creating them through the integration of hand and digital design methods. You will consider social, cultural, environmental and sustainable themes that will become influential to your textile practice. Throughout the course you will employ research methodologies appropriate to the textile design industry and investigate selected textile theorists and writers to critically evaluate, document and reflect. You will investigate the local culture of textile practitioners to inspire and develop unique surface designs. In this course, you are encouraged to play, experiment and learn from failure and take creative risks in the development of cohesive conceptually-based textiles.
learning_outcomes: Conduct practice-based research into textile artist’s/designer’s practices
Reflect on their own experimental textiles using methods to document and evaluate appropriate to the textiles design industry
Design and create textiles with an integrated/ cohesive conceptual basis/ design narrative
Identify and describe textile fibres, structures and processes using language and terminology of the textiles industry

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Fashion 1: Designing Fashion
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Designing Fashion provides you with foundational knowledge of the fashion design process. The course provides understanding and practical skills in the phases from research and concept development to fashion design ideas and sampling for product realisation. You will examine fashion theories, the fashion system, and analyse industry precedents to understand how individual ideas are formed into a fashion collection. This course also introduces fashion for sustainability and the circular economy, particularly exploring the impacts that arise in the production and consumption of garments to identify new responsible opportunities for future fashion practice.
learning_outcomes: Conduct and critically analyse relevant research and effectively communicate outcomes in comprehensive and considered documentation
Apply appropriate skills and knowledge to design, develop and communicate the fashion collection
Demonstrate and apply an understanding of the fashion design process to express innovative ideas for a specific industry market or end user
Evidence an understanding of responsible practice through the application of materials and processes appropriate to the fashion design brief

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Design Professional Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course will help you develop essential skills to transition into the rapidly changing design industry through the principles of professionalism and a commercial grounding in the realities and complexities of design practice. By reflecting on your unique strengths and talents, you will begin to position yourself relative to the challenges of contemporary design practice to demonstrate your expertise for potential employers, clients and collaborators. Through a combination of lectures, workshops, open dialogue and roleplaying, the course will cover design practice essentials ranging from understanding business and finance, legal and statutory constraints, business communication, self actualisation, interpersonal relations, and client and stakeholder management. By acknowledging the equally important roles of entrepreneurship, leadership and followship, you will be better prepared to navigate the design industry of the future.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on current and emerging modes of design practice associated with an emerging professional design identity.
Communicate effectively with peers, potential employers/clients, and other stakeholders within design practice.
Evaluate the impact of statutory, ethical, intellectual, social and financial constraints on design practice.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 48 UOC overall, and enrolment in the Integrated Design major specialisation in a Bachelor of Design program.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Design History and Theory 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Design is ubiquitous and manifests itself through objects, environments, processes and systems. It does not exist in a vacuum. It is contingent on the wider contexts of the world we live in and, importantly, its historical precedence. Design History and Theory 1 outlines historical frames and narratives which have shaped design as a discipline and a profession through the 19th and 20th centuries. The course will introduce you to some of the core movements, theories and protagonists, and equip you with tools to independently explore various trajectories of design and their contemporary legacies. Through a series of tutorial exercises, assessment tasks, and weekly readings, you will develop transferable academic skills, including research, referencing, interpretation and critical analysis of visual and written material. At the conclusion of this course, you will understand the relevance of the study of history and theory to the practice of design.
learning_outcomes: Position design in historical contexts and understand the social and cultural narratives of objects, systems, spaces and modes of communication.
Explore the relevance and purpose of design history and theory to contemporary design practice.
Develop academic research literacy and skills in referencing, interpretation and critical analysis of visual and written material.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Studio 3: Design and Empathy
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This core design studio will advance your empathic design skills by engaging with “others” and immersing yourself in explorative practices and experiential adventures to inspire action by design. You will further develop your capacity for perspective taking and challenging personal assumptions to form design insights and objectives that guide unique project outcomes. A value is placed on curiosity, reflexivity and making connections in your research to contribute to prosocial impacts.
learning_outcomes: Develop confidence in creative exploration of ideas, materiality and processes as a means to challenging personal assumptions and designing with criticality.
Design solutions that foster prosocial impacts and contribute positively to society and broader ecosystems / environment.
Apply the craft of reflexivity, active listening and ongoing dialogue as fundamental design research practices to design for and with others.
Cultivate curiosity regarding “others” (people, materials and processes), as an essential characteristic of empathy in design practices.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DDES1101

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Studio 4: Design and Society
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Note: The course code for this course was previously DDES2100. This course provides a platform for collaboration through a real-world industry or stakeholder brief that responds to issues impacting society. Collaboration and followship are the key drivers of the design process. You will experience contributing to a dynamic and collaborative design process alongside the achievement of an individual project outcome.
learning_outcomes: Communicate design process and conceptual responses to peers and industry stakeholders through effective written, visual and verbal methods.
Reflect on the impact of contemporary scholarly discourse, research and the nexus between collaborative and individual practice on their work.
Evaluate and respond to an industry-driven brief through individual and collaborative practice, engagement, and agile creative development.
Demonstrate research appropriate to a range of stakeholders and contexts through documentation of process.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DDES2101 or FADA2020 or DDES2103

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: 3D Visualisation 2: Virtual Worlds
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This intermediate course within the 3D Visualisation disciplinary studio will help you explore 3D computer visualisations through the creation of a digital 3D environment. Building on the skills already acquired in the introductory course to create a 3D virtual asset in isolation, you will now create multiple assets before laying them out in a complete, fully realised virtual scene. To successfully complete this process, you will need to consider how assets engage and relate to each other and the space they inhabit. The creation of the virtual scene will be conceptually driven and supported by theoretical research. Engaging studio workshops will explore the full Computer-Generated Imagery (CGI) workflow with a particular emphasis on CGI lighting, rendering techniques and clear art direction. This course will provide you with an increased ability to apply the knowledge and skills that are used in the field of computer modelling and Computer-Generated visualisation to the creation of your own 3D virtual worlds.
learning_outcomes: Establish and apply comprehensive self-directed previsualisation and reference gathering methodologies to create a 3D virtual scene for digital media output.
Communicate and integrate detailed theoretical and conceptual processes when working in the field of creative, narrative driven 3D computer visualisation.
Plan and implement 3D Computer Generated Imagery workflow in the creation of a fully resolved 3D virtual scene for digital media output.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DDES1110

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: 3D Visualisation 3: Interactive Environments
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This advanced course within the 3D Visualisation disciplinary studio will provide you with the opportunity to immerse yourself in the field of computer modelling and computer-generated visualisation and refine your knowledge, methods and skills. Expanding in complexity and drawing on the skills already acquired in the preceding courses, you will design and create an experiential, explorable and 3D virtual world. Scholarly research will provide an informed foundation for the creation of a sophisticated, conceptually focussed virtual environment. Engaging studio workshops will explore the full computer-generated imagery workflow with a particular emphasis on how 3D assets engage and relate to each other in a realtime platform, low-poly modelling and a high level of art direction in the creation of your own virtual world.
learning_outcomes: Examine and execute comprehensive self-directed previsualisation and reference gathering methodologies to create a realtime environment for digital media output
Articulate and synthesis detailed theoretical and conceptual processes to the design and creation of narrative driven realtime interactive 3D visualisations
Plan, test and implement 3D Computer Generated pipeline and workflow techniques in the creation of a fully resolved realtime interactive 3D environment for digital media output
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DDES2110

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Object 2: Objects and Place
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course within the Object disciplinary studio will introduce you to the contextual and relational significance of objects. Applying thinking through-making skills you will focus on the context of culture and place to examine social practices relating to dining rituals. Through this contextual lens, you will learn how to develop an understanding of the role of objects in facilitating social and meaningful interactions. Conceptual outcomes will be designed and made using digital technologies and craft processes in the Ceramics Studio. Central to the processes learned is the potential for objects to be produced as multiples using ceramics casting and 3D printing methods.
learning_outcomes: Critique the contextual and relational significance of design objects through the cultural and historical analysis of objects and place
Experiment with a range of materials and methods to apply findings for the design, fabrication and presentation of ceramic objects
Consider the ethical and environmental consequences of ceramic practices relevant to ceramic objects and prototyping
Design and develop innovative ceramic objects that integrate concepts, forms, materials and processes
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DDES1120

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Object 3: Objects and the World
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this advanced course within the Object disciplinary studio, you will explore design-nature relationships through objects and material-led enquiries. You will build on the hand-making and digital skills acquired in the introductory and intermediate Object 1 and 2 courses, developing your knowledge of materiality to engage with and critique ideas relating to ecologies and the natural world. Informed by ecological frameworks such as the issue of material resources or biophilic design influences you will develop material experimentation and prototypes to gain greater insight of your role as a responsible designer and agent of change.
learning_outcomes: Examine and critique the significance of responsible design practice through an understanding of impact and engagement regarding issues of ecology and its application to object design
Demonstrate, apply and synthesise analogue and digital literacies relevant to object design and prototyping
Investigate, document and communicate an effective synthesis of concepts, forms, materials and processes through the design and development of objects
Interrogate and evaluate a range of materials and methods and apply findings to the design, fabrication and presentation of objects
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DDES2120

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Experience 2: Spaces of Exhibition
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This intermediate course within the Experience disciplinary studio will explore the possibilities of exhibition spaces as active sites for participation and collaboration. Building on foundational knowledge and skills acquired in the introductory course, you will explore the cultures of display that influence exhibition practice. It investigates strategies employed by exhibition designers to frame objects and ideas in order to communicate their meaning to a diverse participating public. More than this, you will be encouraged as a designer to be an agent of change – provoking active engagement with collections and cultural spaces. The studio-based classes will explore ideas and theories for designing for museums and galleries. You will develop a creative inquiry-based around narrative composition and sequencing of spaces, and will learn about the integration of mediated experiences and technologies as an important element in contemporary exhibition practice. Adopting an iterative and collaborative methodology you will propose display strategies and prototype designs with consideration of different materials and constructions methods, that can ultimately reframe a visitor’s experience of ideas, objects and spaces.
learning_outcomes: Research, analyse and apply comprehensive theoretical and practical knowledge of experience and exhibition design to inform the development of display strategies and participative environments
Demonstrate and implement problem-solving and design process skills to effectively communicate an exhibition project to a professional standard
Accurately communicate design ideas and outcomes using industry recognised methods and techniques
Investigate ideas, materials and construction methods and apply findings to the development of exhibition design solutions
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DDES1130

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Experience 3: Spaces for Performance
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This advanced course within the Experience disciplinary studio will explore the relationships between people, space, spectacle and culture. Focusing on events as rich, multifaceted sites of experience, you will develop and test ideas and conditions for heightened and collective experiences. Through considered design for a performance, you will continue to hone both analogue and digital skills to an advanced level to represent and communicate your research, ideation and development process. Additional knowledge and skills relevant to the theatre, film, exhibition and event industries will be developed to convey complex (and often unscripted) narrative structures as well as atmosphere and effect.
learning_outcomes: Identify, define and communicate emergent themes relating to social performance and experiential encounter
Speculate on pre-existing attitudes within a design-based context and with comprehensive documentation evidence enquiry
Interpret and deliver an innovative and impactful design outcome, creating a complex and descriptive picture of public performance
prerequisites: Prerequisite: DDES2130

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Graphics 3: Place and Space
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
