This elective course is open to all students enrolled in postgraduate Education programs. It is recommended that students complete this course as early as possible in their program as it will support their engagement and success in other postgraduate Education courses.
learning_outcomes: Communicate effectively with peers, lecturers, tutors and other stakeholders in a range of different academic contexts and activities.
Critically evaluate a range of texts common in education contexts.
Assess your own communication skills and those of your students and implement strategies for improvement.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Education Project 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The purpose of this course is to support you in evaluating and developing your thesis writing abilities and skills. Weekly sessions cover the overall structuring of the thesis; writing the introduction; the literature review; the methodology chapter; discussion chapters; the conclusion and the abstract and understanding examiner expectations with an emphasis on managing the writing process over an extended time period and on managing large amounts of texts. Note: This course is only available to EdPrDoc students.
learning_outcomes: Use the linguistic and discursive resources of academic English to draft thesis chapters, journal articles and conference abstracts
Analyse and compare the structure and organisation of the research genres of the thesis, the journal article, the conference paper, and the oral presentation.
Explain the choices as to how to structure and organise a research thesis or other research genre with reference to current research into advanced academic and professional writing

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Education Project 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The purpose of this course is to provide you with an opportunity to learn how to prepare a research proposal in education. This course reviews the steps in the research process and considers the elements, structure and organisation, and writing style of research proposals in education. It will enable you to plan educational research and outline the steps using appropriate structure and organisation and writing style for a research proposal in education. It will assist you with preparing your proposal for confirmation as well as your oral presentation. During this Term, you will work primarily with your supervisors to prepare for your confirmation in Term 3. Confirmation consists of presentation of your research proposal to your confirmation panel together with an oral presentation on your project. Note: This course is only available to EdPrDoc students.
learning_outcomes: Identify and explain the elements, structure, organisation, and writing style of a research proposal in education.
Recognise and address the practical considerations in a research proposal for a research project in education.
Identify and explain the steps in the research process.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Education Seminar 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This interactive student-led course is a continuation of EDST 5038. It provides you with academic support in analysing, presenting and writing up research results. It is intended that you will report the results, analysis and conclusions of a small research project, with opportunities for academic and peer feedback. Note: This course is only available to EdPrDoc students.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate meaning and importance of research findings, interpret and describe the implications with reference to research and practice.
Construct a comprehensive, well structured explanation of findings from research, making links between evidence obtained and existing knowledge, and drawing appropriate conclusions.
Present data using text, figures and tables, formatted to maximise clarity and ease of interpretation to illustrate key findings from educational research.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Education Seminar 1
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The purpose of this course is to introduce you to ethical matters and dilemmas that you encounter in conducting research. The course will cover aspects of project planning including feasibility concerns around access, participants and time, along with examining sources of tension in the ethical debate, ethical problems and issues confronting the researcher and the national framework and guidelines for research integrity. The course will enable you to plan a research project and identify ethical risks and apply ethical principles to a research project, and to your own professional conduct. Note: This course is only available to EdPrDoc students.
learning_outcomes: Explain and apply practical strategies to manage the fieldwork process in educational research.
Analyse and interpret data using appropriate qualitative and/or quantitative methods in educational research.
Apply ethical principles to the collection and analysis of data in educational research.
Apply strategies to maintain data integrity before, during, and after data collection in educational research.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Foundation 1: University Study Skills in Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you are introduced to UNSW study skills, procedures, academic expectations and educational research. The course aims to increase your knowledge and understanding of communication, research and study skills to assist you in developing an understanding of university expectations as a postgraduate student. You will develop essential study skills through learning about and writing about UNSW academic expectations and educational research.
learning_outcomes: Examine and apply general academic skills to represent and justify critical points of view in written and oral accounts in a university assessment structure
Engage in critical thinking and reasoning to express coherent points of view informed by evidence drawn from academic sources
Critically engage with and interpret academic literature to inform understandings of fields of study in education
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in the 96 UOC or 72 UOC plan of a Master of Education or Master of Educational Leadership

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Quantitative Research
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will learn about quantitative research methods and data analysis at an advanced level. The course will cover research design, population/sampling selection, construction of data collection tools, various types of data collection methods, and data analysis such as multiple regression and factor analysis. Emphasis will be given to the selection of statistical analyses that would be appropriate for different types of quantitative data.
learning_outcomes: Use computer software programs to analyse quantitative data
Understand key concepts and terminology associated with various quantitative data analysis
Select and apply appropriate statistical methods to analyse specific types of quantitative data
Create a set of research questions that can be addressed by quantitative data
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Applied Linguistics program. Or EDST5448 or EDST5458 and enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Foundation 2: Fields of Practice in Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you are introduced to topics in Education. This course aims to introduce you to the main specialisations of Education and to assist you in better understanding Education. The course has a particular focus on the specialised streams in the Master of Education. You will develop an understanding in the various specialisations that define Education. These include Curriculum and Assessment, Educations Studies, Education Systems, Gifted Education, TESOL, Special Education and Educational Psychology.
learning_outcomes: Examine how policies and institutions shape educational practice in local, state, national and global contexts
Evaluate how the role of teachers, students, content and context are understood in different fields of practice in education
Critically review theory and research in education to enhance understandings of fields of practice in education
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in the 96 UOC or 72 UOC plan of a Master of Education or Master of Educational Leadership

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Behaviour Support Strategies
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The focus of this course is on applied behaviour analysis, and how it is accomplished through the use of functional behavioural assessment and skills training. You will learn about the models, theories, and philosophies that form the basis of sound inclusive educational and behavioural practice. You will learn how to assess behaviour, teach new skills, and manage behaviour, both academic and social. The strengths and weaknesses of common school practices for decreasing students' inappropriate behaviour will be discussed, and strategies for promoting prosocial behaviour will be described. You will practice collecting and analysing data and use this information to write behavioural intervention plans. You will also use the knowledge gained in the course to design and implement a social skills training lesson.
learning_outcomes: Identify contemporary and historical issues in behavioural intervention
Collect and analyse data to plan behavioural interventions
Design a positive reinforcement-based classroom management plan that promotes and supports effective teaching and learning
Identify research-based strategies for understanding behaviour and managing classrooms
prerequisites: Prerequisite: EDST5133 and enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Learning: Psychological and Social Perspectives
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: One of the central needs of a teacher is to understand how their students learn. In this course, you will learn about how people learn generally, the degree to which people differ in how they learn, and the strategies required to teach them effectively. You will study core educational psychology topics - including development, cognition, and motivation - and observe them in action in classrooms. In assessment, you will articulate these issues, and report on observations of teaching in a way that bridges theory, research, and practice.
learning_outcomes: Describe teaching strategies that respond to the diversity of students and their learning needs.
Explain how students learn and the implications for teaching
Interpret research into how students learn and how it applies to teaching
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs; 8926 Master of Teaching (Secondary), 8913 Master of Education, or 8963 Master of Educational Leadership

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Teaching Methods for High Incidence Disabilities
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The focus of this course is on students with high-incidence disabilities. In this course, students will be presented with cognitive, perceptual, language, academic learning, and social-emotional characteristics of these populations. Issues in assessment, curriculum and instruction, and placement will also be discussed. This course will provide students with instruction on applying the goals, intervention strategies, and procedures related to psychodynamic, behavioural, biophysical, and ecological approaches to individuals with disabilities.
learning_outcomes: Use research-based strategies for individual curriculum-based assessment, planning, and instruction
Explain laws, policies, and ethical principles regarding education of students with special needs
Discuss seminal issues in education for students with special needs
Conduct independent research into a current topic/issue relevant to learners with learning disabilities, intellectual disabilities, ADHD, or emotional disabilities
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Current Issues in Education 2
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course is part of the Education Professional Doctorate program. The purpose of this course is to provide you with an overview of questions of researcher positionality and the development of a background context in which your research is situated. The course will be conducted seminar style. It is designed to help you articulate your positionality in relation to your research topic and methodology; and to successfully locate academic literature related to questions of researcher standpoint, ethics, and reflexivity. The course also supports the development of the background to the study, in which you will identify and evaluate literature relevant to the issues in education you address in your developing thesis. Note: This course is available only to EdPrDoc students.
learning_outcomes: Critically engage with theory, research, and practice to identify current issues in education.
Use a systematic process to locate and evaluate academic literature related to developing a background to the research topic in education.
Articulate a positionality statement and provide an argument for issues shaping your stance as a researcher.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Intellectual Disabilities
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Students with intellectual disabilities face numerous challenges in educational environments. You will learn about characteristics of students with intellectual disabilities (including issues of definition), relevant legislative requirements, and how to use assessment for educational intervention. You will learn about effective evidence-based practices that you can use to assist students with intellectual disabilities accomplish their educational goals. You will learn about curriculum-based strategies and curriculum adjustments and modifications that you can use in your teaching practice. In this course, great emphasis is placed on a life-span approach to people with intellectual disabilities and their families; and why it is important for professionals to have a holistic perspective. Thus, you will also learn about issues related to social and community inclusion, family, peer and partner relationships of people with intellectual disabilities. You will become acquainted with issues and supports relevant to adults with intellectual disabilities. Throughout the course, you will also learn about the importance of diverse transitions in the lives of people with intellectual disabilities and how these can be supported.
learning_outcomes: Critically engage with the theories underlying the prevailing attitudes towards people with intellectual disabilities.
Perform curriculum adjustments to assist students with intellectual disabilities to meet educational outcomes.
Apply legislation and government policies related to education and life of people with intellectual disabilities in their professional judgements and decisions.
Articulate current issues and trends in regards to the field of intellectual disabilities to relevant stakeholders.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Students on the Autism Spectrum
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Students on the autism spectrum face immense challenges in educational environments. You will engage with current knowledge about characteristics and effective evidence-based practices used to assist students on the autism spectrum to accomplish their educational goals. You will engage with theories, societal attitudes, legislation, and policy to develop your professional judgments and teaching practices. You will learn instructional and curriculum-based strategies and curriculum adjustments that you can use in your teaching practice. You will also learn about challenges faced by families of students on the autism spectrum, and learn effective strategies to promote home-school collaboration. You will become acquainted with issues and supports relevant to adults on the autism spectrum.
learning_outcomes: Critically engage with the theories underlying the prevailing attitudes towards people on the autism spectrum.
Perform curriculum adjustments to assist students on the autism spectrum to meet educational outcomes.
Apply legislation and policy related to the education and life of people on the autism spectrum to professional judgments and decisions.
Articulate current issues and trends in regards to the field of the autism spectrum to relevant stakeholders.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Curriculum and Assessment
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will examine how the policies and practices of today connect with historical contexts, traditions, ideologies and beliefs about curriculum and assessment and how future developments are shaped by events and decisions made in the past. The course covers key issues, policies and events that have shaped reform agendas in the development of curriculum and assessment in New South Wales and Australia on a national level and will consider how these compare to developments internationally. You will be given the opportunity to research, analyse and discuss issues in curriculum and assessment of interest to you.
learning_outcomes: Critically review theory and research in the academic literature to enhance understanding of the relationships between curriculum, assessment and reporting.
Evaluate the impact of ideologies, beliefs and traditions on the role of teachers, students, content and context in examples of curriculum and assessment.
Examine key issues and events that have informed curriculum and assessment change in local, national and international contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Indigenous Contexts of Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course explores the historical, political and social context of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education in Australia and critically examines the social and societal factors that shape Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students’ experiences and outcomes. It introduces you to current research, theoretical frameworks and practical strategies to help in developing your skills and knowledge to critically reflect on and respond to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students’ issues in education. The central focus of the course is to prepare you to meet the Australian Professional Standards that directly concern Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education: the teaching of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students (AITSL 1.4), and the embedding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, histories and heritage across the curriculum (AITSL 2.4). This course includes a three-day intensive “on Country” Immersion Program which will introduce and engage you with local Aboriginal communities, cultures and perspectives, to help raise your awareness about the need for a focus on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives in schools and in teacher education. Successful completion of this course requires you to satisfactorily complete the Immersion Program. More details will be available on Moodle.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of effective strategies to work specifically with Indigenous students, families and communities
Develop a range of curriculum materials and pedagogical practices to embed Indigenous perspectives across the curriculum

Evaluate the concepts of race, culture, identity and diversity with regard to Indigenous education and the impact of historical and socio-political, cultural and linguistic factors on learning and teaching of Indigenous students
Analyse the ways in which current Aboriginal education policies, anti-racism, and programs and services impact on school systems, schools and teachers
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs, 8925 or 8926

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Professional Inquiry
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will examine the professional issues faced by first year teachers, including the culture of isolation (characteristic of many schools); transition shock; workload issues; and classroom management challenges. Strategies for addressing these challenges will be explored. These include mentoring, peer support, problem-based discussion groups, and the sharing of personal narratives and dialogue through face-to-face and online forums.
learning_outcomes: Implement strategies for addressing particular issues arising in the first years of professional practice through Action Research.
Analyse the nature and scope of the multiple challenges facing teachers in their first year of professional practice.

Identify practices that contribute positively to the professional trajectories of new teachers. This includes for example, mentoring, peer support, group problem-solving, collaborative planning, shared narratives, dialogue, and critical reflection.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: EDST6760

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Professional Practice for Special Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will complete 25 days of advanced professional practice, including high-level teaching, observation and critical reflection in the area of special education, together with peer observations and school-based fieldwork. You will gain an advanced level of knowledge and skills in teaching students with special needs, and as a graduate of the program, you will meet the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers in the area of professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Operate independently both within the classroom and within the wider school community and interact effectively with colleagues and members of the wider school community
Design and critically evaluate appropriate programs, including needs analysis, syllabus design, program organisation and processes of assessment and evaluation in Special Education
Monitor, document and report on a range of students' development and implement appropriate feedback mechanisms to enhance learning and teaching

Plan, implement and critically evaluate challenging and original lessons and units of work using a range of different strategies to meet expected curriculum outcomes and varied student needs and interests
Reflect on, describe and critically evaluate one's own professional practice and take responsibility in collaboration with others to identify and address their own learning needs
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 24 uoc overall, and enrolment in a Special Education specialisation in a postgraduate Education program. Students must have completed EDST5106 or complete EDST5106 concurrently. Consent required.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Qualitative Research
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: You will explore, and learn to critique, qualitative research in education; and you will be introduced to some key methodological issues by looking at published and unpublished qualitative writing across different sub-fields of educational research. You will learn about different epistemological and methodological approaches, and, by the end of the course, you will have a good awareness of the issues and components you need to design a small-scale qualitative research project of your own.
learning_outcomes: Critically engage and evaluate qualitative educational research literature in terms of its methodology.
Evaluate qualitative research texts.
Explain methodological issues (such as positionality and ethical considerations) and how these relate to real-world research.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Applied Linguistics program. Or EDST5448 or EDST5458 and enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Coaching and Mentoring in Educational Leadership
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will focus on the role that learning conversations, mentoring and coaching can play in the development of teachers. Models and perspectives on coaching and mentoring will be explored, as well as the development of listening and reflection skills. Action research by students will provide feedback on the various models of mentoring and coaching.
learning_outcomes: Apply theory to a workplace by conducting coaching and mentoring conversations
Critically reflect on experiences of coaching and mentoring in schools in relation to theory
Critically reflect on the application of learning in a school context by mentoring/coaching others using action research methodology
Critically analyse mentoring and coaching skills
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Transitions in the Lives of Students with Disabilities
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, students will be provided with an overview of the numerous transitions students with disabilities face. The focus of the course will be on the preparation, support and planning required for transitioning students with disabilities. Contemporary legislation, polices, methods and service delivery for the education and transitional programming for students with disabilities at different levels (early childhood to primary level, primary to secondary level, secondary to tertiary level, secondary level to vocation) will be discussed.
learning_outcomes: Identify evidence-based strategies, resources, and materials used for transition planning for individuals with disabilities into and out of school and post-school environments.
Describe the role of teachers, transition specialists, and community agencies related to transition planning and services.
Explain your understanding of different transitions stages, policies, and current issues in transition planning.
Identify support systems that promote self-determination and integration in to community and work environments.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed EDST6761 or EDST6765

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Supporting Diverse Learners: Inclusive Practices
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will survey the characteristics, training, and educational needs of students with disabilities, gifts and talents, and culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, emphasising accommodating students with diverse needs in inclusive settings. This includes legal mandates and regulations; characteristics and educational needs of students with diverse needs; and practical, research-based instructional techniques that can be used with these students in the general education classroom.
learning_outcomes: Apply research-based decision making to select appropriate programming options and strategies for students with diverse needs
Explain differentiated teaching and learning
Explain current issues and attitudes affecting policymaking, identification of needs, and educational provision for diverse student needs in NSW
Develop strategies to implement NSW Education Standards Authority (NESA) syllabus documents including literacy, multi-literacies, Indigenous support and EAL/D support
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs, 8925 or 8926

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Oral Communication Across the Curriculum
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will explore current theories underlying oral communication skills, focusing in particular on the learning and teaching of second or additional language learners in schools, both locally and internationally. Topics include theoretical and practical perspectives on oral communication across the curriculum; cognitive and metacognitive processes involved in speaking and listening; issues of intelligibility and pronunciation; genres of speaking and implications for listening; learning and teaching students for whom English is a second language or dialect planning; developing oral communication tasks and activities; assessing speaking and listening in the content areas.
learning_outcomes: Identify, describe and critically evaluate current theoretical assumptions regarding the teaching of oral communication nationally and internationally.
Apply knowledge and understanding of oral communication processes to the evaluation, teaching and assessment of oral communication in professional contexts
Demonstrate a sound understanding of key theoretical and practical approaches in learning and teaching of oral communication through critical inquiry of professional contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Inclusive Education: Policy, Planning and Pedagogy
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course will provide an overview of the principles, policies, and philosophies underpinning inclusion. The Universal Design for Learning approach to curriculum design for students with disabilities or diverse needs will be a central focus as well as evidence and research-based approaches to teaching these students in mainstream school settings. The role of teachers, special educators, and the leadership team in promoting the successful inclusion of students with diverse needs will also be highlighted.
learning_outcomes: Adjust curriculum via modification or accommodations to assist students with disability to meet educational outcomes.
Discuss the prevailing attitudes towards people with disability.
Explain key terms related to disability and inclusion, and articulate the current issues and trends in the inclusion of students with disability.
Apply knowledge of legislation and government policies related to the education and inclusion of people with disabilities using professional judgment and current research.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed EDST6761 or EDST6765

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Creating Engaging Learning Environments
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will draw on a variety of theoretical and practical perspectives, principles and research to provide pre-service teachers with a depth and breadth of knowledge that will enable professional decision-making and practice in establishing classroom management and ensuring student engagement in learning.
learning_outcomes: Plan, manage and deliver productive lessons.
Manage difficult behaviours and create a safe and productive learning environment.
Develop and maintain a positive learning environment in the classroom.
Use strategies and tools to address the diverse learning needs of students and maintain learning engagement.
Engage students effectively in the learning process through activities incorporated into a classroom management plan.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in one of the following programs, 8925 Master of Teaching (Primary) or 8926 Master of Teaching (Secondary) or 8913 Masters of Education or 8963 Educational Leadership

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Language, Literacy and Numeracy
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The course will engage in a substantive exploration of the relationships between language, literacy, and numeracy, assessment and student learning. The course will draw on theory, research and practice related to assessing and teaching students with diverse language and literacy backgrounds and skills in a variety of secondary school contexts.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and principles associated with assessment for learning, including self and peer assessment and feedback, and the use of assessment data and process to identify and improve language, literacy and numeracy skills across the curriculum.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the nature and role of language, literacy and numeracy in the secondary mainstream classroom.
Develop knowledge of a range of effective assessment and teaching strategies for students with diverse language and literacy backgrounds and skills in the secondary school classroom.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 8926 Master of Teaching (Secondary)

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Critical Issues and Practice in Visual Arts Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will use a realist philosophical framework to explore critical issues and practice in contemporary visual arts education. Investigations of the complex relationships between practices in art and art education, creativity, and the nature of students’ learning in art will provide a basis on which you can then critically examine a range of issues in curriculum design, implementation and assessment in Visual Arts in school, state, national and global contexts. Curriculum fads including visual literacy, visual culture and STEAM will be critically analysed in relation to the ways in which they may distort or support curriculum in Visual Arts.
learning_outcomes: Apply a realist philosophy to explain how constraints function in art, art education, students’ reasoning, creativity and curriculum development at state, national and international levels.
Examine issues in programming and assessing art making and art interpretation in art education in school based and broader educational contexts.

Critically analyse and explain how curriculum fads, practices, politics and power relations affect the design and pedagogy of art education curriculum including its assessment and status within the broader curriculum, in local, national and international contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Critically Engaging with Indigenous Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will be immersed in the competing and politicised discourses and school level practices that play a part in what is known as Indigenous education in Australia. The aim of the course is to equip you with skills, knowledge and the confidence that will support you in becoming an active and aware contributor to improving teaching practices and learning outcomes within the Indigenous education landscape. Informed by ideas and strategies coming from a range of theoretical frameworks, you will critically engage with the literature and research that underpins Indigenous education, challenging you to reflexively position yourself within this landscape as active agents of change.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and articulate the historical and contemporary politicised framing of Indigenous education in Australian education policy, curricular, pedagogic and assessment practices.
Articulate a critically reflective understanding of their socio-cultural perspective, position and power within the Indigenous education landscape.
Identify and justify suitable and effective local level education responses that are meaningfully engaging with the complexities of teaching and learning in Indigenous studies.
Select and apply ideas from relevant theoretical perspectives to critique the literature and research linked with Indigenous education.
Articulate a theoretically and empirically well informed critique of the ‘deficit’ perspective in relation to Indigenous students.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Education in Context
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The claim that context matters is ubiquitous in education. What that means and how it plays out in the provision of education across the lifespan and within and beyond traditional education sites is far less known. This course is designed to deepen your understanding of the intimate relations between education and context. Whether you work in early childhood, schools, tertiary environments or non-traditional spaces (e.g., health, military, non-for-profit, corporates), understanding contexts is imperative to achieving the best possible outcomes. This requires you to think beyond the boundaries of any individual educational site and consider the interplay of demography, geolocation, socio-economic status, access to services, among others, and the provision of education. To do this, you will systematically engage with large-scale education and social data to bring to life the theoretical and conceptual tools necessary to analyse, evaluate, problematise and reconstruct the provision of education.
learning_outcomes: Purposefully use education and social data to describe provision of education in a specific context
Analyse and evaluate the provision of education within a pre-defined context
Use principles of provision to resolve violations in the provision of education in specific context
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Thesis Writing and Presentation
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course is aimed at postgraduate research students to evaluate and develop their thesis writing abilities and skills. Weekly sessions cover the overall structuring of the thesis; writing the introduction; the literature review; the methodology chapter; discussion chapters; the conclusion; and the abstract. It also covers examiner expectations, with an emphasis on managing the writing process over an extended time period and on managing large amounts of texts. The course is informed by current applied linguistic and educational research into advanced academic and professional writing. It includes writing a conference paper, a journal article, and preparing for seminar/conference presentations.
learning_outcomes: Explain how to structure and organise a research thesis or other research genre with reference to current research in advanced academic and professional writing.
Use the linguistic and discursive resources of academic English to draft thesis chapters, journal articles, and conference abstracts.
Analyse and compare the structure and organisation of the research genres of the thesis, the journal article, the conference paper, and the oral presentation.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Teacher Language Awareness
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will update and deepen your skills as a language and literacy teacher in the following areas: the nature of language as a phenomenon; language form, meaning and use; language analysis at sentence and supra-sentential levels, oracy and literacy and differences and similarities between spoken and written forms of language; first and second language acquisition and implications for teaching; an overview of the structural grammar of English, focusing on the verb phrase (tense and aspect), modality, and cohesion; scholarship of teacher language awareness. You will be introduced to these ideas through a variety of texts and activity types and referring to a range of recent and seminal scholarly and practitioner voices within the literature in this area.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and discuss structural considerations in the English language.
Identify, describe and critique the principles and issues impacting first and second language learning and implications for teaching.
Evaluate and critique contemporary research on teacher language awareness.
Explain the nature of spoken and written language.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Child Development: Psychological & Social Perspectives
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: How do primary-aged students develop and learn? What, and who, informs their learning? What is the role of cognition, motivation, identity, language, gender, culture, and ability? Using educational psychology as a foundation, you will explore psychological and social perspectives on child development and learning during the primary years of schooling. In order to develop your understanding of young students and how they learn, this course will focus on integrating research findings, theoretical positions, and practical aspects of child development. Specifically, you will be challenged to consider critical developmental issues in relation to your within-school experiences. Completion of this course will enable you to link learning theories and educational practice as a basis for ongoing professional reflection and development of effective primary school pedagogy.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critically evaluate the key implications of a range of research findings about child development for student learning.
Describe the ways in which physical, social and intellectual factors, including socio-emotional, linguistic and cultural factors, impact on student learning in the primary years.
Draw on a range of research-based strategies to assess the specific learning needs of a diverse range of primary aged students, and identify their implications for teaching.
Describe the social, ethnic, linguistic, cultural and religious composition of primary schools in Australia and explain how such family and societal factors may affect learning.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 8925 Master of Teaching (Primary)

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Building Education Systems
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course enables you to describe fundamental concepts, principles, theories, and terminology used in the main branches of education systems research, policy and practice, and apply that knowledge to new and complex environments. This course explicitly brings international and national commitments, legislation, and policy pillars together to develop robust system design principles and to audit and prosecute reforms. The course is of value to current and aspiring systemic personnel and those wanting to better understand how systems work at scale.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles of education system design to new or complex environments
Engage responsibly and sensitively with cultural, historical, and interdisciplinary global contexts in the synthesis of education system design solutions
Describe the fundamental concepts, principles, theories and terminology of education system research, policy and practice
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Educational Research
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course is the first research course in the B.Ed Primary program and will provide you with an understanding of research in education. This will be achieved through exploring different research traditions, research ethics, the research process including issues of validity and reliability, a variety of both qualitative and quantitative research approaches and methodologies used in educational research, the management and analysis of data, and critical thinking and different genres of writing education research and findings. The course will prepare you for conducting your own research project including issues of identifying and formulating a research question; and selecting and applying appropriate research approaches and methods of inquiry. Successful completion of this course is one of the conditions for you to pursue your enrolment into the B.Ed Primary with embedded Honours program.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the strengths and limitations of published educational research
Identify the major approaches and methods used in education research
Plan an education research project with alignment between theory, research questions, and methodology
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 78 UOC overall, including enrolment in an undergraduate Education (Primary) program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Minor Thesis
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will have an opportunity to build on or extend interests developed in your specialist area of education by undertaking a self-directed minor thesis, supported by a supervising academic, in your area of specialisation. The minor thesis must demonstrate synthesis and application of knowledge and skills developed in coursework components of your specialisation to address a particular problem or issue. This is a 12 UOC course. You will enrol in 6 UOC in two successive terms, with the result for the course reported at the end of the second 6 UOC course. Entry into this course is conditional on the following: - The achievement of at least a WAM of 75 (or equivalent) - Successful research proposal - Availability of a supervisor
learning_outcomes: Locate and critically evaluate a wide range of literature relevant to a topic of interest in education
Specify a suitable topic for a minor thesis research project and justify its significance, relevance and feasibility
Use appropriate research methodology to obtain and analyse data in an investigation of a topic of interest in education
Report and interpret the significance of the findings in relation to underlying theory and practice
prerequisites: Prerequisite: EDST5180 and 4071 Education (Primary) (Honours). WAM of 75+, successful research proposal and availability of a supervisor.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Independent research - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Thesis Writing and Presentation
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course is the final research course in B.Ed Primary with embedded Honours program. It aims at developing your thesis writing skills and abilities to evaluate your own writing. Weekly sessions cover the overall structuring of the thesis; writing the introduction; the literature review; the methodology chapter; discussion chapters; the conclusion and the abstract and understanding examiner expectations with an emphasis on managing the writing process over an extended time period and on managing large amounts of texts. The course is informed by current applied linguistic and educational research into advanced academic and professional writing and includes writing a conference paper and journal article and preparing for seminar/conference presentations.
learning_outcomes: Use the linguistic and discursive resources of academic English to draft thesis chapters, journal articles and conference abstracts
Analyse and compare the structure and organisation of the research genres of the thesis, the journal article; the conference paper and the oral presentation
Explain the choices as to how to structure and organise a research thesis or other research genre with reference to current research into advanced academic and professional writing
prerequisites: Prerequisite: EDST5180, and enrolment in 4071 Education (Primary) (Honours). Corequisite: EDST5190 must be completed at the same time or prior to this course.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Learning, Problem Solving, and the Development of Expertise
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: The major focus of this course is to examine how human cognitive structures are organised into a coherent architecture enabling you to learn, think, reason and solve problems. The central role played by active learning in this architecture is emphasised. The course examines how expertise develops and how teaching strategies should be matched to individual needs to promote knowledge acquisition. In this course you will be introduced to cognitive load theory and learn about a number of applications of this theory to the classroom and other educational environments.
learning_outcomes: Explain the evolutionary basis for knowledge.
Identify and explain the structure and operation of human memory.
Discuss how knowledge is constructed.
Discuss the implications of human cognitive architecture for teaching and instructional design.
Describe and explain how expertise develops and distinguish the differences between experts and novices.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Human Development and Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will explore the contemporary understanding of human development across the lifespan (from early childhood through adulthood). You will consider the physical, cognitive, social and emotional developmental patterns and their academic and non-academic implications. Theoretical understandings will be linked to aspects of effective pedagogical practice in school and university classrooms.
learning_outcomes: Discuss and explain perspectives of human development.
Identify key concepts within human development and how they apply to educational settings.
Generate teaching strategies based on theories, constructs, and concepts in human development.
Communicate specialist knowledge within human development and show how it relates to educational settings.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Teacher Learning
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: Teaching is a dynamic, complex profession and teachers work in a challenging, ever-changing environment. Teachers thereby need to constantly up-skill to prepare for all the challenges they will face throughout their careers. Teachers need to have access to, and engage in, high quality professional development across the whole of their teaching career. This course focuses on how teachers learn and develop. It explores three major areas: How teachers learn. The contemporary contexts of teacher professional learning and development. Supporting teacher professional learning in the workplace. This course will enable participants to improve their own and their establishment’s practice in supporting teacher professional learning and development. In addition to exploring contemporary research and theory on teacher learning and development, participants will use this knowledge to develop practical skills. Participants will critically analyse a professional learning program at the school or system level within their context as well as develop a detailed proposal to set up or significantly revise a professional learning program. They will be provided the opportunity to share their proposals with their peers in the class, extending their capacity to both give and receive effective feedback.
learning_outcomes: Understand how teachers learn, the contemporary contexts of teacher professional learning and development, and how teacher professional learning is best supported in the workplace.
Critically analyse a professional learning program at the school or system level.
Plan to continually improve professional knowledge and practice.
Reflect on the application of their learning to their school context.
Enhance their skills and competence in planning and implementing a professional learning program.
Gain an understanding of contemporary research and theory on teacher learning and development.
Increase capacity to give and receive effective feedback.
Engage and support members of their profession.
Present concepts to their peers.
Conduct a practical application of the theory to their workplace through setting up or significantly revising a professional learning program.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Building Resilience in the Workplace
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will learn about the importance of resilience and wellbeing among educators. With foundations in theory and empirical research, this course is also highly practical. You will acquire knowledge of evidence-based strategies for maintaining and promoting your own wellbeing, as well as resources and strategies relevant to school leaders (e.g., principals, head teachers) aiming to promote broader change. You will learn about the importance of educator wellbeing and resilience for thriving students, teachers, and schools, as well as issues specific to certain types of educators (e.g., principals, early career teachers).
learning_outcomes: Generate and implement key evidence-based strategies for promoting your own wellbeing as an educator at the class and school levels
Explain research- and theory-based concepts of wellbeing and resilience as they relate to workplaces in the education industry
Identify key outcomes that are associated with educator wellbeing and resilience
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Individual Differences and Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course explores individual differences and their impact on education and work. It is designed to help educators understand and appreciate the diverse ways individuals learn and develop. Key focus areas include defining and measuring individual differences in intelligence, personality, psychosocial factors, and mental health. This course is ideal for professionals to understand and leverage individual differences to improve teaching and learning experiences.
learning_outcomes: Describe and explain the various types of individual differences.
Evaluate strategies and their responsiveness to individual differences.
Reflect on an aspect of individual differences using real-life examples to illustrate key points.
Understand and articulate the relevance of individual differences for education and/or work.
Critique and synthesise current research on individual differences in education, identifying gaps and proposing future research directions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership, Learning & Teaching program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Motivation in Educational Settings
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: What makes students want to achieve highly and engage deeply in learning? What makes students want to study certain subjects over others? What makes anyone want to do anything at all? In this course, you will investigate questions such as these to understand the role of motivation in how people learn. Topics include values, beliefs, flow, choice, rewards, punishment, and passion, and how they can be harnessed to create learning and wellbeing among teachers, their students, and their leaders in educational settings.
learning_outcomes: Explain why people do what they do and how this relates to educational settings.
Apply motivational theory and research to educational settings.
Use strategies to create motivation and engagement in educational workplaces and learning environments.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: TESOL Advanced Professional Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you are required to work in the school system, with the goal of working towards 25 days of school-based professional practice. The coursework and assessments are linked to the teaching experiences, observation, critical self-reflection, and peer review you will be engaged in while working in schools. The course supports graduates of the program in working towards the achievement of some of the national standards for a proficient teacher. EDST5325 TESOL Advanced Professional Practice, is a practicum class and can only be done face-to-face.
learning_outcomes: Plan, implement and critically evaluate challenging and original lessons and units of work using a range of different strategies to meet varied TESOL student needs and interests
Reflect on, describe and critically evaluate one’s own professional practice and take responsibility in collaboration with others to identify and address their own learning needs
Design and critically evaluate appropriate programs, including needs analysis, syllabus design, program organisation and processes of assessment and evaluation in a TESOL environment
prerequisites: Prerequisite: 48 UOC overall, including any transfer credit granted upon admission, and enrolment in a TESOL specialisation in the Master of Education OR enrolment in a TESOL specialisation in the Graduate Certificate of Education. Corequisite: EDST5440 must be taken at the same time or prior to this course. See Additional Enrolment Constraints below for details of TESOL Assumed Knowledge.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Evaluation of Educational Programs
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will learn to evaluate educational programs, becoming informed consumers of and contributors to what works in education. The course will focus on evaluation theory and practice. It draws from the full range of literature on evaluation, but focuses on the literature and cases in educational evaluation contexts.
learning_outcomes: Explain theoretical and research based procedures that could be used in the execution of a program evaluation in a previous or current professional work context.
Critically discuss the theoretical and practical issues involved in the evaluation of programs in education.
Apply appropriate theoretical and research based evaluation strategies in a plan to evaluate an educational program in a previous or current professional work context.
Discuss the application of program evaluation in education through individual and collaborative inquiry of theory and research based approaches to program evaluation.
Critically appraise different theoretical and research-based approaches to evaluation, and determine relevance for evaluation of programs in education.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership, or Public Policy and Governance program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Leadership Theory, Research and Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will develop an understanding of educational leadership theories and approaches through current research and practice. You will critically analyse the major models and approaches to leadership, including trait, situational, transformational, distributed, and instructional leadership theories. You will also analyse current research and practice in the context of education - including, but not limited to, critical perspectives, social justice and equity, and culturally responsive leadership.
learning_outcomes: Develop a critical and sophisticated understanding of what leadership means in relation to a school or organisational context you are familiar with.
Identify and analyse research evidence, both local and international, with respect to what is claimed on behalf of educational leadership.
Critically discuss the nature of leadership both theoretically and how it manifests in different school or other educational contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Organisation Theory in Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will engage in the application of organisation theory to education, and consider scientific management theory, bureaucracy and professional educators, human relations, open systems theory and contemporary critiques of conventional theories of educational organisations. In addition, you will consider important aspects of organisation, including educational goals, organisational culture, educational technology, the educational environment, inter-organisational linkages, organisational effectiveness, and alternative theories of educational organisation.
learning_outcomes: Investigate the theories about organisations
Analyse or make sense of education organisations
Apply organisation theory to issues of leadership practice in education organisations
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced TESOL Curriculum Design and Assessment
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will explore key issues and themes relating to curriculum and materials design, evaluation, and assessment in the field of language education. You will have the opportunity to think critically about the curriculum, principles for syllabus design, the planning and evaluation of units of work, and the representation of communication and cultures in language learning materials. You will also learn about key assessment practices and reflect on how they could be implemented in your teaching context.
learning_outcomes: Determine implications of various TESOL curriculum design and assessment approaches for your own teaching situation
Evaluate and critique contemporary research available on TESOL curriculum and assessment issues
Identify, describe and critique the underlying principles of TESOL curriculum development and assessment practices
Critically analyse TESOL curriculum design and assessment in light of key theoretical and practical issues and debates
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Applied Linguistics program.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Assessment for Learning: From Theory to Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will explore the underlying philosophy and rationale for assessment for learning. This will include the key approaches and problems in the implementation of such classroom-based assessment, including the implications for the role of the teacher-as-assessor; the nature of effective feedback; how to involve students in self and peer assessment; and the conflicts between such assessment systems and those emphasising large scale testing for student selection and/or school accountability. This course focuses on developing your confidence and expertise in using assessment to effectively support student learning.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a sound understanding of key theoretical, practical and sociocultural problems and approaches in the assessment for learning. This includes debates around trustworthiness and consistency.
Identify, describe and critically evaluate the key assumptions underlying assessment for learning in local and international contexts.
Apply knowledge and understanding of assessment for learning processes to the evaluation and improvement of assessment situations in the student's own context.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Educational Research
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will develop an understanding of research in education. This will be achieved through exploring different research traditions, research ethics, the research process including issues of validity and reliability, a variety of both qualitative and quantitative research approaches and methodologies used in educational research, the management and analysis of data, and critical thinking and different genres of writing education research and findings. The course will prepare you for conducting your own research project including issues of identifying and formulating a research question, selecting and applying appropriate research approaches and methods of inquiry and in presenting the results of your research.
learning_outcomes: Plan an education research project with alignment between theory, research questions, and methodology
Evaluate the strengths and limitations of published educational research
Identify the major approaches and methods used in education research
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership, Applied Linguistics program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Educational Policy: Theory and Practice
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you are introduced to education policy, education policy debates, and some of the major issues facing Australian and international education policymakers. The course aims to increase your understanding of the complexities, advantages, and limitations of education policy and to assist you in becoming effective leaders and practitioners who inform, shape, and influence education policy. The course has a particular focus on federal and state policy in education, including the impact of education policy on schools and students; the interests of stakeholders in designing education policy; the theories of change underpinning education policy initiatives; the implementation challenges of policy approaches, and the impact of various reform strategies on building teaching capacity, accountability, and improving learning for all students. You will develop “policy skills” through writing a policy brief and writing policy-based commentary analysing an aspect of one of the policy issues examined in this course.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse educational policy
Design policy solutions to issues in education
Understand and use research on educational policy
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST5112, EDST5133, and EDST6760

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Developing Literacies: From Kindergarten to University
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course will assist you in understanding, developing and evaluating your literacy praxis by exploring what constitutes literacy within and across a variety of educational contexts and disciplines and how it is shaped and constrained by cognitive and sociocultural factors. The course will include attention to emergent literacies, digital technologies, and multimodal textual forms so as to provide effective and relevant pedagogical approaches to meet the literacy demands of the 21st century. Specific attention will also be given to addressing the needs of preliterate students from refugee and immigrant backgrounds; the aliterate and/or disengaged Australian-born learner; and the differences between everyday and academic literacies.
learning_outcomes: Research current theoretical and practical issues in literacy teaching methods.
Critically analyse the strengths and weaknesses of different methodological approaches to literacy teaching through applying them to students' own teaching situation.
Identify, describe and critique the underlying principles applicable to literacy learning and teaching.

Evaluate and adapt literacy teaching and learning materials to suit students' own teaching context, based on their understanding of the relevant research literature by drawing up a targeted literacy support proposal for a specific learner group.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership program, or Master of Teaching (Secondary). Master of Teaching (Secondary) students must have completed 48 UOC including EDST6760, EDST5112 and EDST5133.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Contemporary Issues in Language Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: You will be introduced to contemporary debates in English language education both in Australia and internationally and will examine these from a range of perspectives. Issues discussed will include language teacher identities in native and non-native language settings; a critical analysis of various language teaching methodologies in changing local and global contexts; and the politics and pedagogical implications of English as a lingua franca. You will learn about key pedagogical issues by drawing on the latest research findings.
learning_outcomes: Critically engage with research literature in the area of English language education.
Explain and evaluate how teacher and learner identities affect teaching and learning.
Critically examine taken-for-granted notions in English language education.
Synthesise ideas in language education to critically analyse English language education programs in different contexts.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education, Educational Leadership, or Applied Linguistics program

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Literature Review in Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course provides you with an opportunity to conduct an in-depth review of the literature on a topic of interest, or issue related to education. It will enable you to develop a deeper reflective approach to education and provide a foundation in working autonomously with guidance from an academic supervisor.
learning_outcomes: Locate and critically review theory and research in the literature related to a topic of interest, or issue in education.
Critically engage in a scholarly inquiry of relevant theory and research literature related to a topic of interest, or issue in education.
Use appropriate structure, organisation and writing style for a literature review on a topic of interest, or issue in education.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in a postgraduate Education or Educational Leadership program. Consent Required

assessment_tasks.task_name: Independent research - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Researching Special Education
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: This course supports you in exploring and critiquing your chosen area of research by locating it in the context of key issues and approaches in special education; and viewing it from a diversity of quantitative and qualitative perspectives. The course provides an introduction to the impact of different epistemological and methodological approaches in quantitative and qualitative special educational research and will also encourage you to build collaboration with others in the course using self and peer review.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the strength and appropriateness of different research methods, including different techniques for data collection, analysis, reporting, and engaging with existing literature.
Critique the methodology of published research in special education.
Apply the principles of research design to a research project in special education.

Articulate key issues in special education research including purpose(s) of doing research, key philosophical issues, researcher/practitioner positionality/role, and the place of research in teachers’ work and in education more broadly.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in the Educational Research specialisation in the Graduate Certificate of Education or Special and Inclusive Education specialisation in the Master of Education

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced TESOL Methodology
faculty: Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture
syllabus_overview: In this course you will gain new or updated skills in the specialist TESOL field. You will engage with advanced language teaching methodology and its practical applications through a program of seminars and online interactions. Topics cover different approaches to English language learning and teaching. These include effective teaching strategies and techniques for teaching reading, writing, listening and speaking, materials development, and the planning and evaluation of individual lessons and units of work. The role of ICT and the internet is addressed as an integral part of the whole course.
learning_outcomes: Integrate key theoretical and practical issues and debates around contemporary TESOL teaching methods and techniques in lesson plans
Critically analyse the strengths and weaknesses of different methodological approaches to TESOL and the implications for students' own teaching situation
Evaluate and adapt teaching and learning materials to suit students' own teaching context, based on their understanding of the relevant research literature
Identify, describe and critique the underlying principles of TESOL methodology
