institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Nuclear Fuel Cycle
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with an in-depth, practical knowledge of the nuclear fuel cycle from the metallurgy of Uranium to the disposition of spent reactor fuel. The course will explore current and future reactor designs, their life cycle, waste management and decommission. Emphasis is placed on the latest advancements in nuclear research that have the potential to transform the fuel cycle. Students will learn from UNSW academics, as well as ANSTO staff who will provide an industry perspective on the fuel cycle. For each stage of the nuclear fuel cycle, students will be encouraged to critique existing technologies and suggest ways to optimize established processes. Students taking this course are expected to be conversant in nuclear engineering and have the skills to engage in self-directed reading, learning, research, and communication in nuclear engineering systems.
learning_outcomes: Compare, contrast and critique different reactor systems, fuel cycles and medical isotope production methods
Formulate solutions to address technological challenges and regulatory aspects associated with decommissioning, environmental protection, monitoring and remediation
Illustrate systems and processes required in nuclear engineering facilities beyond conventional engineering practice
Evaluate and assemble options for the storage, processing, disposal and management of nuclear waste
Describe and discuss the fundamentals of Uranium mining, milling, enrichment, conversions, fuel fabrication techniques and reprocessing routes.
Calculate key parameters for enrichment, fabrication, reprocessing and shielding
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ENGG3741 or ENGG9741 or YENG9741

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Identifying Opportunities
syllabus_overview: One of the major reasons startups fail is because they create a product that the market simply doesn't desire. Understanding how to identify problems, engage with potential customers, and validate ideas is fundamental to startup success. This course offers aspiring entrepreneurs practical tools and frameworks to navigate these complexities. Students will learn techniques to identify real-world problems and rigorously validate their assumptions through market research and customer engagement. They will be able to assess a market and map a TAM SAM SOM of a sector. Upon completion of this course, students will possess the necessary skills to deeply understand the process of customer discovery, deep diving in: personas, identifying customer needs, pain points, and preferences, laying the foundation for a startup idea that genuinely resonates with market needs.
learning_outcomes: Customer Discovery: Engage in customer discovery to articulate customer needs and preferences, and construct user personas and journey maps from the findings.
Market Research: Conduct comprehensive market research to gather relevant evidence and insights on the potential problem space.
Validation Methods: Apply validation methods to test assumptions about their startup ideas
Problem Discovery: Identify and articulate genuine real-world problems, demonstrating an understanding of the importance of addressing market needs and pain points.
Business communication: Use language, visual representations, and/or digital media to insightfully and precisely represent and persuasively convey qualitative and quantitative information.
prerequisites: Enrolment in 5405 Graduate Diploma in Entrepreneurship (Startup Year)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Reactor Physics for Engineers
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with an introduction to the key elements of reactor physics. Students completing this course will be able to discuss aspects of reactor physics and the implications that reactor physics has on the engineering of nuclear systems. Students will be able to perform analyses on simple reactor geometries and describe and understand the main reactivity feedback mechanisms, and their significance, on reactor design and control. Key concepts such as neutron flux and diffusion are first introduced. These are then utilised to demonstrate multiplication and criticality. The neutron life cycle in thermal reactors is described along with fast and delayed neutron production. Reflected reactors and reactor kinetics are discussed including doubling times, reactivity feedback mechanisms, power and temperature coefficients and Xenon poisoning. The course concludes with a discussion on fast reactors and breeding concepts, and a review of the accident at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant. The course material is advanced in nature, due to its interdisciplinary content and the depth of material covered. Students taking this course must have skills expected of advanced engineering students or graduates such that they are capable of modelling, analysing and critically reviewing complex engineering systems. Students must have completed an introductory course on Nuclear Engineering prior to this course, as the material builds on the physical processes at work during fission including neutron flux, criticality, moderation, reactor dynamics and transients.
learning_outcomes: Solve equations to describe the kinetic and spatial behaviour of the Boltzmann Transport Equation for neutrons.
Predict how the isotopic composition of a material changes with time and neutron flux.
Optimise the neutronic behaviour of a nuclear engineering design.
Calculate flux distributions and criticality conditions for idealised reactors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ENGG3741 or ENGG9741 or YENG9741

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Nuclear Safety, Security and Safeguards
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: Students will learn from UNSW academics, senior professionals at the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO) and from the Australian Safeguards and Non-proliferation Office (ASNO) how specific nuclear materials and safety- or security-critical systems are regulated in the organisational, national and international context. The course emphasises both knowledge and application. The assessments include presenting and critiquing safety cases and threat assessments, applying the tools for engineering safety assessments, and planning and communication for a localised nuclear accident case study. All these skills will be applicable in a wide range of contexts.
learning_outcomes: Explain how the operators of nuclear facilities mitigate nuclear proliferation risks
Name organisations, regulations and standards that influence operation of nuclear facilities
Assess consequences of radiological contamination and exposure
Apply nuclear design principles and safety analysis methodologies
Prepare plans and response for a radiological incident
Formulate threat assessments to specify physical protection measures
Present, critique and defend a safety case
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ENGG9741 or YENG9741

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Model and Lean Startup Methodologies
syllabus_overview: Launching a new venture, be it a tech-startup, a small business, or a project within a large organisation, has traditionally been a risky and uncertain endeavour. While there is not a one size fits all blueprint for startup success, understanding the market and leveraging key business concepts and tools such as the lean startup methodology are critical for de-risking a startup venture. This course will equip students with skills to assess market conditions, design experiments to validate business hypotheses, and adapt business models for maximum impact. The course also recognises that a startup's success is often intertwined with its founder's personal brand. Therefore, as students master Lean Startup principles like customer discovery and product-market fit, they will also explore personal branding as a strategic tool. Utilising platforms such as LinkedIn, students will learn to amplify business awareness and credibility, thereby aiding customer discovery and validation processes. Through hands-on exercises and case studies, students will explore lean startup principles, including the importance of traction indicators for gauging product-market-fit across all stages of growth. This course places a strong emphasis on practical skills such as effective communication channels, customer segmentation, and the agility required for experimentation and rapid iteration. The goal is to equip students with the skills needed to build a scalable and sustainable startup venture.
learning_outcomes: Market Validation Techniques: Students will design and conduct effective experiments to validate business hypotheses, gather feedback, and make data-driven decisions for product development and market entry.

Business Awareness via Personal Branding: Students will build brand awareness through utilising professional communication, personal branding, tailored stakeholder messaging and business tools. Students will also identify channels for market communication through the lean startup theory.

Business Model & Lean Canvas: Students will utilise the Lean Canvas to visualise, analyse, and refine their business models, ensuring a clear understanding of key components such as value proposition, revenue streams, traction metrics and customer segments.

Lean Startup Principles: Students will grasp the core principles of the Lean Startup methodology, including the concepts of minimum viable product (MVP), validated learning, rapid experimentation, and iterative development.

Global Perspective on Startups: Students will explore the complexities in launching a startup in a global context. They will identify and navigate the unique cultural, regulatory, and market variations in different international settings, enabling them to to conduct comprehensive competitor analysis and adapt their business models in diverse global markets.
prerequisites: Enrolment in 5405 Graduate Diploma in Entrepreneurship (Startup Year)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Prototyping Design Solutions
syllabus_overview: How do you cross the chasm of idea to prototype? Prototyping and testing design solutions are functions that exist in every successful organisation across all industries, but as an early-stage startup founder, can you prototype an idea without design or engineering experience? Through practical exercises and theoretical principles, students will learn how to transform their design ideas into physical and digital prototypes and how to gain invaluable insights through rigorous testing. Emphasising rigorous testing methods, the course delves into the iterative design process, enabling students to refine and optimise their solutions based on user feedback and real-world perspectives. This course offers students a comprehensive exploration of prototyping techniques and their critical role in driving innovation within organisations.
learning_outcomes: Communicate design intent and structure prototyping and fabrication strategies based on well-considered and validated design inputs.
Identify opportunities to enhance innovation and creativity through rapid experimentation and iterative development based on research, testing, and validated assumptions.
Develop a prototype for user-testing, with supporting documentation that articulates the prototyping process in a design journal with justification of choices made.
Evaluate and discuss user-testing results and feedback for design iterations, user-centric solutions, and construction of design inputs for product development.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 5405 Graduate Diploma in Entrepreneurship (Startup Year) and completion of ENTR9001, ENTR9002, and ENTR9003.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Startup Placement
syllabus_overview: This course offers students a deep dive into the vibrant Australian startup ecosystem. Working with an approved host organisation, students will gain insight into the operations, challenges, strategies and culture unique to startups. The exact nature, activities and emphasis in each placement will vary according to the growth phase of the company, the industry it operates in and resources available as well as the experience, capabilities and aspirations of the student. This course is designed to be flexible to provide a bespoke experience for every participant. The students will have the opportunity to apply their academic knowledge to propose innovative and responsible recommendations to a contemporary business challenge. Students will be spending a minimum of 1 day per week in a company working at either a physical or remote location.
learning_outcomes: Use reflective practices to document personal and professional development gained from the course.

Explore and identify opportunities for professional and personal development within a workplace setting and construct a learning agreement that demonstrates consideration and planning to achieve development goals.
Apply academic knowledge and demonstrate ethical, professional and efficient practices in a workplace setting
Effectively harness, manage and communicate business information using multiple channels across different audiences
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 5405 Graduate Diploma in Entrepreneurship (Startup Year)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Nuclear Engineering
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with an introduction to the key elements of nuclear engineering. It is aimed at giving students a sufficient background knowledge, understanding and vocabulary to demonstrate what differentiates nuclear engineering from other engineering disciplines, and to understand later courses on the Nuclear Engineering MEngSci stream. The course will introduce a wide breadth of topics. These include nuclear fission, reactor physics and engineering, the historical context of nuclear engineering, the impact of radiation on matter, fuel fabrication and the fuel cycle, radioactive wastes and storage methods, reactor accidents, and nuclear safety and licensing. Students taking this course must have the skills of an Honours level graduate engineer such that they are capable of undertaking self-directed reading and learning in engineering systems, performing individual research, and have the required maths and engineering skills.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate reactor designs by their features and major components.
Distinguish approaches to nuclear safety and their principles.
Identify the key steps in the nuclear fuel cycles and waste management.
Solve simple engineering problems relating to operation of nuclear technologies using nuclear-specific concepts, quantities, units and nomenclature.
Analyse the root cause of historical nuclear accidents using principles of reactor physics, reactor engineering and nuclear safety.
Describe the physical processes that govern nuclear fissions, fusion, activation, radioactive decay and radiation-matter interaction.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Reactor Physics for Engineers
school: School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with an introduction to the key elements of reactor physics. Students completing this course will be able to discuss aspects of reactor physics and the implications that reactor physics has on the engineering of nuclear systems. Students will be able to perform analyses on simple reactor geometries and describe and understand the main reactivity feedback mechanisms, and their significance, on reactor design and control. Key concepts such as neutron flux and diffusion are first introduced. These are then utilised to demonstrate multiplication and criticality. The neutron life cycle in thermal reactors is described along with fast and delayed neutron production. Reflected reactors and reactor kinetics are discussed including doubling times, reactivity feedback mechanisms, power and temperature coefficients and Xenon poisoning. The course concludes with a discussion on fast reactors and breeding concepts, and a review of the accident at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant. The course material is advanced in nature, due to its interdisciplinary content and the depth of material covered. Students taking this course must have skills expected of advanced engineering students or graduates such that they are capable of modelling, analysing and critically reviewing complex engineering systems. Students must have completed an introductory course on Nuclear Engineering prior to this course, as the material builds on the physical processes at work during fission including neutron flux, criticality, moderation, reactor dynamics and transients.
learning_outcomes: Solve equations to describe the kinetic and spatial behaviour of the Boltzmann Transport Equation for neutrons.
Predict how the isotopic composition of a material changes with time and neutron flux.
Optimise the neutronic behaviour of a nuclear engineering design.
Calculate flux distributions and criticality conditions for idealised reactors.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ENGG3741

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Startup 360
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the importance of funding and legal frameworks to the success of innovation. No prior legal knowledge is required as students will learn the basics of intellectual property law - for example, copyright and trademarks - and how that impacts business strategy for growth. Students will also explore the funding options and financial frameworks that a startup can use to grow, from angel investing to venture capital rounds. Each of these tools and funding systems are varied and students will learn how to assess the pros and cons of these through real case studies. The students will also actively practise a professional level of communication to a varying range of stakeholders. This will include understanding the purpose, format and audience of a situation to inform best representation and outcomes. This course is supported by guest entrepreneurs who will come to class and share their experiences for real world learning and insights.
learning_outcomes: Business Communication Strategies: Students will practise and implement various communication strategies used in the startup ecosystem, such as networking, storytelling, elevator pitches, and effective communication to different stakeholder groups.

Entrepreneurial Finance: Analyse and articulate the value and use case for the different financial principles and funding strategies specifically tailored to the unique needs of startup ventures including bootstrapping, seed funding, and scaling strategies.

Financial Reporting and Disclosure: Analyse and apply financial reporting standards and disclosures required for investors, lenders, and other stakeholders, ensuring transparency, compliance and accurate representation of financial performance.
Legal Ethics and Professional Responsibility: Students will analyse and apply legal frameworks and ethical standards for establishing and operating businesses in Australia and internationally.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 5405 Graduate Diploma in Entrepreneurship (Startup Year) and completion of ENTR9001, ENTR9002 and ENTR9003.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Functional Anatomy and Biomechanics 3
syllabus_overview: In this course students will apply anatomical and biomechanical principles to the analysis of movement. Lectures will expand on content introduced in ANAT1451 Functional Anatomy & Biomechanics 1 and ANAT1452 Functional Anatomy & Biomechanics 2. Laboratory classes will offer students an opportunity to engage with biomechanical data collection and analyses, while tutorials will provide an opportunity to build theoretical competency.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the effects of mechanical load on the musculoskeletal system.
Demonstrate skills in data collection, graphical presentation, and interpretation of quantitative motion analysis data.
Communicate the rationale for biomechanical measurements and concepts relevant to movement and posture.
Apply biomechanical principles to evaluate normal and pathological human movement and task performance.
Describe mechanisms of musculoskeletal injury and associated preventative measures.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ANAT1452

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Exercise Physiology and Metabolism
syllabus_overview: In this course you will develop the fundamental knowledge and skills to understand how human physiology facilitates exercise and how our bodies adapt over time following exercise training. You will develop pragmatic exercise physiology assessment skills and begin to understand how to utlise various forms of exercise stress to drive desired physiological adaptations to improve performance and health.
learning_outcomes: Describe the function, regulation and interaction of physiological systems relating to exercise and metabolism.
Analyse and interpret physiological data obtained during exercise, and compare such data between time points, individuals and populations.
Demonstrate effective laboratory note taking and written communication skills.
Analyse the individual and integrated physiological responses and adaptations to acute and longitudinal exercise training under both normal conditions and with external influencing factors.
Demonstrate competence in the performance and interpretation of key exercise physiology assessment procedures.
prerequisites: (Prerequisite: SOMS1912 and co-requisite in SOMS1913) OR enrolment in program 3871 Exercise Physiology.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Industry Projects in the Startup Ecosystem
syllabus_overview: Continuing from ENTR9003, students will work as part of a cross-disciplinary student consulting team on a real business challenge for an industry client. The team will be supported throughout by a company mentor, the lecturer, and face-to-face workshops. The students will have the opportunity to apply their academic knowledge to propose innovative and responsible recommendations to a contemporary business challenge. This course is driven by experiential learning, with the students directly seeing how they can effectively harness, manage and communicate business information in a real world setting. Throughout the course, teams will be supported by regular touch points with the lecturer, face-to-face workshops and have a minimum of 2 meetings with industry clients in either a physical or remote setting. Each team's project experience will be different depending on the organisations we partner with.
learning_outcomes: Use reflective practices to document personal and professional development gained from the course.
Utilise appropriate professional digital tools to communicate respectfully in a global environment
Apply academic knowledge to propose innovative and responsible recommendations to a contemporary business challenge
Effectively harness, manage and communicate business information using multiple channels across different audiences to influence business outcomes.
Respectfully collaborate with others and demonstrate thought leadership and initiative in a team environment

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Capstone Project - Launching Your Startup
syllabus_overview: This course offers students the opportunity to consolidate their learnings from the Startup Year program and apply them to building their startup ventures. Working individually or in a co-founding team, students will identify and address genuine market gaps and societal needs, generate globally scalable ideas and iteratively build on the solution. This is the ideal environment for students to experiment with ideas before committing to launching their venture. This course follows the format of an accelerator model and relies on the students' proactivity and self-motivation to progress as rapidly as possible. Students will continue to work on a clear articulation of their unique value proposition, backed by metrics and data. Students will be supported to explore and develop their Entrepreneurial Mindset and Resilience and will have the opportunity to pitch to a group of angel and startup investors for feedback and insights on their own startup.
learning_outcomes: Develop Prototypes/POCs: Leveraging their technical and creative skills, students will develop tangible prototypes or proofs of concept to showcase the value proposition of their startup ventures.
Articulate clearly the unique value proposition of your solution, backed by metrics and data
Demonstrate, apply and adapt discipline specific knowledge, communication skills, digital literacy, and professional acumen through engaging in a new business venture.
Entrepreneurial Mindset and Resilience: Students will cultivate an entrepreneurial mindset, embracing adaptability, risk-taking, and resilience in the face of challenges and uncertainties.

Actively engage in self-reflection and take ownership of your learning journey. Students will demonstrate the ability to manage their time and processes effectively while continuously reviewing their personal performance as a means of driving their ongoing professional development.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in 5405 Graduate Diploma in Entrepreneurship (Startup Year) and completion of ENTR9001, ENTR9002, ENTR9003, ENTR9004, ENTR9005, and ENTR9006.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Exercise and Nutrition
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on the basics of nutrition and exercise for health and wellbeing. In this course you will learn the fundamentals of how to design exercise and physical activity programs and how to use nutrition to enhance exercise and sports performance. You will also develop an understanding of how exercise and nutrition relate to health outcomes, including the role of diet in chronic disease and obesity. You will also be introduced to the performance of basic exercises in our state-of-the-art teaching gym facility.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of diet in the aetiology of chronic conditions and obesity and the metabolic and chronic health consequences of obesity
Describe and apply current Australian physical activity and nutrition population level guidelines
Describe a basic dietary analysis and discuss the implications with respect to general health, well-being, and performance in sport and exercise
Analyse the basic principles of exercise prescription for a variety of exercise modalities
Describe the basic functions of macronutrients and micronutrients including their role in energy balance and health
Describe the evidence for the efficacy of common nutritional supplements and ergogenic aids and demonstrate awareness of prescribed or illegal supplements common in the sports and exercise industry

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Motor Learning and Motor Control
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will develop a broad understanding of how we coordinate, control and learn voluntary movement. This course explores the underlying neurophysiology of motor control and the concepts and processes that underpin controlled movement, motor learning and fatigue that are relevant to the role of an exercise and physiotherapy practitioner. You will gain a greater understanding of the structure of the nervous system and how it affects motor control. In addition, you will gain a better understanding of how motor performance and motor learning can be measured and of the associated theories and concepts that underpin the control of voluntary movement such as attention, memory and sensory integration. By the end of this course, you will have the knowledge and capability to assess motor skill proficiency and design training and development programs that optimise the quality of skill acquisition in a range of exercise contexts.
learning_outcomes: Explain the strengths and limitations of techniques to assess processes of motor learning and motor control
Compare the common theoretical models proposed to explain motor control and the processes of motor learning
Describe the structure and function the components of the neuromuscular and sensory systems as they relate to the control of voluntary and involuntary movements
Assess a client’s motor function in physical activity and exercise, and apply risk management and risk assessment concepts of exercise science associated with motor learning and control
Design motor learning environments and protocols for physical activity and exercise to maximise a client’s specific motor learning and control outcomes
Explain the changes in motor function that may occur with motor learning and development across the lifespan.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT2137 OR ANAT2451

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Exercise Assessment and Testing
syllabus_overview: In this course you will learn how to conduct, analyse and communicate common tests used by exercise professionals for assessment of apparently healthy and clinical populations. These include how to evaluate the health status of your clients and provide exercise recommendations based on client assessment, which are essential skills required for your degree and career.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate proficient and ethical use of generative AI in professional practice.
Identify when further information or supervision from an appropriate health professional is required prior to conducting a health or exercise assessment
Demonstrate evidence-based decision making in selecting appropriate health and exercise assessment procedures
Explain the scientific rationale, reliability, validity, assumptions and limitations of common health and exercise assessments
Conduct and adapt appropriate protocols for safe, effective, and culturally sensitive health and exercise assessments
Record, analyse, and interpret results from health and exercise assessments in forms suitable for multiple stakeholders
prerequisites: Prerequisite: EXPT1155

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Exercise Prescription and Delivery
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on the prescription and delivery of exercise for a variety of healthy populations from sedentary adults to athletes. In this course you will integrate your knowledge of exercise physiology, anatomy, exercise testing, and biomechanics. You will learn how to use exercise assessment results to individualise and deliver exercise programs.
learning_outcomes: Analyse a broad range of exercise modalities and select appropriate exercises and equipment to suit the needs and abilities of all clients from a variety of backgrounds
Design and deliver evidence-based exercise interventions
Appraise data obtained during client assessments to prescribe, deliver, and monitor physical activity and exercise interventions

Design exercise interventions to maintain and/ or improve health and fitness, well-being and performance, that consider the physiological responses to acute exercise, and the adaptations to chronic exercise.

Select and apply learning cues and movement progressions for teaching and correcting movement and exercise technique and identify specific aspects of movement patterns important for performance improvement and injury prevention
prerequisites: Prerequisite: EXPT2168

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Strength and Conditioning
syllabus_overview: This innovative course teaches you advanced exercise testing, programming, and prescription targeted at measuring and improving performance in general, athletic, and occupational settings. Additionally, you will examine nutritional and recovery modalities and enhance your understanding of the of use of ergogenic aids in sport, including banned substances. Following this course, you can choose to apply for accreditation as a Level 1 Sports Trainer with Sports Medicine Australia (SMA) following a short course facilitated by SMA.
learning_outcomes: Explain the processes surrounding exercise, including warm up, nutrition, hydration, and recovery
Demonstrate competence in coaching advanced strength and conditioning techniques
Design exercise-based interventions to maintain or improve athletic performance
Explain ethical and practical implications of doping in sport including the role of anti-doping agencies
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT2154 and Enrolment in program 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Musculoskeletal Clinical Practice 1
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will develop skills in the assessment and management of musculoskeletal conditions of the lower quadrant (including the lumbar spine, pelvis, hip, groin, knee, ankle and foot). Building on your foundational scientific knowledge, you will learn about musculoskeletal pathology, pathophysiology, and the scientific evidence for rehabilitation options for a range of musculoskeletal conditions. You will develop practical skills in manual assessment and manual treatment, and learn how to clinically reason to formulate diagnoses, recognise contributing factors and design treatment plans for a range of lower quadrant musculoskeletal conditions across the lifespan.
learning_outcomes: Apply principles of rehabilitation and biomechanics to inform exercise prescription for a range of musculoskeletal conditions in a multidisciplinary setting
Analyse assessment findings to form a diagnosis for common musculoskeletal conditions of the lower quadrant informed by your knowledge of the clinical sciences
Conduct safe, culturally sensitive, respectful, and patient-centred assessments for the lower quadrant underpinned by a biopsychosocial framework
Collaborate with healthcare professionals to provide team-based healthcare within your scope of practice
Critique the scientific literature to inform your assessment and treatment of common musculoskeletal conditions of the lower quadrant
Formulate goal-orientated management plans for common musculoskeletal conditions of the lower quadrant
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT2137 and EXPT2154 and Enrolment in program 3896 Exercise Science/Physiotherapy and Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Clinical Practice for Chronic Conditions
syllabus_overview: In this course you will learn how to individualise exercise assessment and prescription for clients with a chronic disease. You will learn about the pathophysiology, medication interactions, and specific considerations for testing and training populations, particularly those with cardiometabolic conditions such as diabetes, cancer, and other chronic health conditions in which an emerging and niche evidence base arises.
learning_outcomes: Formulate appropriate assessments and interventions for individuals with chronic disease, taking into consideration client goals, health status , function and self-management strategies
Evaluate the effect of commonly prescribed medications, and diagnostic and medical procedures on both resting and exercise-related physiological responses in individuals with chronic disease(s)
Formulate appropriate screening processes to evaluate and stratify risk for participation in assessments and interventions
Communicate the expected outcomes of evidence-based clinical decision making using an effective, ethical, person-centred approach.
Explain the relevance of client risk factors, and the importance of adverse signs and symptoms relevant for exercise assessments and interventions, in individuals with chronic disease
prerequisites: Pre-requisites: EXPT3148, HLTH2000 and Enrolment in program 3896 Exercise Science/Physiotherapy and Exercise Physiology or 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Physical Activity and Health
syllabus_overview: In this course you will learn about the importance of increasing physical activity and decreasing sedentary behaviour to maintain health and prevent the development of chronic disease across the lifespan. This course uses a strong evidence base to explain how undertaking regular physical activity can boost physical and mental health, with a particular focus on overall health and the prevention of lifestyle disease. Some of the topics covered include the effects of physical activity and sedentary behaviour on the human body, public health recommendations for physical activity and needs across different population groups, as well as the evidence base behind the use of technology to track physical activity and aid exercise. Health-based screening and intervention techniques (including physical activity and basic fitness assessments) will be applied. Assessment in this unit is focused on translating public health guidelines and policy to a non-specialist audience.
learning_outcomes: Identify agencies involved in the promotion of physical activity and describe the potential impact of public health recommendations on promoting physical activity and reducing sedentary behaviour amongst a variety of populations

Evaluate population-level recommendations and Australian guidelines for optimising physical activity and reducing sedentary behaviour across the lifespan and relate the benefits and risks of physical activity
Identify populations at risk of insufficient physical activity or sedentary behaviour and communicate appropriate recommendations for physical activity assessment and interventions
Explain the role of physical activity in the prevention of chronic conditions and maintenance of mental health
Explain the role of sedentary behaviour in the aetiology of chronic conditions
prerequisites: Prerequisite: HLTH1000 and Enrolment in 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Exercise and Health Across the Lifespan
syllabus_overview: In this course you will examine current physical activity guidelines and recommendations across the lifespan to improve health outcomes. You will develop skills to tailor exercise tests and physical activity prescriptions to the specific needs of different populations. Target populations include children, adolescents and older adults, as well as women’s health (pregnancy, post-partum, menopause).
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of social determinants of health to manage clients’ health across the lifespan
Apply the established physical activity guidelines across different age or life stages and discuss health risks associated with a lack of appropriate physical activity
Examine the stages of growth and development from infancy to older age, recognise any atypical growth or development, and apply this to client management

Justify assessments, exercise prescription and monitoring approaches while considering contraindications and considerations associated with exercise at different stages throughout the lifespan while maintaining culturally responsive and person-centred approaches
Conduct and analyse assessments to appropriately prescribe culturally responsive, person-centred, evidence-based, tailored and progressive exercise programs for the stages across the lifespan
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT2154 and EXPT2151

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Rehabilitation for Chronic Conditions
syllabus_overview: In this course you will learn how to individualise exercise assessment and prescription for clients with a chronic disease. You will learn about the pathophysiology, medication interactions, and specific considerations for testing and training populations, particularly those with cardiometabolic conditions such as diabetes, and other chronic health conditions in which an emerging and niche evidence base arises.
learning_outcomes: Formulate appropriate screening processes to evaluate and stratify risk for participation in assessments and interventions
Evaluate the effect of commonly prescribed medications, and diagnostic and medical procedures on both resting and exercise-related physiological responses in individuals with chronic disease(s)

Formulate appropriate and safe interventions and recommendations (by integrating anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology knowledge), and communicate the expected outcomes in an ethical, patient centred and evidence-based approach to decision-making.
Formulate appropriate assessments and interventions for individuals with chronic disease, taking into consideration client goals, health status, function and self-management strategies
Explain the relevance of client risk factors, and the importance of adverse signs and symptoms relevant for exercise assessments and interventions, in individuals with chronic disease
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT3152 and Enrolment in Program 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Neurological Clinical Practice
syllabus_overview: This course is specifically designed for students enrolled in the Physiotherapy and Exercise Physiology program. It focuses on the pathology, pathophysiology, clinical signs and symptoms, and assessment of neurological function, as well as impairments, activity limitations, and participation restrictions arising from disease and trauma to the nervous system. An evidence-based and person-centred approach to neurological physiotherapy is emphasised. The course covers acute neurological disorders (such as stroke, acquired brain injury, and spinal cord injury), cerebral palsy, and neurodegenerative diseases (such as Parkinson’s disease and multiple sclerosis). You will develop competency in the assessment of motor impairments and secondary adaptations, and gain skills in planning and delivering safe and effective neurorehabilitation. The course employs a hybrid learning approach and includes simulated case scenarios, live/ pre-recorded lectures, online learning modules, and practical hands-on workshops focused on applying theoretical knowledge to clinical reasoning and practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective and context-appropriate interpersonal and communication skills with diverse populations, including people of different ages, genders, cultural backgrounds, faiths and neurodiversity, with particular emphasis on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities.
Demonstrate accurate and concise clinical documentation and a clear understanding of professional scopes of practice and referral processes in neurological rehabilitation.

Integrate and apply knowledge of neuroanatomy, pathophysiology, commonly prescribed medications, and other determinants of health and function in people with neurological conditions to develop person-centred physiotherapy and exercise physiology interventions.

Apply knowledge and clinical reasoning skills to conduct safe, effective, and person-centred assessments and outcome measures, identifying impairments, activity limitations, and participation restrictions.

Apply clinical reasoning to deliver, monitor, and evaluate evidence-based physiotherapy and exercise physiology interventions, as well as self-management strategies (including physical activity), for people with neurological conditions.
prerequisites: Pre-requisites: ANAT2452, EXPT2151, EXPT3179 and Enrolment in program 3896 Exercise Science/Physiotherapy and Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Musculoskeletal Clinical Practice 2
syllabus_overview: In this course you will develop skills in the assessment and management of musculoskeletal conditions of the upper quadrant (including the cervical and thoracic spine, shoulder, elbow, wrist and hand). Building on your musculoskeletal knowledge, you will learn about upper quadrant musculoskeletal pathology, as well as a biopsychosocial approach to the assessment and treatment of pain. You will develop your practical skills in manual assessment and manual treatment and develop your clinical reasoning to formulate diagnoses, lists of contributing factors and treatment plans for a range of upper quadrant musculoskeletal conditions and pain presentations.
learning_outcomes: Analyse assessment findings to inform diagnosis for common musculoskeletal conditions of the upper quadrant
Explain the role of exercise, education, manual therapy and other emerging approaches to management of musculoskeletal conditions across the lifespan
Conduct safe, culturally sensitive, respectful, and person-centred assessments for the upper quadrant underpinned by a biopsychosocial framework
Formulate goal-orientated management plans for common musculoskeletal conditions of the upper quadrant
Collaborate with healthcare professionals to provide team-based healthcare within your scope of practice
Apply the biopsychosocial framework to inform management of acute, subacute, chronic and complex musculoskeletal conditions
Select interventions that address contributors to pain and disability in musculoskeletal conditions based on evidence and clinical reasoning
prerequisites: Pre-requisites: EXPT2170 and EXPT2151 and HLTH2000, and Enrolment in program 3896 Exercise Science/Physiotherapy and Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Cardiorespiratory Clinical Practice
syllabus_overview: This course is specifically designed for students enrolled in the Master of Physiotherapy and Exercise Physiology program and introduces common conditions that affect the cardiorespiratory and cardiovascular systems. You will integrate knowledge of cardiorespiratory and cardiovascular anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology and other determinants of health to inform safe and effective exercise testing, assessment and delivery of exercise-based interventions. You will develop competency in evaluating physiological responses and adaptations to acute and chronic exercise. You will also develop skills in appropriate planning, delivery and monitoring of safe and effective exercise-based interventions for people with cardiorespiratory and cardiovascular conditions. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) model will be used to develop clinical reasoning to plan a comprehensive evidence-based and client-centred physiotherapy assessment, treatment and evaluation plan for cardiorespiratory impairments across the lifespan. Indications, mechanisms of action and adverse effects of medication commonly used in cardiorespiratory and cardiovascular conditions will also be critically reviewed.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical reasoning to deliver, monitor and evaluate evidence-based physiotherapy, exercised-based interventions and self-management strategies for people with cardiorespiratory conditions.

Integrate and apply knowledge of cardiorespiratory anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, commonly prescribed medications and other determinants of health and function in people with cardiorespiratory conditions to develop a client-centred physiotherapy and exercise-based intervention.

Apply safe, effective, client-centred assessments and outcome measures to identify impairments, activity limitations and participation restrictions and to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of physiotherapy and exercise-based interventions in people with cardiorespiratory conditions.
Demonstrate accurate and concise clinical documentation and clear understanding of professional scopes of practice and referral processes.
Demonstrate effective stakeholder management skills that include communication strategies that is socio-culturally responsive, including with First Nations peoples.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT3179, EXPT3148, HLTH2000, and Enrolment in program 3896 Exercise Science/Physiotherapy and Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Emerging Areas of Exercise Science
syllabus_overview: In this course you will learn about new and emerging areas of practice in exercise science. These include developments in technology and approaches to training. Featured topics will be those for which there is emerging evidence or significant uptake by the industry. You will learn how to critically evaluate the evidence base, and scientific rationale for these new and emerging trends to formulate your own opinion about the efficacy of the practice.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the evidence for new and emerging areas of exercise science practice
Discuss the physiological rationale behind the use of new and emerging techniques, technology, and approaches to exercise science practice
Compare and contrast opposing views or approaches to contemporary exercise science practice
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT2154 and Enrolment in Program 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Exercise Science Professional Placement
syllabus_overview: In this work integrated learning (WIL) course, you will consult clients under the supervision of exercise scientists, and this will contribute to your required professional placement hours for Exercise and Sports Science Australia (ESSA), the national governing body of Exercise Scientists. You will also study contemporary topics in exercise science that may be relevant for you and your clients at your placement sites.
learning_outcomes: Explain the common contraindications for participation in exercise, identify associated risks and apply appropriate risk management strategies in the professional practice of exercise science and refer onwards when appropriate

Practice within the AES scope of practice and in line with the ESSA code of conduct, in accordance with ethically relevant policies, legislation and regulations that apply to exercise science settings including privacy, consent and record keeping
Demonstrate the integration and application of the exercise science sub-disciplines to support clients to meet their goals
Select verbal and non-verbal communication methods appropriate to the client and or population, carers and other health and exercise professionals
Apply knowledge and skills in a variety of professional exercise science work settings, including the use of telehealth delivery
Apply suitable evidence-based tools and methods to prescribe, monitor, evaluate, and progress exercise based on the needs of individuals
Deliver an exercise-based intervention for clients with medical conditions, injuries or disabilities that have been prescribed by a health professional qualified in clinical exercise prescription
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT2154 and HLTH2000

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Sport and Exercise Psychology
syllabus_overview: This course will develop your theoretical and practical understanding of sport and exercise psychology. You will examine relevant theory and research and draw upon your own experiences to apply sport and exercise psychology principles. You will explore psychological factors that affect participation and performance, and learn how to implement relevant psychological techniques.
learning_outcomes: Explain and apply evidence-based behaviour change approaches to exercise and sport participation
Develop and implement a range of strategies based on sports psychology to improve sport performance
Communicate effectively with clients about issues affecting physical and mental health and well-being, such as burnout and injury
Describe fundamental psychological concepts affecting sports performance
prerequisites: Prerequisites: HLTH2000 and Enrolment in 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Paediatrics and Disability
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will learn how to adapt, apply and engage children and adolescents in exercise programs to support participation in physical activity. This includes those children and adolescents who are well and those who experience barriers to exercise (including medical, cognitive, behavioural and psychosocial challenges). You will develop an understanding of the impact of different conditions on children and adolescents, and how to tailor exercise programs to meet their needs.
learning_outcomes: Design and implement evidence-based, age-appropriate exercise or physical activity interventions that consider the individual needs of the client
Explain the roles physical activity and exercise play in the prevention and management of common conditions in children and adolescents
Select and conduct appropriate exercise assessment protocols for children and adolescents to ensure their safe engagement in exercise and physical activity
Explain individual differences in response to physical activity and exercise, and the implications of those differences for children and adolescents
Examine the role of an exercise scientist working in a multidisciplinary team to deliver effective exercise-based intervention strategies for a variety of paediatric conditions
Conduct yourself in accordance with all relevant ethical and legal frameworks to provide appropriate standards of care to paediatric clients
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT3148 and Enrolment in 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Exercise Oncology
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will gain an in-depth understanding of the pathophysiology and burden of a variety of cancers and be introduced to common treatments. You will learn about the effect that treatments, medications and their interactions have on capacity for exercise and physical activity. You will learn to safely prescribe, monitor, and evaluate exercise programs for people undergoing treatment for cancer and cancer survivors’.
learning_outcomes: Formulate appropriate screening processes to evaluate and stratify risk for participation in assessments and interventions. Take appropriate action regarding changing risk factors and adverse signs and symptoms that may arise before, during and after assessments and interventions.

Design safe and effective exercise-based interventions for individuals with cancer and cancer survivors, based on an integrated knowledge of cancer pathophysiology, and other determinants of health and function

Evaluate the effect of diagnostic procedures, commonly prescribed medications and treatments (including medical, surgical, radiotherapy and other interventions) on resting and exercise-related physiological responses in individuals with, and recovering from, cancer
Formulate strategies to empower clients to undertake safe and effective self-management of exercise during and following discharge from exercise interventions
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT3148 and Enrolment in Program 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Cardiorespiratory Rehabilitation
syllabus_overview: This course is specifically designed for students enrolled in the Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology program and integrates knowledge of cardiorespiratory and cardiovascular anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology, and other determinants of health to inform safe and effective exercise testing, assessment and delivery of exercise-based interventions for people with cardiac, vascular, respiratory and metabolic conditions. You will develop competency in evaluating physiological responses and adaptations to acute and chronic exercise. You will also develop skills in appropriate planning, delivery and monitoring of safe and effective exercise-based interventions for these cohorts.
learning_outcomes: Choose and use relevant technology and equipment efficiently, effectively, and safely
Apply behavioural change principles to support adherence to exercise interventions and to prevent or minimise impairments, limitations, adverse events, and activity restrictions
Describe and evaluate physiological responses to acute and chronic exercise in people with cardiac, vascular, respiratory, and metabolic conditions
Conduct appropriate screening procedures to stratify risks for participation in clinical exercise testing and exercise-based interventions

Describe the effects of commonly prescribed medications on acute and chronic exercise responses that must be considered when prescribing and delivering exercise interventions for people with cardiac, vascular, respiratory and metabolic conditions

Apply clinical reasoning and evidence-based practice to design and monitor the delivery of exercise interventions and select appropriate patient-centred and safe outcome measures for people with cardiac, vascular, respiratory and metabolic conditions

Communicate effectively and respectfully with patients and support person-centred care through shared decision-making, and maintain accurate, timely, and appropriate documentation and records of services
Distinguish when client needs are outside of scope or competence and take appropriate, timely actions to refer onwards to other health professionals
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT4152 and Enrolment in Program 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Neurological Clinical Practice
syllabus_overview: This course builds on the knowledge, skills and attributes developed in EXPT3175. In this course, you will develop new practical skills in the treatment, management and rehabilitation of selected neurological disorders. You will learn to competently assess, treat, teach and train patients and evaluate outcomes of neurological rehabilitation. In addition, you will develop skills in the appropriate prescription of aids and assistive technology to minimise impacts of impairments, enable everyday activity and promote independence, well-being and participation.
learning_outcomes: Plan, implement, and adapt evidence-based, culturally responsive, and client-centred physiotherapy and exercise interventions for people with neurological conditions across the lifespan, incorporating critical appraisal of research evidence and clinical guidelines.

Analyse typical and atypical movement patterns in functional tasks, understand their key phases and components, and apply this knowledge to design and prescribe task-oriented physiotherapy and exercise interventions.

Communicate effectively, sensitively, and respectfully with people with neurological conditions and relevant others, using appropriate education strategies to support understanding and engagement in care.

Integrate and apply knowledge of anatomy, neurophysiology, pathophysiology, relevant pharmacological and surgical interventions to develop client-centred physiotherapy and exercise plans for people with neurological conditions.

Apply and analyse assessments to identify impairments, activity limitations, and participation restrictions, in order to evaluate the effectiveness of physiotherapy and exercise for people with neurological conditions across the lifespan.
Demonstrate understanding of specific clinical and professional issues related to neurological rehabilitation, including psychological resilience and recognition of the scope of practice.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ANAT2452, EXPT2151, EXPT3175, EXPT3178, EXPT3179

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Musculoskeletal Clinical Practice
syllabus_overview: In this course you will develop advanced clinical reasoning skills to guide physiotherapy assessment and management of complex musculoskeletal conditions of the spinal column and limbs including chronic spinal pain, whiplash and headaches, complex referred pain, advanced stage osteoarthritis and bone stress injuries. You will be exposed to advanced manual therapy techniques and exercise prescription skills and apply evidence-based practice to inform physiotherapy management of complex musculoskeletal conditions across the lifespan.
learning_outcomes: Formulate treatment plans for patients with complex musculoskeletal conditions tailored to their individual needs and circumstances, including gender, culture, beliefs, socio-economic status, and personal preferences
Apply the indications and contraindications for the role of advanced manual therapy skills, including spinal manipulation, in the management of musculoskeletal presentations
Appropriately refer and collaborate with other healthcare practitioners to utilise diet, exercise and medication in the management of complex musculoskeletal presentations
Apply evidence-based practice to inform the assessment and management of complex musculoskeletal conditions including acute orthopaedic settings and paediatric conditions
Demonstrate advanced clinical skills to assess and manage patients with complex musculoskeletal conditions
Evaluate the role and use of medical imaging to diagnose and manage complex musculoskeletal presentations.
prerequisites: Pre-requisite: EXPT3179

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Cardiorespiratory Clinical Practice
syllabus_overview: This course will focus on management of clients requiring acute cardiorespiratory support, including those in intensive care units and in post-surgical care. It builds on the knowledge and skills acquired in EXPT3178 Cardiorespiratory Clinical Practice and will focus on cardiorespiratory physiotherapy and exercise in the acute care environment including acute post-surgical care, as well as assessment and treatment of clients with acute cardiorespiratory, neurological and musculoskeletal dysfunction/complications. You will also examine specific clinical and professional issues related to the intensive care and acute care settings and self-reflect on your skills and professional development needs. For example, you will develop your clinical reasoning skills, and learn to undertake evidenced based, appropriate, and culturally sensitive assessment, and safe and effective management of intubated and non-intubated patients. You will develop skills to communicate clearly and effectively in these stressful and high stakes environments and engage in interprofessional, collaborative practice to maximise patient outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Apply high-quality research evidence and clinical guidelines to inform assessment, treatment and outcome measures in acute care settings.
Provide clear, effective, patient-centred, and sensitive communication and education to patients and relevant others in the acute care environment.

Integrate and apply knowledge of anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, and relevant medications in people with acute cardiorespiratory and neurological conditions to develop a client-centred physiotherapy and exercise intervention.

Apply and analyse assessments and outcome measures to identify impairments, activity limitations and participation restrictions and to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of physiotherapy and exercise treatment in an intensive care and acute care environment across the lifespan.

Demonstrate understanding of specific clinical and professional issues related to the intensive care and acute care environment, including psychological resilience and recognition of scope of practice.

Plan, implement, progress and modify evidence-based, culturally responsive and client-centred physiotherapy and exercise treatment in an intensive care and acute care environment across the lifespan including secretion clearance techniques and the management of ventilated, intubated and post-operative patients.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT3175, EXPT3178, EXPT3179

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Specialist Physiotherapy Practice 2
syllabus_overview: This course prepares you to manage sports and musculoskeletal trauma across the continuum of care – from prevention and immediate response to rehabilitation and return to sport. Through modules, practicals, and case-based tutorials, students will develop clinical reasoning skills, understand injury mechanisms, and apply evidence-based assessment and management strategies in multidisciplinary settings. The course also explores hydrotherapy, emergency department care, occupational health and safety, and introduces extended scope practices in physiotherapy.
learning_outcomes: Describe the roles and responsibilities of sports performance staff in a multidisciplinary sports medicine team in preventing and applying immediate care for trauma and sports injury
Demonstrate culturally safe reasoning informed by sports demands and athlete capacity in the removal from, preparation for, and return to sport
Understand and implement emergency/trauma care and work health and safety practices in allied health and extended scope physiotherapy

Apply advanced clinical reasoning in diagnostic procedures, including culturally safe physical examination and appropriate imaging referral and interpretation of reports and selected imaging modalities
Integrate anatomical, physiological and pathological characteristics, using a client centred and evidence-based approach to sports and musculoskeletal injury management
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT2137, EXPT3148, EXPT4156, EXPT4158

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Musculoskeletal and Movement Rehabilitation
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will integrate and apply knowledge of functional anatomy, exercise physiology, biomechanics and pain neuroscience to inform safe and effective exercise-based interventions for the management of musculoskeletal conditions. You will learn about contemporary and emerging approaches to management and rehabilitation of a diverse range of musculoskeletal conditions to prepare you for clinical placements.
learning_outcomes: Conduct safe, culturally sensitive, respectful, and person-centred care underpinned by a biopsychosocial framework

Apply principles of rehabilitation and biomechanics to inform exercise prescription for a range of musculoskeletal conditions in a multidisciplinary setting including risk stratification to inform relevant referal pathways
Synthesise and critically appraise relevant scientific peer-reviewed literature to apply to clinical practice
Discuss pain as a biopsychosocial experience to inform management of acute, subacute, chronic and complex musculoskeletal conditions
Develop and implement interventions that address contributors to pain and disability in musculoskeletal and broader health conditions based on evidence and clinical reasoning
Explain the role of exercise, education, and emerging approaches to pain management across the lifespan in various populations, for musculoskeletal, neurological, and other medical conditions
prerequisites: Pre-requisite: EXPT3148 and Enrolment in Program 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Rehabilitation for Neurological and Neurodegenerative Diseases
syllabus_overview: This course is specifically designed for students enrolled in the Applied Exercise Science/ Clinical Exercise Physiology program and examines the pathophysiology, clinical presentation, impairments, activity limitations and participation restrictions arising from disease and trauma to the nervous system. The course consists of two modules: acute neurological disorders (including stroke, acquired brain injury and spinal cord injury) and neurodegenerative diseases (including Parkinson’s Disease, multiple sclerosis and motor neuron disease). You will develop competency in appropriate assessment of motor impairments and secondary adaptation and develop skills in appropriate planning and delivery of safe and effective exercise and activity-based interventions. The course includes a series of simulated case scenarios, online learning modules and practical hands-on workshops that focus on applying theoretical knowledge to sound clinical reasoning and practice.
learning_outcomes: Implement effective strategies to reduce or minimise secondary impairments and prevent decline in health status
Prescribe safe and effective exercise programs to promote reablement and maximise independence
Analyse the role of exercise for the management of neurological and neurodegenerative disorders
Evaluate, select and implement appropriate outcome measures relevant to treatment and client goals
Apply principles of evidence-based practice with sound clinical reasoning and knowledge of emerging rehabilitation approaches in neurological rehabilitation
Demonstrate understanding of informed consent and communicate effectively and respectfully with clients with cognitive and sensory impairments and other health care professionals and stakeholders
prerequisites: Prerequisites: EXPT3152 and Enrolment in Program 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Exercise Physiology Placement
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will undertake a range of clinical placements in hospital, private practice or community settings under the supervision of an accredited exercise physiologist or other suitably qualified professional. During your placement you will develop your clinical skills as well as generic skills and attributes of accredited allied health professionals including professionalism, effective communication, ethical practice and cultural competence.
learning_outcomes: Deliver patient centred, evidence-based and goal orientated exercise physiology interventions to maximise patient outcomes.
Reflect on and evaluate your own performance to identify strengths and develop plans for future improvements.

Integrate core knowledge and skills to plan, conduct and interpret an appropriate exercise physiology assessment that is patient centred and uses appropriate outcome measures, technology and equipment for a range of clinical presentations.
Provide empathetic and respectful care tailored to individual needs and circumstances including gender, culture, beliefs, socio-economic status and personal preferences.
Collaborate appropriately with other healthcare professionals to ensure the provision of appropriate team-based healthcare in a range of different healthcare settings.

Apply, analyse and reflect on your verbal and non-verbal communication with individuals, carers, families, other healthcare professionals and relevant stakeholders to build rapport and to ensure the delivery of high-quality care.

Demonstrate professional behaviour in accordance with all ethical, legal and professional standards as defined by the relevant Professional Standards, Codes of Conduct and compensable scheme frameworks.
Formulate evidence-based patient centred treatment plans based upon assessment findings and care principles for patients with a variety of diseases and injury states across the lifespan
prerequisites: Pre-requisites: Students enrolled in 3897 and completed EXPT4152, EXPT4136, HLTH3000, EXPT3174, and EXPT3170

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Specialist Physiotherapy Practice 1
syllabus_overview: This course aims to help you develop advanced clinical reasoning and professional practice skills for complex physiotherapy and exercise physiology practice. It includes integration of ethical, person‑centred decision‑making, culturally responsive and trauma‑informed care, and management of people with diverse needs across the lifespan and includes emerging technologies and sustainable models of care that prioritise patient safety, equitable access, ethical practice, and planetary health.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate clear, accurate, effective and culturally responsive, written and verbal communication, including timely and professional clinical documentation
Assess personal learning and wellbeing needs reflecting own biases and implement strategies to engage in personal and professional development to maintain and improve professional practice.

Plan, evaluate and adapt a comprehensive evidenced based management plan that demonstrates efficiency, effectiveness, cultural responsiveness, trauma informed care responsive to individual client needs, and sustainable health care practices

Demonstrate the ability to critically evaluate and integrate emerging technologies and sustainable models of care into practice, prioritising patient safety, equitable access, ethical practice, and planetary health

Critically evaluate the complex and interrelated factors, including social and cultural determinants of health, that influence clients’ needs and responses to interventions, and own scope of practice and onward referrals

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Physiotherapy Placement 1
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will undertake clinical placement across two terms in a hospital, private practice or community setting in either rehabilitation, acute care, primary care or in a rural setting. During your placement you will develop clinical skills specific to the placement as well as generic skills and attributes of physiotherapy professionals including professionalism, effective communication, ethical practice and cultural responsiveness.
learning_outcomes: Apply physiotherapy clinical skills safely and effectively with informed consent by planning, implementing, and evaluating culturally responsive care that supports person-centred, participation-focused goals.

Collaborate effectively with clients and interprofessional teams through clear communication, accurate documentation, advocacy, and education strategies that promote understanding and self-management.

Demonstrate professional and ethical practice by complying with legal, cultural, and professional standards, site-specific policies and safe work procedures, and by prioritising client safety, personal health and resilience, and practicing within scope.

Apply evidence-based clinical reasoning and decision-making by critically appraising research and assessment findings, integrating best available evidence into routine practice, and managing risk to improve care quality.

Reflect on practice and engage in self-directed improvement by evaluating performance against benchmarks, responding to feedback, identifying learning needs, and developing and implementing plans for ongoing improvement.

Manage time, risks, resources, and workload to deliver efficient, safe physiotherapy care whilst contributing to leadership through activities such as clinical case meetings, client advocacy discussions, or delegation to support staff.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Complex and Chronic Conditions
syllabus_overview: In this course you will focus on gaining the skills and knowledge required to assess, design, and deliver exercise and physical activity interventions for those with multiple chronic illnesses or comorbidities.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of commonly prescribed medications, their potential interactions and implications for both resting and exercise-related physiological responses

Integrate knowledge of pathophysiology of multiple chronic and complex conditions, and apply these to inform safe and effective movement, physical activity, and exercise-based interventions for individuals with multiple diseases and comorbidities
Apply principles of biopsychosocial care and person-centred care to promote health and wellbeing for individuals with multiple diseases and comorbidities
Formulate appropriate assessments and outcome measures relevant to client goals and treatment, and evaluate health status, function, capacity, and progress to inform clinical reasoning
Demonstrate effective, concise, respectful, and informative clinical documentation, including case notes and reports, and apply appropriate record keeping practices
Formulate appropriate screening processes to evaluate and stratify risk for participation in exercise for those with multiple diseases and comorbidities

Formulate evidence-based exercise prescriptions, interventions, and recommendations which address health and treatment-related client needs, preferences, goals, and abilities, assessment findings, as well as social and cultural determinants of health.
prerequisites: Co-requisite: EXPT5120 and Enrolment in 3897 Applied Exercise Science/Clinical Exercise Physiology

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Physiotherapy Placement 2
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will undertake clinical placement in a hospital, private practice or community setting within one of the following areas: rehabilitation, acute care, primary care or rural/remote. During your placement you will develop your clinical skills required for the placement as well as generic skills and attributes of physiotherapy professionals including professionalism, effective communication, ethical practice and cultural competence.

Provide empathetic and respectful care tailored to individual needs and circumstances including gender, culture, beliefs, socio-economic status and personal preferences
Reflect on and evaluate your own performance to identify strengths and develop plans for ongoing improvements

Deliver patient centred and goal orientated physiotherapy interventions to maximise patient outcomes
