institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Analysis and Agile Product Management
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is an intermediate (Level 2) Information Systems (IS) course that provides a contemporary understanding of business analysis tools, skills and methodologies used in the process of creating digital solutions. Business Analysis is the practice of enabling change in an organizational context, by defining needs and recommending solutions that deliver value to stakeholders. The course will specifically focus on business analysis as practiced within an Agile Scrum framework. In completing this course, you will learn to take a product-oriented view of solutions and understand how contemporary organisations manage the process of solution creation. The course will hone the conceptual and analytical skills required for analysing business problems and processes, understanding customer requirements, managing stakeholders, and developing product roadmaps. This course covers material that is foundational to the discipline of information systems; it assumes completion of the core information systems course INFS1602 Digital Transformation in Business. This course provides you with concepts and skills that are essential in careers such as business analysts, business systems analysts, product owners, product managers, consultants, and developers.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply the Agile Scrum framework including roles, ceremonies and artefacts in an organisational context.
Understand and apply business analysis tools, techniques and methodologies.
Create high-fidelity prototypes of digital solutions that solve customer needs.
Understand and explain the lifecycle of building digital solutions.
Apply Agile Scrum project management techniques to work collaboratively in groups.
Articulate and explain the role of business analysts and the various knowledge areas of business analysis.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS1602 or INFS2602

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Artificial Intelligence Fluency
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This interactive and engaging course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of artificial intelligence (AI) and its real-world applications. The course is delivered in a three-hour seminar format. It aims to give students a historical overview of the development of AI and its underlying concepts, to understand its current and potential impact on individuals, organisations, and society, and to analyse and discuss the future of AI and its potential applications. Additionally, the course will equip students with the knowledge to use AI for productivity and creativity and to engage with AI responsibly, considering ethical considerations and responsibilities. Moreover, the course will be accessible to students without a technical background in mathematics and computer science. No prior knowledge of AI is required. This course is a core requirement for the new AI in Business and Society Major/Minor ,and a co-requisite for LAWJ2000 - Governance for Responsible AI. LAWJ2000 is also a core course in the same major/minor.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the potential benefits and risks associated with the use of AI in individuals, organisations, and society.
Describe the underlying concepts of AI technology and its development and evolution.
Analyse the future of AI and its potential applications in various industries and sectors.
Assess ethical considerations and responsibilities associated with AI.
Collaborate with AI to improve productivity and creativity in real-world scenarios.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Database Management & Big Data Infrastructures
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: INFS2608 is a Level 2 Information Systems (IS) course that continues students’ study of IS by covering various advanced topics pertinent to Big Data. Building upon the principles and theoretical fundamentals taught in INFS1603, students will learn to apply data design to Big Data systems, specifically data warehousing. Through this course students will be taught the complexities of Big Data systems through business case studies. Students will learn to distinguish the elements that make up Big Data and appraise the journey of building Big Data from start to finish. It is crucial for students to be able to evaluate the design and architecture of Big Data technology. This will cover emerging technologies and trends in Database Design, Data Management and Big Data. Students will also apply strategic thinking to enable effective data management. Situating oneself as a business person, students will practice how to navigate big data systems, make sense of the data and lastly generate insights to solve business problems. Through collaboration, students will look at Big Data from the perspective of a data project manager and be capable of explaining technical details to a wide range of stakeholders, in order to activate the use of data within an organisation.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate to solve complex data related problems to generate a business proposition and presentation.
Evaluate Big Data analytic strategies for decision making.
Apply the basic principles of database design to Big Data infrastructure with considerations of cultural environments.
Investigate emerging technologies and trends in Database Design, Data Management And Big Data in a business context.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS1603 or COMM1822 or COMM2822 or COMP3311 or COMP9311

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing Cybersecurity in the Digital Age
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: With the proliferation of smart devices, interconnected systems and most recently, artificial intelligence, the importance of cybersecurity has never been more critical. Breaches can disrupt lives, businesses, and governments, causing immeasurable harm. Robust cybersecurity systems are not just necessary; they are critical. This foundational course introduces essential concepts in organisational cybersecurity management and data governance. Beginning with an exploration of the symbiotic relationship between human and technical influence, we will then build up your understanding of how data governance and cybersecurity management work together. Through independent and teamwork, you will apply your knowledge to real world case studies, and strengthen your problem-solving skills as part of a responsible cybersecurity management practice.
learning_outcomes: Explain the fundamental concepts and processes involved in cybersecurity management.
Examine data governance, data management and cybersecurity practices, and define how they work together to develop an effective cybersecurity solution.
Assess an organisation's data governance and cybersecurity practices to identify potential risks.
Use regulatory frameworks to assess the legal and ethical implications of cybersecurity practices, including the regulatory impacts on privacy protection and data quality.

Collaborate effectively with team members to address cybersecurity challenges, reach consensus on actionable solutions, and communicate findings using language suitable for both technical and non-technical audiences.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS1701 or INFS3617 or COMP1337

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Digital Innovation Management
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Innovation and technology are the twin engines driving progress in our world today. INFS2631 provides comprehensive understanding of the digital innovation process through insights into current innovation models, strategies, tools, and technologies. By applying theoretical concepts to real-world case studies, you will explore the digital innovation management landscape, gaining conceptual insights into shaping ideas into innovations. This course will provide a strong foundation for your future work with digital innovation initiatives and prepare you to navigate the complex, technology-driven business environment.
learning_outcomes: Provide an overview of the digital innovation financing landscape and the traits of various financiers.
Explain how digital innovations are diffused and adopted or why they failed to do so.
Apply user-centred methodologies to conceptualize, prototype and manage digital innovations.
Analyse and evaluate digital innovations recognizing strategies, ethical considerations, and potential risks.
Describe and explain the digital innovation process, including sources and patterns of innovation.
Explain the importance and mechanisms of digital platforms and innovation ecosystems.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS1602 OR INFS2602

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Supply Chain and Logistics Design
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is an intermediate (Level 2) Information Systems (IS) course. This course offers a broad examination of the key issues involved in the management of supply chains within the broader framework of an organisation's overall competitive strategy, including communication, sourcing, inventory management, warehousing, and logistics. Students will learn the interconnectedness of business units and organisations within the supply chain. The COVID-19 pandemic has taught organisations the importance of logistics and supply chain management as a source of critical competitive advantage. In the post-pandemic future, logistics and supply chain management will represent a greater challenge as well as a tremendous opportunity for most organisations.
learning_outcomes: Explain and analyse how cross-functional drivers, such as sourcing, pricing and information technology, may be employed to improve the performance of a supply chain.
Explain and analyse how logistical decisions (e.g., sourcing, facilities, inventory, and transportation) impact the performance of the firm as well as the entire supply chain.
Explain and analyse the bullwhip effect of a supply chain, including its primary causes and the strategies to dampen the effect.
Explain and analyse the strategies for managing service supply chains including service capacity, demand, and customer waiting.
Interact and collaborate effectively with team members to achieve group objectives.
Explain and analyse inventory issues and recognise the role of inventory in supply chain operations.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS1602 or INFS2602

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Programming for Data Analytics
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is an intermediate (Level 2) Information Systems (IS) course. It introduces students to important concepts, techniques, and technology solutions relevant to programming for data analytics. This encompasses both programming solutions for the purpose of conducting data analytics as well as programming supported by analytics systems (e.g. data-informed / data-driven application development). Course content is presented through three learning modules. These include Python syntax, business data processing, and managerial issues. In Module 1, students systematically study Python syntax. In Module 2, students learn how to analyse business data using Python. This module teaches from the basics of data analytics to exploring many different types of business data. Students learn how to prepare data for analytics, perform simple statistical analysis, create meaningful data visualisations, and predict future trends from data. In Module 3, the course introduces students to emerging technologies as well as the social, legal, and ethical issues relevant to the technologies discussed in this course. Throughout the course, students are introduced to a number of Python libraries for data analytics.
learning_outcomes: Develop ability to interpret and write Python code for the management, manipulation and processing of data.
Describe and apply programming technologies for generating insights from business data.
Demonstrate knowledge and implementation of ethical, legal, and social considerations related to business data processing, as well as insights into various technologies and techniques.
Synthesise data analysis results and communicate the findings effectively.
Demonstrate ability to effectively perform data analysis as part of a team using real-world data.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM1190 OR INFS1603 OR (COMM1822 or COMM2822)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Information Systems and Technology International Study Tour
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course affords students the opportunity to develop knowledge and understanding of international aspect of information systems/technology (IS/IT) business operations (e.g. AI, block chain, IoT, business analytics, e-commerce etc,) through the firsthand observation of businesses in Asian-Pacific countries such as China, India, Hong Kong, and South Korea. The central components of the course include a two-week study tour to one Asian country, in which a number of leading international and national companies, including companies operating in the IS/IT sector and those in other sectors with a significant IS/IT footprint, will be visited in order to enable students to develop an appreciation of the ways in which IS/IT transformed business operations and business systems differ across national boundaries. After returning to the campus, students are required to submit a written report on a topic of interest and based on their observations of the businesses and the country. A group presentation and personal reflection report are to be delivered prior to the end of the Term. This course is offered to a maximum number of 25 students currently enrolled in UNSW Business School. Eligible students wishing to complete this course will be required to submit an online Expression of Interest by the advertised date. Please enquire with the School for further information.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical concepts from Information Systems disciplines to practical situations in international business, drawing from academic literature, industry trends, and contemporary examples.
Identify and analyse IS/IT trends and problems within emerging digital businesses.

Critically analyse and evaluate the implementation and impact of IS/IT-enabled business projects within the selected Asian-Pacific country, identifying key factors for success and potential challenges.

Identify and apply cultural differences, developing the skills to effectively conduct business and make culturally-aware recommendations and decisions in an international setting, with a focus on Asian-Pacific business practices, norms, beliefs, and values.
Demonstrate employability by developing self-management skills, interpersonal skills, teamwork and collaboration, and cross-cultural awareness.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Completion of 96 UOC which (1) includes a minimum of 30 UOC of INFS-coded courses OR (2) includes COMM1190, COMM2501, COMM2822, COMM3050 and COMM3501. Students must also be in Good Academic Standing.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Practising Ethical AI and Responsible Digital Innovation
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This Level 3 course takes a deep dive into the societal impact of digital technologies, tackling the “wicked problems” that come with technological advancements – such as digital surveillance and exclusion. Students will explore the digital landscape through a critical lens, learning to weigh the unintended consequences of technology alongside the benefits of digital innovation. Throughout the course, students will engage with the latest Information Systems (IS) research, tools, and methodologies to better understand and navigate the complex intersections of technology, organisations, and society. With a strong focus on the responsible management of emerging technologies – including artificial intelligence – the course brings in real-world industry perspectives and projects, offering hands-on experience in tackling pressing challenges in digital technology management. Students will critically evaluate both the benefits and risks of digital technologies, develop inclusive strategies, and implement responsible practices that enhance societal well-being and protect individual rights. By the end of the course, students will have the skills and knowledge to lead responsibly in digital innovation, ensuring technology serves society as a whole. Learning takes place through a mix of interactive seminars, research-driven discussions, and project-based collaborations, providing a dynamic environment where students can apply theoretical insights to real-world scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Apply research-integrated methods, regulatory frameworks, and industry standards to investigate the complexities of real-world digital responsibility challenges.
Evaluate real-life scenarios to understand how digital technologies lead to challenges in organisations and societies, including legal, regulatory and governmental challenges.
Explain the multidimensional impacts of digital technologies on individuals, organisations, and society, highlighting the dual aspects of advancements and their potential negative consequences.
Cultivate leadership and teamwork skills to address digital challenges, developing management strategies and practical know-how essential in contemporary professional environment.
Synthesise knowledge from various industry and societal perspectives to guide responsible digital technology innovation, aiming for sustainable and ethical practices.
prerequisites: Minimum of 96UOC completed at UNSW prior to this course

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Business Analytics
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Business organisations acknowledge the importance of utilizing high-quality information about their capabilities and those of their competitors for effective decision making to be competitive and generate value. This course will provide you with the fundamentals of implementing and managing business analytics in organisations. You will dive into data visualisation by introducing key concepts in data visualisation and visual analytics. You will develop the ability in applying various data visualisation techniques and tools, such as Power BI and SAS Visual Analytics, to produce effective data-driven visual reports in different context. It also develops student's ability to effectively communicate insights derived from the visualisations to inform business decision.
learning_outcomes: Apply Business Analytics frameworks, techniques, and tools to optimise data collection, analysis, and management for improved decision-making.
Formulate strategies using data to support managerial decisions and securing competitive advantage.
Synthesise the complexities, crucial elements, and organisational consequences of cultivating a business analytics proficiency.
Evaluate the ethical ramifications of big data and analytics on responsible business conduct, ensuring integrity and accountability.
Generate insightful visual analytics to interpret datasets, creating dashboards and data-driven visual reports for effective communication.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM1190 OR enrolment in program 3959 OR [enrolment in program 3671 double degree program and completion of 72 UOC]

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Process Management
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This Level 3 course examines how enterprise processes can be designed, analysed, and improved to be sustainable, lean, and customer-focused in today’s competitive marketplace. Students explore the principles and methods of Business Process Management (BPM), focusing on how organisations align processes with strategy using information technology and other resources. The course develops capability in documenting processes using Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN), enabling explicit representation for evaluation and redesign. Students also engage with quantitative and qualitative approaches to analysing process performance, including data-driven techniques such as process mining, to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and sustainability risks. In addition, the course introduces the responsible and critical use of generative AI tools to support structured business process discovery. Students learn how to simulate stakeholder engagement, synthesise process insights, and create coherent process artefacts while exercising professional judgement and analytical rigour. Through 3-hour face-to-face seminars, students actively engage with case studies, modelling exercises, applied analysis, and technology-enabled process evaluation. The course emphasises higher-order thinking, requiring students to evaluate complex process environments and propose sustainable, evidence-based improvements grounded in contemporary organisational practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate, synthesise, and create business process artefacts using generative AI tools.
Analyse process performance using quantitative and qualitative tools and methods, with a focus on sustainability for efficiency and impact.
Document processes using a Business Process Modeling and Notation (BPMN).
Explain how Business Process Management enables sustainable organisational strategy and design using Information Technology and other resources.
Propose and plan a sustainable process improvement solution.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2603

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: User Experience and IT Service Design
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is an advanced Level 3 Information Systems course aimed at providing you with knowledge and skills relating to user experience (UX) and IT service design. This course builds on the knowledge and skills covered in INFS2603 (Business Analysis and Agile Product Management), advancing your requirement gathering, problem solving, teamwork, design and development skillset. UX professionals focus on how users interact with and experience a product, system or service. This course exposes you to the practices and tools that UX professionals engage with in the workplace as well as current and emerging user experience and service design practices in organisations. In taking this course, you will learn to work like a UX professional, analysing and interpreting customer needs through user centred research activities and then applying knowledge of design principles and practices that are required to solve organisational problems. Working in groups, you will evaluate design solutions and iterate their own designs based on generated insights. As part of your group work, you will create a compelling pitch to communicate insights, risks, and opportunities for your design solutions.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise the role of a UX practitioner in designing products and services.
Identify current and emerging user experience and service design practices in organisations.
Evaluate design solutions and iterate based on generated insights.
Apply knowledge of design principles and practices to solve organisational problems.
Analyse and interpret customer needs through user centred research activities.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2603

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Enterprise Architecture for Scalable Cloud Solutions
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: INFS3701 is a Level 3 Information Systems (IS) course that extends your knowledge of IS networking infrastructure, cybersecurity, and governance, with a focus on enterprise-level cloud solution architecture. Building on concepts from INFS1701 (Networking and Cybersecurity) and INFS2701 (Cybersecurity Management and Governance), this course explores how modern organisations architect and manage scalable, secure cloud systems. The course is structured around three key areas of learning: Architecting Scalable Cloud Infrastructure: Learn how to deploy and scale cloud-based systems using various architectural models, including Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS). Cloud Security and Governance Guardrails: Explore how to secure cloud environments through proactive governance practices and automated guardrails. This includes identity and access management (IAM), policy enforcement, compliance monitoring, and incident response planning to ensure cloud systems remain resilient, secure, and aligned with organisational policies. Service Delivery of Enterprise Cloud: Examine the organisational and operational aspects of delivering enterprise cloud services. Topics include Quality Assurance (QA), Incident Management (IM), and Service Level Agreements (SLAs), with emphasis on IT governance and service management. By the end of the course, you will be equipped to architect, implement, and manage enterprise-level cloud solutions aligned with security, scalability, and governance best practices.
learning_outcomes: Design, write and evaluate containerised application architectures for scalable and continuous deployment.
Explain and apply enterprise solution architecture principles in developing solutions for cloud-based business applications.
Design, write and evaluate client-server designs for business applications.
Design, write and evaluate cloud-based enterprise solution architecture plans for small to medium scale business problems.
Interpret, review share, and collaborate on programming code and technical information relating to cloud-based business applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2701

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Information Systems Innovation & Transformation
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is a Level 3 Information Systems (IS) course that concludes your study of IS through the application, integration, and synthesis of knowledge from previous IS courses. INFS3605 is the capstone IS course, organised around experiential projects where you apply IS knowledge to solve real-life problems and create IS artefacts. The course uses the UNSW Sandbox model (unsw.to/sandbox) and is centred on real-world challenges. You will work in a team to engage in active learning and problem solving, with opportunities to collaborate with industry mentors as you develop your analysis and solution. Across 10 weeks, you will follow an iterative process to design, build, and improve your artefact through cycles of planning, development, testing, and refinement, using Scrum as a coordination structure. Active weekly engagement is required. You will need to contribute consistently to team progress, participate in weekly learning activities, and show ongoing competency development over time. Assessments are competency-based, using both individual and team evidence, drawing on weekly progression and engagement, the evolving artefact and project outputs, and reflection informed by feedback from industry mentors, peers, and the teaching team. Assessment adopts a competency-based approach that emphasises demonstrated achievement of learning outcomes through authentic tasks, reflection, collaboration, and professional communication. Students are assessed against clearly defined competency standards aligned with the course learning outcomes. Students must demonstrate competency in all assessment components to successfully complete the course.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively within an Agile Scrum team to develop and deliver digital solutions.
Demonstrate effective communication skills to articulate problem-solving processes and convey the impact of digital solutions.
Identify the key attributes of quality, project management, effort estimation, testing, maintenance, and evaluation in digital artefacts and their design processes.
Reflect on individual and team problem-solving experiences, clearly articulating key lessons learned.
Critically analyse problems and develop viable software solutions using appropriate Information Systems research methodologies.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: (INFS3700 and INFS3604) OR (INFS3700 and enrolled in 3964 and completion of 120 UOC) Corequisite: INFS3703

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Information Systems Project Management
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is an advanced (Level 3) Information Systems (IS) Course. This course aims to equip you with both theory and practical skills in the management of projects and programmes concerning the development and implementation of business solutions in the information systems context. The course will cover both predictive and adaptive approaches of project management used in contemporary organisations and will give students an exposure on fundamental components and plans for projects. This course is suitable for students who intend to be project managers as well as those who will work as part of a project team in contemporary organisations. The course aims to further develop you as a scholar and future business professional. The course will refine your communication skills and group-work skills, improve your time management and enhance your research skills. The course assumes no prior experience of project management but does assume that you have completed the IS core course INFS2603 Business Analysis and Agile Product Management. The course is delivered in a three-hour in-person seminar format. Note: this course was previously offered as INFS2848. Students who have taken INFS2848 will not be able to enrol in this course.
learning_outcomes: Examine issues in managing change in the Information System project management landscape by identifying risks and justifying strategic alignment.
Examine fundamental Information System project management components, methodologies and standards.
Operate collaboratively with team members and build the capacity to enable others to contribute towards achieving team objectives.
Construct a variety of comprehensive project plans using tools, to develop business solutions.
Develop actionable recommendations and communicate them effectively using verbal and written communication methods.
Examine ethical and cultural implications in managing information system projects.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2603

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Artificial Intelligence for Business Analytics
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is a Level 3 course that examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning enable organisations to transform data into actionable insights to address business problems and make better data-driven decisions. In response to the growing need for AI-related skills in organisations, INFS3822 is designed to equip students with the necessary knowledge and competencies in AI-driven analytics. In response to the growing need for AI-related skills in organisations, INFS3822 is designed to equip students with the necessary knowledge and competencies in AI-driven analytics. This course adopts an active learning and Problem-Based Learning (PBL) approach and places students’ learning experience at the forefront. Through extensive hands-on experience using state-of-the-art AI techniques (e.g., natural language processing, pattern recognition and machine learning algorithms) to analyse structured and unstructured data in business contexts, this course engages students in practical exercises on AI-driven analytics to address real-world business problems. Building on the foundational knowledge acquired in COMM1190, INFS2822, or COMP1010, students will consolidate their learning and critical thinking on how to apply AI and ML techniques using a variety of software such as R, Python, and SAS Viya for automated ML to conduct analytics applied to real-world business problems. On successful completion of this course, students will acquire highly demanded skillsets in AI-driven analytics, equipping them to address challenges and solve complex business problems when they enter the workplace. This course is delivered in a 3-hour face-to-face seminar format with a blend of pre-seminar and post-seminar independent study activities.
learning_outcomes: Develop collaborative teamwork skills for solving AI-driven business problems.
Consolidate analytical and critical thinking skills to solve real-world business problems using AI-driven solutions.
Explain the rationale behind the application of supervised and unsupervised predictive models to analyse structured and unstructured data, to solve real-world organisational problems.

Discuss ethical implications aligned with SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals) principles/objectives when implementing AI-driven analytics and articulate their impacts on individuals, organisations and society at large.
Communicate effectively the business problem at hand, explain the outcomes of the predictive models generated by machine learning algorithms, and unravel actionable insights.
Identify and apply AI-driven business analytics technologies, their underlying concepts and business applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2822 or COMM1190 or COMP1010

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Analytics Methods
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Today's organisations operate on a global scale and collect huge volumes of data from multiple sources. Management recognises the need to learn how to gather and manage data, transform it into new insights, and translate those insights into effective front-line and strategic actions in order to have a better understanding of business performance and gain competitive advantage. This course will provide you with advanced business analytics methods for Predictive Analytics. The methodologies related to Predictive Analytics are classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning. While our main focus is on employing supervised and reinforcement learning methods for predictive analytics projects, analysts may also utilize unsupervised learning techniques during a predictive analytics project to gain better understanding of the data and accelerate the predictive modelling process. You will implement these methodologies using Python, which is widely used thanks to its large toolkit in data processing and analysis. Business case studies will be introduced alongside the technical aspects of Python coding.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate with team members to achieve team objectives.
Examine the ethical implications of data analytics and communication and their impacts on business and society.
Compose a narrative that illustrates and solves a business problem, and present it convincingly with the aid of visual analytics.
Predict future outcomes based on historical data through the application of analytics programming language tools.
Apply analytic techniques to solve problems and identify opportunities for growth in the business context.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2822

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Continuity, Incidence Response, and Disaster Recovery
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course provides an in-depth examination of business continuity, incident response, and disaster recovery planning for organisations. Students will learn about the various types of cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities that organisations face, and the strategies for mitigating these risks. The course will also cover legal and regulatory requirements related to business continuity, incidence response, and disaster recovery planning, emphasising the importance of compliance. Students will gain an understanding of how to design and implement effective business continuity, incident response, and disaster recovery plans tailored to the specific needs of an organisation. They will learn how to test and evaluate these plans to ensure their effectiveness. In addition, the course will address the critical roles of communication and collaboration in the success of business continuity, incident response, and disaster recovery efforts, as well as the importance of ethical considerations in cybersecurity management. Through case studies, discussions, and practical exercises, students will develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills necessary to manage cybersecurity risks effectively.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the impact of unexpected incidents on the continuity of business operations.
Develop testing methodologies to evaluate the effectiveness of BCP, IRP, and DR plans.
Analyse legal and regulatory requirements related to BCP, IRP, and DR planning.
Design and implement effective business continuity planning (BCP), incident response planning (IRP), and disaster recovery (DR) plans tailored to specific organisational needs.
Apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to analyse complex incidents and develop appropriate BCP, IRP, and DR plans.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2701

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Social Media Analytics
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Social media and advanced Web technologies, including generative AI like automated video editors, natural language generation software, and image recognition systems, have driven the rise of digitally empowered consumers challenging businesses to thrive on social media. In this digital era, consumers are taking over online conversations and actively engaged in generating and disseminating multimodal content across social media platforms in the form of images, videos, audio, text, and emotional icons. Businesses striving to stay ahead of the competition leverage unstructured social media data to design and implement successful social media strategies. In this course, we equip students with the necessary knowledge and competencies to collect and analyse unstructured social media data using recent technologies such as R, SAS Viya for text analytics, Social Network Analysis, Microsoft Azure AI Services and Google Vision AI. Workshops are practical and designed to challenge students to develop their critical and analytical thinking through real-world case studies and extensive hands-on activities to address business problems. Upon successful completion of the course, students are expected to demonstrate both a professional mindset as well as technological confidence regarding social media analytics and its implications in the business context. Note: Students are strongly encouraged to complete either INFS3603 or COMM2501 before undertaking INFS3830.
learning_outcomes: Develop collaborative teamwork skills to effectively communicate the key findings of the analysis to stakeholders.
Discuss strategic issues related to social media use to address business problems and support decision-making.

Consider ethical implications aligned with SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals) principles/objectives when conducting social media analytics and articulate their impact on individuals, organisations, and society at large.
Use a variety of analytical tools to conduct unstructured social media data analysis.
Apply analytical techniques/methods to generate actionable recommendations in the form of innovative solutions to implement successful social media strategies for business.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM1190

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Cybersecurity Trends and Best Practices
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: As cyber threats become more complex, organisations must take proactive measures to prepare for and prevent potential incidents. This course will provide students with an understanding of contemporary cybersecurity practices and equip them with the necessary skills to manage and respond to potential cybersecurity incidents. Students will learn how to formulate and prioritise measures to prevent, reduce the impact of, and prepare for a variety of attacks. This includes learning about various cybersecurity controls, frameworks, and best practices that are grounded in data on actual attacks. Additionally, the course will cover methods for implementing cost-effective and efficient automated controls. Beyond technical aspects, this course will address managerial and organisational issues such as critical incident response, internal and external communication, and refining security frameworks. Students will also learn about the short- and long-term implications of cybersecurity incidents and how to effectively manage and respond to them. These principles, practices, and recommendations can also be applied to a range of critical and adverse situations such as crises and natural disasters.
learning_outcomes: Develop incident response plans for cybersecurity incidents.
Identify various cybersecurity vulnerabilities and how existing and emerging tools may be used to mitigate these.
Demonstrate communication and teamwork skills relevant to various stakeholders in cybersecurity settings.
Identify and evaluate existing cybersecurity frameworks for various settings.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS3929

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Cybersecurity Intelligence and the Incident Response
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course provides a strategic overview of cybersecurity intelligence and incident response, tailored for students in cybersecurity management. It focuses on equipping students with the ability to identify and address cyber threats while considering the ethical, social, and sustainable dimensions of decision-making. Students will learn to analyse cyber adversaries’ tactics and strategies, develop intelligence-driven strategies, and implement effective countermeasures. Emphasis is placed on practical, user-centric approaches to strengthen organisational security and preparedness. By the end of the course, students will have the tools and knowledge to effectively manage cybersecurity incidents, enhance organisational resilience, and safeguard critical assets.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively in teams to design and implement practical solutions for complex cybersecurity scenarios.
Apply incident response frameworks to manage cybersecurity incidents and evaluate post-incident outcomes to improve organisational preparedness.
Analyse cybersecurity threats using intelligence-driven methodologies to determine appropriate mitigation strategies.
Formulate strategic decisions for organisational challenges by synthesising cybersecurity intelligence and incident response frameworks.
Evaluate the ethical, social, and sustainable implications of cybersecurity decisions to propose responsible management strategies within an organisational context.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS1701 and INFS2822

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Web3 and Blockchain Applications
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Blockchain is a decentralised ledger technology based on cryptographic properties that is regulated through a consensus mechanism without an intervention of a trusted intermediary. Although functionally identical to a distributed ledger, the integrity of transactions in the Blockchain is protected through the involvement of network actors in maintaining, updating, and validating all transactions in the network through consensus. By design, a blockchain is virtually immutable and resists data modification. Despite originating as the foundational architecture for transferring value across space and time, the application of blockchain technology has since progressed beyond its original purpose and is now in its 3rd generation. The blockchain popularised by the applications of cryptocurrencies has the potential to redesign many fundamental aspects of our society. Artifacts like decentralised immutable identities, the ability to conduct transactions and businesses without heavy reliance on trusted third parties, significantly reduces the transactional risk involved in such interactions. It could serve as the foundational infrastructure upon which a new society and economy could be designed. The course aims to introduce students to the world of blockchain innovations with a heavy focus on those that will manifest in the web3 environment such as the metaverse, AI-enabled commerce, self- sovereignty-based governance, and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs).
learning_outcomes: Communicate an argument effectively in oral and written form.
Evaluate the range of cultural, security, privacy and ethical issues that could be addressed through the Blockchain technology.
Explain how organisations could use the Blockchain technology to aid in integrating with the web3 environment.
Describe decentralised consensus mechanisms, their benefits and limitations.
Explore different characteristics of entities that will constitute a web3 social and economic environment.
Describe characteristics and components of the Blockchain technology, and the manifestation of cryptocurrency use cases in society and economy.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Risk Management in Cybersecurity
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: As corporate information systems and networks grow more complex, companies are now exposed to more and increasingly sophisticated cyber attacks. Cybersecurity has become an essential component of every business by protecting its critical IT assets from unauthorised access. While it is not possible to eliminate cyber threats, companies must focus on managing their cybersecurity risk to achieve digital resilience. On the other hand, companies are increasingly required to meet cybersecurity standards and frameworks, and embed compliant practices into their risk management plans. Poor management of cybersecurity can create business risks that have implications for the business’s ability to continue its day-to-day operations, meet its obligations, its reputation and its strategic plans. In this course, you will investigates cybersecurity and technology risks in a systematic manner and look at the current theory, methods, standards and best practices for their identification, assessment, analysis and mitigation.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the compliance requirements in the IT/OT (Operational Technology) environments.
Develop a risk management plan to explain how organisations can best identify, analyse and monitor their IS/IT risks in organisational and team settings.
Plan and undertake a preliminary analysis of organisational IS/IT risks using common IS/IT risk analysis tools and techniques.
Present a cohesive, evidence-backed analysis of a cybersecurity issue to a non-expert audience through team collaboration.
Discuss the overall framework of risk management applied to IS security problems, including risk assessment, risk control, and risk implementation stages, and contingency planning.
Discuss the implications of IS/IT and online environment related to security problems in organisations, from a management perspective.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS2701

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Information Systems Consulting
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on the key concepts, practices and issues in engaging and providing IT consulting services, from both the client and the consultant perspectives. The course examines the value propositions of IT consulting, how IT consultants engage with organisations and key stakeholders, and how they help analyse and solve business problems. The course seeks to familiarise you with the IT consulting process, common consulting frameworks and the benefits and limitations related to their use, key types of IT consulting engagements, and current trends in IT consulting related to the opportunities and challenges brought about by rapidly advancing technologies.
learning_outcomes: Recommend to an organisation an appropriate and sustainable digital strategy that draws on latest advances in technologies and counters disruptive market forces.
Work effectively and responsibly in a multicultural team environment.
Explain the value proposition of IT consulting and how it can aid organisations in dynamic market environments.
Write and deliver logically and professionally presented consulting reports.
Analyse and explain how to effectively manage the risks and ethical considerations of IT consulting engagements.
Analyse the IT consulting process and how to effectively engage with internal and external stakeholders.
Use appropriate IT consulting frameworks and methods for analysing business issues and latest technological trends.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in (INFSAH Honours specialisation of 4501 program) OR (INFSCH Honours specialisation of 3964 program and completion of 144 UOC)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Information Systems Strategy and Management
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on advanced concepts, practices and issues in the strategic management of IT. The course covers four key themes. It begins with an exploration of the strategic value of IT, including the role of business-IT alignment in realising that value. Second, the course explores strategic IT decision processes, including planned and emergent strategy-making and IT governance. Third, the course examines strategy implementation issues, including the role of IT leadership, project and portfolio management, and sourcing decisions. The course closes with a review of the strategic role of IT-enabled innovation and current trends in strategy and IT.
learning_outcomes: Examine the value and role of IS/IT in assisting organisations to meet strategic goals.
Apply IS/IT strategy development and decision making processes, and examine their alignment with the overall organisational strategy.
Critically review and explain the strategic management of IT, including key issues and challenges, capability and governance.
Investigate strategic potential and report on strategic implementation in IT management.
Using industry skills and techniques, evaluate an organisation's current state, analyse the strategic contribution of IS/IT and propose opportunities for further improvement.
Work effectively and responsibly as part of a team to apply and contextualise theory to industry.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in (INFSAH Honours specialisation of 4501 program) OR (INFSCH Honours specialisation of 3964 program and completion of 144 UOC)

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Principles of Research Design
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is a Level 4 Information Systems (IS) course that introduces Honours students to the IS research discipline. The course familiarises students with how knowledge is produced, debated, and communicated in Information Systems through close engagement with academic literature and the development of foundational research skills required for Honours study. Seminars focus on understanding the purpose and structure of academic research, with particular emphasis on reading, interpreting, and evaluating IS journal articles. Students learn how literature reviews function in research, how research problems are motivated from prior studies, and how different research traditions in IS shape research questions and claims. The course also introduces core research design concepts so students can understand how theory, research questions, and methods align within a study. During the weekly practical seminars, students analyse and discuss published IS papers to identify arguments, contributions, theoretical positioning, and research design choices. Students develop the ability to critically interpret and synthesise prior research and construct a structured literature review. They also design an initial research proposal by formulating research questions, identifying a research approach, and outlining a study suitable for their Honours project. The course provides the intellectual and practical preparation necessary for students to undertake their Honours research project with confidence and academic rigour.
learning_outcomes: Develop skills in developing theoretical and practical contributions.
Advance research skills including conducting literature review, understanding theories, analysing topic of research using selected theories.
Assist students in developing research writing skills.
Prepare students for conducting an independent study including formulating research questions and selecting a research approach, applying research methodology.
Develop skills for applying IS research methods and techniques for data collection and analysis.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolled in Honours majoring in Information Systems.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing Complex Projects
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: INFS4858 provides you with a comprehensive introduction to project management in an information technology/information systems context but also applicable to other contexts in which project management principles apply. This course will explain the need for project management and the issues associated with managing projects. It will explain the key phases of the project management cycle and describe the various tools and methods used in each of those phases. The course will consider both theoretical and practical perspectives and equip you with the necessary skills to be able to better manage or participate in projects. The course is built around the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBoK) from the Project Management Institute.
learning_outcomes: Explain the components of effective project management.
Discuss and explain new emerging and contemporary issues in the IS project management landscape.
Construct project communication, human resource management, risk management and procurement management.
Construct a workable project management plan that includes scope, tasks, time and costs components.
Explain the role of project management software methodologies, standards and project management professional bodies in the management of IS/IT projects.
Work effectively and responsibly in a multicultural team environment.
Assess the performance of a project and make recommendations accordingly.
prerequisites: Enrolment in Streams: Enrolled in an Honours Program majoring in Information Systems (INFSAH OR INFSBH OR INFSCH)

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Research Methods
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This is a Level 4 Information Systems (IS) course that continues students’ study of IS by furthering their knowledge and skills in relation to research methods and analytical skills. Topics to be covered in the lectures include an overview of knowledge in both qualitative and quantitative research methods and techniques, research design, and thesis writing. In doing so, the philosophical and epistemological assumptions underpinning the research approaches and methods should be clearly presented. This course follows from INFS4886 (Principles of Research Design) to provide deeper knowledge and experience in applying commonly used qualitative and quantitative research methods to the research process. In particular, students will learn how to implement a research plan. Students engage in the research process, from identifying, discussing and formulating a research problem, understanding, applying and extending a theory, to selecting and applying appropriate methods of inquiry (both quantitative or qualitative), and to communicating and presenting their results and contributions both verbally and in writing. The course aims to provide knowledge of research methods essential to the execution of high-quality research in business and/or in IS. The objectives are to: Advance knowledge in IS research methods and techniques of data collection and analysis. Prepare students for conducting an independent study, including formulating research questions and selecting and applying a research method. Advance research skills, including conducting literature review, understanding theories, analysing the topic of research using selected theories. Develop skills in developing theoretical and practical contributions. Assist students in developing research writing skills. This course is essential for students’ ability to conduct research, and therefore INFS4887 is a mandatory course for all Honours students in the IS discipline offered by the School of Information Systems and Technology Management. Principles of Research Design and Business Research Methods courses are designed to prepare students for independent research studies for their Honours or Master’s theses.
learning_outcomes: Apply different data collection and data analysis techniques.
Explain how to conduct quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis.
Construct and document an appropriate research design, including argumentation for data collection and analysis methods/techniques.
Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner.
Analyse a variety of research approaches and methods..
prerequisites: Prerequisite: INFS4886 AND enrolled in Honours majoring in Information Systems.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Cybersecurity Leadership and Risk Management
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Information systems and information technology (IS/IT) underpin the operation of most facets of most organisations. IS/IT provide means by which organisations process their transactions, the mechanisms by which business stakeholders communicate, the information required to manage the performance of the business, and the capability for the business to pursue its strategic plans. The reliance on IS/IT by organizations involves a broad range of risks to all the IS/IT assets within and connected to the organizations. These risks relate all standard categories of IS/IT assets including software, hardware, networks, people. These risks relate to the correct operation of the systems themselves, the integrity and security of the data, information and intellectual property they manage, the development and implementation of new systems and the improvement of existing systems. Poor management of these IS/IT risks can create business risks that have implications for the business’s ability to continue its day to day operations, meet its obligations, it reputation and its strategic plans. These IS/IT risks need to be identified and managed in a systematic way. This course investigates these risks in a systematic manner and looks at the current theory, methods and best practice for their identification, assessment, analysis and mitigation.
learning_outcomes: Plan and undertake a preliminary analysis of an organisational IS/IT risks using common IS/IT risk analysis tools and techniques.
Discuss the overall framework of risk management applied to IS security problems, these include risk assessment, risk control, and risk implementation; as well as contingency planning.
Assess the implications of IS/IT and online environment to security problems in organizations, from a management perspective.
Explain how organisations can best identify, analyse and monitor their IS/IT risks in organisational and team settings.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in (INFSAH Honours specialisation of 4501 program) OR (INFSCH Honours specialisation of 3964 program and completion of 144 UOC)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Digital Capabilities for Business
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course builds the foundation and functional knowledge about information systems by exploring how organisations can leverage new technologies, data and business processes to build digital capabilities needed to compete in an ever-changing digital economy. The course, taught in a 3-hour weekly seminar format, will focus on the value of digital capability, the systems and technologies that support, enable and manage these digital capabilities. Drawing upon real-world problems and challenges, students will apply the use and suitability of contemporary and emerging tools and technologies to a variety of contexts and scenarios. This will culminate in an appreciation of how these technologies affect: the operation and management of businesses; the relationships that businesses have with external entities (including customers, suppliers and regulators); and the products and services that businesses can offer.
learning_outcomes: Examine the core information systems components in digital transformation.
Produce logical and well-justified plans for the leveraging of information systems tools to optimise organisational efficiency and effectiveness and to compete in a global marketplace.
Work collaboratively and effectively as part of a team to deliver an information systems transformation.
Critically analyse a range of cultural, security, privacy and ethical issues faced by individuals and organisations in the context of information systems transformations.
Evaluate both external and internal business environment models and processes, and apply them to formulate sound digital strategies.
Evaluate and apply different approaches in developing and implementing information systems projects.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Analysis and Agile Product Management
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Business analysis is the practice of enabling change in an organisational context, by defining needs and recommending solutions that deliver value to stakeholders. This course develops the core knowledge areas of a business analyst in the context of developing, analysing and implementing information systems. The course will focus on digitally-enabled change in Agile environments, including analysis and application of the Agile Scrum framework. Using real-world challenges and problems relating to business analysis and agile product management, the course will hone the conceptual and analytical skills required for analysing business problems and processes, understanding customer requirements, managing stakeholders, and developing product roadmaps.
learning_outcomes: Examine the lifecycle and requirements of building digital solutions for customers across a variety of industries.
Design detailed and well-researched digital solutions in an organisational context, and apply those solutions to respond to complex customer needs.
Work effectively and collaboratively as part of a group to apply Agile Scrum project management techniques.
Apply and justify the use of different business analysis tools, techniques and methodologies.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Optimising and Transforming Business Processes
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course examines how business processes can be critically analysed, redesigned, and improved to support organisations that are sustainable, lean, and strategically aligned in complex competitive environments. It explores advanced principles, methods, and tools of Business Process Management from a managerial and enterprise-wide perspective. Students develop capability in modelling complex processes using Business Process Modelling Notation (BPMN) to support structured analysis and strategic redesign. The course integrates data-driven techniques, including process mining, to interpret real execution data, diagnose performance gaps, and evaluate organisational impact. Students also critically evaluate and leverage generative AI tools to support structured process discovery and the creation of business process artefacts in ambiguous and dynamic contexts. Through three-hour face-to-face seminars, students actively engage with case studies, modelling exercises, applied analysis, process mining activities, and technology-enabled process discovery and evaluation. The course emphasises higher-order thinking, requiring students to critically evaluate complex process environments and propose sustainable, evidence-based improvements grounded in contemporary organisational practice.
learning_outcomes: Document business processes by using Business Process Modelling and Notation (BPMN) to create clear and detailed process maps.
Apply digital analytics and process mining tools to evaluate, analyse, and enhance business process performance.
Critically evaluate, synthesise, and create business process artefacts using generative AI tools.
Design, create, and implement strategies that utilise digital technology to boost efficiency and innovation in business processes.
Evaluate how digital technologies support Business Process Management in enhancing organisational strategy and design.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing Digital Innovations and Emerging Technologies
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Information systems and technology (IS/IT) innovation drives the initiatives that fuel digital transformation, enabling organisations to fundamentally change their operations and deliver enhanced value to customers through new and improved digital products, services, or processes. This course provides you with a comprehensive understanding of this IS/IT enabled innovation process through insights into current innovation models, strategies, and frameworks, with a particular focus on emerging information technologies and artificial intelligence (AI). You will learn about IS/IT innovations' unique characteristics and industry dynamics, focusing on how emerging information technologies such as generative AI, cloud computing and digital platform-based business models create new opportunities. You will also learn to analyse various digital innovation sources, types, and patterns and collaborate in teams to formulate strategies for managing digital innovations. The course also covers the financial aspects of digital innovations, including funding and commercialisation. The course also introduces fundamental responsible IS/IT innovation framework, integrating ethical and sustainable aspects into digital innovation design. Through case studies and group projects, you will gain the skills and knowledge to drive IS/IT enabled innovation within your organisations.
learning_outcomes: Explain the industry dynamics of IS/IT-enabled innovations by analysing the sources, types, and patterns.
Analyse and explain the modes of mobilising financial resources and commercialising IS/IT-enabled innovations.
Examine the role of emerging technologies in creating innovation opportunities.
Evaluate and integrate principles of responsible IS/IT-enabled innovation, considering ethical implications and sustainability concerns.
Analyse and explain the unique characteristics of IS/IT-enabled innovations.
Collaborate in teams to formulate IS/IT-enabled innovation strategies.
prerequisites: Co-requisite: INFS5602 or INFS5700 or INFS5917

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Business Analytics
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: In today's data-driven world, businesses rely on analytics to drive strategic decision-making and gain a competitive advantage. This course provides students with a foundational understanding of how data can be leveraged to support management decisions and enhance business performance. Students will explore key business analytics frameworks, techniques, and tools used to collect, analyse, and manage data. The course offers hands-on experience in examining datasets using visual analytics tools, including Power BI and SAS Visual Analytics, to develop dashboards and create data-driven reports that effectively communicate insights. Additionally, the course delves into the challenges and organizational impacts of building analytical capabilities, emphasizing critical success factors for implementing business analytics solutions. Students will also examine the ethical implications of big data and analytics, with a focus on responsible business practices. Through interactive discussions and practical applications, they will develop the skills to collaborate with analytic teams and effectively communicate findings to stakeholders using compelling visualizations. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to critically assess the role of data in business, apply analytical techniques to real-world problems, and make informed, data-driven decisions.
learning_outcomes: Investigate the challenges, critical factors and organisational impacts associated with being business analytically capable.
Analyse the ethical impact of big data and analytics on responsible business practices.
Discuss and evaluate Business Analytics framework, techniques and tools used in gathering, analysing and managing data and apply them to enhance decision making.
Effectively utilise visualisations to communicate with analytic team members and influence stakeholder.
Examine datasets using visual analytic techniques and communicate findings using dashboards and data driven visual reports.
Critically evaluate the role of data in supporting management decision-making and gaining competitive advantage
Research the emerging and global trends of business analytics tools and practices in industry.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Artificial Intelligence Fluency
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This interactive and engaging course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of artificial intelligence (AI) and its real-world applications. The course is delivered in a three-hour seminar format . It aims to give students a historical overview of the development of AI and its underlying concepts, to understand its current and potential impact on individuals, organisations, and society, and to analyse and discuss the future of AI and its potential applications. Additionally, the course will equip students with the knowledge to use AI for productivity and creativity and to engage with AI responsibly, considering ethical considerations and responsibilities. Moreover, the course will be accessible to students without a technical background in mathematics and computer science. No prior knowledge of AI is required. INFS5704 is the core course for the new AI in Business and Society MCOM specialisation.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the future of AI and its potential applications in various industries and sectors.
Explain the historical development and evolution of AI technology and its underlying concepts.
Evaluate the potential benefits and risks associated with using AI in individuals, organisations, and society.
Evaluate and communicate AI's ethical, social, and economic implications globally.
Collaborate with AI to improve productivity and creativity in real-world scenarios.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: AI in Action
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: AI in Action introduces Master of Commerce students to the practical application of artificial intelligence (AI) in business and organisational settings. The course explores how AI can support communication, decision-making, knowledge work, automation, and service delivery across a range of professional contexts. Delivered in a three-hour seminar format, the course combines conceptual learning, hands-on experimentation with contemporary AI tools, collaborative activities, and real-world case discussions. Students will learn how to identify opportunities for AI, design AI-enabled workflows, and evaluate the effectiveness of AI-supported solutions. Students will experiment with a range of AI technologies, including conversational AI systems, research and knowledge-management tools, generative media applications, and emerging autonomous and agentic technologies. Rather than focusing on developing AI systems from scratch, the course emphasises the effective use, evaluation, and implementation of AI technologies to address real-world challenges. Students will learn how to frame meaningful use cases, communicate AI’s value to stakeholders, assess benefits and risks, and design solutions that combine human expertise with AI capabilities. Throughout the course, students will develop practical skills in deciding when and how AI should be used, communicating effectively with AI systems, critically evaluating AI-generated outputs, and applying AI responsibly. They will explore how AI can be incorporated into organisational processes and workflows while considering issues such as transparency, accountability, privacy, fairness, governance, and societal impact. Weekly discussions will also examine contemporary developments in AI from around the world, encouraging students to critically engage with emerging issues in regulation, governance, innovation, and the future of work. Working individually and in teams, students will design, prototype, evaluate, and communicate AI-enabled solutions to real-world problems. By the end of the course, students will have developed the confidence to lead AI-related initiatives, assess the suitability of AI in different contexts, communicate AI’s value and limitations to stakeholders, and responsibly integrate AI into professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply AI technologies to support problem-solving, communication, decision-making, knowledge work, and service delivery in professional contexts.
Collaborate effectively in teams to design, evaluate, and present AI-enabled solutions that demonstrate innovation, relevance, and practical feasibility.
Identify and evaluate appropriate AI technologies and approaches to address real-world business and organisational challenges.
Communicate the design, outcomes, value, limitations, and implications of AI-enabled solutions effectively using a range of professional communication formats and channels.
Critically analyse and reflect on the ethical, organisational, and societal implications of AI adoption, including issues relating to fairness, transparency, privacy, accountability, and governance.
Demonstrate the ability to use AI technologies as productivity and creativity enhancers to support innovation and contribute to positive business and societal outcomes.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM5007

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Artificial Intelligence for Business Analytics in Practice
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Artificial intelligence (AI) and Machine learning (ML) have transformed how businesses and organisations operate in an increasingly competitive environment. Although AI provides organisations with opportunities to convert data into actionable insights to address business problems and make better and more efficient data-driven decisions, there is still a talent gap regarding this critical skillset. In response to the growing need for AI-related skills in organisations, INFS5705 course is designed to equip students with the necessary knowledge and competencies in AI-driven analytics. This course adopts an active learning and Problem-Based Learning (PBL) approach, and places students' learning experience at the forefront. Through extensive hands-on experience using state-of-the-art AI techniques (e.g., natural language processing, pattern recognition and machine learning algorithms) to analyse structured and unstructured data in business contexts, this course engages students in extensive hands-on exercises on AI-driven analytics to address real-world business problems. Building on the foundational knowledge acquired in NFS5730, or COMM5007, students will consolidate their analytical competencies and critical thinking on how to apply AI and ML techniques using a variety of software such as R, Python, and SAS Viya for automated ML, to conduct analytics applied to real world business problems. On successful completion of this course, students will gain highly demanded skillsets to tackle challenges and solve complex business problems when they enter the workplace.
learning_outcomes: Discuss ethical implications aligned with SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals) principles/objectives when implementing AI-driven business analytics and articulate their impacts on individuals, organisations and society at large.
Develop collaborative teamwork skills for solving AI-driven business problems.
Consolidate analytical and critical thinking skills to solve real-world business problems using AI-driven solutions.
Identify and apply AI-driven business analytics technologies, their underlying concepts and business applications.
Apply Machine Learning algorithms to analyse structured and unstructured data, solve real-world organisational problems to make data-driven decisions.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: COMM5007 or INFS5730

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Information Technology Infrastructure for Business Analytics
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Performing business analytics functions on huge volumes of data generated from various day-to-day operations requires a solid understanding of how data captured at the operational level can be re-structured and used at the enterprise level to gain maximum effective results. This course will provide you with data management knowledge in both operational and analytical database systems and infrastructure aspects, including theoretical foundations as well as meaningful hands-on experience.
