Yet, some estimates suggest that up to 75% of all organisational change fail to deliver the results that were anticipated. The course introduces you to various established change management theories and the tools and techniques that are associated with effective change management. Students will have the opportunity to analyse how artificial intelligence initiatives affect organisational structures, incentives, risk management systems, and stakeholder relationships and apply change management frameworks and insights to the development of a change management plan that can be applied for artificial intelligence-enabled transformation. The course further explores leaders’ ability to adapt change processes over time and investigates various leadership styles (transformative, adoptive, and ethical leadership) for change management. Emphasis is placed on i) diagnosing and mobilising organisational readiness for artificial intelligence adoption, ii) sequencing and implementing change interventions while building commitment and managing resistance, and iii) sustaining transformation in environments characterised by technological uncertainty and institutional scrutiny. The focus is on practical, theory-informed leadership of artificial intelligence-enabled change in complex organisational environments.
learning_outcomes: Apply your understanding of leadership styles for managing resistance, sustaining change, and maintaining accountability in artificial intelligence-enabled environments.
Explain key theories and frameworks of organisational change and systems thinking as they apply to artificial intelligence-enabled transformation.
Design a structured artificial intelligence change intervention that integrates strategic alignment, governance considerations, and stakeholder engagement.
Analyse organisational readiness, stakeholder dynamics, and system interdependencies in the context of artificial intelligence adoption.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Designing Responsible AI Systems
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course develops applied capability in designing responsible artificial intelligence-enabled socio-technical systems with a strong user-centred and systems design orientation. Students learn to anticipate unintended consequences, model harm propagation, design mitigation mechanisms, embed safeguards within user experience and workflow structures, and establish monitoring and continuous improvement processes. The course moves beyond evaluation of AI risks to mitigation engineering. Students apply structured harm forecasting, user journey mapping, responsible UX design patterns, safeguard configuration, monitoring threshold logic, and recalibration planning to real or case-based AI systems. By the end of the course, students are able to design AI-enabled systems that balance usability, performance, accountability and sustainability. The competencies developed form the design foundation for strategic integration and leadership accountability in the capstone course.
learning_outcomes: Analyse AI-enabled socio-technical systems, including user interactions, workflow structures, data flows, and decision authority, to identify design implications
Apply user-centred design methodologies to prototype AI-supported processes that prioritise usability, transparency, and contestability.
Model unintended consequence pathways and identify intervention points for mitigation.
Design integrated safeguard architectures that combine UX mitigation patterns, organisational oversight mechanisms, and monitoring structures.
Develop structured implementation plans incorporating iterative testing, monitoring thresholds, and continuous improvement processes.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Students must complete ZZBU0032 Responsible AI for Business and Society before taking this course.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: AI Leadership and Strategy Capstone
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This capstone course is the integrative research and professional practicum of the Master of AI Leadership and Strategy. Students undertake a substantial, individually assessed project that applies rigorous inquiry to a complex artificial intelligence-enabled organisational challenge grounded in their current organisation (or equivalent professional context). The course requires students to design, investigate, and justify a responsible artificial intelligence initiative through structured research, critical analysis, and evidence-based reasoning. Students synthesise prior learning across artificial intelligence strategy, responsible artificial intelligence, philosophy, risk management, systems design, technical feasibility, and organisational change into a coherent, research-informed executive action framework. Students progress through a structured research and executive decision cycle: defining a research question, conducting contextual and stakeholder analysis, evaluating consequences and trade-offs, developing and sequencing implementation logic, and defending and recalibrating strategy under scrutiny. The course culminates in a substantial AI Leadership Portfolio, including a formal executive defence and research-informed decision audit. The capstone embeds training in applied research methodology, ethical inquiry, and scholarly communication relevant to artificial intelligence-enabled organisational contexts.
learning_outcomes: Design and articulate a strategically aligned AI initiative integrating business value, responsibility and regulatory awareness.
Synthesise interdisciplinary evidence to design and justify a strategically aligned artificial intelligence initiative integrating business value, responsibility, and regulatory awareness.
Demonstrate adaptive accountability by responding to structured critique and recalibrating AI strategy decisions under executive scrutiny.
Develop and defend a coherent implementation roadmap supported by explicit methodological justification and accountability architecture.
Develop and justify a defensible AI implementation roadmap balancing performance, accountability and organisational constraints.
prerequisites: Maturity requirement: Students must have completed a minimum of 48 UOC to enrol in this course.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Policy evaluation methods
syllabus_overview: In this course students learn a set of statistical tools and research designs that are useful in conducting high-quality empirical research. This course will focus on methods for estimating causal effects of various types of interventions.
learning_outcomes: have an in-depth understanding of econometric/experimental tools to evaluate economically relevant policies
be able to present and discuss your findings.
know how to choose, defend and apply the appropriate estimation model(s) to the estimation of treatment effects taking into account the structure of the data
be able to critically evaluate experimental designs and program evaluations
know how to analyse the data collected from the field or created in an experiment, and to derive conclusions
prerequisites: Enrolment is restricted to specific programs. See UNSW Online website online.unsw.edu.au for details.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing Yourself and Others
syllabus_overview: For managers to be successful in an organisational environment, they need to develop an understanding of their own abilities, areas for development and the need to develop an understanding of the approaches that they can take when working with others in their team(s), across the organisation and across organisational boundaries. Drawing on insights from management, leadership, organisational behaviour and human resources fields, this course allows students to put together a personal development plan that they can use as they commence their business careers.
learning_outcomes: Set goals for your future development in order to proactively manage your career
Gain awareness and self-knowledge of your key competencies and characteristics and reflect on how to use these effectively in the workplace
Gain awareness of leadership styles and consider what type of leader you want to become
Identify and develop teamwork behaviours for bringing out the best in others
Analyse and systematically enhance your communication and feedback skills
Determine your values and understand the role values play in decision making and ethical leadership

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Strategic Decision Making
syllabus_overview: This course covers the fundamentals of Game Theory and its applications. Game Theory is a revolutionary way of analysing strategic interactive situations. It is basic to the understanding of market competition among large firms, the designing of incentive contracts, bidding at auctions, bargaining, and other similar problems central to economics and business. This course covers simultaneous and sequential games and their solution concepts, games of imperfect information, repeated games, and a selection of applications and case studies.
learning_outcomes: be able to explain insights into real-world phenomena derived from game theory to a non-technical audience
apply game theoretic tools to real-world strategic situations, analyse incentives faced by players, and derive conclusions about behaviour
demonstrate an understanding of game theoretical tools and solution concepts
prerequisites: Enrolment is restricted to the Data Science programs (8646, 5646 and 7446).

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Financial Management
syllabus_overview: This course introduces core concepts and principles associated with the financial management of organisations. Drawing on financial and management accounting and aspects of corporate finance, this course introduces students to core business skills including the ability to read and interpret financial statements, an understanding of sources of revenue and drivers of costs as well as insights into the ways that organisations are financed and how this impacts the business. Students will also be introduced to principles of extended reporting, such as integrated reporting, that seek to provide insights into the financial performance of organisations but also their social impact. Students will have the opportunity to apply the concepts covered in this course to real world examples and will gain an appreciation of how these concepts can be used to help shape business decisions. By the end of the course, students will feel confident in using accounting and financial information.
learning_outcomes: Understand the contents of both internal and external financial reports.
Research the financial performance and position of reporting entities.
Communicate financial information to interested stakeholders in an ethical and professional manner.
Apply analytical tools, techniques and frameworks to evaluate and critically examine the contents of both internal and external financial reports.
Explain the objectives, concepts and relationships that underpin both internal and external financial reports.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Foundations of Marketing
syllabus_overview: This course introduces you to the exciting world of marketing and incorporates the traditional foundations of marketing including brand management, product strategy and brand positioning through to understanding customers, customer analytics, integrated marketing communications and promotion and brand metrics and measurement. You will be taught marketing concepts and practical skills that are used by the world’s leading organisations. You will also learn about the ethical and sustainability challenges of marketing and will discover how marketing is being used to help build a better world.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of marketing fundamentals to address a variety complex business challenges
Apply key concepts in marketing to contemporary real world examples
Develop persuasive communication skills across different communication channels and formats
Recognise ethical and sustainability issues associated with marketing and identify ways in which these issues can be addressed by marketers
Demonstrate an understanding of the role of marketing in contemporary organisations and be familiar key concepts and frameworks used in marketing.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Business Economics
syllabus_overview: Economics is a social science that studies the ways in which people interact with one another and make decisions in a world characterised by limited resources. The goal of this course is to provide you with comprehensive tools to 'think like an economist' – that is, to be able to use economic principles to ask and answer questions about how the world works or the effects of policies. We will cover topics such as how individuals or firms make decisions about the demand or supply of a product, how we can determine the efficiency of a market, and how we evaluate the costs and benefits of government intervention in a market. The course is delivered via Playconomics, the first Massive Interactive Immersive Course platform in the world. The ZZBU6003 Playconomics comprises the textbook that covers all the microeconomics and macroeconomics course topics (in both pdf and eBook format, with the associated educational videos), the economic simulation (i.e., a videogame), and Academia – the online community portal that also seamlessly integrates a wide range of assessments (in standard – Multiple Choice or Short Answer – format or game related).
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the change in outcomes following a change in economic conditions, using the standard models of microeconomics and macroeconomics
Identify and evaluate the best strategies to implement at both a microeconomic and macroeconomic level
Identify and assess international economic considerations in microeconomics and macroeconomics problems
Understand the reasons for and outcomes of government intervention in the economy
Identify and assess environmental and sustainability considerations in microeconomics and macroeconomics problems

Understand the standard models of microeconomics and macroeconomics (including assumptions) and apply these models to determine the outcome of changes in a variety of economic dimensions both qualitatively and quantitatively
Communicate and present ideas logically and professionally in a succinct, clear manner and work collaboratively to complete a task

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Law, Regulation and Ethics
syllabus_overview: Corporations and the individuals who work in them need to ensure that they operate lawfully and in a manner that meets stakeholder expectations and broader community standards of acceptable behaviour. This is true across business entities, not-for-profits and in the business of government. It requires managers to understand and be accountable for compliance with a complex array of legal and non-legal rules and expectations, derived from different sources. The reputational risk which flows from decisions influenced by personal, professional and institutional ethics can be amplified enormously by social media. This course is designed to equip students with the analytical tools to identify and manage the governance, compliance and risk management issues that arise from law, regulation and ethics in the context of businesses’ relationship with society.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical thinking skills in the analysis of legal and regulatory issues that arise in business
Analyse corporate governance trends in the context of their social impact
Identify, comprehend and apply issues arising from law and regulation in the context of the ethical operation of a business and associated reputational risk
Research sources to appropriately address regulatory and ethical issues

Analyse legal, regulatory and ethical issues in a logical and structured way, including by identifying problems, researching relevant sources, proposing an outcome and identifying possible challenges to the proposed outcome
Construct written work, analysing law, regulation and ethics, which is logically and professionally presented
Communicate ideas in a succinct and clear manner

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Strategies for Disruption
syllabus_overview: Disruption, driven by changes in technology and other forces, is radically reshaping many industries and changing the playbook for companies to survive and succeed. In this course you will gain greater understanding of the forces that are shaping disruption and what companies should be doing to take advantage of this disruption. Drawing on examples of industry disruptors like Netflix, Uber and Airbnb you will learn some of the key strategies associated with successful disruption. You will also get insight into the strategic options available to incumbent organisations in the context of industry disruption and have the opportunity to apply these insights to a real-world case study. As a result of taking this course you will have a great appreciation of the strategies that companies should adopt in rapidly changing environments.
learning_outcomes: Apply the understanding of disruption and strategy to a real-world case
Demonstrate a familiarity with key concepts in corporate strategy
Clearly and professionally communicate elements of a strategic response to industry disruption
Understand the range of strategic options that industry incumbents can pursue in response to disruption in their industry
Draw insights from case studies of disruptive innovation by companies across various sectors and industries
Identify the causes of disruption across various industries and sectors

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Career Navigator
syllabus_overview: The awareness of the benefits of career development learning is on the rise, both at an individual level and in supporting both policy as well as social goals. This course provides an opportunity for Master of Management students to gain the knowledge, skills, attitudes and behaviours to manage their career in self-directed ways. They will be exposed to a range of career development theories and models that will assist them to gain clarity on their post study careers and the skills required to achieve their career goals.
learning_outcomes: Investigate choices, challenges and effective strategies to use during career transitions.
Use up-to-date work search tools and professional communication skills to create and engage in work opportunities reflective of preferred future
Understand current employee recruitment and selection processes.
Apply ethical frameworks and theories of influence; creating positive processes, shared purpose and perspective taking capacity in order to positively advance career and workplace projects

Participate in lifelong learning supportive of career goals using self and peer coaching practices in order to build and maintain a positive self-concept and develop strategies for responding positively to career transitions

Explore the nature of career development (through the lens of various theories and models) and their impact on the career-building process of self and others. Investigate choices, challenges and effective strategies to use during career transitions
Engage in career planning and development that seeks to raise awareness of employment bias and stereotypes within changing economic, social and employment conditions
Demonstrate effective career decision-making skills, knowledge and attitudes supportive of career goals, using relevant and accurate career-related information, analysis and critical thinking

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing with Digital Technology
syllabus_overview: Managing with Digital Technology aims to increase technical literacy of managers and leaders. The main objective of this course is to give managers a high-level overview of the fundamental concepts, main topics and problems in contemporary information technology and how they relate to business settings, and thus equip them to make better decisions regarding applications of technology, even if they are not technologists themselves. This course takes a top-down approach and emphasises high-level mastery of important concepts in information technology. Students who successfully complete this course will feel confident in any technology organisation and will have an appreciation for the problems in the field, how they affect or constrain business decisions and how it all works. The course prepares students for product-management roles. Similarly, more and more industries, especially traditional service industries, are creating their own products to deliver more capabilities to their customers and require new capabilities from their managers. A successful product manager needs to master the business side of developing a product as well as be able to interact with a wide range of technical and non-technical stakeholders - from customers through to product engineers and user experience specialists. Managing with Digital Technology equips founders to succeed in technology endeavours. Successful start-up founders will come across technology from day zero. Virtually every business idea today involves technology - often entire stacks of various technologies. Founders with a non-technical background must rely entirely on their technical co-founders, if they are lucky, or on the word of developers and other technologists they hire, to help them realise their dream. They are often faced with difficult choices and this course aims to equip them with the knowledge and confidence to make informed choices not just in business but in technology as well.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate emerging business technologies used to deliver user experiences in a competitive marketplace
Devise complex and compelling arguments to key stakeholders that ensure potential future funding of technology projects
Analyse the key technology-related drivers of organisational decision making and the value of technology to deliver competitive solutions
Adapt customer insights to develop innovative technology products that can be used to expose new market niches
Critically review the role of the customer and their user needs as the driver of technological advancement and innovation of products and services
Identify risks associated with new technology deployment and adapt mitigation strategies

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Strategic Consulting Project
syllabus_overview: This course provides an opportunity for you to apply the academic knowledge and professional skills developed across the program to a real world contemporary challenge. You will work in small project teams to provide recommendations to your partner organisation, considering the broader global environment in which it operates. You will consider how your personal growth and development throughout the program has increased your ability to be an effective team member and to influence others to drive change. This course is delivered fully online and consists of pre-workshops modules, online discussion boards and industry partner meetings. Students are required to spend a minimum of 80 hours working with a partner organisation, on a project basis, on a genuine business issue for the partner organisation. This is supported by learning activities provided by UNSW academics, company mentors and business leaders.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on your experience across the program and identify how this experience has increased your ability to be an effective team member and to influence others to drive change.
Evaluate the ethical, environmental and/or sustainability considerations within the environment the organisation is operating.
Assess the impact the global environment has on future organisational strategies and goals.
Apply disciplinary and inter-disciplinary theoretical knowledge to provide evidence based, practical solutions to real work challenges.
Select the appropriate tools and channels necessary to work effectively with others to meet milestones and communicate outcomes.
prerequisites: Maturity requirement: Students must have completed a minimum of 36 UOC to enrol in this course

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
syllabus_overview: In this course, you will build entrepreneurial skills as you identify, analyse and propose a solution to a meaningful unsolved problem. Practical tools and frameworks will be introduced for critically developing solution concepts, performing competitive analyses, designing experiments to validate concepts and rapid prototyping. You will learn how to effectively communicate and pitch new ideas. After this course, you will have: • a changed mindset, so that you can experience the world from an entrepreneur’s perspective; • sharpened skills in finding problems worth solving, mobilising people and resources to solve them, selling your ideas and skills and creating value; and • taken a step towards creating your own start-up, with mentors, support structures and fellow UNSW students to bring your ideas and companies to life.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate solution concepts using Customer Discovery methodology through the Business Model Canvas and Value Proposition Canvas
Identify the common characteristics of successful entrepreneurs and understand the processes and support mechanisms that enable them to succeed.
Use language, visual representations, and/or digital media to insightfully and precisely represent and persuasively convey qualitative and quantitative information
Define a problem statement developed from a compelling societal need, generate multiple alternative solution concepts

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Human Resource Policies and Practices
syllabus_overview: It is often said that people are an organisation's greatest resource. This course introduces you to the policies and practices that organisations use to ensure that they are making the most effective use of their human resources to drive organisational performance. It focusses in particular on the role of the human resource management function in achieving these outcomes, the different forms that it takes across organisations and the changing nature of the HR function in contemporary organisations. In doing so, it provides an overview of the employment cycle and the contribution that effective HR policies and practices can make to each stage in this cycle.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the ways in which HR policies and practices impact employee outcomes and organisational objectives
Generate recommendations for configuring HR policies and practices that can better respond to current events and meet future demands
Recognise how core HR functions are evolving to meet the needs of contemporary organisations
Review key HR policies and practices in the context of current cases and organisations
Discuss a range of effective HR policies and practices

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Employee Wellbeing and Engagement
syllabus_overview: This course aims to advance knowledge in managing employee wellbeing and engagement. As key employee outcomes, this course will cover a broad range of Human Resources Management (HRM) policies and programs to best support employee wellbeing and engagement across current challenges and contexts. In working to create positive work environments, this course will cover many human resource considerations across change, organisational support, employee development, emotions, learning, and workplace relationships.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess various approaches for managing wellbeing and engagement across different groups of employees and contexts
Identify best (and emerging) practices for building engagement and supporting employee wellbeing in relation to current challenges
Apply evidence-based management theories to promote positive employee outcomes
Relate how to measure and monitor employee wellbeing and engagement
Justify human resource management practices in terms of anticipated employee outcomes

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Sustainability and Human Resources
syllabus_overview: All organisations are facing pressures to improve their performance of sustainability from various sources including capital markets, government regulations, consumer and increasingly their own employees. The Human Resources (HR) function has an important role to play in helping organisations effectively embed improved sustainability practices, and by the same token the ability of HR to perform its role is impacted by organisation's approach to sustainability. In this course students will be introduced to the sustainability challenges that organisations face and will assess the contribution that the HR function and HR policies and practices can make to addressing these challenges. You will examine examples of how the HR function is engaging with and supporting organisations' initiatives to improve sustainability and will develop strategies for how HR in your organisation can work with different stakeholders to improve social and environmental outcomes. Please note late enrolment is not permitted for this course.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on your own values, practices and role as a potential agent of positive change.
Articulate approaches and strategies that the HR/ People and Culture function in organisations can adopt to help address sustainability challenges.
Describe the main sustainability challenges faced by your organisation and how these might impact and be impacted by different HRM policies and practices.
Demonstrate your understanding of the role that business plays in society, domestically and internationally.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Human Resource Information Systems
syllabus_overview: The application of information technology has revolutionised the way in which organisations operate and has had a significant impact on the evolving human resource management function. Human Resource (HR) plays a strategic role in ensuring the practices of an organisation align with its goals to achieve sustained long-term success. In this course, students will critically analyse the administrative and strategic value of a Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS), as relevant to local and global organisations, and identify and examine the issues relating to the use of HRIS in contemporary business settings. By evaluating the technologies and methodologies of HRIS, students will identify opportunities for data collection and analysis, and will construct and present HRIS solutions for the automation and effective cost management of HR information.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the impact of HR Information Systems (HRIS) on human resources management, including the integration of HRIS with other HR functions, such as recruitment, performance management, and payroll

Critically assess the challenges and opportunities associated with the use of HR Information Systems in a global context, including issues related to cultural diversity, language barriers, and differences in technological infrastructure
Develop strategies for the effective implementation and adoption of HRIS, including change management, stakeholder engagement, and training and development
Analyse the HR Information Systems (HRIS) needs of an organisation and select appropriate HRIS solutions based on organisational requirements, budget, and technological capabilities

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Strategic Rewards and Performance Management
syllabus_overview: This course examines contemporary compensation and performance management from both applied and theoretical perspectives. In relation to current trends and challenges, you will gain an advanced understanding of designing pay and performance systems. In terms of the expectations, motivations, and implications involved with managing pay and performance, this course builds understanding by discussing potential solutions to practical problems for Human Resource Management.
learning_outcomes: Assess the alignments and implications of different approaches to managing pay and performance for strategic HRM.
Identify motivational theories which influence employee compensation and performance
Evaluate organisational expectations and implications involved with designing pay and performance systems
Apply potential solutions to practical problems within managing pay and performance
Identify and develop pay and performance systems which are fair, effective, and sustainable

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion
syllabus_overview: Both shifts in culture and recent worldwide events have brought the concepts of diversity, equity, inclusion, belonging and justice to the forefront, yet shown that society must continue to grow in acknowledging, understanding and applying these concepts. In organisations today, diversity and equity, inclusion and belonging (DEIB) are ‘2 sides of the same coin’. They lead to better top and bottom line outcomes in organisations and benefit individuals and society. These are common expectations of ethical organisations, and meet the expectations of socially responsible stakeholders. In this course, you will learn the importance and value of DEIB in the workplace and gain actionable insights to develop practical frameworks and measurable goals. You will have the opportunity to apply these frameworks and build sustainable, evidence-based strategies and plans that drive organisation value and support safe and respectful, diverse and inclusive workplace experiences.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate different models and approaches to diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging (DEIB)

Recommend strategies to effectively communicate and engage with stakeholders, including employees, senior management, and external partners, to promote buy-in and support for diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging initiatives
Develop a strategic approach to diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace across the employee lifecycle
Discuss the impact of diversity, equity and inclusion on the performance and wellbeing of society, organisations, leaders, teams and team members.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Change Management
syllabus_overview: Organisations are increasingly having to adapt and change in response to rapid changes in their environment. Yet, some estimates suggest that up to 75% of all organisational change fail to deliver the results that were anticipated. As there are many factors which influence the success and failure of organisational change initiatives, this course introduces you to different theories of change alongside the tools and techniques that are associated with effective change management. You will have the opportunity to apply these frameworks and insights to the development of a change management plan that can be applied to organisations today.
learning_outcomes: Explain and Justify appropriate theories and models of organisational change
Consider how interpersonal relationships and group dynamics influence the success and failure of organisational change
Identify a range of application tools and techniques as part of effective change management
Apply your understanding of change management theory alongside available tools for practice to implement changes for individuals and organisations

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Human Resource Strategies
syllabus_overview: The need for sustained competitive advantage has made the strategic management of Human Resources (HR) increasingly important for long term business success​. This course is designed to provide students with an understanding of the principles and practices of strategic human resource management and will introduce key frameworks, theories, and constructs in the field to examine current issues and debates and to identify how HR strategies can increase employee well-being and organisational effectiveness. Students will examine the fit between HR practices and concepts, and will build a strategic framework to integrate and influence strategic decision making within an organisation. By assessing the needs and skills of a workforce, students will be required to critically analyse and to develop HR strategies to better reach an organisation's goals of enhancing workforce productivity, improving employee and supervisor relations, fostering an environment conducive to a diverse and inclusive worklplace, and strengthening employee retention.
learning_outcomes: Develop and implement strategies to effectively communicate and engage with stakeholders, including employees, senior management, and external partners, to promote buy-in and support within an organisation.
Evaluate the effectiveness of HR strategies, using appropriate metrics and analytics, and develop strategies for continuous improvement and optimisation of HR strategy development and implementation.
Develop a comprehensive understanding of HR strategies and their role in supporting organisational goals and objectives
Assess different HR strategies and their application to different organisational contexts, and develop effective HR strategies for organisational success

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing People and Organisations
syllabus_overview: The organisations we work in are rich and complex systems in which many interactions, relationships and processes are played out daily. The complexity of these interactions often makes them difficult to understand and manage. This course is designed to introduce you to some of the key ideas, current issues and debates about management and managing others within an organisation. With a focus on core functions such as decision-making, planning, organising, leading, each unit in this course will contribute to bettering your undertaking of managerial roles so that you can become a better manager of yourself, others, teams, and organisations.
learning_outcomes: Gain an understanding of teaming and discuss how to design, manage, and lead effective teams.
Develop skills to network and influence relationships with various stakeholders, including senior management, employees, and external parties, to achieve organisational objectives.
Understand how to plan, organise, lead, and make decisions in a range of organisational environments from simple to complex.
Apply the frameworks and models to engage in critical reflection of your experiences in the various managerial roles in which you participate.
Describe and critically discuss different frameworks and models that inform managerial life inside organisations.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Organisational Development
syllabus_overview: In an increasingly competitive, challenging and changing global environment, viable organisational development and design is becoming an essential and critical strategy component. For sustained success, businesses need to continuously align strategy with culture, internal processes and communications. This course will equip you with the skills and expertise to help an organisation enhance and improve the effectiveness and efficiency of its processes, structures, and culture, at all levels. You will be asked to critically evaluate and analyse the relational dependencies and interactions of an organisation's components and to build a planned and longer-term systematic approach in strengthening people and culture, influencing stakeholders, implementing and managing organisation-wide change, increasing productivity and reducing staff turnover.
learning_outcomes: Integrate organisational development into overall HR strategy and planning
Develop a strategic approach to aligning organisational development initiatives with organisational goals and objectives
Describe organisational development and its role in improving organisational effectiveness, agility, and resilience

Design strategies to effectively communicate and engage with stakeholders, including employees, senior management, and external partners, to promote buy-in and support for organisational development initiatives

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Human Resources Analytics
syllabus_overview: Across a variety of different fields, organisations are increasingly using data and the insights that can be gained from this data to help inform decisions and shape their strategies. There are significant opportunities for analytics to inform the effective management of human resources across a broad range of dimensions. This course introduces the areas where analytics can support various aspects of human resource management and examines how data is being used to help organisations improve the performance of their people. Students will get hands on experience applying data analytics techniques to HR data sets and develop an understanding of how HR analytics can be best integrated into HR strategy, policies, and practices.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret HR data to support evidence-based decisions.
Evaluate ethical challenges and legal considerations in the use of HR data.
Prepare and manage HR data using appropriate cleaning and validation techniques.
Communicate HR insights effectively to diverse audiences.
Effectively integrate both qualitative and quantitative HR data to develop actionable recommendations.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZBU6501 Introductory Data Analysis

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Attracting, Evaluating and Retaining Talent
syllabus_overview: This course covers human resource management (HRM) practices involved with attracting, evaluating, and retaining talent. In relation to recruitment, selection, and retention, this course will help you navigate key HRM processes. In this course, students will develop practical skills in relation to effective recruitment and selection. In terms of talent management, this course will explore ways in which organisations and HRM professionals can better support and retain employees.
learning_outcomes: Develop and extend skills in conducting candidate interviews and writing recruitment messages from an HRM perspective
Demonstrate understanding of existing employee recruitment, selection, and retention practices in organisations
Assess best practices for attracting, evaluating, and retaining talent
Analyse how talent management aligns with employee outcomes and organisational goals
Apply leading turnover theories to better support and retain employees

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Leadership Development
syllabus_overview: The current global labour skills gap crisis has turned focus towards human resources. Growing complexity, uncertainty and increasing regulation in the labour market, has highlighted the importance of a purpose driven culture and the need for leadership skills, and qualities, at every level of an organisation. This course will equip students with the framework to implement leadership development programs to ensure contemporary and viable leadership within an organisation. Students will be introduced to strategies to train, develop and motivate themselves and others, in key leadership skills to better enable an organisation to deliver on its strategic objectives. Through an understanding of the critical leadership qualities required by an organisation, students will have the capability to support a culture of learning, develop effective corporate succession planning, implement coaching for strengthened employee engagement, improve retention strategies and enhance workforce productivity to overcome business challenges.
learning_outcomes: Identify and address challenges in developing and nurturing effective leadership at various organisational levels
Develop strategies to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders
Leverage ethical and responsible leadership to cultivate sustainable team and organisational excellence
Critically evaluate different approaches to advance and implement effective leader development initiatives
Develop a comprehensive understanding of leadership and leader development

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introductory Data Analysis
syllabus_overview: A key foundational step for business analytics is understanding the ways in which data can be presented and analysed. Introductory Data Analysis provides a solid basis from which data analysis techniques can be applied to solve business problems and support evidence-based decision making, with a specific focus on the use of Microsoft Excel. This course will cover methods such as charts, descriptive statistics, probability distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and basic regression models. These methods will be the foundations for more advanced courses using statistical and econometric methods.
learning_outcomes: Interpret, formulate and communicate statistical findings in a clear and concise manner.
Use and interpret descriptive and inferential statistics.
Evaluate the range of ethical, cultural, and social issues confronting individuals when collecting and reporting data.
Explain basic statistical methods and know when and how to apply appropriate methods in practical scenarios.
Apply a range of appropriate statistical tools and techniques to identify, analyse and solve business problems.
Independently use Excel’s graphical and statistical capabilities.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Introduction to Employment Law
syllabus_overview: Employment Law deals with the law governing the formation, content and termination of employment relationships. This course will examine the complex integration of the body of federal and state statutes, industrial instruments and the common law contract of employment. Students will gain insight to the formation, duration and termination of an employment contract and the ability to comprehend terms expressed, implied or otherwise incorporated into the contract of employment. Students will be assessed on their understanding of the rights and liabilities of employers and employees under contract, legislation, awards and industrial instruments and what remedies are available to parties for breach of employment contracts, regulations or awards.
learning_outcomes: Discuss ways to avoid breaches of an employer’s legal obligations
Recommend practices that promote high performance and productivity within the legal framework
Identify the legal risks throughout the employment lifecycle and explain the consequences of non-compliance and inadequate employee management
Demonstrate understanding of the legal framework and compliance requirements pertaining to employment

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Analytics and Business
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: Business Analytics entails the use of data to support business decision-making. The field has emerged as a crucial element of contemporary business practice. With the amount and range of information available to organisations growing exponentially, the ability to harness this information for evidence-based management has become a key capability. This course presents the fundamentals of implementing and managing business analytics in organisations including: decision making; business analytics concepts and frameworks; technologies and tools required for descriptive analytics, predictive analytics, and prescriptive analytics; frameworks for putting analytics to work; technologies and tools required for business analytics; the governance, oversight and business value gained from business analytics within organizations; ethical and social implications of business analytics; future directions for business analytics.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the goals and roles of the various stakeholders in an analytics project.
Describe the purpose and value of using analytics systems to achieve organisational goals.
Determine the key tasks and components required for an analytics project.
Recognise the strategic and operational issues addressed by analytics.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Visualisation and Communication
school: School of Risk and Actuarial Studies
syllabus_overview: Data visualisation and communication are increasingly important as complements to the study of analytics. The ability to present visual access to the huge amounts of data that business creates is an essential skill for any analyst. Easily digestible visuals and graphics are often the simplest and most powerful tools to enable communication of business insights gained from data. In this course, students will learn what makes an effective data visualisation and how to create interactive data visualisations. Visualisation in Tableau and other tools including cutting-edge graphical, immersive techniques will be explored. There will also be a strong focus on developing the skill of data storytelling. Students will learn how to combine data, create effective and engaging data visualisations and construct powerful stories to drive change.
learning_outcomes: Communicate data insights effectively to a variety of audiences.
Critically evaluate and interpret data graphics.
Produce appropriate high-quality data visualisations using a variety of techniques.
Apply data storytelling techniques to a range of business problems.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZBU6501 or ZZSC9001

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data and Ethics
syllabus_overview: This course provides the conceptual foundations for ethical data analytics practice. You will learn to consider data analytics in the context of the broader social, economic and value systems within which data analytics takes place. You will identify ethical concerns and apply ethical thinking tools and frameworks to resolve actual ethical dilemmas. This course also provides you with an understanding of key regulatory frameworks and legal principles related to data generation, manipulation and use.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on your own values, practices and role as a potential agent of positive change.
Identify the principles of data stewardship, governance and integrity.
Situate data analytics within broad and complex contexts.
Apply ethical frameworks and principles to data analytics scenarios.
Evaluate the consequences and impacts of data decisions.
Identify the legal, regulatory and privacy considerations relating to data in key jurisdictions.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing People, Analytics and Change
syllabus_overview: Using an evidence-based approach, this course explores the people-related elements of a business's strategy and looks at the ways in which data analytics both drives and supports change in organisations. The course focuses on developing skills in designing and implementing successful organisational change processes.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the human side of analytics at the intra-personal, interpersonal, organisational and societal/ macro levels.
Identify the perspectives, interests and needs of stakeholders in an analytics environment.
Conceptualise and explain complex and dynamic relationships between change, people and analytics.
Identify and apply key actions and processes required to successfully implement change in an analytics context.
Evaluate models of change management and their application in an analytics setting.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Analytics and Consulting
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on the key concepts, practices and issues in engaging and providing analytics-based consulting services, from both the client and the consultant perspectives. The course examines the value propositions of consulting, how consultants engage with organisations and key stakeholders, and how they help analyse and solve business problems. The course seeks to familiarise you with the consulting process, common consulting frameworks and the benefits and limitations related to their use,and current trends in consulting related to the opportunities and challenges brought about by rapidly advancing technologies.
learning_outcomes: Apply appropriate consulting frameworks and methods for analysing business issues and strategies.
Explain the value proposition of analytics consulting and how it can aid organisations in dynamic market environments.
Analyse and explain how to effectively manage the risks and ethical considerations of consulting engagements.
Describe key consulting processes and how to effectively engage with internal and external stakeholders.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Financial Modelling
school: School of Accounting, Auditing and Taxation
syllabus_overview: Financial Modelling will explore the techniques used by analysts in the business environment to facilitate financial decision-making processes within uncertain contexts. This course aims to engender skills and confidence to effectively create and use financial models, helping students to better understand and communicate the practical value of financial models, and to build this literacy for their future work. Students will develop and extend their skills in high-level critical thinking, problem-solving, and analysis. Students will also develop a set of practical tools and techniques to help them make effective judgements about a organisation’s current financial situation and future performance based on best-practice financial modelling principles.
learning_outcomes: Review and critique financial models against best-practice principles
Describe the value and use of financial models to understand the current financial situation and analyse the potential future performance of a business
Design and construct financial models that adhere to best-practice principles
Communicate confidently and effectively within a business, using the tools and techniques of financial modelling.
Evaluate and apply pertinent spreadsheeting analysis techniques to solve problems
Analyse and break down complex problems into simple conceptual models
prerequisites: ZZBU6501 Introductory Data Analysis

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Predictive Analytics
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: A critical aspect of analytics is to generate predictions which are used as inputs into decision making. Predictive analytics applies statistical models and machine learning methods to data to give insight into potential futures. This course exposes students to predictive analytics methods to develop students’ ability to use analytics to drive decision making. To develop these skills, students will learn predictive analytics methodological theory (e.g., linear and logistic regression, classification and regression trees, and neural networks). Students will then build and interpret a variety of predictive models to analyse data describing problems with real-world relevance. Emphasis will be placed on using predictive analytics robustly to create value.
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles of predictive modelling techniques such as linear regression, logistic regression and decision trees.
Build predictive analytics models using traditional and modern software (e.g., R and DataRobot).
Apply statistics and data visualisation to explore real data.
Generate actionable insights from data visualisation, classification and prediction modelling techniques.
Identify organisational benefits from modern visualisation and automated machine learning.
prerequisites: Pre-requisite: ZZBU6501

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing Customer Analytics
syllabus_overview: To understand consumers and build a relationship with customers is the first step of every marketing decision. To be effective, marketing managers should know how to identify what target customers need, where they go to shop and how to interact with them in a marketplace. This course integrates customer relationship management (CRM) and big data analytics in applications ranging from attracting new consumers, retaining customers and encouraging referrals to re-inviting infrequent or lost customers using prediction, recommendation and natural language processing.
learning_outcomes: Clearly and effectively communicate the business value of customer data analytics
Explain the customer life cycle and develop data-driven CRM techniques.
Use relevant data analytics tools to identify and analyse customer needs.
Make model-based actionable decisions in a CRM context.
prerequisites: ZZBU6501 Introductory Data Analysis

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Database Management
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: This course will provide students with an understanding of the key concepts, principles and characteristics of Big Data, databases and database management systems, as well as the associated analytical tools and technologies for developing solutions to large-scale business problems. Students will develop conceptual and practical knowledge of database structures and systems, through the study of data modelling, relational design, query and programming languages and normalisation theory. The course will prepare students for future database challenges including database security and integrity.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate competence in the use of SQL to create, query and manipulate databases.
Critically review the concepts, principles and key characteristics of big data, databases and database management systems.
Build and utilise database solutions to support big data analytics.
Evaluate and propose relevant and feasible database infrastructure solutions for specific business analytic problems.
Apply conceptual database modelling techniques and normalisation techniques.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Fully online - Standard (usually weekly or fortnightly)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Foundations of Marketing Analytics
syllabus_overview: Foundations of Marketing Analytics will help to develop students’ capabilities of using advanced analytical tools to address marketing problems – key skills that numerous companies have stated they look for in marketers, particularly in challenging business environments. Students are exposed to a range of statistical tools and techniques, from classical statistical tools to emerging big data techniques. The emphasis is not on formulae of statistical tools, but on how to apply and interpret a range of statistical techniques to help answer marketing-related questions. The course is organised around daily marketing problems. Students are strongly encouraged to start thinking as marketers by asking questions of their data, setting their own direction for the analysis in the project and thinking about how a company could utilise the results in practice.
learning_outcomes: Choose appropriate data sources and analytical tools to design a sophisticated analytical study.
Translate the output from analyses into managerial insights that is understandable to marketing managers.
Gain an overview of advances in marketing analytics.
Competently and confidently communicate research findings.
Use advanced analytical tools to analyse a variety of data collected by marketers.
prerequisites: ZZBU6501 Introductory Data Analysis

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Social Media & Digital Analytics
syllabus_overview: This course explores the impact of the social media and digital technology on marketing. This course introduces students to the analytic methods that can be used to convert social media and digital data to marketing insights. Students will examine the impact of social media and digital technology on customer acquisition, customer retention, customer development and customer relationship management. This course provides learners with the foundational skills of social media and digital analytics including the creation of monitors and common analytical metrics. This course also aims to enable students to analyse social media and digital data and to develop relevant marketing strategies in a digital world. Furthermore, the course introduces students to the underlying theories of social media and digital technology as well as practical experiences relevant for business. On successful completion of the course, students are expected to gain good analytical skills and marketing insights regarding social media and digital technology.
learning_outcomes: Analyse social media and other digital data and integrate it with data insights
Identify relevant consumer behaviour using analytics
Communicate data insights effectively
Develop plans that reflect the digital marketing strategies and its relationship to broader organization strategies
Critically review digital marketing decisions based on legal, moral, and ethical considerations

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Analytics Capstone
school: School of Information Systems and Technology Management
syllabus_overview: The capstone project is the culminating experience of the Master of Analytics program and provides you with the opportunity to apply and integrate your knowledge and skills in an actual professional context. You will undertake a range of applied professional tasks to complete your project. This involves a relevant literature review in the selected focus area, application of design thinking and other analysis tools, project implementation using analytics methods/toolsets, and critical reflection of real-world practice. The course provides you with a variety of resources and activities that are carefully designed to support your journey to complete this capstone project. The course combines theory and practice to encourage active engagement and self-reflection and enhance your learning for professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Formulate and communicate evidence-based solutions to industry problems and issues
Critically reflect on self-leadership and professional capabilities
Apply knowledge and skills in analytics to business scenarios and professional practice.
Evaluate analytics practices and outcomes in the light of ethical and legal considerations.
prerequisites: 36UOC and enrolled in Master of Analytics (8437)

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: FinTech Ecosystem and Industry Insights
syllabus_overview: The course gives an overview of the major changes that have recently occurred in the financial services industry. It includes a series of discussions of some of the main disruption concepts in this space, highlighting the main types of business models adopted, the skills required to succeed in this industry, and the future career opportunities that can still arise. This course focuses on financial technology (FinTech) case studies, which will be backed by testimonials from industry executives who will share their experiences with the program participants through recorded interviews. These executives will share practical challenges, trends that they observe in the industry, and the upcoming opportunities that they envision for a career in FinTech. These experts will be from different areas of FinTech such as crowdfunding, data mining, robo-advice, payments, foreign currency transfers and regulation.
learning_outcomes: Compose FinTech solutions illustrating what types of innovation and disruption have the potential
Demonstrate understanding of the global FinTech landscape, explaining the role of banks and financial service providers in shaping and responding to innovation and disruption.
Describe the banking and finance ecosystem and the role of consumers in shaping this ecosystem.
Apply disruption methodologies and industry knowledge to practical case studies and problems.
Link behavioural finance theories to technological advances in banking.
Identify the possibilities, boundaries, challenges and complexities of technology in the context of banking and finance innovation.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Decentralised Finance
syllabus_overview: This course gives students an introduction to cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, and the way they’re used in decentralised finance (DeFi). The course works from the basic concepts surrounding currency, to the evolution of the first blockchain technologies, to modern decentralised financial markets and their (attempted) regulation. The course covers Ethereum and smart contracts, which form the basis of further topics including automated market makers, decentralised borrowing and lending markets, stablecoins, on- chain derivatives, DAOs and insurance. The course will also examine blockchain scalability (layer 2 solutions), the evolution of fundraising, regulation and implications and applications in traditional finance. The course will involve practical activities with cryptocurrencies, trading, and creating your own cryptocurrency (ERC20 token).
learning_outcomes: Engage in DeFi native collaboration and identify how it differs to traditional finance
Assess the value proposition of Bitcoin, Ethereum and DeFi
Analyse key trends and developments related to DeFi
Interact with DeFi applications such as DEXs, DeFi lending, yield aggregators and stablecoins

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Technical Tools for FinTech
syllabus_overview: This course deals with the implications of technological advances on the current and future states of the financial services industry. The course introduces Python as a useful tool for financial analysis and application of such tool range across different FinTech areas, such as digital currency (Bitcoin), settlements (Blockchain), hedging, trading strategies, and financial advisory. The learning is project-based, with emphasis on writing robust programs that execute a desired solution to a realistic problem. The fundamental techniques and methodologies discussed in this course are designed to facilitate problem-solving in the advanced courses covered in the overall FinTech Program.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate implications of technological advances on the current and future states of the financial services industry.
Develop a toolkit of common tools used in financial markets.
Apply a variety of technical tools in real-world settings in the financial services industry.
Translate abstract financial theories into usable tools for competing in the financial workplace.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: RegTech Applications for Banking and Finance
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on the set of rules, controls, policies, and resolutions put in place to dictate corporate behaviour in the FinTech industry. The last few decades have seen a rapid growth in regulations, aimed at addressing key concerns emerging from crises and scandals within the banking and finance world. Regulators have implemented tougher regulations, improved their own monitoring and detection capabilities, and imposed expectations on participants to improve their detection of internal and external misconduct. The growth in the finance industry and the move towards electronic banking needs a system-based approach to regulation management. This course is designed to provide an overview of the types of requirements that apply to modern financial corporations and the core types of systems that are deployed to address these requirements.
learning_outcomes: Develop a Compliance Risk Assessment for a chosen financial institution.
Critically evaluate RegTech solutions and their implementation as part of broader governance, risk management and compliance practices.
Describe different types of RegTech systems currently used or under development in financial institutions and markets.
Evaluate the role technology-based solutions play in implementing elements of a compliance framework.
Demonstrate understanding of the role of regulators in relation to risk management and regulatory expectations
Evaluate the compliance frameworks within which financial institutions and markets operate, their structure, and role in risk management.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Problem-Solving Methods for FinTech
syllabus_overview: This course applies the techniques and methodologies covered in ZZBU8504 Technical Tools for FinTech to solve real problems from the financial services industry. Using a hands-on approach, the course helps students develop their own toolkit for solving problems in derivative valuation, risk analytics, and standard statistical modeling. In addition, advanced topics on time-series data, sentiment analysis, and graphical visualization methods will be covered. This course emphasizes applications in finance.
learning_outcomes: Develop a toolkit of common tools used in financial markets.
Translate abstract financial theories into usable tools for competing in the financial workplace.
Select and apply appropriate techniques and methodologies to solve real problems from the financial services industry.
Apply a variety of technical tools in real-world settings in the financial services industry.
prerequisites: Pre-requisite: ZZBU8504

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Management for FinTech
syllabus_overview: FinTech is all about dealing with different types of data from the financial services industry. It is essential to learn about the various types of database systems available, as well as about their pros and cons. There is no one-size-fits-all solution when it comes to dealing with data. This course will help students to understand which database to use given the characteristics of the data, which can be either quantitative or qualitative, structured or unstructured. After completing this course, students are expected to develop data management skills and be able to deal with many different data issues that can emerge in real-world circumstances.
learning_outcomes: Efficiently work with structured and unstructured financial data
Employ good design practices to develop solutions for data management in real-world financial markets
Gain real problem-solving experience
Demonstrate familiarity with industry-standard data management applications
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZBU8504

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Tech Disruption in Payments and Transfers
syllabus_overview: This course will first convey in-depth knowledge of all aspects of the payments and transfer industry, one of the fastest-growing segments at the forefront of the FinTech revolution. We will start with the existing payment infrastructure, discuss simple innovations at the point-of-sale, more complex payment eco-systems, international transfer solutions as well as the prospects of central bank digital currencies. Second, we will use multiple frameworks to systematically analyse incumbent solutions and new entrants under strategic and marketing, economic and financial, ethical and regulatory considerations. Case studies and guided research into contemporaneous industry participants as well as expert interviews provide additional practice and insights. Regularly, students will be invited to bring their personal and professional experience into the course in discussions and other student-led activities. In the end, this should enable students to independently analyse the market that is most interesting to them or most related to their work, recognise pain points in existing solutions, identify gaps and opportunities and systematically assess them using what they have learned in the course.
learning_outcomes: Identify opportunities and frictions in existing systems.
Analyse innovations in payments and transfers and assess their impact.
Apply knowledge to case studies and practical problems.
Discuss how the emergence of non-traditional banks, crypto and digital currencies will affect the payment and banking industry.
Explain the major traditional payment systems in use today.
Discuss the economics and business models of new entrants and the value they create.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Tech Disruption in Funding and Lending
syllabus_overview: This course deals with funding and lending in the modern age of rapid technological change. It explores the business models and financial mechanisms behind innovative funding arrangements and discusses their disruptive potential as well as relevant risks. Topics include, but are not limited to, ICOs, peer-to-peer lending, token and security-based crowdfunding, and liquidity pools. The course allows students to view the issues from three different perspectives: users of capital (borrowers), providers of capital (investors), and market designers (regulators or platform owners). Learning is reinforced by relevant assessments, such as testing one’s investment performance in a crowdfunding market (without putting actual capital at risk). It is further supported by cutting-edge research, which highlights opportunities and application challenges in a constantly evolving crowdfunding space.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate different features of a crowdfunding platform design and recognise their impact on borrowers and investors.
Compare the lending models of banks and alternative capital providers and describe their relative strengths and weaknesses.
Map the structure of an ICO funding process and perform basic due diligence on ICO campaigns.
Identify investment opportunities and risks associated with investing in new digital asset classes.
Adopting different perspectives, argue in favour or against specific regulations affecting the crowdfunding industry.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: AI in Consumer Finance
syllabus_overview: This course explores the transformative applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within the consumer finance sector. It examines the types of AI used in fintech and banking, consumer attitudes towards AI, and the ethical considerations surrounding its implementation. The course also addresses challenges such as biases, hallucinations, and the alignment of objectives, as well as strategies for ensuring proper usage and promoting transparency.
learning_outcomes: Identify and develop strategies for consumer and staff demand or aversion towards AI in financial services.
Apply ethical frameworks to AI applications in consumer finance, and discuss the importance and challenges of aligning AI objectives with ethical standards and business goals.
Evaluate the risks associated with biases and hallucinations in AI systems, and compare biases in AI with human behavioural biases.
Identify and describe different types of AI used in fintech and banking.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: InsurTech Applications
syllabus_overview: This course aims to inspire students to launch a start-up that disrupts the sector and solves some of the challenges customers face with insurance. By sharing practical examples that bring theoretical and complex concepts to life, this course will instil passion and enthusiasm in students. These practical examples are supported by direct experiences of insurance as customers, highlighting the important role insurance plays in their lives and the significant financial opportunity there is in disrupting the sector. Applied concepts underlying what InsurTechs are and the problems they are looking to solve in the sector will enhance the students’ understanding of InsurTech applications and will eventually enable a greater appreciation of the importance of insurance in customers’ lives, the key pain points customers face, the role technology has in enhancing the sector and outcomes for customers, start-ups, and end customers.
learning_outcomes: Clearly and professionally communicate the elements of a potential insurance product.
Demonstrate a familiarity with the key concepts in insurance and InsurTech.
Apply the understanding of InsurTech ecosystems to develop an insurance product.
Articulate insights from successful insurance and InsurTechs on disruption, meeting customer needs and driving growth.
Demonstrate an understanding of the global and Australian InsurTech landscape.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Robo-Advice
syllabus_overview: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of robo-advisors, highlighting their role in today's financial planning and investment management. Students will begin by building efficient portfolios using Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) and gaining hands on experience with practical applications in Excel. The course then delves into behavioural household finance, focusing on common investment biases and mistakes made by households. Students will examine potential solutions to these issues, including traditional financial advice and the use of ETFs. Later, students will investigate the empirical benefits of robo-advisors, supported by real-world examples.
learning_outcomes: Analyse, construct, and modify investment portfolios that maximise the reward-to-risk ratio, and understanding deviations from fundamental values, such as market anomalies.
Explain the foundational concepts of traditional financial theory, behavioural finance, and household finance as they relate to robo-advice and decision support.
Evaluate various behavioural biases exhibited by clients, linking these biases to demographics, financial literacy, and common investment mistakes to achieve better investment outcomes.
Design or critically analyse financial decision support tools, utilising insights from behavioural finance to tailor recommendations to client circumstances.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Managing a FinTech Startup
syllabus_overview: This course is intended to expose students to the challenges associated with creating and managing a startup in the FinTech industry. It covers the common requirements for any startup firm, such as the design of a business plan, fund raising, mentoring, among others.
