In addition, training in the methods of psychological inquiry and in the critical evaluation of research is also provided. This course is appropriate for students with and without a background in science. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Communicate and discuss ideas in psychology effectively in written and oral forms, including in constructive critiques to peers.
Apply and incorporate knowledge about the scientific methods in psychology when explaining and describing phenomena in physiological psychology.
Apply psychological theories to explain, describe and compare the neural bases that underpin a range of human behaviours.

Identify and contrast the major concepts and theoretical and empirical evidence for the physiological processes that underpin associative learning, neurobiology, cognition, abnormal psychology and perception.
Explain and evaluate the importance of evidence based diagnostic tools and treatment strategies in clinical psychology.
Critically analyse the psychology literature including research methodology, experimental design and interpretation of the results.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Analysis and Methods of Psychological Inquiry
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with knowledge about the characteristics of science, scientific method, experimental design and data analysis in behavioural sciences. It provides a comprehensive foundation in critical thinking, enabling students to design and execute experiments, analyse and interpret the results, scrutinise and critically evaluate published research and discriminate between evidence-based information and pseudoscience. The course progresses from a discussion of different methodological approaches and data collection techniques to descriptive statistics, foundations of hypothesis testing and the introduction of specific statistical tests. This course is appropriate for students with and without a background in science. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Scrutinise non-experimental based information using scientific methods and critical thinking.
Apply knowledge about research methods and statistics to critically evaluate results of evidence-based research.
Recognise and evaluate experimental ethics in behavioural sciences in the context of experimental research.
Describe the evidence-based research, major concepts, historical trends in statistics and research methods used in behavioural sciences.
Apply principles of empirical research in behavioural science to formulate testable hypotheses and design experiments.
Communicate and discuss the outcomes of experimental research and data analysis.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZPS5001 and ZZPS5002

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Advanced Data Analysis and Methods of Psychological Inquiry
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with advanced knowledge of statistics and research methods in behavioural sciences. The course activities will teach students how to analyse data obtained in various experimental designs using a computer-based statistical package. This course is appropriate for students who have acquired foundational knowledge of research methods and statistics taught in PSYC5003 course. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate research designs with multiple group comparisons, including factorial and mixed designs, focusing on data analysis and interpretation of the results.
Report experimental results, analytical details, relevant theoretical and empirical information, and conclusions, communicating in written format.
Select appropriate statistical methods and perform data analysis using relevant computational tools.
Identify gaps in previous research and develop arguments for different experimental designs and data analysis to answer research questions and test hypotheses.
Assess ethical issues in data analysis and reporting and identify errors in data presentation.
Apply knowledge of advanced statistics and research methods to analyse and interpret experimental results.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZPS5001 and ZZPS5002 and ZZPS5003

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Behavioural Neuroscience
syllabus_overview: This course examines the elementary processes of learning and memory and the neurobiological mechanisms that underpin them. These include: learning about relations between events (Pavlovian conditioning), learning about relations between one’s behaviour and events (Instrumental conditioning), and how these forms of learning control behaviour. There will be an emphasis on the current experimental and theoretical research, including the role of neural systems in supporting behaviour, the role of molecular signaling cascades and neuronal encoding in learning and memory. The course is appropriate for the student with knowledge of advanced statistics and research methods in Psychology. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Design a research experiment and justify its importance by integrating empirical evidence, relevant theories, and knowledge of ethical treatment of animals in research.
Describe and evaluate experimental methodologies used in behavioural neuroscience research with respect to current empirical and theoretical evidence.

Assess and explain the implications of theoretical concepts and research findings from the field of behavioural neuroscience on understanding mental health issues such as anxiety, addiction and schizophrenia.
Construct effective scientific arguments by reviewing and synthesising relevant empirical evidence and theories in neuroscience.
Identify the ethical issues involved in animal and human research, including the importance of ethical guidelines in animal research.

Identify the major concepts of behavioural neuroscience, with a focus on the principles of associative learning, the neurobiological mechanisms of fear, habits and addiction, and memory and forgetting.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZPS5001 and ZZPS5002 and ZZPS5003 and ZZPS5004

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: The Individual, Culture and Society
syllabus_overview: This course will provide an advanced overview of topics relating to self-identity, culture and sociality. Topics will include the formation of identity, cross-cultural psychology, indigenous psychology, biological mechanisms underpinning social learning and attribution, as well as social disorders. The course will cover the principles and methodology of research into social phenomena such as affiliation, attraction, group behavior and prejudice. The course is appropriate for the student with knowledge of advanced statistics and research methods. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Identify, examine and critically analyse evidence and effectiveness of assessment practices and strategies related to issues with marginalised, minority and indigenous groups within the current and historical perspective.
Critically evaluate primary and secondary reports of evidence-based research and provide a critical analysis of the validity of the secondary reports.
Compare and evaluate different research methods and research evidence in social psychology.

Recognise and compare major theories and research evidence in human social behaviour, group dynamics and social influences, indigenous psychology, morality, aggression, emotion and the individual in society.
Effectively communicate relevant results and issues in research in social psychology to broad audiences and in different formats.

Critically evaluate literature and develop an evidence-based argument for issues related to the impact of majority cultures on minority cultures and indigenous populations within the context of social psychology.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZPS5001 and ZZPS5002 and ZZPS5003 and ZZPS5004

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Perception and Cognition
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to those areas of psychology that are more closely concerned with “the mind”. The fundamental principles underlying human perception and cognition introduced in the course are perceptual organisation, perception of spatial layout, perceptual learning, object recognition, attention, memory storage and retrieval, problem solving and decision making. The course is appropriate for the student with knowledge of advanced statistics and research methods. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Review and evaluate evidence from the relevant perception and cognition literature to identify gaps in previous research and develop an evidence-based argument.
Identify and compare major concepts, theories, and research evidence in the field of perception and cognition.
Assess and explain the implications of theoretical concepts and research findings from the field of perception and cognition on understanding various human behaviors.
Apply knowledge of different research methods and data analysis in the perception and cognition research.
Select and apply appropriate statistical methods to analyse data, answer research questions and test hypotheses in the field of perception and cognition.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZPS5001 and ZZPS5002 and ZZPS5003 and ZZPS5004

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Psychology Across the Lifespan
syllabus_overview: This course will address topics relating to the development and interaction of biological, cognitive, emotional and social processes across the lifespan. These topics will be investigated in different stages of life including prenatal and early development, childhood, adolescence, late adulthood and senescence. The course will also address the aetiology of psychological disorders related to these life stages such as developmental disorders and dementias. The course is appropriate for the student with knowledge of advanced statistics and research methods in Psychology. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Research and examine the literature on human development across the lifespan by utilising appropriate research methods in developmental psychology.
Work effectively in a team, including providing constructive feedback, and reflecting on your role as a team member.
Communicate effectively about theories and evidence in developmental psychology in written format.
Analyse and evaluate evidence related to the development of behaviour and mental processes in the context of developmental psychology and scientific research.
Formulate an evidence-based argument using concepts, theories, and research findings in developmental psychology.
Identify the psychological, social and biological mechanisms that underpin developmental change across the lifespan by incorporating current theoretical and empirical evidence.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZPS5001 and ZZPS5002 and ZZPS5003 and ZZPS5004

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Abnormal Psychology
syllabus_overview: This course will provide a contemporary view of issues associated with human mental health and psychopathology. It will introduce and discuss the notion of abnormality in behaviour, how a range of mental disorders are diagnosed, the prognosis and treatment in human mental disorders as well as the stigma and media coverage of mental health. There will be an emphasis on the current experimental and theoretical research and evidence based clinical practice. The course is appropriate for students with knowledge of advanced statistics and research methods in Psychology. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Identify and compare the empirical evidence related to the causes of mental disorders and medical and psychological treatments for specific disorders.
Explain and discuss the outcomes of experimental research and data analysis in abnormal psychology using various formats and different contexts.
Evaluate, summarise and effectively communicate theories and empirical evidence in the field of abnormal psychology utilising the scientific method.
Recognise the impact of prejudice, attitudes and discriminatory behaviours on the aetiology, diagnosis and treatment of psychological disorders.
Apply theories and empirical evidence within the field of abnormal psychology research to discuss personal, social and organisational issues in applied settings.
Analyse and interpret the evidence for aetiology, underlying mechanisms, diagnostic criteria and treatment of mental disorders.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZPS5001 and ZZPS5002 and ZZPS5003 and ZZPS5004

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Psychological Assessment, Ethics, and Professional Skills
syllabus_overview: This course will provide an overview of the design and implementation for a range of psychological assessments, tools and practices. The course will further explore the importance of ethics in psychological research, application, and clinical practice. Students will have the opportunity to develop basic professional skills required for further study and practice in the field of psychology. This course provides fundamental knowledge for further studies in psychology including honours, masters and PhD programs. The course is appropriate for the student with knowledge of advanced statistics and research methods. The course content will be delivered via asynchronous (pre-recorded) lectures, synchronous tutorials, readings and self-paced modules and quizzes.
learning_outcomes: Identify the core concepts in psychological testing, assessment, ethics and application.
Analyse and evaluate theories and empirical evidence for the application of psychological assessment tools in the context of applied psychology.
Describe and explain test construction, implementation and interpretation in applied psychology by utilising research methods and data analysis.
Understand and apply the principles of research and uses of psychological assessment in applied psychology.
Effectively communicate about the principles of psychological assessment, ethics and application in different formats.
Discuss and apply ethical values that are key to research and applied professional practice.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZPS5001 and ZZPS5002 and ZZPS5003 and ZZPS5004 and ZZPS5005 and ZZPS5006 and ZZPS5007 and ZZPS5008 and ZZPS5009

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Behaviour in Organisations
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to human behaviour in organisational settings. Students examine individual, group, and cultural factors that shape workplace behaviour, performance, and decision making. Emphasis is placed on applying behavioural principles to understand organisational dynamics, develop critical insights, and engage responsibly and ethically in professional contexts. Students gain foundational skills in interpreting evidence, analysing behaviour, and communicating insights professionally.
learning_outcomes: Analyse individual and group behaviour to identify factors influencing workplace outcomes.
Examine foundational concepts, theories, and frameworks in organisational behaviour as they apply to professional contexts.
Apply organisational behaviour insights to propose responsible and ethical solutions to workplace challenges.
Communicate evidence-informed analyses and recommendations clearly and professionally.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Visualisation for Data Science
syllabus_overview: This fully-online course introduces students to data visualisation in the areas of statistical analysis and data science. Students will learn how to make their own effective and impactful visualisations using software tools including R. There will be a strong focus on developing the skill of data storytelling: combining data, its visualisation, and a narrative to create a powerful story to drive change. Key topics include visualisation for exploratory and statistical data analysis and interactive visualisations such as dashboards. Note: This course is only available to students enrolled in 7446 Graduate Certificate in Data Science, 5646 Graduate Diploma in Data Science, or 8646 Master of Data Science Programs.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and interpret data graphics, including understanding and interpreting the output of software packages.
Apply data storytelling techniques to a range of problems in data science, statistics, and applications.
Produce appropriate high quality data visualisations using a variety of software packages and techniques.

Communicate data insights effectively and successfully to a variety of audiences. Successful communication can include accurately portraying insights, promoting understanding, or informing effective decisions.
Apply basic principles and concepts of data visualisation design.
prerequisites: Completion of ZZSC9001: Foundations of Data Science.
Enrolment in 7446, 5646, or 8646.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Research and Evidence in Organisations
syllabus_overview: This course develops skills in interpreting and evaluating research and data in business psychology. Students engage with research design, measurement, and data interpretation in organisational contexts. Emphasis is on critically evaluating evidence, making informed judgments under uncertainty, and responsibly applying research to support professional decision making. Students gain confidence in interpreting findings and communicating insights without requiring advanced technical analysis.
learning_outcomes: Apply principles of scientific inquiry and evidence generation in business psychology.
Assess research quality, limitations, and implications, considering methodological and ethical factors.
Interpret and evaluate research findings and data relevant to organisational contexts.
Communicate evidence-informed insights and professional judgments effectively.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Behavioural Science and Decision Making
syllabus_overview: This course introduces behavioural science principles and their application in organisations. Students explore cognitive, social, and emotional factors influencing decisions and behaviour. Emphasis is on applied reasoning, evidence-informed decision making, and ethically responsible interventions. Students develop skills to analyse decisions, interpret behavioural evidence, and design practical strategies for organisational challenges.
learning_outcomes: Analyse decision-making processes, identifying factors that influence behaviour.
Explain key behavioural science concepts and frameworks using organisational examples.
Communicate evidence-informed behavioural analyses and recommendations professionally.
Apply behavioural insights to propose responsible and ethical recommendations for organisational challenges.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Applied Business Psychology (Capstone)
syllabus_overview: This capstone course integrates learning through an applied business psychology project. Students analyse complex organisational challenges, synthesise psychological, business, and ethical perspectives, and develop evidence-informed strategies. In this course, there is an emphasis on professional judgment, critical reflection, and persuasive communication of recommendations to diverse stakeholders.
learning_outcomes: Communicate recommendations effectively to multiple stakeholders in context-appropriate formats.
Integrate psychological and business frameworks to analyse complex organisational challenges.
Develop evidence-informed strategies addressing organisational problems using business psychology insights.
Reflect critically on professional judgment and capacity in applying business psychology principles.
prerequisites: Students must be enrolled in the Master of Business Psychology and have completed at least 48 UOC.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Behavioural Science and Digital Disruption in Organisations
syllabus_overview: This course examines how digital technologies reshape behaviour, decision making, and collaboration in organisations. Students explore the behavioural implications of how organisations use digital technologies to structure work, make decisions about people, and manage change. Students develop capability in assessing the human impact of technological change and communicating responsible and evidence-informed recommendations in professional contexts.
learning_outcomes: Analyse behavioural science concepts and frameworks as they apply to technology-driven change in organisations.
Apply behavioural insights to design and justify responsible and evidence-informed responses to challenges arising from digital disruption in organisations.
Evaluate the behavioural and ethical implications of technology-driven practices in organisations.
Communicate evidence-informed behavioural analyses and recommendations clearly and persuasively to professional stakeholders using appropriate formats.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Regression Analysis for Data Scientists
syllabus_overview: Regression is a set of statistical techniques widely used to analyse relationships between several variables. In this course, students will explore the applications of a range of regression techniques, including: linear regression; generalised linear models; logistic and Poisson models; penalised regression methods; variable selection and cross-validation; local and spline regression, including penalised, smoothing, regression, and thin plate splines; and generalised additive models. The lectures will be complemented with worked examples using the R data analysis and statistical programming software. This online course covers the same topics as in MATH5806 and is only available to students enrolled in the online Diploma of Data Science and the online Master of Data Science.
learning_outcomes: Compare and utilise various regression models and techniques along with their applications, intuitions, strengths and weaknesses.
Apply the appropriate regression technique to analyse a given data set.
Use output of statistical software along with the theoretical formulas to provide a logical model for a given data set.
Choose the appropriate R packages/functions to apply an appropriate regression technique in the analysis of a given data set.
Interpret the output of statistical software to describe the results of the regression analysis.
Present the results of regression analysis in an appropriate format for a range of intended audiences.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in 5646 or 8646 and have completed ZZSC9001 Foundations of Data Science and ZZSC5905 Statistical Inference for data scientists or equivalent

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Mining and Machine Learning
syllabus_overview: Recent technological advances have given organisations access to enormous data sets that raise challenges for data analysis. Hence, a wide range of data mining methods and tools have been developed to extract information, discover patterns, and enable predictive decision making. Machine learning is the algorithmic approach to learning from data. This course covers the key techniques in data mining and machine learning together with theoretical background and applications. The following topics will be covered in this course: regression and classification problems, data mining performance evaluation, gradient descent learning and backpropagation neural networks, tree-based learning and ensemble methods, clustering and dimensionality reduction, and practical aspects of machine learning applications.
learning_outcomes: Select and define an appropriate representation for data to be used as input to and output from a machine learning algorithm.
Compare different algorithms according to the properties of their inputs and outputs and in terms of similarities and differences in their mathematical and computational aspects.
Develop machine learning algorithms using computational and mathematical techniques to solve learning problems.
Understand the limitations of machine learning and data mining concepts.
Use Machine Learning algorithms on real-world data sets and collect results to enable evaluation and comparison of their performance.
Apply key concepts from the foundations of computational and statistical learning theory and demonstrate their applicability in Machine Learning.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ZZEN9021 and enrolment in either the 5646 or 8646 Data Science program.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Statistical Inference for Data Scientists
syllabus_overview: This intensive course provides an introduction to probability and distribution theory and introductory Statistical Inference. Students will learn the fundamental principles of inference: sufficiency, likelihoods, maximum likelihood and Bayesian methods. Estimation, confidence set construction and hypothesis testing, and computationally intensive methods such as the bootstrap method are also discussed. This course will take the flipped classroom approach and is delivered completely online. Students are assigned the “homework” of watching video lectures and reading materials relevant to the online lecture session. During the session, a recap and overview of the content will be given and students will practice what they’ve learned through examples and tutorial problems. This course is only available to students enrolled in the postgraduate Data Science programs 7446, 5646, 8646.
learning_outcomes: Calculate key population parameters of interest to test hypotheses and to construct confidence regions.
Use computer packages to generate output for the most common inference procedures and for computer-intensive calculations such as bootstrapping.
Apply key methods of statistical inference from first principles of probability theory.
Apply fundamental principles of statistical inference to solve appropriate problems.
Apply various likelihood-based and Bayesian inference methods to analyse data and solve problems.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Multivariate Analysis for Data Scientists
syllabus_overview: This fully-online course gives students a methodological background in Multivariate Analysis as a backbone of Applied Statistics. It introduces some of the most commonly applied multivariate techniques, such as: mean vector and covariance matrix estimation and testing, estimation and testing of correlations, principal component analysis, canonical correlation analysis, cluster analysis, factor analysis, discriminant analysis, Support Vector Machines and structural equations. Students will study the properties and the importance of the multivariate normality assumption in the context of each of these methods. Computing and data analysis feature prominently in this course. Note: This course is only available to students enrolled in the Graduate Diploma (5646) or Master of Data Science (8646) Programs.
learning_outcomes: Analyse datasets using multivariate techniques, interpret results, and draw conclusions on the real-world problem at hand.
Use multivariate terminology, notation, concepts and methods to successfully analyse multivariate data.
Apply the properties of multivariate normal distribution to justify optimality properties of Statistical Inference procedures based on multivariate normality.
Code a simple multivariate analysis using R language.
Formulate and solve inference problems that use multivariate statistical procedures involving covariance or correlation matrices.
Perform a range of multivariate inference procedures using the R software.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Must be enrolled in 5646 or 8646 and have completed ZZSC9001 Foundations of Data Science and ZZSC5905 Statistical Inference for data scientists or equivalent

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Bayesian Inference and Computation for Data Scientists
syllabus_overview: After describing the fundamentals of Bayesian inference, this course will examine several detailed aspects including: the specification of prior and posterior distributions, Bayesian decision theoretic concepts, the ideas behind Bayesian hypothesis tests, model choice and model averaging, and various model types such as hierarchical and mixture models. An important part of Bayesian inference is the requirement to numerically evaluate complex integrals on a routine basis. Accordingly this course will also introduce the ideas behind Monte Carlo integration, importance sampling, rejection sampling, Markov chain Monte Carlo samplers such as the Gibbs sampler and the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm. This course is only available to students enrolled in the Online Masters or Graduate Diploma of Data Science. Material is delivered 100% online through a series of self-guided lessons which include challenges, practice questions and videos. Questions can be asked on the discussion forum. Webinars will be held to guide students through the material and to help answer further questions that cannot be raised in the discussion forum.
learning_outcomes: Extend statistical knowledge beyond classical statistical techniques to demonstrate when the Bayesian approach can be beneficial.
Explain the philosophy and background concepts underlying Bayesian inference.
Identify and explain the importance of computational techniques that are critical for Bayesian inference.
Perform Bayesian analysis on real-world data.
Construct Bayesian models for practical examples and discuss their advantages and disadvantages.
prerequisites: Must be enrolled in 5646 Graduate Diploma in Data Science or 8646 Master of Data Science.

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Foundations of Data Science
syllabus_overview: This is an intensive course that covers the fundamentals of Data Science as it is applied in Computer Science, Economics, Mathematics and Statistics. The course will introduce topics such as databases, data analytics, data mining, Bayesian statistics, statistical software, econometrics, machine learning, and business forecasting. The course also introduces the Data Science and Decisions program, indicating the relevance of the courses that follow in the program (including electives) and their place in data science and its applications. This course includes lectures, tutorials, and workshops and is delivered completely online. The course will take the flipped classroom approach. Students are assigned the “homework” of watching video lectures and reading materials relevant to the online lecture session. During each session, a recap and overview of the content will be given and students will practice what they’ve learned through examples and tutorial problems.
learning_outcomes: Apply probability rules in a given setting to calculate key quantities.
Use R/RStudio to perform statistical computations and simulations.
Use key theoretical tools to explore the properties of random variables.
Apply various data visualisation tools, perform regression analysis and draw casual inference from data.
Apply key methods of statistical inference in applied settings.
Apply fundamental data science techniques and tools, including machine learning, Naïve Bayes classification, Decision trees, K-Nearest Neighbour, unsupervised learning and neural networks.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Enrolment in Data Science 8646 or 5646 or 7446 or Financial Technology 8433 or 5433 or 7434

institution: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)
title: Data Science Project
syllabus_overview: This course exposes students to research methods in applying data science techniques to a research project. The course serves as a capstone in the Master of Data Science program. Students will be required to apply and demonstrate their learning from the courses in the program. It also requires students to present their work in visual and verbal forms including a presentation.
learning_outcomes: Students will be able to apply robust research methods to design, build, or evaluate a project as it relates to data science.
Students will be able to communicate technical information clearly, both verbally and in writing
Students will be able to work effectively in a project team, and lead when required
Students will be able to critically reflect on a specialist body of knowledge related to data science.
Students will be able to manage their time effectively, and make reasoned trade-offs over competing demands
Students will be able to work from a set of requirements, elaborate them, and produce a specification
prerequisites: Enrolled in 8646 and completed 48UOC of courses within the program
